title: This App Fraudulently Charges Subscription Without Even Downloading.
body:
I received a targeted ad on Facebook over a year ago to do a $1 trial of the program through my web browser. I got a single message sent to the spam email attached to my Facebook account saying I’d be charged $39.99 every other month. It said to activate my premium subscription with a link in that email. I never activated the subscription until today because I didn’t know about it. They never sent a reminder email after clearly knowing the “premium subscription” hadn’t been activated, but they’ll gladly steal money for services not being rendered. How else would you explain me having to click the activation link from 6/14/25 TODAY, make a web account for the first time TODAY, then download the app for the first time ever TODAY to cancel via a web page within the app? I’m disgusted that I was preyed upon for having ADD and my disease process was exploited for their financial gain. It charges Apple Pay, but not in a way that it’d show up under iCloud or App subscriptions. My state law mandates one click cancellation for online only services; this required multiple platforms and excessive clicks through at least 3 minutes worth of this useless program. I have reported this company to the Attorney General and want my $279.93 refunded immediately. Feel free to keep the single $1 I agreed to pay. 

495 other people have mentioned having this problem too, so it’s not my own stupidity. They intentionally conceal their billing and I’m sure the every other month charging helps it from being detected as a recurrent bill/subscription service. This was not picked up by full Norton Financial tracking, nor was it readily identified by other spending trackers. 

These developers should be ashamed of themselves for exploiting folks with mental health conditions. I’ve deleted all social media accounts and have made a dedicated effort to improve my digital hygiene. I’m willingly subscribed to about 10-15 other services, so I do not have an issue with subscription services provided that I’m willingly signing up for them.

title: The billing practices of this app should be illegal—hundreds of dollars of duplicate bills
body:
The alarming thing about this app is that it promotes itself as ADHD support then discretely makes multiple frivolous debit card charges that someone with ADHD is less likely to notice happening. Then it creates a tedious hours-long process to correct the matter or unsubscribe from accounts if you want to stop being billed, knowing that many people with ADHD will be too exhausted to go through that. 

wish I could attach a screenshot of my bank statement in which 15 out of the last 20 transactions are duplicate unauthorized charges made by this company long after I canceled my subscription. Even when I signed up they claimed the fee was a monthly charge, but they try to charge me twice a week. 

Here’s what happened. I was signed up for this app for less than 5 minutes before the first duplicate credit card charges started rolling in. The first round was three identical $25 signup charges, which meant they billed me $75, three times what I authorized. I realized my mistake and canceled my account. But—days later, they charged me $75 again in three separate $25 transactions. 

The company simply directs you to their opaque unsubscribe process, saying they won’t stop billing you unless you unsubscribe in the *exact same way* that you signed up. There are several signup methods and they aren’t able to say which one you used. There is no other support that they provide. Unfortunately, unsubscribing is not an option because, according to their systems, I already canceled my subscription. There seem to be multiple ghost accounts I have no access to, there is no way to identify what signup method they think I used so that I could unsubscribe by that process. 

Ultimately, I had to close the bank account they were billing me at, which, again, takes valuable time. But I still get weekly fraud alerts from my bank notifying me this company is still trying to bill the debit card which no longer exists. 

I believe this type of business practice is illegal in my state, and I have reported them, but it needs to be a federal crime.

author: Español Andy

title: Speechless
body:
TL,DR: I do not recommend you download this app. I do not recommend you provide this app with your credit card information. This app has many bugs. This app promises too many simultaneous features and will leave you confused as to what you did in the app. This app prompts you to purchase many additional apps all at once. This app hurt my brain and made me dumber for using it. This app made me financially poorer (even though it’s a free trial). It’s like the D0n@lď Tr¥^^p of apps. Do not—I repeat, do not—take the five star reviews seriously. They simply cannot be real. Have a fine day. 

>>>Fabulous is without doubt the most convoluted & confusing app I think I’ve ever tried using.

Found about this online and took their questionnaire. I agreed to their free trial outside of the app (DO NOT DO THIS!!!) and used Apple’s HideMyEmail feature to protect my anonymity. 

I immediately found myself on a webpage asking for a small fee to pay their people for the “free trial.” I am nice and apparently gullible because I stupidly agreed. Then they sent me to a page that asked me to ¿sign up for other apps? At additional fees? And separate trial periods? Like… I was SOOOO lost! 

So, I downloaded the app and tried signing in… which was a nightmare. It asked me if I wanted to subscribe and stuff despite me providing my email address/username. This got me to thinking that maybe I agreed to one of Fabulous’s sister apps and maybe I didn’t even know what I was trying to do! Then I couldn’t sign into the original website without having to retake the questionnaire again! I finally found a login page which required email verification. I push the button in the email and get directed to the beginning of the questionnaire… AGAIN! 

I honestly have no idea HOW I FINALLY got into the app, but I did. It prompted me to tap on a play icon overlaying a pretty picture of some dude ¿rafting? ¿I think? Which brought me to a list of things me and Fabulous’s little sprites would set out to accomplish. Cute. I pushed on a button… nothing. Couldn’t go back. Couldn’t go forward. I closed the app and HAD TO GO THROUGH THE ENTIRE SIGN IN AGAIN. Did it… bc I’m patient and kind. Landed again on the rafting guy then the list then the nothingness. Redownloaded the app. Same thing. Downloaded one of their sister apps. Couldn’t make heads or tails of it. Finally, in this app, it brought me to a water counting page… because, in order to learn good habits, you must start by counting cups of water… you know…like every other self-help app? 

In the midst of this, my credit card company who could care less about a $1000 out of the blue charge to a kayak company in the middle of the Serengeti called repeatedly until I finally answered asking if I legit made this $10 purchase. That, too, was an absolute nightmare.

I canceled my subscription (I think? Lots of people here say they did too but got hoodwinked and charged later anyway). 

I do not recommend this app. I REALLY do not recommend providing your credit card information to this thing. This app did not help my ADHD and made me feel a certain kind of crazy that I was not aware that I am so capable of.

title: Subscribe through app store not their app
body:
Summary, I didn’t find the app helpful after trying twice. For me personally it as annoying. But more importantly, I thought I canceled, apparently didn’t because they don’t make it easy. They charged me for the next year but I had 0 notification & had no idea I had this subscription. I just happened to notice months later. So no notifications about an auto-renewal, no receipt or a cancellation email. They would’ve got away with charging me forever for nothing. 

I have tried this app twice. The first time it was engaging during the trial then no more involved assistance it was basically on you to keep up with your goals. 

Now it’s TOO much going on in the app like a whole story & almost forced you to do things. I only tried for a few days-a month at most & ultimately decided it wasn’t for me. Well last year I guess I didn’t cancel a full 24hrs before the trial ended so they wouldn’t refund my $14 despite having deleted the app & not using it. 

Welp, thank god I don’t use my bank card on Apple pay often because I just noticed in Aug that I was charge yet again for THIS year back in April! Unfortunately I forgot to cancel I guess because they don’t make it easy. I swear I did before deleting the app but you have to do it through their website. But the real issue is that I wasn’t emailed a receipt so had I not stumbled across the payment I would’ve never known & they would’ve kept charging me $14 for nothing every year. Apple sends me a receipt & has all of my subscriptions in one place for review & cancellation. I don’t have to guess or hope I find them. So I highly recommend only subscribing to things through an app store or a credit card that sends you alerts for any payments made. Also turn on notifications for any time any card is charged. Most of mine are on but apparently I didn’t have them on for this bank card. Also my mistake. But still, these companies know what they’re doing. 

Fabulous, you guys need to send receipts & honestly renewal alerts ahead of time for people like myself that weren’t even using the app, to cancel. I also didn’t receive a cancellation email I had to screenshot it for proof. But I immediately received one to come back! That’s shady.

title: Scammers
body:

And yet… I was charged again.

I contacted support, explained what happened, and requested a refund. They refused.

That’s an unacceptable experience. If your own app tells a customer their subscription has been cancelled, the customer should be able to trust that cancellation.

My advice: don’t trust the cancellation screen. If you cancel, contact support directly, insist on written confirmation by email, and keep an eye on your credit card statements afterward.

I’m leaving this review because I don’t want other customers to learn this lesson the expensive way.

The Fabulous App: 1 star. Would give 0 if I could.

body: Last week I cancelled my subscription through Apple, which had been charging quarterly for premium. Today I was charged for a full year price. It also gives no further information as to how they continue to access payment info, as this new charge was sent independently without any Apple involvement or record under my subscriptions. If you want to use the app, do not engage in the free trial and do not upload any payment information, but I suggest avoiding it entirely as it also relies heavily on AI in addition to these deceptive billing concerns. I am extremely disappointed as I have recommended this app to others in my capacity as a mental health clinician, will no longer be doing so and will be advising my clients about the predatory billing

title: Maybe good intentions, but fradulent
body:
It seems like a good app if you have endless money to pay them. They talk about developing the skills to build good habits and expand into other apps for anxiety, better sleep, or mindfulness, but the way they introduce them to you is very fraudulent. I was at my lowest point and signed up for this app to give it a shot. I signed up for a fabulous trial and was impatient to get to the lessons but kept getting pop up adds recommending other programs that could help: Elixir, Clarify, Lumiere, and Lune. To continue to the content I just kept clicking okay and signed up for 4 free trials of $39.99 each of bundled apps. When it finally came time to cancel the trials because I did not feel the app helped me I had to find each subscription manually and cancel individually (even though they were bundled). And this is why I came to the conclusion that they are scammers because if your goal really is to help people why would you structure your app in a way that is a money trap. They count on the fact that you won’t catch little details such as “cancelling the subscription at least 24 hours before” or that cancelling one subscription does not cancel others. I’m honestly disappointed because I feel slightly exploited when I was in a poor headspace but I guess everyone needs to make their money. I strongly urge others not to get this app, but if you do, read the fine print and know what you’re signing up for.

Update: I’ve contacted fabulous 3 times now and am still getting $39.99 charge attempts on my card even though they’ve reassured me that the auto-renewal was cancelled.

title: NOT for neurodivergent IMO
body:
I really wanted to like this app because it has a great reputation for people like myself, but the onboarding completely lost me. The review is a little long but it’s worth the read.

The biggest issue wasn’t the goals themselves. It was that the app immediately requires you to start making choices before you can explore or do anything else. There isn’t an option to simply explore the app, learn how it works, or ease into the experience first. Instead, it essentially says, “Select this to continue,” with no alternative path forward.

For people with anxiety, burnout, or some neurodivergent people, getting started is often the hardest part. I downloaded the app because I needed help with that, and the onboarding didn’t support that for me. Don’t immediately ask me to do the very thing I’m struggling to do.

It felt like signing up to learn horseback riding and, instead of introducing you to the horse or explaining the basics, someone immediately hands you the reins and says, “Here’s your trail.”

I don’t need endless customization. I just wanted another path, like a brief introduction or walkthrough before getting started. Let me get comfortable before telling me where I’m going.

Another thing that also disappointed me was the advertising. The ads gave me the impression there would be a more in-depth questionnaire to personalize my experience, but I never found one. I was also surprised to see the app marketed as being helpful for people with ADHD and other neurodivergent users because, as someone in that audience, the onboarding didn’t feel designed with my experience in mind.

That approach may work well for many people, including neurotypical people, but for me it increased my anxiety instead of my motivation.

If an app is designed to help people with motivation and action, it shouldn’t assume everyone is ready to act the moment they open it. Some of us seeking help need help taking that very first step. 

I truly hope the developers consider offering 2 onboarding paths: one for users who are ready to jump right in, and another for users who need a little time to understand the app before getting started. I think that small change could make the app more accessible to an entirely different group of people and help more users succeed.

For many of us, simply opening the app for growth is already the first victory. Meeting users where they are, instead of where they hope to be, could help more people continue the journey and ultimately succeed.

Unfortunately for me, this wasn’t a neurodivergent-friendly onboarding experience.
author: Sha Rari

title: Predatory Pricing Structure
body:
Update: After contacting support as directed in the developer response, I was told:

“At the time of purchase, the renewal date and billing details were provided, and it was stated that the trial or subscription automatically renews unless it's cancelled at least 24 hours before the renewal date.”

Basically, “sucks to be you, we already got your money.” This seemed like an AI generated support response, and wasn’t actually relevant to my request. The relevant portion of the response was that the charges were just non-refundable.

So, if you actually have ADHD, this company is absolutely predatory, you will be subjected to literally five different upcharges if you try to sign up for the trial, all of which appear identical! And some of which sign you up for ADDITIONAL, SIGNIFICANT monthly recurring charges. Just stay away from these people. Nasty, preying on people like that.

Original: 

It sounds like a great app and idea, and then you go to sign up… First, there’s no free trial, and you’re guilted into paying for a two week trial and sign up to the $20/month membership automatically afterward. After you accept, there are five(!) additional upsell pop up screens that you have to click through, that all look quite similar. So I did the second one, thinking that it was confirming the regular membership. Nope, $10 worth of PDFs, and ANOTHER $20/month “bundle” membership.

Then there are like four more screens asking for money! And probably additional memberships! Like, how much do you expect people to pay you? $100 up front for the trial and $100/month for all the “content” offered?

For an app that claims to take care of people with ADHD, this is absolutely predatory, right out of the gate. Enjoy the $26 you scammed out of me, cancelled immediately.

title: Predatory Clickbait is all this is.
body:
I don’t know how this app has 4.4 stars. I downloaded the app and within 20 to 30 seconds knew that all these add-ons and subscription bundles were intended to catch users who didn’t cancel their trial. The app itself was pointless and within minutes I canceled my trial. Or at least I thought I did. I was even refunded the one dollar for the initial charge. But as I later found out all the other apps connected to this app had added my billing information, even though I didn’t subscribe to them.

Fast-forward to two nights ago and four charges came through from this app. USAA immediately declined them and I went to the website and my details said subscription was canceled. I tried to delete my info, but as soon as I clicked on, cancel subscription to delete account link went away. I thought everything was fine and dandy until USAA told me that they had blocked my card until I spoke with them.

I had the card turned back on under the presumption that everything was canceled and today the fabulous company that they are ran four more charges through my Apple wallet. When I went back to the fabulous website, surprisingly all four subscriptions showed active, even though I had canceled them two separate times.

Apps like this are trash and pray on consumers who are interested in trying an app that appears like it’s going to be helpful only to fall victim to these predatory tactics of forced subscriptions and impossible ways to cancel and delete your information. be warned!

title: Be wary of your card information
body: Have barely even used the app, I forgot to set up the notifications to have it delivered to me in my phone’s Focus settings, but this is not about that, this is about what they do when you give them your card details for a free trial. I got the one week and realized I just never saw the notifications for it, so I went to cancel it, and it gave me the option to extend it for one week, so I thought maybe, why not, and extended it and marked down the exact date it would renew, so I could go online and cancel it. Little did I know, they hid a whole other charge underneath the main one for the only app of theirs I had an account on, a “bundle” subscription on top of the one I was signing up for a trial for, for apps I did not even have. I never attempted to cancel that one because I didn’t even know I had given them consent to attempt to charge me for it at all. This morning, I received a message from my bank stating that they blocked a fraudulent charge, and a website’s name. Since I was not expecting any charges, because the date for the renewal was not for a week, I stated that it was not me who attempted the charge, and immediately my card got cancelled and now I have to wait around for a new one, and I have to go through and update my card information now for all my bills. All because of this incredibly deceptive and scammy app that I never even got around to using. I am irritated beyond measure and dearly hope they get hit with a class action lawsuit, any business this scummy with trying to get your money is not worth a cent on principle. If they had a product good enough, they would just be upfront about everything and allow the product to speak for itself, ESPECIALLY since it appears that they target ND people and those with ADHD, meaning they target those who are most likely to forget to track their subscriptions and how many times they got charged for something. Honestly, just disgusting overall and I am so irritated by the utter inconvenience, I would give it zero stars everywhere if I could. Never ever give them your card info, only get your free trials through the App Store and remember to cancel as soon as you decide it is not for you!

title: A Fitting Title:
body:
So far, I have been—at the least—very satisfied with the design aspects of this app and the ways with which it goes about helping others achieve their goals. Usually, in my usage of other self-help apps, I would think something among the lines of, “Oh my! I truly cannot wait for my problems to be all better! I am immediately going to be much more of a better person with this cure-all app for my life~!!” Needless to say that’s not true. In my experience, a problem is a problem, and there seems seldom a way to get rid of such—especially when said problem is within oneself. This app, however, seems to be more realistic. Its scientific backings definitely intrigued me, and I would be lying to say otherwise. In a simple way—or maybe just a more elaborately structured one—this app describes a process and instills a sense of understand as to what will be directly required of you (or not) in order to change your life for the better. That’s all, I believe. Not really a review; just an opinion. 

	One last thing: I don’t know what merits the praises of a stranger may have, but to everyone who genuinely had hopes about this app when it was being made and put their heart into it, good job. I do mean that, too.

title: SCAM - DO NOT DOWNLOAD!
body:
This app is incredibly deceptive, requiring a “activation” link to start using the app, that tricks the user into opting in to a $39.99 subscription bimonthly. They make it unreasonably difficult to unsubscribe and delete your account, and offer no help for requesting refunds.

They claim you can request a refund from the Apple App Store, but the app is “not eligible” for one.

In the app itself, the user is constantly pressured to upgrade and buy extra add-ons. I did not agree to any of this. All I did was agree to the $1 download charge and click the “activate” link in an email, as is common for new accounts.

The fact that they bury text about future charges after a trial period in this “receipt” and activation email is manipulative and infuriating. This all happens with an app that is supposed to help busy people who feel overwhelmed.

I bought this app because it was listed as an “Editor’s Choice” and claimed to be award-winning and backed by rigorous research. IT IS A SCAM.

body:

They do not have my make purchases through Apple so you cannot easily cancel your subscription. You have to wave your way through the website to find where you can cancel your subscription. I am still waiting for their support to respond to address this issue. 
From my perspective this seems like a quick cash grab from many people who are genuinely trying to better themselves who end up suffering because of it. Please if you get this app, check a dozen times that you have properly canceled your subscription.
Edit: After a week of emailing them back and forth and them not being able to give me a clear reason why my charges weren’t refundable, it was only after I told them I’d be disputing this with my bank that they confirmed my account/subscription was cancelled and that ALL charges have been refunded. Once my refunds process I’ll still be locking all charges just to make sure. But just know that being persistent works. Do not let them give you a refund for just 1 charge, make sure you get ALL charges refunded. The fact that they try and give you 1 in the beginning to make you feel like you got something back means they know they’re operating a scam.

title: Horrible- Don’t Waste Your Money!
body:
I genuinely cannot believe how bad the Fabulous app turned out to be. It markets itself as a life-changing wellness and productivity tool, but in reality it’s an overpriced collection of repetitive notifications, generic self-help advice, and locked features hidden behind an absurd subscription paywall.

The app constantly pushes expensive premium plans while offering very little actual value. Most of the content feels recycled, shallow, and designed more to keep you subscribed than to help you build meaningful habits. For an app that claims to improve mental wellness, it creates more frustration than motivation.

What makes the experience even worse is how incredibly difficult it is to cancel. The cancellation process feels intentionally confusing, buried under multiple menus and subscription settings that seem designed to wear users down. Even after attempting to cancel, the app continues pushing upgrade prompts and retention offers nonstop.

The overall design may look polished, but underneath the aesthetics is a manipulative subscription machine that overpromises and underdelivers. There are countless free or cheaper habit-tracking apps that provide more functionality without the aggressive monetization tactics.

Save your money, save your time, and avoid the headache.

title: Not ADHD-friendly and very overwhelming
body:
This app is not designed for people who struggle with legitimate, diagnosed ADHD, but that is who they are marketing towards. If you’re not careful, you end up paying for multiple subscriptions of $40+ a month for apps that I found completely inaccessible from the start.

After a lengthy quiz that supposedly builds your “personalized journey,” you pay whatever you’re able to ($1 minimum) for a “free trial.” The “personalized” piece also didn’t feel personalized based on my answers. The “journey,” tone, and overall app felt generic and not catered to me or anyone neurodivergent. 

Opening the app, I was immediately overwhelmed by unavoidable pop ups of quotes, reviews, credentials, and long paragraphs explaining the science behind different therapeutic approaches. Anyone struggling with motivation, ADHD or not, isn’t going to feel like reading all that. 

Eventually it gave me  a goal for the week, that followed my “personal journey” but it was to ~drink water every morning~ which didn’t align at all with the goals or struggles I outlined in the quiz, and was honestly insulting.

Canceling is a whole process too. You have to jump through hoops and cancel each app they made you download, or you’ll get charged for 3+ subscriptions. It honestly feels like a trap for vulnerable people looking for help.

title: Subscription Scam Artists
body:
This app is a complete scam. I was charged three times in one day for a subscription I did not authorize, and the only explanation I received was a vague email referencing multiple wellness kits I do not recall approving. The creators seem more focused on profit than on their users, showing little concern even when charges are made without proper authorization.

It is also extremely difficult to cancel this so called subscription. The process feels intentionally complicated and lacks clear guidance. A wellness app should be user friendly, intuitive, and supportive, but this one is clunky, confusing, and frustrating to navigate.

Companies in the wellness space should prioritize transparency and flexibility with subscriptions, or at the very least provide clear support to help users manage their accounts.

As a professional in the wellness field, I strongly recommend staying away from this app and choosing a more transparent and user friendly alternative.

body:

When I tried to cancel, they offered to extend for another free trial I accept accepted, only to find out that they had indeed charged me later on. I then try to request a refund. They refuse to acknowledge this at all, just simply stating no refunds and closing your request.

Now the app itself, still not great. Doesn’t even have a simple feature like Duolingo that makes it so successful, which is being able to see your streak to motivate you over the months easily. The app is very complicated, it is kind of tricky to figure out how you follow your journey. And not easy to pick up. Definitely requires effort to learn which I was too busy to do! As I’m sure many of you are.

Anyway AVOID this company and their related products at all cost unless you like being misled and charged for something you didn’t even use. With no help given when you ask for it.

UPDATE 3/2026 wow the saga continues. 3 months later I now find out they charged me AGAIN last month??? Why? I deleted the app in a rage in December. 

Oh and to respond to their response. I’ve had multiple emails with their support email which is just canned responses that keep closing my ticket as resolved.

title: Life-Changing Habit App for ADHD
body:
I absolutely love this app. As someone with ADHD, staying consistent with routines can be really difficult, but Fabulous makes it feel achievable instead of overwhelming. The step-by-step habit building, reminders, and motivational guidance keep me on track without making me feel pressured. It turns small actions into real daily routines.

What I like most is that it focuses on progress, not perfection. The structure helps me stay organized and build better habits for my mornings and overall wellbeing. It’s visually beautiful, easy to use, and actually motivating.

If you struggle with focus, routines, or ADHD, this app is definitely worth trying. It has helped me stay more consistent and feel more in control of my day.

title: Pricey — but impressive if it fits your budget
body:
These apps genuinely work well and are beautifully designed. It's clear that real intention went into the user experience, habit-building structure, and overall functionality. If you're serious about personal growth and enjoy guided systems, they can be powerful tools.

My main concern is the pricing.

I was placed on the Fabulous Premium bimonthly plan at about $40 twice per month, roughly $80 for a single app. That already feels expensive, but what really adds up is how strongly the platform encourages you to integrate their companion apps.

I activated several free trials to explore the ecosystem, and if I continued with all of them, the total would come to about $270 per month, before personal coaching. My quote for  coaching was $60 per month, bringing the potential total to around $330 monthly. Interestingly, someone else I know was quoted about $87 per month for coaching, so pricing may vary based on promotions or user specific offers. Either way, the lack of clear, consistent pricing makes it harder to plan it financially.

To be fair, the quality is there, the apps are engaging, motivating, and thoughtfully built. But the costs can actually quickly without you realizing just how much you’re committing to.

Bottom line: Great platform with real value, but take time to review every subscription carefully. This is best suited for people who intentionally budget for premium wellness apps rather than those looking for a more affordable option. 

I read this five stars to help boost visibility so more people are aware of the real costs. The apps are strong, but the financial commitment is something you should fully understand upfront.

title: meh
body:
I’m not sure who this is intended for and neither are the developers.  It is an app that doesn’t seem suited for anyone with mental health issues as it is entirely overwhelming and bloated with so many features. Finally, if for some reason you are able to make sense of the crowded user interface, then you need to be at rock bottom with no sense of responsibility whatsoever and also totally incompetent.  It seems counterproductive to the user base because if you were completely bereft of sense, it’s hard to imagine you could afford the ridiculous monthly rate for this “premium” service. 

I wanted to use this app to complete a specific goal.  Instead, I got roped into establishing a healthy habit of “drinking water.”  I already do that and don’t need an app to remind me to drink when I’m thirsty, let alone a reflection of what to do to stay hydrated.   

I want to like this app; I do.  I think the discover tab that has a bunch of infographs with suggestions of self care are more helpful than the interactive portion.  Of course there’s no way to track those things nor do these static images stay accessible since they change every day.   

Fabulous says this research and the app’s configuration were based on input from studies at Harvard, Stanford and a bunch of other prestigious universities.  To me it sounds like they got some pseudo social media therapists and maybe paid them to use those universities’ facilities rather than it being sanctioned by academics that actually attend the school.  

Save your money and do a search for infographics on your favorite social app.

title: Initial setup is miserable, feels like scammy subscription company not confident in their product!
body:
It’s one thing to boast absurdly confident statements, and it’s another to try scare you into subscribing immediately. Multiple subscription screens in they say you won’t see an offer this good for at least twelve months. I had done some initial question at this point but haven’t even used the product yet. 

I get it’s good to have confidence. I have some other worldly confidence with some things in my life which has helped me in some areas (like with sports). I struggle with confidence in other areas. I think it’s often with good reason because of my failures haha. Of course I can improve that with better practices. But, back to the app, while it’s good to have optimism and confidence, it comes across as fake when it’s like “it’s easy, just do this!” When you’re dealing with people with severe ptsd, adhd or other severe issues, many of us are aware it’s gonna be a windy adventure towards getting better. Coming across too confident on how easy it’s going to come across as fake, unrealistic and likely… not effective because you’re living in a fake world ignoring many of the harsh realities than many of us deal with. 

One more side note. Being prompted a ton about building a habit of water drinking in the morning despite me not wanting it is super annoying. Being told a bunch of how much it’s going to help me is extra. I already do this naturally and always have. Please make it more customizable if you want to make this genuine. 

I get some of these practices might be good for some, but man I’m shocked at how miserable of an experience this was setting this up this morning.

Customers receive no notice that they will be charged after the free trial or when they are charged.

title: Beautiful Ap, Predatory Charges, Shocking $300 triple charges after Trial
body:

It's the opposite of calm-more like a high-pressure sales trap. I started the seven-day trial, but the day it ended, over three hundred dollars in triple charges slammed my bank from all these "premium" services auto-subscribed billed bi-monthly without clear warning.
Since I went through Apple, they used a hidden secure email, making unsubscribing a total nightmare no easy button in the app or subscriptions list. My nervous system was in overdrive.
Unless you're loaded and don't mind throwing money at pretty interfaces you'll never use, steer clear.
Bank's fraud team saved me, but not everyone's that lucky. Avoid this bait-and-switch.

title: Sneaky billing and horrible customer
body:
I signed up for a subscription in August and realized after a few days that it wasn’t something that I would use. I canceled during my free subscription and I have an email confirmation of canceling three days before the renewal period. A couple months went by and I realized that I was getting charged $50 a month for the subscription that I had canceled. I emailed them and got an automated response that they would not give me a refund. I emailed it again with screenshots and proof of my cancellation, and I got the same exact Response saying that they would not give me a refund. I emailed a third time and demanding a refund or I will go to my bank, and I got the same response again saying that they will not give me a refund. So now I have to go to my bank and try to get three months worth of subscriptions refunded to my account and I will have to change my debit card number in to prevent this from happening in the future. If I go to the site right now and try to cancel I can’t because I canceled three months ago. 

Update: It took months and dozens of emails back-and-forth to get two out of three of the $50 charges refunded to my account. I had to threaten to go to my bank and get the charges reversed. After several months, they finally told me that somehow when I subscribed to one product, I ended up with a subscription to multiple other products, which was never my intent, and that’s why when I thought I canceled the service, I didn’t cancel everything. I stand by my original review that this is an intentionally sneaky and underhanded way to make money off of people who do not want a subscription.

author: Caitlinsamom

title: Deceptive Subscription Model
body:
I cannot take this app seriously. It promotes science backed behavior change, yet relies on a subscription model that feels deliberately opaque. Managing the subscription is confusing, and the in app link to do so fails entirely when signing in through Google. That crosses from poor design into deception.

This kind of design is harmful. A wellness app positions itself as a tool for self improvement, trust, and personal agency. A broken or obstructed subscription system undermines that trust and removes user control. When cancellation paths are hidden or nonfunctional, people are pressured into continued payment through friction rather than choice.

That is not a neutral business decision. It exploits time, stress, and cognitive load, particularly for users seeking support during vulnerable periods. Any product claiming to be science backed should meet a higher standard of transparency and basic functionality. Failing at that level causes financial harm and damages confidence in legitimate behavioral health tools

title: Confusing spiderweb of add-on habits
body:
I can see how this app might be helpful for those who seek rigid structure in establishing habits. But it is NOT the gentle habit coach it claims to be. Its aggressive upselling, when combined with its condescending attitude toward users are off-putting to me. 

I can’t even list the number of times I was being hit by unsubtle pushes for add-on apps. More add-on pushes than actual help with habit-making from the app itself—like, “Sure, we can help you a little, but you can’t really succeed unless you pay for This Other App and add it to your daily habits as well.” How many subscription apps does it take to set up some daily habits? 

There’s no customization to accommodate individual preferences and needs. You’re not even asked for them so that you can opt in or opt out of condescending notifications. 

It’s also a little condescending in its mimicry of the Duolingo “You must do this daily or lose your progress and lose the pats-on-the-back you get from participating Every.Single.Day.” As with Duolingo, you can purchase “freezes” to avoid being shamed by missing a bit because you’re sick, on vacation, or otherwise can’t log in.

If you prefer a rigid structure and myriad daily check-ins for establishing daily habits that someone else prescribes for you, this might work. If you can manage aaaaaall the aggressive add-on sales pitches, afford them all, and then adopt them as a tangled spiderweb of new habits.

title: Unclear subscription cancellation . No phone support
body:
I found Fabulous through an ad on X and signed up to try the free trial. I didn’t like the product (too many “apps/kits” and it felt confusing), so I believed I cancelled in the app around Dec 5.

Then on Jan 5, I was charged four separate transactions by “Fabulous SAS”:
	•	$29.99
	•	$39.99
	•	$39.99
	•	$39.99
That’s nearly $150. There is no way I intentionally signed up for that many paid subscriptions at once, especially for a service I did not continue using.

When I contacted support, they told me these were “past due subscriptions” and then sent me a link explaining cancellation must be done on their website. That was the first time I understood the cancellation method. The cancellation flow is not clear and sends you between app and website, which makes it easy to think you cancelled when you haven’t.

Another issue: there’s no customer support phone number. When billing issues happen, email-only support is slow and stressful.

If you try this app - which I won't advise you to do anyway:
	•	Take screenshots of every cancellation step.
	•	Confirm cancellation in the correct place (app vs web).
	•	Watch your card closely for multiple charges, especially if you tried any “kits/apps.”

I can’t recommend until subscription management is centralized and cancellation is simple, transparent, and confirmed clearly. I am writing this detailed review and I hope it will save someone out there. Don't fall for the many X ads it doesn't worth it.

title: Billing trap disguised as a wellness tool
body:
Auto-renewal is on by default, refunds are basically “no,” and the trial must be canceled more than 24 hours before it ends or you’re charged for the full subscription. Miss that window by a few hours and you’re out real money. That’s not user-friendly, it’s predatory.

The cancellation process is not clearly explained during signup, and their terms even pressure you not to dispute charges with your bank. That alone is a massive red flag.

Live coaching is worse: no refunds at all, fees if you reschedule within 8 hours (even for technical issues), and you can still lose your money if the session never happens properly.

For what is basically habit reminders and motivational content, the price is absurd. Add to that heavy data collection (health habits, device info, tracking, long-term marketing use after cancellation), and this app feels more focused on locking in revenue than helping users.

If you value your money, your time, or your privacy, skip this.

title: I like it, BUT…
body:
I think it does what it sets out to do. Things I like:
Goal setting and establishment of habits. I also like the fact that the message is not all unicorns and rainbows. They give you some grace and tell you there will be days where you struggle. Some days you will fail and that’s ok as long as you keep trying. 
I like the daily motivational messages. I especially appreciate the quotes from famous/inspirational figures and the early messages have made me realize that small changes will add up over time. Sounds simplistic, but they‘ve had some interesting points that have „clicked“ w me. 
I’ve been doing this for a week and I’m progressing in a positive way.  To be fair, I didn’t start deep in a pit of despair/rock bottom, BUT over the past 5 years, I’ve gone through a lot and the result has been bad habits, not taking care of myself and letting my house and parts of my life unravel. So I do have a fair amount of work to do …
Things I DONT LIKE :
I paid for premium but I’m still getting multiple messages, some sneaky, to try to get me to try other/ additional apps.  —Freq daily pop ups to sign up for x or y apps. I PAID for premium. I shouldn’t have to see these EVERY DAY. 
The app is a bit confusing in how it is set up. I’m not habit app naive.  It should have clear sections on motivational messages vs habits you are establishing vs other parts. etc.  Sometimes I feel like I have to search for what I need to do. (And then another ad for another app!)
There is a daily path w a ghost figure. I’m not too crazy about this. The figure (which represents me) is creepy IMO and the accompanying text is in quasi (forced) rhyme.  That can grate after a while. 
Finally, there are a fair number (daily) spelling and grammatical errors. Enough for me to notice them and it makes you wonder, if the developers are sloppy in this regard, how much attention /effort are they putting into the actual program? 

In sum, I’m seeing changes. I like the motivational messages. They are informative and inspiring without being preachy, but the issues listed above need work for me to continue membership past this year.

Addendum: after about a month, I gave up. Overall, the app seems to have multiple layers and is circuitous, which makes it confusing on a daily basis. I invested in a habit app which is much clearer and I can much more easily track my progress. If you need motivational messages, search elsewhere. I’m sure there’s an app for that that is much less confusing

title: Predatory Subscription
body: This app is creepy and I don't like it. I have autism and ADHD and downloaded it on a whim, opened it, saw all of the pop ups and tutorials, and immediately got overwhelmed. I think I paid a couple dollars to "try it out" and then it charged my card for a premium subscription the next month once I had already forgotten about it. After ignoring the app and its repetitive notifications for about two months without opening it, I finally fought my task avoidance enough to open it and cancel my subscription. This took like ten minutes for me to do, because it's hidden in a menu, and it pulls up a pop-up within the app that I couldn't access with my VPN on, so I had to turn that off. And the app has so many pop-up tutorial and other notifications that I kept having to swipe away. Once I finally found the correct settings to cancel my membership, the first time I tried to, it only paused it for two months. I had to click through the entire cancel screen (with an offer to keep my membership for a lower price, which also gave me The Ick) to properly get rid of my membership and promptly uninstall the app. If you actually have a mental disability on the level of ADHD and/or autism, I would highly advise you not to install this app like I did, because of these predatory behaviors. It unsettles me greatly that this app is designed the way that it is for a demographic of people that are usually much more susceptible to falling into traps like these.

title: Not what I expected, and the “free trial” isn’t free.
body:

I found it unnecessarily complicated, and it wasn’t clear what was included in the premium trial versus what was being upsold. The habit suggestions were extremely minimal (like drinking one glass of water a few times a week), which didn’t motivate me to keep opening the app. I was expecting more science based insights about habits and procrastination, similar to Noom, but much of the content felt vague and philosophical rather than practical.

The app emphasizes that it was created by Ivy League educated developers, which set an expectation for deeper educational value that, for me, fell flat and felt out of touch.

Also worth noting: the “free trial” isn’t actually free. You’re encouraged to pay upfront, and the fee (about $17) is non-refundable. I paid it, quickly realized the app wasn’t a fit, and couldn’t get a refund. If you’re reading this and still want to try Fabulous, don’t fall for the guilt trip and pay upfront. Consider my $17 your free trial.

title: Love but needs adjustment for moms
body:
I’m a special needs mom of a teenager and I just had a baby 6 months ago. Add ADHD to the mix, and every day is a balancing act between meltdown and miracle.

Fabulous has helped me build pockets of structure where there used to be none. I’m creating routines I actually remember to do even in chaos.

But here’s the thing: time blocking isn’t built for moms. Especially moms like me, whose time is ruled by kids, needs, therapy, and survival.

I can’t always ‘block distractions.’ Sometimes my distractions need diaper changes or meltdown support.

It would mean so much to see Fabulous introduce mom-friendly features like adaptable scheduling, “mom mode” templates, or even routines that auto-adjust based on the flow of our day.

Moms don’t need apps that demand perfection.
We need tools that move with our reality, not against it.
Fabulous is almost there. Just make space for us too.

title: Fabulous is, well, FABULOUS!
body:
Frankly, I have never enjoyed an app anywhere near as much as this one. I find Fabulous to be more profound and useful than any other app, ever. It provides me with gentle encouragement daily, a consistently positive environment, and is effectively nudging me towards sustainable personal growth. I have worked really hard over years trying to come up with a system that really serves me, trying a large number of to-do and reminder-type apps, daily planners (including designing my own), time blocking, calendars and alarms, thinking days, journaling, deep work … you name it! Fabulous is the first system that is actually consistently helping me, and, surprise surprise, it brings together several of the elements I’ve already tried into one effective bundle.

I have ADHD, which, among other things, means my brain’s executive function isn’t good at keeping me on track. The Fabulous app has turned out to be a key tool in managing my ADHD. In the three months since I started using Fabulous, I have seen a consistent uptick in my ability to accomplish my daily goals. I have set up morning and evening routines that I complete on a nearly daily basis. I also have created additional routines, which I am able to make progress on most days of the week. 

The app is also realistic, it regularly acknowledges that we are imperfect humans, bound to fail some of the time, but then it picks me right back up and offers fresh encouragement. I dig how the three short daily coachings—morning, focus, and night—include quotes from notable thinkers, poets, philosophers, scientists, artists, and the like. And I really appreciate that I have learned to celebrate even the smallest step forward, which greatly helps to keep me engaged. (We ADHDers lack dopamine, the happiness hormone, so accomplishing things can leave us feeling deadened, rather than joyous.)

When I first tried Fabulous a few years ago, I thought the app was too woo, but I was wrong. Its approach is science-based, having originated out of Duke University’s Center for Advanced Hindsight. I was also a bit put off by how much the app cost on first offer, but eventually came to a price I could afford. Now that I understand the remarkable breadth and depth this app offers, I’d be willing to pay more than I do. A funny thing to say, but actually true!

title: Typical Glitchy Mess for Mental Health Apps
body:
*Update - it’s been a year and I’ve contacted support three times and it still freezes more often now than it did when I wrote orig review. Zero stars if I could. 

TLDR - An app isn’t going to help your severe mental health, ADHD or procrastination bc they’re all too buggy for someone w these conditions to tolerate. They just add to it. 

Lots of glitches. Most times when I complete a routine, the congrats screen freezes. 

Also every single time, if you check off more than about 4 things on a routine list, the check boxes stop working. 

I’ve emailed them and they say to go to the settings and “redownload everything”. I’ve done this twice. 

I’ve made some pretty big strides in progress through talk therapy and EMDR the past two years, so the bugs don’t infuriate me like they would have a couple of years ago. 

But a mental health app that only adds to your frustration, an ADHD app that glitches and gives you reasons to switch your focus or just does it for you, and a procrastination app that puts obstacles in your flow and gives you another reason to “do something else” and takes up more of your time for no reason (which is every single ADHD app I’ve ever tried) isn’t worth paying a subscription for. 

Bothers me that anyone and their mother can throw together a glitchy clunky app and make a liveable income in 2025.

title: Misleading Payment Model
body:
The app itself works acceptably well for habit-building and has a pretty UI to draw you in. However, I cannot recommend the app as their subscription model is misleading and intentionally hard to cancel. I was advertised a $1 subscription, and then received a $40 payment a few weeks later. I thought I cancelled the plan immediately after and then deleted the app, only to find another $40 charge today 3 months later. In the cancellation process today, they only allowed me to cancel my subscription after jumping through 4-5 different windows trying to re-sell me the subscription I already had, change to a monthly plan instead, etc. Based off of the other reviews, I clearly am not the only person who has had this problem.

I can’t help but feel like with Fabulous’s marketing and their main demographics, their aim is to set up a Planet Fitness-style model where they make money from people struggling with ADHD by tricking people into keeping their subscriptions going. As an alum from the dev’s school (which was a major part of the advertising I saw for the product), it is disappointing to see questionable financial models be the focus for what could be a genuinely helpful app.

A quick search online shows many complaints about this app being a scam and charging inappropriately. Yet it’s featured in the App Store as getting the “Editors Choice” award and I am unable to leave a review!!
What is going on here? Why is Apple not addressing this issue? The charge does not appear in our Apple account, so it is impossible to Report, as you are only allowed feedback on apps where a charge is listed. 
Please delete this app from your store immediately as it is preying upon your customers and it’s not hard to find that this was brought to your attention many times before.

title: Well Done & Helpful
body: I was very skeptical about self help apps, but Fabulous is probably the best one I’ve ever seen. The aesthetics are gorgeous and you can tell that a lot of time was put into the design. I just realized that I have ADHD, and I’m going to see a psychiatrist next week, so I haven’t seen results yet, but I honestly feel like I’m in good hands with this app. I’ve honestly been subscribed for months, and I was going to cancel because I wasn’t using it, but something told me to open it up last week, and I’m glad I did. My favorite part is definitely the information from researchers, scientists, professors, and other professionals in the field. It makes me feel like they’re using tried and true techniques. I’m looking forward to continuing on this journey. If you’re looking for a self help app, I’d suggest you give Fabulous a try.

title: Scam: Users Beware!!
body: Only came on here to warn others of the scam this app perpetuates. I ONLy signed up for a $1 and within a week the tried to charge me $39.99 for a subscription I never signed up for. Now, only 24 hours later, they charged me AGAIN for a service I already cancelled and never signed up for in the first place. Customer service is only available through a form you have to fill out, and they limit your complaint to only 250 characters. Thankfully, they reversed the charge immediately but the support response I received said they “cancelled my subscription for me.” I cancelled on the 28th, and was charged again on the 29th. They are just trying to make a quick buck off people they don’t think are paying attention or on those they think they pull a fast one on.

title: Intentionally Confusing Subscriptions
body:
The app itself is good and helpful.
Unfortunately their confusing subscription model feels intentional, especially considering it's a developer promoting wellness and clarity targeting people with ADHD and other issues.
You can start a trial and buy a subscription through their apps. Mind you these subscriptions are not done through apple’s API so they can be managed easily.
When you want to manage your subscription you will likely end up in one of four places:
• Your profile on the app
• A website to *only* look at your subscriptions and bills
• A separate website to view your profile and
*only cancel* your subscription
• The App Store
This makes managing your pricey subscription difficult and it definitely feels like it's taking advantage of the people these apps are catering to.
I was still charged $39.99 even though I cancelled before the trial was over.
Overpriced for what you get as well. Just go buy some self-help workbooks and you will be on your phone less and achieve the same or better results. Without the scammy feeling subscription model they implemented.

title: Subscription process and status not transparent
body:
The app is good in helping users build habits. But it is obvious that the subscription/unsubscribe process is intentionally kept confusing.

In summary, you cannot find any information about your subscription or how to unsubscribe in their app or on AppStore under “my subscriptions”. You have to go to the Q&A page, which takes you to their website where you can unsubscribe.

I was charged for a 3 month premium subscription after my trial, but when I tried to find out more about when and how I was charged, there is no information about it anywhere in the app or even under “my subscriptions” in AppStore. Trust me, I spent no less than 20 minutes and made multiple attempts trying to find this information.

The oddest part is that even though I was automatically charged for a premium subscription, the app did not give me full access to the premium functions until after I went on their website to CANCEL the subscription.

The subscription cancellation process is very confusing too because they keep asking if you want to keep your subscription with a bunch of random add-ons. They also flip the color of the buttons on the last page to confuse users (in previous pages, the “keep my subscription” option is not highlighted, but on the last page it is).

I saw another review in April commenting about the same issue. Not sure why the developers haven’t fixed any of this because it is a SIGNIFICANT issue in their app and prevent users from managing their own subscriptions.

If you’ve used other habit tracking apps and they didn’t work for you, I haven’t seen anything unique in this app that’ll change things for you. If you forget to log your activity/check the box then your streak is gone, this is going to happen especially when a habit you’re tracking is simple and you’re already in the habit of doing it everyday meaning you might not wait for the reminder or might forget to get into the app and check the box. (You’re actually very likely to forget logging some things because it starts you off with very simple tasks, like drinking water in the morning which is a great practice but after a while you’re probably gonna forget to pull your phone out after you drink water) Other apps allow you to retroactively log an activity if you forgot to check the box when you did it the previous day. Pretty cool animated graphics though.

title: Unethical Billing Methods - BEWARE
body:
I signed up for the Fabulous app thinking I was joining a free basic plan with a $1 trial, clearly described as an optional path to premium. I never activated the premium subscription once the trial ended, but was still charged $40 every two months which was twice in total. I only discovered the charges when I changed my card and received a failed payment notice for $50.

When I contacted support, they refused to issue a refund, claiming that the charges were outlined in their terms and conditions, even though I never opted NOR ACTIVATED into the premium plan or received any clear warning that the trial automatically converts into a recurring paid subscription regardless of your activation.

The billing terms are confusing and misleading, and it feels like the app is designed to take advantage of users who trusted that “$1 trial” meant what it said. I’m disappointed because the app itself has potential, but the deceptive subscription model ruins the experience. Be cautious and double-check your subscriptions before downloading, this kind of practice should not be allowed. How difficult would it have been to refund $80 in an act of goodwill to a non premium user ?

title: Predatory, intentionally confusing and taking advantage of people who are already struggling
body: I downloaded this app looking for help and relief. I have struggled my entire life with feeling like a lost cause because I don’t have good habits but I do have plenty of bad ones. Basic everyday things are a struggle for me. Getting out of bed, brushing my teeth, taking care of my family and home. I manage to do enough to mask it and I’m attractive so I get away with a lot but in my life it has eroded my self confidence and greatly influenced the trajectory of my life. I don’t feel like I can work, maintain friendships or be a good mom. I have an amazing son and all day I’m mentally admonishing myself for all of the ways in which I have failed him and I’m not good enough and my partner will probably leave me. I see the promises a program like this makes and I get a sense of hope- that’s what they intend, it’s how they attract you. Download it and sit down to get to work… it doesn’t work. I decide to google and see what others have experienced besides the App Store having 4.5 start reviews and see that many others have struggled with using the app and then canceling the app. They have intentionally built a program for the sake of making cancellation a complicated process and getting as many charges as possible on people who already struggle with paying things on time and managing money and knowing they definitely did something right. They count on us not being competent, capable adults. Successful lawyers and business people aren’t downloading an app like this, it’s just vulnerable people looking for hope. I decided to cancel my subscription and knew since I signed up through an instagram ad I would probably have to do it on their website and not the App Store. I googled and saw the list cancellation right under their main page listing in Google results so I clicked on it. I was made to answer several questions and confirm multiple times I wanted to cancel, did not want an extended trial, did not want a discounted price etc. Then it confirmed my subscription was cancelled and offered me a ‘gift’ subscription of Luna app for my *best night of sleep ever* which I declined. I closed the browser thinking I was canceled and done but disturbed about it all I went to ChatGPT to ask about the legitimacy and legality of what they’re doing here. I realized I probably should have screenshotted my cancelation confirmation because I had seen where others said they had been charged a year later after canceling and the window now was asking me if I was sure I wanted to cancel. I went through another group of prompts trying to get me to keep the subscription I had ALREADY CANCELLED and once I again cancelled that subscription there was a page showing me the subscriptions I had, the Fabulous subscription I had cancelled and then another subscription for a bundle of products I didn’t know I was signed up for. I went through the process of answering questions and denying offers for discounts and extended trials and ALSO cancelled that subscription. I will be saving all of the screenshots I took and copying this review to repost. I’m setting a reminder to post it again in case it’s taken down or lost in the shuffle because I don’t want people like me to suffer anymore than we have to. This is insanity and should be illegal.

title: Money grab
body:
First of all, don’t be fooled. The free trial is not free. The cost keeps changing and the trial period extends with lures to upgrade your membership but they insist you “can cancel anytime”. I made a point of setting a reminder to cancel this app long before the “free trial” period ended, only to find there is no real intuitive way to cancel before being charged. So I contacted support through the app to cancel and received this response (again long before the free trial was up): “We regret to inform that in line with our T&Cs, the set-up fee for the trial period is non-refundable.

Auto-renewal for your subscription has now been canceled so there won't be further charges after the end of the trial period.” 

Uh huh. Convenient. If you do decide on the trial, you need to go to the website to cancel. Except they don’t tell you this til you contact support and they charge you to cancel. 

Second, there is so much going on in this app, but not much of it is helpful. Lots of bright colors and whimsical fantasy characters and repeated quotes make it hard to tell what you are checking off as completed. It did get me to drink water in the morning, but other than that I found it more annoying than helpful.

Third, they have a plethora of “self-improvement” apps, and it seems like the main goal of each one is to market all the others. I was looking for a helpful app to get my life on track, and instead got caught in a deceptive marketing scheme.

title: Their AI coaching admits to giving “inaccurate, biased, incorrect” health advice never validated by
body: they sell and share your information way beyond they make you believe They collect your health data, fitness habits, mental health status, and wellness struggles then share it with partners for marketing, service providers for ads, and internal teams without meaningful restriction. Their AI coaching admits to giving “inaccurate, biased, incorrect” health advice never validated by human experts, yet you assume all liability for any harm while they face zero consequences. Age requirements conflict (13 vs 15 vs 18) allowing minors to share mental health and body image data that gets monetized. Your coaching conversations become their intellectual property and train their AI systems while being processed through “anonymization” they control. They cannot guarantee security and explicitly state they can’t prevent unauthorized access to your health information. Data transfers to US servers for non-EU users bypass stronger European privacy protections. Partners receive your health data “with your consent” buried in terms for sending marketing offers. Third-party advertisers (Facebook, Twitter, Google) use cookies to track your wellness app behavior for targeted advertising. You get zero refunds even if their AI gives harmful health advice that worsens your condition. French law jurisdiction means US health privacy protections don’t apply to your data or any disputes about misuse.​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​

title: Capitalism strikes again
body: I was a daily user of this app abut 10 years ago, and it made a big impact on me at the time, kick starting my self-improvement journey. It’s great to see that after all these years the app’s continued to improve, and that the lessons it incorporates are still so useful. Unfortunately, the price is ridiculous, and I frankly find it disgusting considering this app is targeted at people who are struggling to get a grip on life. You suggest habits related to improving one’s finances, then demand users pay $40 for 3 months of a glorified habit tracker, when most of the frills I’d be paying for are things I’m not interested in… I just want unlimited habit tracking, some basic insight, and a gameified interface that keeps me motivated. If I were to pay for premium, I would have the constant feeling of money being wasted, which is a bad feeling—the opposite of what I want from such an app. I do understand that apps are businesses and development/upkeep costs money, but there should be tiers perhaps, with a $5/month tier that includes the features I mentioned, or an ad-supported tier, or a way to earn credits by using the app every day. Anything to make your app accessible to people who don’t make 6 figures.

body:

God forbid you forget your password…like most ADHD people 🙄 because you’ll never be able to cancel. 

I’ve been through the runaround with support and they told me there was nothing they could do so my only option to keep them from charging me forever was to close the bank account it was attached to. Definitely a scam in my opinion.

title: Too many in app sales pitches
body:
I’m spending $20 a month on this app and I’m constantly bombarded by exercises which I think are part of my subscription. Once I complete the exercise — usually a questionnaire that takes up time — I find out that the next step is not covered by my subscription.

This really puts me off and starts my day in a bad way, which is the opposite of what this app should be doing. One reason I got the app was to help with my distractibility and procrastination. Constantly distracting me with exercises that are not covered to my subscription is counterproductive.

I understand that these apps need a business model, but it’s unreasonable to have the first thing the app presents (when I open it) be a sales pitch disguised as part of my existing subscription.

The app should be very clear about what is covered by my subscription *before* it sends me down rabbit holes that use up valuable morning time  & distract— only to end with a sales pitch.

title: Prey on the Vulnerable
body:
I checked out this app because i am involved in the mental health world. It seemed so promising at first, but quickly became confusing and convoluted. In order to have some features you have to download other apps. The free trial is difficult to cancel and I ended up getting charged FOUR times before Fabulous would finally let me cancel. A part of the issue was I could not see my account page in any of the apps (I have Videos I sent to the customer support page), so I could not cancel the subscription myself. They did not refund the multiple payments despite the technical difficulties and clear intent via written correspondence. 

Ultimately, my low rating comes from this companies willingness to prey upon the vulnerable. People who need help reach for this app, and are met with a company who only cares about siphoning their money. I highly recommend you look elsewhere for support. And if you are struggling, know that it’s always darkest before the dawn. Good things are ahead for you. 

Just not in this or affiliate apps.

title: Definitely helps, but can use some decluttering
body:
I have been using this app for a few weeks, and I plan to use it for the next few months to incorporate some healthier habits in to my day. I have been going through a fertility journey that has caused depression and a feeling of being stuck and lost. I used to be very disciplined, so I am hoping this app will help me get back on track and I can honestly say that it already has in a short amount of time. 

Some of the things I love: the app will choose simple habits for you (like drink water first thing in the morning, stretch for 1 minute every day). When you’re depressed, it can be hard to think of and create these goals for yourself, so I love that they choose them for you. I also love the daily coaching and how they seamlessly integrate it in to your routine. The lessons are helpful and I have learned a lot about my behaviors. 

Some of the things I don’t love: there is A LOT going on in this app. The first time I opened it, I immediately thought to myself, “there is no way I will be using this for more than a day” because it was wildly overwhelming and confusing. I decided to push through, and I have a general idea of where things are now, but I still don’t understand the flow of the app. This needs a lot of work. There is also a ton of advertising for there other apps, which needs to be toned down.

Overall, I do think this app is helpful, but it needs to be decluttered and the flow needs to be improved.

title: Payments Odd
body:
Setting up the account for this walked me through steps which prompted me to start with paying minimum $1 to use the app generally. I selected the $1 option and chose to skip about 5 “offers” for other apps and declined what I thought was premium. The app then welcomed me to premium, and when I went to my account settings I was subscribed to pay over $20 a month. After I cancelled the subscription immediately, I checked the invoice link through settings which shows a $30+ purchase, with the plan scheduled to cancel at the end of the month. Overall extremely confusing interface. I’m sure the app is helpful to some behaviorally, but I will not be trying it given the risk of spending more than I am aware of. 

This part is just nitpicky, but: the ai generated art used across the platform is tough on the eyes. For example, when setting a goal to drink water, there is a generated image of a man holding a water bottle behind his face, and a blue mouth. Off-putting. 

To the devs: I hope you can reduce the amount of repetitive payment prompts when using the app, as it creates more opportunities for accidental subscription—your application is advertised to people who are in a hard place, do not make it worse by adding financial worry. And for the graphics, try some softer color contrasts? Have the art either produced by a graphic designer or make it simple vectors. At the very least, review the ai-generated images before integrating them into the app.

title: Terrible experience with Fabulous
body:
Unfortunately, I did not have a “fabulous” experience.

I was charged $49.99 plus $39.99 in the same month for subscriptions I didn’t want or fully understand. When I asked support why, they said one was for Fabulous Premium and the other for a “bundle” of their other apps — apps I never used or asked for.

When I requested a refund after the seven-day trial, they simply pointed to their T&Cs and said I wasn’t eligible. No help, no explanation—just “it’s policy.”

Canceling is equally frustrating. Even after canceling through my iPhone subscriptions, I had to log into a computer to fully cancel. That extra step feels deliberately designed to trap users into paying longer.

I liked the app at first, but after this, I feel completely taken advantage of. I had just given birth, wasn’t using it, and simply wanted a break—but instead of support or an easy cancellation, I was met with confusing charges and dismissive responses.

When I came here to write this review, I saw I wasn’t the only one facing the same issues. That says a lot about how this company operates.

Fabulous may look polished on the surface, but their billing and customer service practices are misleading and predatory. I won’t ever return, and I strongly caution anyone considering it to think twice.

Knowing how support handles issues like this, I expect they’ll read this review, give a generic acknowledgment, and take no real action—just the same dismissive responses I’ve already received.

title: Super deceptive billing!
body:
They “signed me up” for $1, and a “14 day trial,” which I cancelled halfway through…only for them to THEN start charging me $39.99 for a “biweekly subscription plan” - yep, you read that right - that’s $40 every TWO WEEKS! That’s $80 per month, which is $20 MORE than what their ANNUAL plan supposedly is! I had to contact my bank because they kept charging me despite me cancelling on their website! They ultimately charged me FOUR TIMES - so that’s $160 they took from me, when I used their app literally not ONCE. Seriously, don’t do it!!!

UPDATE AFTER DEVELOPER RESPONSE BELOW:
Thank you; however, being referred to your subscription management page is not helpful to me. When I downloaded your app, which is called one thing EVERYWHERE in the app, in the App Store, etc., I agreed to a 14 day trial, & I understood that I would be billed a recurring subscription if I did not cancel well before the 14th day. This is why I set a reminder on my phone on day 7, a full WEEK before the trial was over, to decide whether or not I wanted to keep the subscription or cancel. I went and cancelled & received a screen message confirming it. Then, fast forward a week, & I get a totally unfamiliar bank charge. It’s called something COMPLETELY different than your app/program’s name & has NO customer service # or website listed so I couldn’t even reach out to determine who/what it was for. Even my bank couldn’t help track it down for me. Two weeks later, there it is AGAIN. Finally through googling around I was able to track down that it was still YOUR app, despite me cancelling. So I went BACK to your website that you’re referring me to & went through the process of cancelling AGAIN. At no point was I able to get a hold of an actual human being to address this. The address I found wasn’t even in the U.S., &, despite the fact that I’m SURE you can see on your end that I never even USED your app/program, I of course have NO recourse or way to obtain a refund for services NEVER used & cancellationS NEVER processed. So, your response below, which actually is the ONLY ACTUAL response I’ve gotten to ANYTHING, which tells me that reviews are what make you tick….does me NO good. I stand by my initial review - EXPENSIVE SCAM, don’t make the same mistake I did!

title: DO NOT DOWNLOAD or SUBSCRIBE
body:

the application is not user-friendly and requires several steps to even access premium features. If you sign up for a trial, but don’t use it, it is very difficult to unsubscribe, impossible if you don’t go through all of the profile setup first. The customer support is unwilling to refund past months even if you haven’t opened the app since initially downloading to try it out. 

I signed up for a free trial almost a year ago with a card whose account I don’t check regularly so when I finally noticed that Fabulous has been charging me $19.99 every two months since October, I reached out to support about the fact that I never used the app because it was not a very well-designed usable app and not at all helpful for my ADHD symptoms, they were unwilling to refund any of the past months even though they should have a record showing I never opened the app or even set up a profile for my account. title: Complete waste of money
body: By far the stupidest purchase I've ever made. It's supposed to help you build good habits- instead there's just a million things to click on, none of which seem relevant or helpful for building habits or managing ADHD. It makes you read "letters" and listen to "coaching" - if I wanted that I'd read a self-help book or listen to a podcast (both of which would be a better experience than this app, and are FREE). If you want to help people build habits, you need simplicity- not an app that completely overwhelms with nonsense. And the fact that you can't adjust to your situation makes it so much worse- I don't need to be reminded to drink water, eat breakfast, go to the gym. I do those things already. Instead, I need to be reminded to get off my phone, find a hobby, etc. Deleting this app after 1 week.

title: Scammy and unethical
body:
