But I kept trying with it and realized I hated the constant notifications. It was too much for someone already dealing with ADHD. 

So I went to go cancel my (what I thought was) free account. First, it took far too long going through the app to then going to the website to actually find the subscription section to cancel. 
There I found out that I still had the bundled subscription and I was just about to get charged another $60 in another week!!

So scammy and unethical. 

If it took one click to accidently subscribe to the bundle, which I never intended to do and I still don’t believe I ever signed up for, it should be one easy click to cancel everything and delete the account. 

I’ve now deleted the account and deleted the app.

title: I really like it, but it’s inconsistent and glitchy
body:
I’ll start with the positives: the app is very aesthetically pleasing. I appreciate the methodical adding of habits so it’s manageable and lasting. I really love the coaching narratives.
What drives me nuts is that when I open it during the afternoon, it’s prompts me to “click here if you’ve drank your morning water” when I’ve already checked this several times that day. And then it goes through every other habit, regardless if I’ve already completed it. Inefficient much?

Sometimes the app it’s just glitchy. For example, it will be noon and it will say tomorrow afternoon is the next “upcoming event” when I haven’t completed this afternoon’s or this evening’s habits.

It’s got one job. Keep me on track on my habits, which includes being clear whether I’ve completed each daily habit. And yes, I’m oversimplifying it, but it’s too expensive for not being able to do what it’s intended to do.

As someone with severe ADHD that literally ruins my life, these apps together have been a game changer. 
Again, I’m shocked. lol. 

I don’t stress too much about completing all my tasks and my full routine each day, and I think giving myself that grace has been the key in the improvement I’ve made. Don’t take it too seriously, let yourself have tiny improvements. Before I started, I was barely getting anything done at work and at home. Then when I started following the app, I started getting a little more done each day, little by little. And now this week I feel so proud of myself that I’m completing the full triangle AND with energy! (huge because I literally never have energy for anything!) 

I’m sure part of this is novelty, of course, but I’ve never stuck with anything this long. And they add new topics/habits/strategies every few days/week that it keeps it new and interesting to hold my interest and keep checking in each day. 

The tips they give are so helpful and I really try to implement the advice they give to help me with my tasks. And so far so good. I couldn’t recommend these apps enough.

title: Forgets progress - defeating, confusing, expensive
body:
I was really excited to start using this and have never paid this much for an app before. Ever. I thought I was investing in my future. Not only is this app extremely confusing to use, and doesn’t give solid reminders, but it has no way to go back and check off that you completed something the day prior, so it starts your “journey” over as if you didn’t do what you were supposed to do because you didn’t physically go into the app, which isn’t great for ADHD - it needs to be more easily accessible with the ability to change past progress on busy days. 
On top of this, the app forgets that you already checked something off for the day. Today, not only did it forget that I had already checked off the first two items of the day, and made me do it again, but when I check the items off once more, it started me back at day one of my journey, and that is not accurate at all. The whole point is to help you see the progress you’re making to keep you motivated, but if it can’t keep track of your progress, it makes you feel like you aren’t getting anywhere, and if it’s too difficult to figure out how to check things off in the first place, the result is the same… It’s so incredibly discouraging and I’m very upset that I have spent money on this. If it was an investment that helped me in my life, it would be so worth it. But I would’ve been better off setting alarms and using a paper checklist or journal, which Is what we’re trying to avoid, right? 
Oh, and the amount of ads for slightly different apps by the same company is insulting and makes you feel used like the company is just trying to make money and doesn’t actually care about helping the customer, which… the rest of my experience communicates as well. 
On another note, the music send to play randomly and is difficult to control even when the app is closed!
Lastly, there needs to be better proofreading.  There are so many spelling and grammatical errors. The low level of quality for writing or even quoted citations is absolutely unacceptable at this price. This has been a deeply frustrating experience.

A couple of weeks ago there was an update where the timer showed in the little screen on top of the iPhone, I really liked that because I could look at different screens while in a routine and know what the timer says. Quickly after like two weeks that change to a Picture in Picture small screen that doesn’t even show the time left. The screen is in the way, why would I need to see a PIP of this app. Messing with this video screen yesterday caused my app to crash and routines defaulted to their original titles. Today there was a new little AI robot on the timer screen to help you complete the routine, I don’t need motivation to drink water, I just need to remind myself constantly to do it. None of these settings are optional even though I pay for premium. I don’t understand why the app needs to change every day, this app is about routines and its users are looking for stability. I’m going to look for another app, I don’t even use the other features but I think they’re pretty neat.

title: Take out the ads for another star. Remove glitches for one more
body: If after reading this, you decide to subscribe, please do it through the App Store not through a link from Instagram or something the App Store subscription seems to work fine. I did subscribe through Instagram first and it was much more expensive and definitely a bit hard to cancel. That being said, I love how this app really encourages you to take habit change in tiny bite size steps, and celebrate your accomplishments. However, for a paid app, it is incredibly difficult to navigate through all of the ads, for the other apps also produced by the same developer. It is ironic, if not downright hypocritical to encourage people to download and pay for more apps to “improve themselves”more and more when the science behind what they are telling us in this app is to take it a tiny bit at a time. Also, there are just some weird things like when you’re trying to listen to the daily coaching a little voice will chime in in the middle of it and say almost done like you can’t figure that out for yourself by watching the progress bar it really interrupts the flow of thought. You also can’t add the habit you want to work on. They’re constantly suggesting that you add some other habit that has never even occurred to you that you want to develop. All in all, I have learned some things and think there’s some really good research behind all of this, but the app itself is pretty weak. They promised a community, but in comparison to other community apps, I’ve used there is almost no engagement. The “circles“ are also incredibly difficult to navigate. I will probably not renew my subscription unless they fix at least one of these major flaws.

title: Watch the Free Trial Cancel by Date
body:
I canceled my free trial the day prior to its end thinking that would be it.  Turns out they bury in their fine print you gotta cancel 24 hours prior to the end of the trial day.  Huh? Even airlines let you cancel up until the day of departure, but a technology company has this asinine policy?  Incredible!  Also says in their FAQs that the free trial must be cancelled before the renewal date, NOT 24 hours BEFORE the renewal date.  What a scam.

Follow up: Just to be clear, the language in their FAQ section (not the legal language no one ever has time to read), says “If Premium isn't for you, make sure you cancel the trial before the end date to avoid it becoming a subscription.”  Just know that that apparently means “make sure you cancel the trial [24 hours] before the end date to avoid it becoming a subscription.”  I’m sure they didn’t leave the time frame out of the FAQ language on purpose and bury it in the legal contract language for a reason.  No chance they’d ever want to take your money for literally providing no services.  🙄

What’s the point of advertising a trial period of x days, when the trial period is ACTUALLY x-1 day?!?  Don’t take the WHOLE trial period to figure out if you like the product.  You only have A PORTION of the trial period, the rest of the trial period isn’t really a trial period, it’s this nebulous region where the product is theoretically free, but you will be paying for it “tomorrow”.  In the words of the great Jim Gaffigan… “Ridiculous.”

UPDATE: Surprise, surprise!  I got yet ANOTHER monthly bill from them for some hidden charge.  It’s mind boggling the scam they are pulling.  YOU HAVE TO BE SUPER DILIGENT when cancelling this service.  They will find a way to take more and more of your money.  (Unreal that Apple promotes them.)

title: Not good. Overbuilt. Taxing to use.
body:
I really wanted to love this app but it was too much. 

For the simple habit of drinking water each morning there were so many notifications, prompts to do things, graphics, etc. 

The app is constantly prompting you to read your daily letter, read the evening coaching, read the comments other people who use the app have made about the coaching, look at a graphic of a person climbing a mountain, with progress points that say “day one” “day two” etc…. but the graphic doesn’t change as you make progress so you don’t experience the satisfaction of seeing the progress points being hit? 

Even just updating your streak after you complete your daily habit requires sitting through so much “stuff” that you can think you updated your streak for the day but you actually didn’t…so then the next day it’s like “Oh, you didn’t do it yesterday, that’s okay, you get two freeze days so you don’t lose your streak”—which, first of all, I didn’t ask for “freeze days” (cheat days?) and I would never sign up for that, if I miss my habit I just want to lose my streak. Isn’t that the point of this? And two, I DIDN’T actually break my streak, it’s just this app is so overdeveloped with nonsense that I didn’t realize I didn’t update my habit tracking for that day.

When I first started the app I really liked the fact that there was a heartfelt note that seemed to speak to the real experience I was having (wanting to get my personal care habits back on track) but after that it just never stopped. 

I don’t want preachy coaching from an app, I don’t want to be constantly inundated with graphics and quotes and comments from other people. I don’t want a daily letter. I just want to track my personal care habits in an app that gamifies habit building. 

Furthermore, the app is constantly trying to sell the other apps made by this developer to me. Even when I was canceling my subscription—which was difficult to do and I had to confirm SEVEN TIMES while they kept offering better and better pricing, and finally were like “As a parting gift, we would like to give you the opportunity to get this other app we made…”

Disappointing, overbuilt, waste of time. If you have 30 minutes a day to dedicate to navigating the app and preachy letters, etc, maybe this app is for you. If you just want to track your habits to keep yourself on track with your self care, download Streak. That’s what I did and it’s much better.

title: Frustrating
body:
I wanted to like this app but I couldn’t even start to use it. I was already turned off by the carousel of “free trial” offers once I signed up. One additional offer is fine but I believe this one had no less than 5. There was an offer for an ADHD app, an offer for a sleep app, and at least two different offers for coaching. It was really irritating to encounter that delay when I was trying to just set up the app. Is this an app for people with ADHD or the checkout page for a budget airline? 

Those annoyances aside, the biggest issue is the integration of the setup. I opened the app, went through the steps, and then it asked to verify my email. I went and did that. Selected my trial. Linked to PayPal for future payments and then tried to go back to the app. The app did not recognize that I had already set it up. It kept prompting me to verify my email. When I opted to skip, it tried to take me through all the onboarding questions again. There was no way to bypass that. I opened and closed the app multiple times (only to hear the dreadful opening noise that I shouldn’t even hear because my phone’s sound is off) and it did not change. At that point, I had wasted enough time and gave up and deleted it. 

To make it worse, it then was difficult to cancel my trial because it somehow wasn’t under my other subscriptions through Apple and I had no log in. I had to mess around with it for another 15 minutes to make sure it was canceled. What a giant waste of time. 

At minimum you need to make sure that once the email is verified, the user should be taken back to the app and move forward from there. That is a massive glitch. If I go to Amazon right now in my phone’s browser (or iMDB or Netflix) I will be either prompted to migrate to the app or it may just open automatically. That is standard practice. I should not have to set up my account twice to use the app when it was your protocol that forced me to leave to verify my email address in the first place. How about you do a text code verification instead, like an adult.

title: Predatory Billing Practices – Stay Away
body:
This app markets itself as a mental health tool, but its business model is anything but ethical. Like many others with ADHD, I signed up years ago hoping for support, and canceled when it didn’t work for me. Yet I’ve continued to be charged $29.99 with no way to cancel through Apple or my account—because the subscription was secretly linked to a different app (“Clarify”) I never knowingly used.

After digging online, I found dozens of users with ADHD reporting the exact same issue—long-forgotten subscriptions, no cancelation option, vague email responses, and refusal to issue refunds unless you persist. It’s manipulative and preys on the very executive dysfunction many of us are trying to manage.

Apps meant to support mental health should not rely on shady, confusing billing tactics. This experience left me feeling exploited, not empowered. Shame on Fabulous.

title: Intentionally Confusing Subscriptions
body:
The app itself was helpful while I used it. Unfortunately their confusing subscription model feels intentional, especially considering it’s a developer promoting wellness and clarity.

You can buy a subscription through their apps. When you want to manage your subscription you will likely end up in one of four places:
• Your profile on the app
• A website to *only* look at your subscriptions and bills
• A separate website to view your profile and *only cancel* your subscription
• The App Store

This makes managing your pricey subscription difficult and feels like it’s taking advantage of the people these apps are catering to. Now add one, two or three other apps that operate on the same model that they advertise through the app you’re already paying for.

The app itself is fine, it was useful while I used it. But it’s difficult to look past the poor user-experience of profile and subscription management.

title: Beware! This is NOT a Christian approved app!
body:
If you have any respect for the God of the Bible, you might want to skip this app. I couldn’t even give this app a chance because of all the disturbing occult imagery before you even get to try it out. It opens with its slogan being “it’s not magic, it’s science” yet it’s full of magical and offensive occult imagery. these symbols are deeply rooted in magic, occult, and spiritual traditions. Whether people realize it or not, exposure to certain imagery does brain wash you and influence perception, emotions, and even subconscious beliefs.
The constant exposure to this imagery desensitizes people to its occult roots or subtly condition them to be more accepting of concepts that displease God who warns strongly against anything related to magic or the occult. Symbols of triangle with eyes everywhere, potions and ghostly looking artwork is all I had seen within the first 5 minutes of downloading. Even if people don’t consciously adopt occult beliefs, repeated exposure can create familiarity and comfort with these symbols, making them more open to mystical or divination themed ideas. Symbols have real spiritual power, and even if they seem trendy, they often carry deeper meaning and consequences.
I didn’t get to actually try the app so I gave it 2 stars instead of one because I’m sure it works for what it was designed for, I just can’t use with a clean conscience.

Also if you are in ED recovery look out because they have lots of lose weight focused reminders and verbiage that can be triggering.
Thanks Fabulous team of the past, you all helped me through some bad times and I recommended you to everyone. To the current team, I hate that your product is for extractionist profit now. title: Finch is better. This app doesn’t actually care about people.
body: I did this app for less than a week and I hated it. I thought I was unsubscribed because I didn’t see it in my App Store subscriptions however, apparently the way I did this subscription. I actually subscribed to them on their website. They proceeded to charge me for a month while I was busy taking care of a surgery where I had an organ removed. Checking for this type of expense was not my highest priority at the time. They refused to refund me anything even though they even stopped emailing me at some point. I only discovered that I was still paying for this from Rocket Money. If the app actually cared about people and was ethical, they would see that I never once used their app during any period of time on the first week. And refund me at least some of my subscription fees at that time I’m writing this review. They have refunded me zero dollars and site their subscriber agreement. I will reiterate that any app that exists because a majority of people are forgetting their subscriptions that app doesn’t deserve to exist. If they try to claim that they are successful because many people willingly pay for them then what do they have to to lose to refund the occasional subscriber that has forgotten their at least some of their subscription fee? As far as I’m concerned, they are not ethical, and they do not deserve your business. If you’re looking for an app, that’s focused on mental health and mindfulness. I highly recommend Finch instead. They’re much less greedy, they actually care about the people that subscribed to them, and the app is 1000 times better.

title: Beware: Misleading and Money-Grab Scheme
body:
I downloaded Fabulous thinking it was a helpful habit tracker, but it quickly became clear that this app is nothing more than a sales funnel for other apps. When purchasing their “bundle,” you’d assume it grants access to all their habit-forming tools. In reality, you only get previews—each additional app requires a separate, costly subscription.

I mistakenly purchased one of their “sister” apps, believing it was included. It wasn’t. When I reached out for a refund, I was met with a firm no refunds, ever policy. This is an intentional, deceptive business model designed to squeeze as much money as possible from users.

If you’re looking for a genuine habit tracker, stay away from Fabulous—there are far better (and more ethical) options out there!

title: Great gamification motivator for goals.
body: Nice goal check off gamification app. Poppy graphics, bells when you click a goal as complete, moving bars ahead and gaining points and objects for your completion. To be honest I do not really interact with the avatar (letting them wear, use objects etc.) and it is not quite transparent to me how to go about doing that. Now, in honesty, I am not very savvy at all with tech, apps, programs, so a more tech savvy user may find that all quite transparent and easy. I do like checking the goals off and the goal box for any particular goal turning green if you do it consistently to increasingly dark shades of red as you miss your target over more and more days. The red is a motivator to go ahead and get those neglected goals done. That, I guess, is the power of gamification. Also, points are assigned for completing goals and when you complete a neglected one for the first time in a while you get a big number of points. Even too behind to use those, I enjoy seeing the big points rack up. Motivation again, gamification.

title: Convoluted
body: I would give 0 stars if I could. Despite never activating the subscription via an email sent when I first signed up, I was still charged, and when I contacted customer support, they couldn’t locate my account (because it wasn’t activated). I had already canceled all my Apple subscriptions in Apple Subscriptions” on my phone including Fabulous, months ago when I first signed up, and my account showed that the subscription would end in November. However, the app didn’t specify a year, leading me to believe it was November 2024—when in reality, I can only assume it meant November 2025. If I had already paid and canceled, why am I still being charged monthly? This isn’t a contract requiring a full-year commitment. If the subscription is canceled, payments should stop. Customer service was unhelpful, despite the app claiming to offer refunds for users who “forget to cancel”, which is misleading for an app marketed as ADHD-friendly. In addition to all of these the app is and all of its sister apps are difficult to navigate and not user friendly considering its intended audience. I would not recommend this app (or any of its sister apps) to anyone especially those with ADHD.

So imagine my surprise when I continue to be charged for something that's not even installed on my phone. I've been going back and forth with customer "care" and they refuse to refund the charges. I send all the proof that I cancelled my subscription and was approved for a refund and this is the response I got:

"Hi there,

Thanks for your reply and for sharing your thoughtful feedback with us.

Although we truly understand your situation and frustration, I'm sorry to say that unfortunately we won't be able to proceed with a refund for your purchase. As previously mentioned, the renewal date was displayed at the time of signing up and it was stated that the subscription automatically renews on an ongoing basis unless cancelled prior to the renewal date.

This refund request will now be closed, but please do let us know if you need assistance with anything else.

Best,
The Fabulous Member Care Team"

I cancelled prior to renewal and even had DOCUMENTATION to prove this! So yeah, definitely a scam and I'll be reporting to the Better Business Bureau.

title: Incessant self-promotion
body:

The tactics used to push subscriptions are blatant and feel trashy. What’s worse is that even when you recognize the psychological tricks at play, they’re still hard to resist. It feels like more effort went into manipulative marketing than the actual self-improvement tools this app claims to provide.

If I say no once, don’t throw a discount at me like I’ll suddenly change my mind. I’m saying no on principle. And I’m not signing up for a “free trial” just to risk forgetting to cancel—something the developers clearly count on. It’s predatory.

I’m using this app to manage ADHD symptoms, not to have them exploited.

title: Extraordinary Depth and Intentionality
body:
The ‘Fabulous’ app is nothing short of a profound masterpiece, an intricately designed tool that guides you with both clarity and poetic grace through the often turbulent journey of self-improvement. What sets it apart is its remarkable depth, a vast reservoir of psychological insights that are presented in a way that feels both intimate and empowering. Rather than being a typical wellness app, it feels more like a thoughtful companion, seamlessly blending evidence-based practices with the soul of personal reflection.

The app’s architecture is intentionally crafted, leading you through gentle yet powerful rituals that nurture meaningful habits. Each step, no matter how small, is underpinned by the wisdom of behavioral science, yet the delivery is so beautifully humanized. It’s not just a checklist of tasks but a mindful journey, prompting you to be present in the moment, while simultaneously fostering long-term transformation. Each new habit introduced feels like an invitation to rediscover yourself—not through lofty goals, but through achievable, thoughtful actions rooted in purpose.

It truly captures the essence of intentional living, providing both the practical tools and the philosophical nourishment needed to make lasting change. Its extraordinary ability to marry psychology with poetry, science with art, is what makes it such a transformative guide, gently shaping you into the best version of yourself.

title: Don’t pay $$ for apps that purport to help neurodiverse folks but rather prefer to take advantage.
body:
I am posting this review/warning under both the Fabulous AND Clarify app pages because it is the developer’s dishonest method of not appropriately handling these charges of getting BOTH apps that created this issue.

I want to warn everyone against subscribing to any product offered by Fabulous, an app that purports to help people with ADHD but seems to better practice taking advantage of what can be attributed at least in part to symptoms of ADHD and neurodiversity.

I decided in November to take advantage of the free trial offered. As part of the on boarding, I was also offered a free trial of another app designed by Fabulous supposedly even more targeted to ADHD, an app called Clarify.

I found neither app really worked for me that well, or at least, they didn’t draw me in enough to want to use them. That’s fine—every brain is different, and everyone has different things that may/may not work for them.

Before my free trial ended, I logged in to my account to cancel, and yes, my Fabulous account WAS in fact canceled, and I received confirmation. I looked for information about Clarify, but there was nothing separate, nor did I receive any separate notifications from Fabulous OR Clarify stating that a separate trial was ending and I would be charged.

After canceling, I did not go into either app again.

But recently, I noticed a charge on my credit card from the same day I cancelled by trial. The charge was listed on my statement as “FABULOUS APP PARIS” and was for $29.99. The cancellation email only offers instructions on how to reactivate your subscription; it offers no information or warning about any other subscriptions or apps. In fact, while it tells you how to reactivate, it does NOT even have a single hyperlink connected to any support or account pages.

When I went to look for how to get back into the account page (as I had actually purchased the subscription directly from within the app, and it did not go through the App Store or my apple account, even though I had logged in using Apple), I had to find the original activation email which had a link to my account page. When I finally clicked that link today, I suddenly saw the Clarify account and it showed that it was still active.

I immediately cancelled the account and then searched for a way to contact them to request a refund for this amount that I did not believe I should have been charged, and that was connected to an account that I had never used since I believed I had canceled it at the same time as canceling Fabulous.

There is no support email address to contact Fabulous. You simply submit a request through their site. To their credit, they responded to me quickly, but their responses were wholly unsatisfactory, essentially saying, Too bad!

I received a receipt for my initial Clarify subscription, but I have never received any further correspondence nor receipts from them. The only reason I even know about the charge was from my credit card statement, which, again, does not mention “Clarify.” 

There are terms on the receipt email that state, “Please note, if you purchase more than one Fabulous product, other products may be renewing on separate dates and applicable receipts for those products may be sent separately.” However, once I canceled Fabulous, while I received the cancellation confirmation, I never received ANY separate receipt regarding the auto-renewal charge nor did I receive any warning that my trial was ending. I have received nothing from them whatsoever other than their decision not to refund this money.

This is simply horrible customer service. Had I been utilizing the app even a single time after my cancellation of Fabulous or after the renewal date, or had I allowed the auto-renew to happen more than once, I would understand being unwilling to make the consideration. But that is not the case. Their communication is at best lacking, especially charging a credit card without sending an email receipt/notification after. At worst, it is a ploy to grab some extra money for unused services.

I sent three messages back and forth with their support staff before writing this review. After the first refund denial, I wrote that I would post reviews and contest the charge with my credit card company. Instead, their final response to me, written in faux-apologetic language that equates to saying: , We’re so sorry that we can’t offer you this customer consideration because you’re too stupid to have figured out that nuances of our cancellation policies that require separate cancellations for products that you purchased at the exact same time. (That’s not a quotation, but it is what their message essentially says.)

Their final response to me ended with: “This refund request will now be closed, but please do let us know if you need assistance with anything else.”

Either way, this is not a developer that I would ever consider purchasing anything from again., regardless of how interesting a product may look. I would suggest others stay away as well unless you are ready and prepared to skip having a “free trial.” There’s a good chance it won’t turn out to be free.

title: Watch out for UNAUTHORIZED Charges!
body: I thought I’d try this app. They offered me a trial and then a bimonthly charge of $39.99. I didn’t want to pay that amount so I declined the offer. IMMEDIATELY they offered me the same plan for a bimonthly charge of $19.99. First issue…why not offer me the $19.99 price to start with? Then when I opened the app to “activate” my plan I was offered a “Premium Bundle” for a $59.99 bimonthly charge. It popped up in a window in the middle of the app with NO exit button. There was a button that said “accept” then a “continue”  box. I did NOT check the accept option but pressed continue because there was no other way to go forward. When I checked my subscription it had enrolled me in the $59.99 plan PLUS the original $19.99 plan. This is just another corporate app that preys on people who agree to one plan but get charged for another. Be VERY careful!

title: Predatory scam
body:
I signed up for help with ADHD, the product structure itself was not that useful or supportive to me, which is not a crime. What i
IS criminal is that the subscription costs $40 per month, which was not made clear when I signed up, and the company makes it difficult to cancel as you cannot access your billing info from inside the app. On top of that, I learned that I had been signed up for a $30/month subscription to their app Clarify that I never signed up for. 

It all felt intentionally misleading and like they are preying on people with ADHD joining impulsively and forgetting or not noticing the charges. Based on their responses to the other one star reviews here, I don’t think they care about making a user oriented experience, I think they are content with getting $70 out of people for a few months before they get angry and cancel. I’m not one to leave reviews, and certainly not bad ones, but this was a massive disappointment and made me feel manipulated.

title: Overwhelming, and Unnecessary Ads
body:
I first got fabulous a few years ago to try and develop some good habits. At the time I appreciated the gradual buildup of habits. But over time it felt like I was doing a lot of unnecessary things that weren’t meaningful to me. At some points it had me choose a minimum number of habits to implement, from a list it provided. Some of these felt silly (leaving sticky notes around your home with a random symbol that reminded you to pause and be grateful, or something?). Just not stuff that was for me. 

Anyway, I fell off the app, cancelled my subscription. Here I am again trying to see if I can get back into it. The UI is overwhelming. The functions within the app are as well. There’s just SO MUCH going on. There’s also a ton of very busy art now, for every challenge, journey, etc. Sure, it’s pretty. But it’s just too much to look at. 

I tried to restart the very first journey. Read the first letter about the importance of drinking water. And in it they included a plug for a random water bottle brand. Come on yall, we’re trying to build healthy habits here, not get more advertisements pushed at us. Even more ridiculous that it’s in the Premium version.

Guess I’m deleting again, and I won’t be coming back 🤷

title: Absolutely love this app!

I have one piece of feedback- it would be even better if the routines played one after the other over the course of the day. For example, I was recently traveling, which meant that I was going to bed late. Even if it was before midnight, the app was ready to play the morning routine instead of evening. Then when I manually chose evening, it played the evening of the following day and dropped my streak. 

Now that I am home I have an early morning routine because I have things to do at 5 am, after which I go back to sleep. Instead of playing the 5 am routine it plays the 7:25 morning routine, and I have to stop it to change to the correct one. 

Maybe some integration with Health would help, so it could be aware of sleep-wake cycles?

title: Content is fantastic, their business-side is messing it up
body:
I love the intent behind this app, but the fact of the matter is that the business side of this company is over, exerting themselves and cutting corners apparently. 

This app has a lot of great advice and the routines are great. But it will NOT stop aggressively pushing their other apps and paid services. It’s comically ubiquitous across the whole experience and has probably lost them a lot of users. 

Because the business-side are such vampires, they likely also cut corners on hiring technical talent. The app has the ability to share most anything with a friend via a link, but the link is always broken and takes them to the wrong part of the app.

Please, for the sake of this great idea, convinced the business people to chill out and focus on the good sides of the app, and not trying to make paid customers into higher paying customers. Be satisfied with a smaller profit margin and the margin will grow.

title: 0/10 for transparency
body:
Let me start by saying I work in the mental health field. I do think this has some good unique content but it is confusing and overwhelming to navigate at times. 

My biggest complaint is that I saw this on an instagram add as a pay what you want trial. My mom had passed away that week so I did it. But with her death life got hectic and I didn’t even set the app up. I checked my subscriptions on Apple and it wasn’t there. So I figured the trial hadn’t started because it didn’t have login credentials. But it is INDEPENDENT of the App Store. So before I’d even opened it once it charged me and locked me into a premium membership. I was not given the details of renewal so I couldn’t set a reminder to cancel. Each related app is an additional charge so I was out $140 without even knowing id signed up for anything. To unsubscribe you have to go to their actual website.

Reminding me to eat breakfast and occasional pep talks that are buried and often forgotten aren’t worth what I paid. I feel mislead and taken advantage of.

title: SCAM!
body:
I came across Fabulous from an Instagram advertisement. I took the test, paid a dollar for my plan, then when it offered me a $200 subscription at 75% off and the 14 day free trial period; why not? 
After signing up it immediately charged me $50 (and the $1 to set up) then had me download one of their apps. That’s when I discovered the advertisement on instagram wasn’t just for one app but 6 individual apps all with their own subscriptions!
I reached out for my $50 refund and to cancel the subscription and in seconds got a response saying “We regret to inform that in line with our T&Cs, the set-up fee for the trial period is non-refundable.” Mind you this is what the $1 was for, the subscription fee was $200 but 75% off… So, basically every subscription for each app is $200 and the apps offer nothing that Google doesn’t already help people with ADHD find. This is taking advantage of anyone with ADHD actually trying to find ways to improve their life. Absolute Scam.

*I will be leaving a review on each of their apps to warn others about the individual subscription fees.

title: What a JOKE - BOTS - FRAUD
body:
This company doesn’t care about you or anyone with mental health challenges. They will respond to your help emails with BOTS time after time and NEVER READ YOUR EMAIL. 

All they care about is getting your money. They care more about keeping your money and refusing refund rather than building lasting relationships with their customers. Mark my words, this company will FAIL. 

If your company model is based on HELPING PEOPLE, especially people who struggle to get organized, manage tasks, remember to do all the things, you don’t treat them like garbage when they try to cancel or request a refund. You don’t have BOTS respond to them over and over and never read their emails that they spent time and energy to write and then make it sounds like you did in an automated response that was sent out before I could even close my email app. 

They may make money for a while using these tactics, but their company will fail to create lasting customers and people who speak highly of them and share their experience with others. 

DO NOT WASTE YOUR TIME. If anything this will become a detriment to your mental health. Just sad.

title: Do not use this app
body: I would give this 0 stars if I could. I wanted to explore the app to see if it was a good fit for me and decided within 20 minutes that it was not and so I deleted my “free“ account and deleted the app off my phone. I even checked in my Apple subscriptions/payments to make sure I was not getting charged and it did not show the app listed anywhere at all. Lo and behold my credit card has been getting charged for three months at a rate of $39.99 every month for a subscription I did not intentionally sign up for and I don’t even understand how I’ve been getting charged. It took me over an hour and a half to try and simply get a refund and make sure I’m not getting charged in the future. My credit card company refunded the charges, but the fabulous app customer service sent me an auto-reply email stating they would not refund my credit card because I had not canceled within 24 hours of “signing up”. Which was objectively untrue because I downloaded and deleted the app all within about 20 minutes on the same day. It should not be so easy to unintentionally sign up for a paid version of the app and get charged for a subscription when you have in fact, deleted the app and your account. And it should not be so ridiculously difficult to get a proper refund for a product I never used even once.

title: Subscription based program that immediately tried to sell add ons
body:
I heard about Fabulous on a website, did a questionnaire and signed up for a trial before even downloading or looking at the app. When I signed up for the trial, they suggested you pay $1, $10 or $39 for a trial period- your choice. I did one dollar since I really didn’t even know what it was going to be. I got a confirmation email with a link to download the app and instructions how to start your personalized program that was supposed to be based on the goals you chose  taking the questionnaire. Before I could even check out the app, I had to go through all these screens trying to sell me extra stuff. It felt predatory, especially since I didn’t even know what the program consisted of yet. 
I declined all the extras and finally got to check out the app. ironically, when I downloaded the app, I got an automatic email offering me a completely free trial session for 30 days
Anyway I ended up doing about 5 days of the program, then decided to cancel.  It’s what’s in a good time for me to start something new but I also couldn’t get past that predatory vibe first impression. The program seemed OK, I could see where some people may benefit from it. I personally really dislike subscription based services, add-ons, upsells, etc

title: Predatory Payment Options
body: I have no clue what’s going on with the payment options. There is a free trial but the only way you can get to it is by spending money. How much money? If you don’t like it, you get offered a NEW DEAL with a TIMER that you get 10 minutes to choose the reduced plan which was somehow unavailable to you before you hesitated. So now it’s $80 a year but you still have to pay at least a dollar for the free trial. I am so confused and I find this sort of monkeying around to be predatory, especially on those who already struggle with mental health problems and executive functioning. Congratulations Fabulous, taking advantage of those who need you the most.

title: Deceptive Billing Practices + Bad Customer Service
body:
I had signed up for a free one week trial through the Apple App Store and canceled it on day 1 through the App Store Subscriptions page. on the last day of my free trial fabulous offered me a one month extension of the free trial. I accepted it but after a couple of weeks, still wasn’t using the app much. before my last day of the one month trial, I went back into the App Store to make sure that my subscription was canceled and saw that it indeed was.
however, on the renewal date, I was still charged! I reached out to Apple directly and it took them a couple of weeks to figure out that I had not been charged through Apple - my card had been charged directly by fabulous!!

after reaching out to fabulous support, they informed me that they would not return the charge and that I was responsible for canceling my subscription through their online website now, instead of through apple. After being unable to log into their online website to cancel my subscription, I reached out to support again, and they continued to refuse to give me a refund “because they had clearly stated the renewal date”. I tried several times to explain to them that I thought my subscription was canceled because Apple showed it to be canceled and explained that my problem was not with the date, but rather the fact that they had changed methods of billing me! They continue to refuse to refund me and in order to prevent further billing, I had to completely deactivate my Fabulous profile because I still could not log into their online page to manage my “membership”. BEWARE!!!! bad billing practices can often be remedied by good customer service but fabulous has neither!!

title: Great, but make sure you’re in a good place before you start

Indeed, there is an undertone of “oh, just pull up your socks!” to some of the coaching. You need to be sure that you are in a place where you can handle being told “onward and upward!” every day, all day. This app may be most appropriate for the “worried well”.

title: I keep coming back
body: So many times I have tried to conquer the first mountain, but this time is different because I took a break to try it all on my own. I put in the effort and research to learn what works for me by juggling apps and spreadsheets. But the answer was right here all along, waiting for ME to be ready. OCD would not allow me to just do someone’s else’s program, and ADHD made it hard to stick to any routine on my own. This just works. I press play, and its like a Pavlovian response. I had to figure out first on my own what I wanted, then add it to the routines. These were all things I had been tracking and struggling to do, and this just guides me through what I have chosen so that I follow through. The focus aspect for ADHD (and even PTSD) cannot be overstated. The calming ambient music, the full screen tasks, the simple check marks to move on to the next one and the satisfying noises they make allow me to calmly be in the moment. If I am distracted, the music is still playing. The task remains on my screen. I don’t forget! My two cents for anyone starting this app for the first time is to take it slowly, actually follow the program. If you’re OCD like me and already have fifteen tasks you do every morning, just add them and follow your own path. Its finally working for me not only because I am ready, but because its SIMPLE. It replaces a few apps for me and, again, the focus aspect cannot be overstated. It just immerses you in the moment.

title: I should have listened to Reddit re: scammy subscription practices.
body: **Final update** I finally figured out what happened! They slip in a subscription for their Clarify app during the sign up process! You think you’re signing up for the paid version of Fabulous, but the name has been swapped out. SHADY!! Which also explains why people contact Fabulous, cancel Fabulous and still get charged, month after month. Why can’t Fabulous let us know this?? You have to log into a separate part of the website to cancel this hidden subscription, just like when you try to cancel Fabulous.  Don’t bother trying to contact them for help, either. They only allow 250 characters and pre-written options.  **Update:** I did everything exactly as they said on the support page they keep sharing on here in order to cancel my subscription prior to the free trial period ending and they STILL charged me $29.99! ****Original Review**** I was looking for an app to help me build a routine and structure. The reviews I read said this app had some sneaky subscription practices, but I thought I was savvy enough to understand what I was signing up for. The website also had all of these award stickers from places like the NYTimes. It must be a decent company, right? NO! That was not the case! This review is for the website sign up process. I’m still not even clear on what shenanigans were going on, but I’ll explain it the way I understand it. To begin, you do a short quiz & at the end they offer you a “free” trial for 14 days. Then they immediately ask that you pay what you wish—so what’s free about it? There is no option for $0. They give you 3 choices: $1, $10, and recommend $14.71. They say $14.71 is at cost. I chose $1, considering I had heard about their reputation for messing around with subscription pricing. The very next page asks you to sign up for an extended subscription that will bill after the 14 day trial period. The price offered was $39.99 every 3 months. I figured if I liked it, $13-ish a month wasn’t as bad as some of these apps trying to get you to pay by the week! I clicked through. Mind you, there is no way to say no to signing up before you’re allowed to start the free trial, but that’s not unusual, UNFORTUNATELY. The very next page was offering a $49.99 plan for their premium plus, or whatever the next tier was. I didn’t even read it. No option to say no. If that wasn’t enough, the page said it would charge after my BIMONTHLY $39.99 subscription. I KNOW the subscription I said yes to was supposed to be for THREE months. Now I knew I had to get out of there & cancel immediately & that’s exactly what I did. I’ve never cancelled a subscription so quickly in my life! The cancellation screen gave me all these reasons to stay and offered me SIGNIFICANTLY lower pricing. I think there was a $29.99 plan for 6 months. Forget it. They don’t actually give you what they offer anyway. Why would I let them trick me again! Keep this company AWAY from your credit card! I’m shocked by the endorsements and reviews this company has. Would’ve loved to try it out, but I’m deleting the app & keeping an eye on my credit card bill for the next several months.

title: SCAM - no longer related to Duke University, MINUS 100 stars if it was possible.
body:
They keep trying to charge my card EVERY single day. The app is no longer connected to Duke University - North Carolina. Their office is in Europe, and they DO NOT have an email to contact them directly. Only through their app website form. I requested my plan cancellation 3X to no avail. I have been ignored over and over again.
This is the last attempt to cancel, but it came back to me because it was a no-reply email from their accounting department. So maybe they read my review and stop this non-sense, borderline harassment. I already paid them $69.98, that is plenty of money to scam someone. Enough is enough. 
Like the othet reviewer that posted on Wed this week, I will report this app everywhere possible.

“Please cancel my subscription as I already requested.  This is your 3rd notice. See below.
These screen shots  are dated from 11/9/24.
I paid $49.99 on 10/24/24, and then $19.99 on 11/1/24. I am extremely uncomfortable with these amounts that I paid and I regret trying to subscribe to your service. And now everyday I get warnings that my cards is receiving attempted charges from you in the amount of both $19.99 and $29.99. I feel this was an app to help with stress. And now I feel I am being harassed by your accounting department. I ordered the cancellation of both my memberships (that I just signed up for a few days before) on 11/9/24 for both Fabulous and Clarify. 
Please remove me from your system. stop trying to charge my card several times a month.
I greatly appreciate your help! Happy Holidays! “

UPDATE: if you look at all 1 star reviews and the message from the developer- they are identical. They don’t even bother actually looking at the situation. In summary, you are held hostage, they don’t negotiate a refund, and more importantly, I am going to pay another $29.99, on top of $49.99 plus $19.99, to get rid of them for once and for all. Again, an app that is supposed to be helpful, not actually having a real customer service, that CARE for their customers. Again, at this point it doesn’t matter how good their app can be - I couldn’t even start looking at it, for fear I would get charged more and more. And again they are NOT CONNECTED TO DUKE UNIVERSITY. It is a click and bait. Good luck to those that use and eventually want to quit.

body: I cannot explain the value I’ve gotten out of this app. I thrive with structure and this has given me a considerable amount more of it in my life. I’m nearly 5 years into using Fabulous and it’s genuinely one of few things that have kept me moving. Between the onboard meditation modules, the stretching modules and being able to set my own routines up throughout the day, I’ve gotten tenfold what I’ve put in. My day starts right. My anxiety has lowered significantly. I embrace my struggles and use them to steer my hope now which would have seemed impossible five years ago. If you struggle with a negative mindset, self care and self-structure, I can’t recommend this app enough. The community is uplifting, the guided modules are simple but impactful and I’m just incredibly grateful for the mere hope I’ve gained access to as a result of consistent use of these tools over the last five years.

I've emailed support a few times WITH ZERO REPLIES FROM THEM. Fortunately I used Apple Card and Apple flagged the charges as suspicious and never let them go through. The lame part is my Apple Card will constantly get blocked for normal use until I verify with Apple support that it's just this dumb app trying to charge me over and over. DO NOT START THE TRIAL.

title: Worst customer service ever!
body:
I tried signing up for a free trial 2-3 weeks ago. Didn’t seem hard at first until trying to navigate the app further which ran me in circles. Kept asking my login info, etc. Somehow, I ended up signing up for three different free trials/subscriptions using two different payment methods, although I wasn’t positive at first. One of them was using Apple Pay, so I was able to cancel it immediately. The other two were set up through PayPal.
Once suspected I erred, I wrote to Customer Service at Fabulous to explain and asked them to please see if I did create other subscriptions, and if so, cancel them immediately before money would get withdrawn. Another 1-2 weeks later (not the 4 days the app promises), I got an email response only to say that they are inundated with customer requests and they’ll get back to me as soon as they can, which they still have not done! 
Sure enough, money was taken out of my PayPal account today for TWO subscriptions, one at $29.99 and the other at $39.99. Plus for the initial trial, I even (stupidly) donated $10! So now I’m out $79.98 while on a fixed income and am no closer to getting assistance with my neurodivergence.
My advice: looks like a cool app, but be warned about the friendliness of it and constantly changing prices at which you can subscribe to it. And use ApplePay or credit card, because otherwise, you’re probably screwed out of a refund.

body: This product that I don’t use has become a tax I pay for having ADHD thanks to poor customer service. Not for me. I got a notice of high email volume and the response was delayed. Eventually I was denied a refund for a premium membership in a personal message then an separate notice of a free 90 days on the app (that I don’t find useful and want to cancel) without any context as to why I was receiving it. I hoped the email showed I was restored to trial status and could now cancel, but no, they are bent on keeping my fee. Fine. But the account management system is still leaving me in limbo and feeling powerless to actually manage my account ie, ensure I am never charged again. It takes me in login loops and does not provides clear language confirmation as to HOW I am subscribed nor an easy button to cancel / ensure it won’t auto renew. My advice is to get a bullet journal and not have to deal with the backend confusion of this app and its sister apps which are constantly being internally advertised in it.

title: Depression at its finest
body: I can’t blame Covid. I was depressed a few months before lock down. I spiraled further into destructive habits such as not taking care of myself or my environment. My house became a place of shame. I became walking shame. I downloaded this app on a whim of ONE DAY I’ll make a change. ONE DAY I’ll clean my house. ONE DAY I’ll get said task done. Well that one day was 8 days ago! My anxiety I typically have with doing things is eliminated by something so simple as the app telling me to slow down and take it easy so as to not overwhelm myself when I add routines. Let me tell you routines help! I’ve seen the difference of what it can do to my morning. Fabulous gives me the chance to sit and reflect and write down things that otherwise I just suppress and throw back into bad habits. I am taking small bite size steps towards my goal of being a healthier self. Last night I cleaned some dishes that have been sitting there since last thanksgiving! And this morning I tidied up my bathroom! Today I feel like some sunshine and fresh air and will take a walk instead of hiding away in my dark apartment. I found this app when my life was in jeopardy of losing all light. Fabulous gave me hope that I can overcome the darkness day by day. Thank you to all the individuals that put this amazing app together. I needed help but I was so anxious and overwhelmed by seeking help I never did. Without Fabulous I do not believe I would be 8 days in doing the things I am doing or looking at myself in the mirror and not crying.

title: More difficult to navigate than it used to be
body:
I’ve used Fabulous on and off for several years. There are things I love about it that keep me renewing the annual subscription, but the UI has changed in the last year or two and is much more difficult to navigate in my opinion.

There used to be a button in the middle labeled “make me fabulous” or something like that. It would let you choose categories like guided meditations, stretching, and the one I used the most, deep work. Now, I have no idea where to find that menu, if it’s there at all. I am only able to access the deep work feature by going through my afternoon routine since I added it there at one point.

The longest streak I ever got on my morning routine was around 70 days. I love the little pictures of the “journey” that illuminates a new area each day you continue your streak. However, that only goes for 2 or 3 weeks. It might sound silly, but seeing the next part of the picture actually really motivated me to maintain my streak.

I also realized from that longer streak that the app maybe isn’t really built for people to use long term? The daily coaching things repeated once every 3-4 weeks. The messages are always a nice reminder, but by the third time hearing the same one, I was a little disappointed there weren’t more than 20-30 in the rotation. I don’t know if that has changed by now— that streak was a couple years ago.

The one thing I love the MOST about this app is the deep work feature, specifically the long ritual to ramp up for a 4 hour deep work session. I renew every year for this alone because when I’ve tried to do the deep work ritual without the app, I don’t usually have the discipline to complete it as slowly as the app dictates. Even if I’m not planning to work for 4 full hours, I will do that ritual for any amount of deep work because it works better than anything else to get me in a productive mood. By the time I get to the end of the ritual, I am itching to start working. For someone with adhd, finding something like this that consistently works is huge. I do wish there was ambient music on the deep work feature, though, and that the app didn’t have such a tendency to crash in the middle of your 4 hour session.

title: BEWARE!  PREDATORY AND POSSIBLY ILLEGAL SUBSCRIPTION CHARGES!  Read the reviews before downloading!
body:
PSA: if you feel you’ve been charged unfairly, please file a report worth the FTC, your state’s attorney general office, and others - it’s easy, and it is your right to do so!

It is my understanding that under the FTC Negative Option Rule (16 CFR Part 425), businesses are required to make subscription cancellations as easy as the sign-up process. This subscription service fails to provide an easy cancellation method, which appears to be a violation of this rule.

I signed up for a “free” trial and even donated the recommended $16 to cover the costs of the trial period.  I had the app for less than 24 hours and felt it was childish and not at all what I needed, so I went through the steps to cancel and delete from my iPhone.  2 weeks later I’m getting charged $40, and yet I can’t even log in!  I emailed their customer support and received a generic chatbot email stating that they could not find my account but that based on their terms and conditions I could not get a refund.  I have no idea if they will be continue to bill me.  I called my bank and blocked future billings, but from their online help articles it sounds as if they use collections for unpaid invoices.  I’m feeling absolutely grifted, and have no confidence that they will leave me alone from here.

title: Great idea, needs work and is overpriced
body: I love the idea of this app. It's got a great framework and the idea of building tiny habits is excellent. I really wanted to like the execution more. It is a bit hectic and not that well organized IMO. One of the initial habits the app adds to your routine is exercise. After finishing the initial journey and starting a new one (the better sleep journey) it added exercise to my daily plan again without any concept that it had already added it for me in the first journey. Adding a habit I already established after only 3 weeks of using the app makes no sense to me and shows a disconnect and lack of consistency at times. Furthermore, during my "free trial", it ended a few days earlier than the date on my subscription and was already telling me to "upgrade" and blocking off the premium features I was theoretically supposed to have until Oct 17 (stopped working on Oct 14). If they were charging under $10 a month I'd say it would be worth keeping it and assuming they would fix these glitches because the good part of the app is really excellent (the habits, the daily coaching sessions, the other various resources, are all very good). But until it's less glitchy and more consistent it's not worth that much money to me and feels overpriced. Also it's super annoying how often they are pushing you to review them and how many random apps they want to you to download. This just adds to the overall feeling of being too hectic. But still, despite my gripes, I think they are trying to do something that is super helpful for people and I appreciate that.

author: Smelvin R

title: The most helpful app around for managing my life and my well being
body:
UPDATED REVIEW:

Thank you, Fabulous Developers! 

High praise and kudos to you for taking all of the negative feedback and turning it around. 

The additional targeted apps, which you previously wanted me to pay a lot of extra money for, are now all included in my single existing subscription. I'm loving the Ambience app and the Enchant app so far. There are also apps focused on managing ADHD, setting goals & finding your purpose, anxiety & stress management, healthy eating, and sleep. 

One of the main reasons I stopped using the Fabulous app for the past two years, besides the obnoxious notifications, was the cumbersome and overwhelming design. The graphics themselves were amazing, but there were so many different features available that it was hard to find what I wanted, when I wanted to use it. Hard to know where to start looking for what I needed within the app. Moving some of these features into other dedicated apps has solved most of that. 

For anyone who feels that life can be stressful and overwhelming – mentally, emotionally, physically – this app is for you!

Highly recommend!

ORIGINAL REVIEW, 2 out of 5 stars

Excessive money grabbing for additional apps is off putting:

This app is very helpful for routine building and growing your emotional well being. Or, it used to be. The excessive notifications put me off. There’s no middle ground, where you can choose the notifications that will be helpful, but opt out of the ones that are bothersome. The notifications are supposed to make me feel supported, but I just feel nagged. 

Also, the app now bombards me with ads and offers for their other apps. I pay for the premium membership, so I should’t be spammed by the people I’m already paying. The additional apps they want you to sign up for require a lot more money for essentially the same service. 

I’ve seen a lot of reviews about wrongful, illegal billing after customers have cancelled their subscriptions, and poor customer service when they try to get their money back. 

Be wary of signing up. But, if you can tolerate the app maker’s obnoxious money grabbing & the nuisance notifications, the app itself is great.

title: slimy, disingenuous marketing
body:
They roped me in with an ad that was explicitly framed as a research study to help people overcome burnout, procrastination, and feeling “lazy.” The next question on the survey was about having been diagnosed with ADHD, and the following questions were about your barriers to success, major struggles, etc. At the end of a survey, I was shown a screen that promised a “personalized plan.” I knew at that point it was gonna put the results behind a paywall or at least ask for my personal info, and I was right. 

It’s dishonest to frame your ad as a research study, especially because it was targeted at people like me who suffer (and I do mean suffer) the consequences of having ADHD. It’s unfair and disingenuous to rope people in with a false promise “just a two-minute quiz!” that purports to help them with time-management and procrastination issues that have very and devastating effects on their lives. Just look on any ADHD-related forum online and you will quickly learn that those folks are desperate to get any kind of solace and support, they’ll participate in any study and try any product that offers a shred of hope. So to take advantage of that desperate need is just distasteful - I’d even go so far as to call it disrespectful. Just say up front that you’re a paid organization tool, and stop pretending to be some valiant service to the ADHD community.

For example, the iPhone version of the app makes it pretty hard to log in by visually obscuring the place to enter your pw, for the sake of making the screen pretty, and by making the phone think the pw field is for email, which makes it totally inconvenient to log in with the 1Password password manager. Another example: The iPhone app and iPad app, logged in with the same hard-fought credentials, don't know anything about each other. I might as well be 2 different people. For the number of devices I have, thinking of wealth distribution, maybe I should be even more different people. But this thing isn't free. It's not even what I would consider cheap, soooo .... I expect seamless integration across devices. The first lessons mention taking small steps and going slow to build new habits, but the interface itself is not structured like that. It offers a whole candy store of more tips, some to read, some to hear. I feel like this app got started by scientists, but captured by marketers who revised the plot. Maybe future releases will make it more intuitive and on track.

title: Inaccessibility Predatory & Disappointing
body:
I have never written an app review, but this experience was especially absurd so I felt the need to inform a potential audience about the miscommunication and inaccessibility of this app. I downloaded the app to try out the free trial since I have been wanting to build a better routine. About a week in, I was underwhelmed by the limitations of the start of the “journey” and realized it wasn’t going to be for me, so I decided to cancel the trial. I went into my account information to try and manage my subscription, but only saw an option to delete my entire account. I went ahead and did that, but decided to check the article online about how to cancel the trial in case deleting my account wasn’t enough. It said that if I had started it through the app, I just had to go into my subscriptions page in my apple ID and cancel it there (a process I have done several times before). I went into that page and didn’t see any subscriptions there, so I figured that by deleting my entire account the trial/subscription was thus cancelled. So I thought it was resolved. 

A couple weeks later, I see that my credit card has been charged 40 DOLLARS by the “Fabulous App Paris”. In shock, I submit a refund request explaining my situation. The response I get is that, since I read the Terms and Conditions, I could not be issued a refund. As far as I know, reading the terms and conditions does not preclude one from miscommunication on behalf of the app and any faults in locating the subscription. I was told I had to visit the Fab WEBSITE (which I never had, as far as I can remember) and cancel the subscription from the account page there. In order to prevent further charges, I visited the website and was told I had to ACTIVATE my account in order to access it at all. So not only did I myself know I never used the functionality of the app for which I was charged, the program ITSELF knew this. I went through and officially cancelled my subscription, as well as expressed my disappointment to the app team for their response several days ago. I have yet to receive any response. 

The target audience of this app is, pointedly, individuals with ADHD— me included. Accessibility for such individuals when it comes to bureaucracy is tough as it is, but this convoluted, illogical process seems especially predatory given the app’s marketing strategy. I hope something will be done to remedy this, but, in the meantime, I felt the need to warn potential users of this complicated and frustrating ordeal.

title: Loved at first, but Spammy  Upsells DOZENS of times a day
body:
When I first started Fabulous Premium I loved it so much I’d intended to buy the year subscription, but I’ve just about had it with the extremely AGGRESSIVE, never ending upsells! 

It wastes my time to keep getting sent to the App Store to buy the other apps they RELENTLESSLY shove down your throat. It loses any credibility they had as far as feeling they are a trustworthy company. Even worse, HALF of the Fabulous App itself is covered in UPSELLS forcing their other apps on me! If you have a premium version of an app it should not be nothing but upsells. I’m a Capitalist who loves sales people and marketing. If even I think it’s ABSURDLY, over the top AGGRESSIVE level of sales push, then it’s really bad. I feel they’re taking advantage of people.

It does have stunningly beautiful art, gorgeous sounds and (PARTS) of it are scientifically backed. I do wish there was more flexibility w some things and that it would give me more freedom to refuse the ads and refuse getting on their social media. Almost all research shows more harm than good from social media. That’s one more thing that makes them money, but that is not good for me. I had to restart my phone to avoid being forced to sign up for their social. 

I’m not sure but went from 100% planning on doing the year down to about a 30% possibility now. Wayyyy too aggressive! Waayyy too much time wasted on their pushy, pushy, questionable sales tactics. It makes me doubt them deeply. I believe it would also be harmful to anyone emotionally vulnerable who uses this app. It’s training the person not to think for themselves. 

I hope they get someone on the team to examine the ethics of the invasive approach they are using. Obviously they want to make money, but I think they could still make money with a more ethical approach. I hope they fix the app to make the focus making money with an app so good people want more; not what they are doing now.

title: Not for me
body:

I am a direct, plain and simple, no fuss kind of person who needs some structure to reign in some ADHD and the resulting focus issues to manage my responsibilities. 

That said, for me Fabulous has a patronizing interface. They call the user a “traveler” which  made me feel as if I had exceeded the recommended age limit for the app. 

The app interface is horrible. You cannot map where things are because they move. Buried features. Extremely difficult to find a features you believe you may like the next time you open the app. Cartoonish visuals which again made me feel like I was using a child’s app. 

My last comment is that the advertising is misleading. They advertising it like a productivity app but I did not see that. 

There are some great Reddit threads and internet reviews if you are interested in Cognitive Behavioral Therapy apps and well as productivity apps. Find one that fits the way your brain works.

title: Fabulous when it works. Zero tech support when it doesn’t.
body:
This is an amazing app. It has high quality media, it’s got a great program to guide you through the “mountains” of developing the habits that you want to develop. The prompts are always helpful insights. 

Although I haven’t participated much in the in-app community, it’s there and it’s robust. My one complaint (it’s not a true complaint, just the acknowledgment that I may not be the most common user type) is that the community is mostly geared towards starting out at ground zero. For example, the social development circle has a lot of conversation around how to find friends when you’re isolated, but asking for tips for best work/meeting engagement only nets the crickets. 

Finally, tech support. It’s awful. Rather, it’s nonexistent and seems to be largely saying a thing is answered in the troubleshooting FAQ even when it’s not. I like the app enough that I’ve had the patience to wait over a month since my second and I still haven’t heard “we understand your problem.”

As far as I can tell, it’s possible for journey progress to get corrupted and no way to refresh from where you are. Instead, I think you have to start over. That’s where I am now. Loading my saved progress gets me glitches like:

- Repeating daily coaching,
- Missing letter content from journeys, and
- Occasional missing daily coaching all together that’s not a factor of internet access. 

Going through bug testing now to see if it works with 100% fresh install. It really is worth it when it works. (Full Disclosure: Part of the reason for this review is to motivate tech support to provide support.)

title: Deceptive and unethical practice, anti-consumer
body:
Over one year ago a free trial that I apparently had with Fabulous, an app I never used (I logged in once to try to create a profile to build a routine and it was so overwhelming and labor-intensive I logged out and never ever logged in again) converted to a paid annual subscription. I had no idea—was not warned or notified. Never used the app. 

Fast forward a year. One year later I was charged again for an annual subscription with no notice. I saw the charge on my bill and was shocked. This practice is incredibly deceptive, and it’s not something I’ve experienced before with ANY apps I’ve used. They send a “your subscription will renew in x days” email and offer transparency.  

I immediately reached out to Fabulous (after creating a profile and completing the setup experience FOR THE FIRST TIME) to kindly request a refund. The team replied that they wouldn’t refund it per policy. I explained my situation and also that I have ADHD, a condition that apps like Fabulous claim to support through targeted development or programming. 

Nevertheless, denied again. So now Fabulous has been paid twice, two years in a row, by me—someone who HAS NEVER USED THE APP. I will be sharing this information widely to help others like me who might mistakenly think this company intends to help people who want to create structure and support their personal development and wellness.

I tried to message you all on Instagram and I tried to go on your website and send you a personal message so as to not have to do this, concerned if anyone will read this and respond… I was one of the first trial people when you all first began your journey. title: Cancelled but still charging
body:
Don’t give this app your credit card info. Even after you cancel during the trial, it will still try to charge you $39.99. My credit card keeps getting locked because this app is continuously trying to charge me.

Update on 8/18 - I received an email from their support team telling me I should have cancelled via the website. I cancelled the app subscription not long after I downloaded the app. I still received a charge to my card for $39.99, but because it was not an active iOS subscription, my Apple Card fraud alerted me to the charge. I checked my Apple IOS active app subscriptions and found no active Fabulous active subscription. I disputed the amount but not before the fraud alert locked my card. It took a while for Apple to investigate and eventually my card was unlocked and the charge removed. I have a screenshot from July 13th that I had to provide to Apple Support to prove that I had no active Fabulous subscription. Fabulous attempted a second time to charge me for a subscription I did not have. I left a review on the App Store to alert your development team that the app is continuing to charging me despite me and Apple Support confirming I have no active subscription to this service. Rather than researching the bug/issue, the support team said I should have just cancelled the subscription via the website - when I had already cancelled it, and had no record of having an active subscription. The support team put the responsibility on me, as though I had not done my due diligence before making a complaint. It took time trying to figure out how to unlock my card with Apple and caused unnecessary financial issues with my daycare not being able to process a weekly payment via my credit card, hence my continued  frustration with this company. I’m posting this update to my review and with the recommendation that their support team not first place the blame on the end user and instead to reach out to find out what the confusion may be. I would have been all too happy to help troubleshoot this issue but I was blamed for just simply not cancelling via the website (when I did, it’s not my fault their website was not syncing with the active iOS subscriptions).

title: ‼️ ⚠️ SCAMMERS ⚠️ ‼️ Use this app if you want them to steal from you
body:
WARNING ⚠️ STAY AWAY FROM THIS SCAMMER COMPANY ⚠️ 

So I got this app trying to improve myself. After a bit I decided I didn’t need it anymore and cancelled my subscription. I had confirmed that they cancelled the annual membership and life moved on. 

Then next year they charged me for no reason. After getting in contact with them and some annoying back and forth they finally refunded me. But that’s not the kicker.

Now 2 years later, a new phone, new phone number, new debit and credit cards, they still somehow charged me. So I contacted customer service and they didn’t care because I didn’t have my original account. So I went digging to get on my old account from 2 years ago. I got a hold of them through it, showed screenshots of my bank charge, $39.99, the date, and showing it was from fabulous. But they said we can’t “find your account” and that was that. LIKE DO THEY HAVE ANY IDEA HOW ANNOYING AND TIME CONSUMING IT WAS TO GET ALL MY OLD ACCOUNT INFORMATION AND PASSWORD THAT I NO LONGER REMEMBER. 

Needless to say they DIDNT refund me, so if you want your money stolen after you cancel the membership then this app is perfect for you. Definitely stay away!

(At first the only thing I had to remember was to open the app instead of remembering to do all my daily self-care tasks! What a relief!)
