title: It does what it’s meant to do and doesn’t ask too much of you!
body:
I thought it would have faulty information/advise or unreliable sources, but what it’s been saying has been sound so far and from sources I find fairly solid. I also thought it would be hard to use, but everything seems easy to locate and a lot of it just pops up when you need it! But my main concern in getting the app was that it would immediately demand money or would have a sucky free option that’s only effective if you pay for premium, but to my surprise, it hasn’t required anything really so far! I don’t have money at the moment, but with the cost they ask for, (especially with the student discount), I would definitely pay for it no question about it!

As a very introspective person, I’ve already developed a good understanding of my mind and the things I need to do to balance out my life, but I’ve always struggled with actually knowing if I’m right or not. I have ADD, (like ADHD without the hyperactive), and I really needed an app to mark down the things I did and the things I need to do, and this has been a great app for that!

I would definitely recommend this app for anyone who needs help with organization, productivity, and/or motivation.

title: An absolutely amazing and HELPFUL app!!
body: I've never left a review for, well honestly, anything before, but this app has genuinely left me feeling more inspired and motivated than anything else I have ever tried in order to become more motivated, organized, and satisfied with life. I'm not diagnosed with ADHD, I have never been tested, but my parents and I have been positive I've had it since I was very young. I struggle greatly with staying organized, get paralyzed with fear and anxiety at even the smallest notion that I have something on my to-do list, and procrastinate to an extent I've never seen in anyone else in my life. It's been really hard to just keep up with life, through my educational career as well as in the work world afterwards. I get burnt out easily and struggle to maintain the energy to do even the smallest daily tasks. To get to the point, I used this app and its accompanying apps for only a week a while ago, just till the free trial ended, and I already can't praise it enough. Other habit tracking apps, even other ones that gamify habits and mental health and exercise, never worked for me because I felt like I had to organize the apps and choose the habits myself, which then paralyzed me with that anxiety and indecision as it felt like an added responsibility to my day. This app is already structured, and adds habits slowly, one at a time, that genuinely help you feel more energized and motivated each day. And it is not just a tracker at all, but rather is formulated as almost a fantastical journey, all while motivating and explaining the science behind the journey to you. It doesn't overwhelm you, as it starts very small. It makes you feel like you are truly doing something for yourself, and beginning an actual journey towards betterment in a way I've never experienced before. I genuinely, in that one week trial, felt happier in the mornings, had more patience at work, got more tasks done at home, felt more confident and adventurous, and became more in touch with my true feelings and goals in life. I was excited to visit the app and complete my goals for each day, and I loved the animations and storytelling that made me feel like the hero of my own journey. It sounds kind of silly to be hyping an app like this after only one week, but I'm renewing my subscription today and paying for premium and I'm genuinely so excited to do so and continue to better my life. This app and the creators are one of a kind and I'm so grateful I found it and now have the tools and motivation to build my life up one day at a time.

title: 🚩claims to use research, but immediately says you “just need to build habits”
body: If they were really using research, they’d know that ADHDers DON’T BUILD HABITS. Systems are as close as we get, and they use the words interchangeably, claiming the result is autonomy. It’s not. I always cancel my subscription when I do these free trials because they make their money on people who forget. Apparently I didn’t this time. It charged me $40 for a quarter (4mo) after a 1 month free trial I didn’t use. When I went to cancel, they offered me 6 mo for $25 or 1 mo for $2 (which I’m sure has another $40 fee after). But you just took my $40, which could have almost gotten me a year? Def not. The whole basis of this app is to build habits. They conveniently didn’t include that part of the app name in the ad. I didn’t even start the program before because it’s 100% focused on you having the ability to create habits. I know, it’s in the name! But hey, it’s “specially created for ADHDers”. So, I’ve gone through the intro now and my initial impression was correct. I’m already doing everything it says it will help me with. None of it is habit. I did a 90 day “habit challenge” once and I’ve literally never done that thing again since. I even studied habits at one point in my degree. I knew it was an issue, but didn’t know why until the research more recently. My brain will never create a habit. I already have an app that send me daily routine reminders. It sits untouched every day, like every other one of these useless “ADHD” apps. Wait of time and money. Just one more thing to add to my ADHD tax bill for the year.

title: A lovely little app
body:
Fabulous is a 5 out of 5 concept with a 4 out of 5 functionality. The app’s lessons and pacing are well designed, and I can already see an improvement in my mood one week in. Checking-in with myself daily now feels effortless. I only wish using the app felt the same way. 

The app’s organization is clear enough (albeit a bit cluttered), however completing tasks often takes one down interface paths that feel incomplete or leave the user with no further links to follow. There a multiple ways to complete daily goals (by checking boxes on the home page or by entering guided goal interfaces through a user’s routines). Depending on which route the user takes to complete a goal, they are offered vastly different resources. For example, when completing the meditation routine through the guided goal interface users are provided with progressive lessons on how to meditate. However, when completing the meditation routine through the home page check boxes, users are brought to a pop-up page that offers no resources. It was only on my 3rd day of meditating that I stumbled upon the meditation guides mentioned. Simplifying user app pathways would go a long way in improving the overall quality of the app. I’m looking forward to future iterations!

body: I tried a few apps to help me with motivation and developing habits. This one is the best, it teaches me to start off small and I mean small steps. I do tend to start off with what I think is a small step but I also start off with like doing 4-5 things at a time. Realizing that I was doing too much and too fast even though i normally take on a lot on a daily, nothing really stuck to me I always wanted to do more and try something else if I didn’t feel like I didn’t see any improvement within a week or two. And when I felt like a failure I usually quit, but not with this app. There are guided activities, challenges and coaching in the app and that really helps me when I feel down and want to give up, or when I feel like I need that competition with myself to get the groove back. I’m loving this app so far, I really would like to see where I’ll be in a year just from using this app!

Even those last two months were not desired.

Alongside that, while the app is super pretty and cute with lots of nice tones, in my personal experience, it isn’t practical at all and actually induces ADHD  - because when you open it to get something done, all the colors and the various elements end up taking your attention… having to rewrite your daily tasks takes forever, nothing is organized or easy to follow… 

It’s just an overstimulating app with a few music tracks and lots of pretty graphics.

I recommend using Spotify for music, getting a good playlist and finding a very boring app for tracking tasks so you’re not distracted by it.

But that’s just me. I think they definitely made something pretty to look at. 

I hope they improve their payment/cancellation process as it already is one of the most expensive apps I’ve ever tried.

title: Incredible app
body:

Second, when life is beating you, and you are trying to rebuild your habits, this app gives you an extra source of motivation

In my case, motivation was not there anymore, so I needed something simpler, something more family-like; I needed encouragement. For example, the Drinking Water Habit has been what gave me the feeling of being productive on my worst days

This app is like having a personal grandma who doesn't give up on you even when you give up on yourself

I’m only human and it’s okay to make mistakes and if you “fail” at something that doesn’t mean that you aren’t good enough or that you have to give up. author: Emmandaline

title: Day 1
body:
So far so good with the opening start to the journey. I joined after hearing about the app from chat GPT listing helpful apps to build better habits/routines. Will update review periodically. 
The 4 stars is mainly because it felt like the app was glorifying itself too much for my taste with its only backup evidence being from the findings of the creator. At least that is how it came across to me. The start is a little slow to get past all the “please trust us and the research we did” to then get into actually putting in markers that we want track and actually start work on building the habits. Again this is day 1 so I am hopeful it just gets better from here. 
Only other critic I have at the moment is there is no night shift option. For the past 4 years, in 6 days out of the week I am asleep during the day and wake up to work all night into the next day. I was able to figure out how to change morning routine start time to when I wake up. Hopefully when I unlock afternoon and evening I will be able to set it up to match the kind of life I am living and want to have. 
That said I do like the visual and reminder options.

title: Buyer beware
body:
I downloaded this app thinking it would help me build better habits. I quickly found it overwhelming. At the time, I had signed up for the free trial of premium and then, as we always do, forgot to cancel so I was charged. Cool, that’s on me. I promptly cancelled my subscription, or so I thought. 
Fast forward a year, and on my anniversary, I get a mysterious charge. When I investigate I realize it’s this app. Go to cancel, again!, try to request a refund, and realize the refund request link is a dead link and it takes you in circles. No customer service so nothing I can do except hope it went through this time. This app is very misleading so watch out. Also, to add icing on the cake, after cancelling again this year, apparently I have opted back in to marketing emails?! I saw other reviews saying the same thing about difficulty cancelling so this is a true issue with this app and the developers really need to do something about that. And maybe not put up dead links on their website if people would like a refund for a subscription they had already cancelled.

title: Disappointing Experience (Free Version)
body:
As someone who struggles with forming habits and managing ADHD symptoms, I was hopeful when I downloaded the Fabulous app. However, my experience with it has been overwhelmingly disappointing.

First and foremost, the app failed to take into account my specific needs and preferences when they suggest habits. This lack of customization made it difficult for me to engage with the program effectively.

Moreover, the content within the app felt overly simplistic and at times even patronizing. The messages and prompts often came across as shallow affirmations rather than meaningful guidance. For example, the reminders about "Duchenne smiles" and generic habit suggestions based on weather conditions felt disconnected from the real challenges face in forming and maintaining habits.

Furthermore, the heavy promotion of their other app, 'Clarify,' which supposedly targets ADHD symptoms. Felt misleading. Upon exploration, it became apparent that 'Clarify' offered little differentiation from 'Fabulous' and was locked behind a paywall.

In summary, while Fabulous claims to offer science-backed methodologies for habit formation, my experience suggests otherwise. The app's lack of customization, overly simplistic content, and misleading promotions left me feeling frustrated and disillusioned. I would not recommend it to others seeking genuine support in improving their habits or managing ADHD symptoms.

title: Does a disservice to Dan Ariely’s reputation
body:
I was excited about this app because it’s reputedly started by behavioral psychologist and author Dan Ariely, who I’ve learned a lot from over the years. While the Journey experiences are a bit corny, I was on board with it. I was even okay with the sudden $54 charge for a one year premium subscription that somehow got set up as my automatic subscription choice when I opted into the free trial and gave them my payment information.
What I’m not okay with is my experience with customer support. I was making incremental progress on the app and completed my first Journey and also started tracking a new daily habit every day. Then I got a new phone and lost all my progress. Premium subscriptions offer a “restore journey progress” option which I tried, going back to a date before my new phone was activated. The system was buggy, though, and did not successfully restore my journey progress.
Emotionally, it’s humiliating to now open up an app I made such good initial progress in only to get bombarded with “You can do it!” messages and corny animations. The app no longer speaks to my actual journey and where I’m at in my habit formation goals. It’s frustrating to me that multiple customer support requests have proved unable to resolve this issue, and that my in app experience remains so poor. 
I would have expected a better app with the name of Dan Ariely behind it. Unfortunately, based on this experience, I can’t recommend this app to others

title: So far so good
body:
I started using the app a few days ago and found it motivates me with the reminders and the routines. I like that it incorporates daily messages to help with your mindset if you need a mental pick-me-up. There’s a few improvements that can make the app a little more user friendly but overall it’s very practical and useful for daily life. 

Using the application has made me better with doing annoying or seemingly overwhelming tasks by putting them into a routines, which you create depending on time of day along with day of the week. From there, you get reminders and use the app to complete your routines. For me, this is very helpful and what I need to give me that extra push for things like “eat veggies” or “floss.” In addition, the app also takes you on a journey, and gives little readings or quotes to motivate you/improve your mindset. Depending on what struggles you may be having, the journey you are assigned (which you can change) can be different. 

Overall it’s an electronic to do list with motivational features within it to help you with perspective. It’s working very well for me thus far.  Personally, I get a little release of dopamine every time I get to complete a routine.

title: …All 3 of those problems are still present.
body:
There was a review from 2 years ago complaining about the lack of customer support, chat, and the issue of cancellations. All 3 of those problems are still present. 

It feels near impossible to cancel and after following the prompts several times to try and get this subscription cancelled, I’ve done the same / variations of the same thing over and over to no avail. 

So glad I used a cash app card and not my bank account because I can’t cancel the subscription unless i send an email, stalk my email for a response, then I have a short time period to respond to them before I have to start the process all over. All the while this payment for $39.99 keeps trying to find its way out of my cash app. 

I can’t even focus on the positives of the app being helpful because I can’t get past the scam that is subscribing/unsubscribing from the app. 

It’s 2024. It’s not hard to add an AI chat box to the app/site to help navigate these issues.  I’m sure reviews would be much better especially since communication / cancellation is my only major complaint of the whole app experience (though user experience can be a bit shotty with app navigation but not the point)

Edit: I already know the developer response to this review is going to be “go to our help section and our team can help” If it was that easy to do, people wouldn’t still be complaining about it at least 2 years after another negative reviewer mentioning the same issues. 

Yall are constantly updating the app for performance and bugs. how about you finally make it so that subscribers, who are often neurodivergent people, don’t have to fight a war to cancel if they feel like. I mean I can’t even cancel it from the App Store????? 🤯 

It’s giving, unethical behavior.

None of the features are even remotely worth looking into it will make you $40 poorer. It’s also extremely sketchy that the subscription is convoluted to cancel, and that is most certainly done on purpose. Additionally, the subscription is done separate from Apple services, so you won’t see it on your app subscriptions. title: I don’t usually leave reviews BUT…
body:
I’ve known of Fabulous for probably 5 years now. The first time I had it, I honestly wasn’t very serious about changing my life. I just wanted to try this cool, new productivity and mindfulness app. I loved it, BUT I wasn’t the type of person to be committed to anything for long PLUS I was an overachiever. So of course, even when the program suggests to start with only one thing at a time, I stacked up everything I wanted to change in my life into the app and guess what? I failed—MISERABLY—and eventually deleted Fabulous. Looking back at the last few years of my life, that was definitely a recurring theme in so many areas of my life. 

Within the last 8 months, I had an identity crisis and realized that that version of me is someone I actively DO NOT want to be. I’ve been on a journey of relearning the most basic habits ever and now that I’m in the understanding that life cannot be rushed, I’m unwilling to attempt to overachieve and plow through my achievements.

I’ve redownloaded the app cuz I LOVED the interface and functionality so much. The storytelling is incredibly engaging. The visuals are stunning and gamified. I honestly have no complaints and I know it's worth everything I give it (money included). I’m grateful that there’s a community aspect of it because that helps me to built my environment with others in the same frame of mind.

One year from now, I’m hoping to look back and realize that I planted a series of tiny seeds everyday and it has blossomed into something incredible.

The daily schedule starts off slow but quickly adds more notifications and tasks. Between this and the constant “buy more” it’s just a lot. 

The content is great though. There are some solid points and explanations hidden behind all the noise. I just could not recommend this to anyone actually struggling with ADHD or organization versus just needing a little help and motivation.

title: Great idea, poor execution
body: I’ve been on Fabulous for about a month, and I am absolutely better for it. I’m building good habits slowly, and I have some confidence that, at least in the short-mid term, they’ll stick. The recorded coachings are wise (at least so far), and I’m a better person for it. However, it’s an app that hasn’t been play-tested enough. For example, it will ask you at night to start each morning saying that “you feel energized and the day is going to be great”. However, your morning task list will have a new addition, and you’ll immediately (that night) be asked “Did you say this morning that you feel energized and that the day is going to be great?” So then you either have to lie to maintain a streak or lose it. That’s just one example. There’s any number of things that expect a simple time sequence that’s impossible to follow. It’s like no one actually tested this and just rushed it out the door. Also, they use impressive animations in the first week (during the time they encourage you to give a rating), always with “to be continued” suggestions. So you think, “wow, that’s a great thing to follow.” Those are replaced after the first week with a single image in the next three weeks, and then that disappears. I get you’re being trained, but a lot of these ratings are probably based in part in that early flash. It’s misleading. And now you’re conditioned to see more good things from the app fade off. I’ve reached out to the company on these and other issues (I care about this program; it could be so much better with proper testing). But no one’s responded weeks later. So there’s that. I think it’s worth a try, it can help. But use a thirty day trial before committing (they seem to be easy to acquire). It’s good enough I’m sticking with it, but I’m waiting for the next thing to disappear.

Simple things I took for granted like drinking water, now seemed to roll off my day with ease. Long story short, I didn’t delete it. In fact, I added to my daily routine and I am down 18 lbs. title: Beware the free trial
body:
TL;DR - I’m out $50 and a couple hours of frustrating effort from a free trial I canceled 5 minutes after I started it.

This app is deliberately difficult to cancel. I installed the app and set up an account with a free 7 day trial. After 5 minutes I knew it was not what I was looking for. So I deleted my account. The message at the end of account deletion said deleting your account doesn’t cancel pending subscriptions. The support page said that since I set up the app on my iPhone I should look in my Apple subscriptions. There was no subscription there. So I figured I was good.

Two weeks later I notice I’ve been charged the subscription fee. Back to the support page. If you can’t find your subscription in Apple subscriptions you might have signed up via the web page (I hadn’t). Just sign in with your account to see your subscription (account is deleted).

Next I look for a way to contact a real support person. Only option is a bot with pre-programmed options. I can’t find a combo of options that will get me to an answer or a real person.

My final last ditch effort: I create another account using the same email address. I am then able to access the subscriptions and cancel. The support bot won’t help me get a refund, so I’m out the $50 annual fee, but here’s hoping I really won’t get charged again next year.

title: Wish this worked for me, not enough personalization
body:
I’ve given this app shot for several months now, and I had also previously tried it out, and I found that while it was somewhat helpful, in the end, it became like more of an added chore than it was helpful. 

I find that it’s not very good at personalizing to your unique needs. For example, the starting habit for everyone is drinking water in the morning and for me I already do that all the time so that felt really boring and uninspiring. It would be more helpful if it perhaps asked you about what habits you already have in place and then helped you build on top of that. 

Also, the ads make it seem as though it gives you some sort of personality test and then adjust your morning routine to fit your personality and or unique needs and it doesn’t do that at all or at least I didn’t see how it could, and maybe that function exist but if it does, it’s difficult to find because I didn’t see it and I was using this app on a daily basis for many months. 

I think this could be great for people who are just starting out on creating habits and who are not neurodivergent. I am ADHD and HSP and I just didn’t find this very helpful for either of those. 

I think this app has great potential, and it could greatly improve by offering a more personalized approach. Perhaps, with the advent of AI, the developers could work on integrating the technology to help a person create a more tailored routine and help a person identify what routine might work for them, they are particular needs, goals and struggles.

title: Things I wish I’d known before buying
body:
I have appreciation for this app, which did help me for some key months in my wellness journey. And I continue to use it occasionally now; the beautiful sounds and pictures really do make a difference in my motivation. The morning routine is something I haven’t been able to replicate on another app. But I wish I had known a few things before investing. Had I known these things I would have tried other apps and not become “addicted” to this one for my morning habits. I much prefer stoic for being a much more ethical app. 

1. Data only goes back a month. This is absolutely crazy to me. I can’t export my data in an easy format to see when and how I’ve fallen off my habits, and that really devalues the app for me. 

2. Daily coachings are a finite bank that repeats; I have been using the app for about 5 months worth of days and have heard them all; every coaching is a repeat now.

3. The UI is beautiful but not terribly functional in certain ways. The challenges are really odd in the way they don’t integrate with the routines part of the app. Also they made a big change where they rebranded a section of the app called Make Me Fabulous but their materials still reference it, which means when it asks you to do a task using resources on the app, it’s often incredibly hard to find the resource, and you have to ask support which brings me to …

4. Getting app support is absolutely infuriating. That seems to be a trend in apps now but on this one, it’s particularly enraging because you are forced to upload a photo in the chat bot - it won’t let you past the bot to an email (no live chat function) unless you do a screen shot. They’ll email back relatively quickly but it is still asynchronous; there’s no way to get immediate phone or chat support; and the email back is usually some really maddening flowery version of “the app doesn’t do that” 

5. Sharing a quote or coaching with friends results in the most annoying advertising ever. And usually it’s hard to find the quote or coaching and not apparent to the recipient what the heck you’re sending them. Other apps don’t do this- I can share a quote without marketing like crazy to my friends. 

6. Similarly, trying to give the 30 day guest pass results in the most annoying behavior science experience ever where they basically have to sign up for the app and put their credit card info in, which I guess ok, fine. But 

7. Motivational voice bug: this is the thing I wrote my first review about and was the beginning of the end of my love affair with Fabulous. Whenever I am on Bluetooth headphone or speaker using a habit that is one of its presets, it intermittently announces cheesy things like “you’re over halfway there.” This is obviously annoying during eg meditations. You can’t turn it off without turning off the music and the other sound effects. The other option is to make up your own habits, but I enjoy the pictures and prompts of the preset habits. So usually I just listen to it on my phone speaker rather than a Bluetooth … this fixes the issue but also annoys everyone around me, like my woo woo music is playing while the kids are trying to get ready for school.

title: HARD PASS

This is just another “go to bed early so you can have a strong start” one size fits all spouter of nonsense. Sorry, but science has proven repeatedly at this point that some people (people with ADHD and similar conditions) don’t even go into deep, restorative sleep until 3-5am, so pushing us to go to bed earlier and get up later is literally asking us to run on LESS QUALITY sleep because it will make us better at (full in the blank). 

This app is a hard pass for me. My morning routine is not where I need help, but no matter what information I put it, it always starts there. Forget it.

I looked online for some resources and discovered this app. I was drawn to the science-based research that provides the foundation for the Fabulous app. For me, I went ahead and tried it. I immediately found the app extremely flexible and easy to tailor and incorporate into my daily life. 

 I knew that I want to enjoy life more, but not sure exactly what steps to take. I get bored quickly with self help books. However, with the Fabulous app, there are many what I call ‘micro-lessons’ on self reflection, health tips, nourishment considerations, journaling, daily joys, mindfulness, self care, meditation, physical tips, and these are easy to read & absorb. The app provides these micro-lessons  with beautiful graphics, sound, animations, fabulous quotes, and is very pleasant to use! I smile often while using the app. I got the annual plan after the trial, and glad I did. 

A couple of huge reasons I like Fabulous: (1) it inspires me to explore more options than my usual thought processes and (2) it encourages me to use my (sometimes quite rusty) imagination! Its a 12 on a scale of 1-10!!!

It is impossible to get support/help. Both the help center and “contact us” links take you to the same bot/gatekeeper that provides useless articles and no way to get past it to an actual human. Any help you find through search engines leads you to a user forum with users giving advice, not actual answers. And, the app, even with the premium subscription, constantly pushes their other apps to you. It’s a giant advertisement for other apps even after you are paying for it. If you ever click on the coaching button you end up in a no-exit questionnaire that closing and reopening the app is the only way out without signing up for coaching. 

I want to love this app so much and will continue to try to use it, but if you are switching from another routine/habit app I’d wait until this new UX they’ve launched is baked. I feel like they launched a half-finished product or update that is designed more as an advertisement than a helpful app.

title: Confusing to navigate and cancel subscription
body: Within a few days of using this app, I realized it wasn’t a good match for me and attempted to cancel my subscription so I would not be charged the annual fee after the 7 day trial period. The cancellation process is confusing and I’m not sure I did it correctly. One of the reasons why I was cancelling was because the app interface is too confusing and overwhelming (I’m neurotypical and very visual) and it was still too much for me). Because my payment information had already been taken through PayPal, I assumed I would be charged. I opened the Fabulous app and tried to log into my settings to cancel my subscription. There is a note that you cannot edit your subscription within the app, but must go on the web to do so. On the web, my options for canceling my subscription included the web, Apple Pay, and Google there was no option to cancel if you had signed up through the app (?). I went through every option and then was told I couldn’t access my settings unless I finished setting up my account. I set up the account and then was prompted to upgrade to premium at this point. I was confused as to whether I would be charged at all so I went to the help chat option, which just routed me back to the original article. I’m still unsure whether I will be charged for the subscription at the end of the seven day trial. I can’t imagine trying to navigate this process if I had ADHD, as others have mentioned. Please consider making this option for canceling your subscription more transparent for the sake of your users.

title: Not enough choice for users.
body:
I like this app, and it has helped me to establish routines and stick to them. 
However, the challenges are a disappointing experience for me. They ask if you are ready for a challenge, but you are given a limited selection to pick from. Why can’t I select one from all the available options? Then you are asked to choose at least 3 methods of accountability to keep you on track. A disproportionate (it seems to me) number of them involve other people. Give someone a sum of money to hold for you as a “bet” that you’ll complete the challenge. Or post about it to instagram. Get a buddy to do it with you or to check in with. Join a group to update everyone every day. They are trying to incorporate an element of public praise or shame to drive you to complete the challenge. I get that this strategy is effective for many people. But many of us, including myself, are introverts who are very private and don’t like to share our personal business with random strangers on the internet, and the opinions of random strangers don’t affect us. There are a couple of accountability methods that are effective for me, but I dislike being required to select 3 methods before I can move on with the challenge. 
Today they asked for feedback on these motivators, and requested that you address them one at a time. After I submitted my input on one of them, I couldn’t get back to that screen. The back button took me back to the Home Screen. 
If there is a menu for questions, concerns, a Contact Us button, I haven’t found it in the weeks I’ve been using this app.
It seems highly structured, and regulated for “most people.” I expected it to be more friendly to neurodivergent users. 
It’s a pretty good app and I plan to continue using it, but I think more individualization would dramatically improve it’s usefulness for ND folks.

title: Incredibly helpful!!
body: Highly recommend this app for self-empowerment to build the life you want.  This app uses behavioral science and educational psychology (akin to Mr. Rogers) to empower to think, behave, and build a life that you feel happy in.  The app includes strategies for learning how to be resilient and anti-fragile (i.e., seeing chaos or difficulties as opportunities to be the best version of yourself).  The app is organized according to journeys.  Each journey guides your thoughts and behaviors, and gives you time to master the lessons and build the life you want in that particular area.  Better yet, the app recognizes that you can only learn so much at one time, so it cycles through essential lessons several times.  This approach truly empowers you to create and manage your own happiness.  The app empowers you to see your own dignity as a human being and your own natural wealth as a human on the earth with the sun, stars, and your own breath of life.  The app enables you to focus on things that are within your circle of control and build contentment there.  In my personal journey, which has some big challenges I had to face, it took about three months to see a substantive change in how I thought, behaved, and felt.  I’m excited about the future and curious to see how I evolve my inner landscape.

body:
I’ve had fabulous for about 2 weeks. On the idea of working with my goals. Process is really slow at the beginning with the foundation of drinking water, breakfast and exercise and your main corner stones. But baby steps right? Hopefully after 3months I drop by with another review. Hopefully the app will help with goals I’ve had I'm mind.

I L O V E the daily coaching. Very insightful and pulling quotes from various sources. With the visuals and actually hearing a soothing recording voice is quite nice. 

Ok so here is my beef with the app. Wish apps and companies would realize that a lot of us don’t have the 9-5 job. I’m a flight attendant and my career takes me all over the globe in different time zones. Sometimes I’m dashing ahead a day and losing another one. Half the reason why I’m downloading apps like this is to find routine in the chaos. Just be aware that not all of us get up at the same time or have a set schedule.

And my big beef with this app is the constant advertising of other apps that fabulous provides. Feel like I’m being force fed content I don’t want. Maybe do a questionnaire before starting process to see where customers needs might fit each app? The advertisement stuff really almost ran me away from my 7free day trial.

title: From depressed to empowered
body:
I’ve paid for the subscription and this is my second year having the app although the first year I hadn’t used it consistently. Once I seen the payment come out again this year I decided instead of deleting it I’d really commit and give it another shot considering I really liked the daily focus coaching and I’ve been declining in progress I had made while using it. 
I can 100% argue that this app is like your own pocket therapist! I’m not one to want to talk through my problems but I have an ear for other perspectives and this app just makes it so easy to organize your thoughts, write like you have an in-app journal, listen to coaching like very short podcasts, and even plan out routines and tasks to really help you execute and feel accomplished! Whoever created the structure knew what they were doing and what they’re audience struggles with. 
Now, I’m not saying this app holds the answers to all our problems but it sure helped me develop an optimistic outlook, more self confidence, emotional stability, and organizational growth that I’d convinced myself I no longer had the willpower to create. I truly love this app and hope that the depressed, lonely, or unmotivated person reading this takes the chance like I did and bet on yourself!
author: Struggling & Broke Student

title: Caution: Subscription Required for Free Trial
body: I recently encountered an unsettling trend with the Fabulous app, which requires users to commit to an annual subscription fee of approximately $40 to access what is marketed as a ‘free’ 7-day trial. This approach seems to rely on the possibility that users may forget to cancel their subscription before the trial period ends, leading to an automatic charge. In my view, this business model is predatory and takes advantage of consumer inattention. I am writing this review to raise awareness among potential users to be vigilant and to encourage them to think twice about supporting such practices. It is essential for apps to earn their revenue fairly without banking on customers’ forgetfulness.

title: Ignore Customer Refund Request within 48 hours. Blame customer. No refund.
body:
This review is for Customer Service. STILL DO NOT HAVE MY REFUND. I was charged $39.99 unexpectedly on 9/12/23 for a subscription renewal. I immediately checked my iPhone subscriptions and it did not show up, so I went onto the website and started a chat with support. The chat was helpful and said that because it was WITHIN 48 HOURS of the renewal, I could receive a refund. Chat confirmed that I would receive a email with the support ticket. I proceeded to cancel my subscription and never received that support ticket/refund email after the chat. After waiting a few few weeks I went through the SAME PROCESS again with Chat. This time, they DID send me an email, but said “because it is not within the 48 hour period, I do not qualify for a refund.” I explained what had happened (that I DID cancel within 48 hours, but they didn’t send me the follow up email). After long waiting periods in between emails, Alicia from Customer Service continued to state that I cannot get a refund. She continued to completely disregard my explanation of what happened. I have been so patient and now I’m angry. I explained to support several times in a very kind manner what happened and they clearly don’t believe me. Why would I take all this time and energy to try to get $39.99 and make up the fact that I had a full Chat Conversation on 9/13? The general rule of customer service is to listen to the customer. It is Fabulous’ problem that somehow their chat didn’t send the email and open the ticket. I had the conversation with your chat “bot” or “person” or whatever and waited PATIENTLY for the follow up email that I was promised. 

I have not used Fabulous once in the last 8 months and I tried to cancel WITHIN the first 48 hours and was told I was going to get an email about the refund. Fabulous did NOT send me that email. In ADDITION, my subscription did NOT show up in my iPhone b/c I did it through the website, so it was DECEIVING b/c it showed on my iPhone subscriptions that I didn’t have a subscription. 

I rarely do reviews because I’m a very busy mom and work full time. All I want is the $39.99 refund because it was UNJUSTLY charged and I did due diligence to resolve the issue.

I really enjoyed the app as I said before, but I didn’t have time for one more thing on my phone as I said. Now, this has completely ruined any chance of me referring anyone to it or trying it again, plus my time has been completely wasted, my energy, and you’ve now got a 1-star review.

title: Exactly what I hoped it would be!
body:
I’m a chronic procrastinator and have a very poor routine. I downloaded this app a couple weeks ago and I really enjoy it! The graphics are beautiful and happy, the voices and music are soothing and lovely, but the coaching and learning aspect of it are the best! It’s very educational and it really makes the process feel like a joyful journey and it includes cute stories that make you want to come back the next day and complete tasks to hear the next one. They include life lessons in them and seem to be a portrayal of yourself. I also appreciate that it takes the decision making out of it for me. The journey is completely guided and it adds habits one at a time that are universally beneficial. But there is also an option to add your own habits. I’m excited to see where continued use of this app gets me, but I’m having fun so far and would recommend trying it! Really commit for a week! What do you have to lose? 
Also, it gave me a deal after the free trial for one year for just about $17! Totally worth it if it works!

title: So needed in my life
body:
It’s been years since I found an app I really appreciate. This app is having more impact on my life than any counselor I’ve ever had.

Somewhere along my path I began a negative self-talk that I allowed to define me. It became so present in my life, I accepted it as my “emotional home”. I’m more valuable than that. Would I give a loved-one constant doses of discouraging feedback? Of course not. Am I a loved one? ABSOLUTELY! My work is to allow that to become my new emotional home. I need to be my own biggest fan.

This app does so much to open my eyes in a way that will build habits. It’s going at an unfamiliarity slower pace, with an unfamiliar consistency of tiny habit changes.  Adding small steps on top of existing steps allows the existing steps to become my new “normal”. THATS real change. I’m so happy I found this app.

title: If you want to just give personal info and be handled
body:
The interface on the screen looked fine. But as soon as you open up to try the app it starts with a series of questions. Which isn’t the worst idea. Before you even understand what is going on with the app, you’re forced to put in your email. Then it comes up with some weird contract and tells you to sign and commit to it.

‘Always remember you won’t live forever.’ That’s your worldview, not mine, and I’m not committing to it. I’m Christian, as a born again believer I will live forever, I won’t suffer the second death. It’s a truth I hold near and dear and live by and would love to share with other people. But I would say please make it clearer it’s not for those who hold other worldviews differing than your own. Or better yet, give a person the autonomy to write their own commitment statement. I unfortunately can’t get past the onboarding process to even test the other app features, without compromising my my beliefs and values.

title: This app is Beautiful, Gracious, Thoughtful, and Supportive
body:
*When* I commit, this app keeps my life on track. That being said, I (probably like many users) am not neurotypical, and I really struggle with basic routines, meeting my basic physical needs, and living an organized life. I don’t just use this app for things like “do yoga” or “meditate;” I also need to add things like “shower,” “brush teeth,” and “drink water.” It may seem silly to some, but I’m sure there are those out there that understand what it’s like to not naturally do those things on a daily basis.
I have jumped in and fallen off of this app again and again, and I think they do a very nice job of sending considerate notifications, phrasing their challenges and alerts in a creative and welcoming way, and while I know I will fail again and again, I appreciate the thoughtful UX they have curated. I also love what I know of the company, and that’s so important to me when selecting services. It seems to be an international, remote working environment with good values and a diverse team of creative designers, writers, engineers, and business professionals of other kinds. I don’t know what it’s like behind the scenes, but they *seem* to uphold their app values internally within the company, and I respect that! Thank you for creating such a lovely app that has gotten me back on track again and again.

It is quite possible I’m not using it correctly, but then that means that my first feedback is that it isn’t very intuitive to use. The main landing page is crowded and I feel my goals and habits get lost in all the other options. I wish the design was cleaner and made it easier to focus on my current habit development. A few times (like this morning) the app has a special announcement for me and it is to “introduce” the idea of habit building….again, focusing on a habit I’ve been doing for 12 days (drinking water in the morning). I’m going to keep using it and hope it gets more helpful because I already paid for the year. I hope the developers will continue to make improvements. The graphics are lovely, it just needs some work for usability.

Writing this review has been the most complicated part lol.

To expand on the above points, the interface of this platform is designed in such a way that it seamlessly delivers information without bombarding the user with excessive details. Whether you are a tech-savvy individual or someone who prefers a simpler approach, navigating through the platform is a breeze.

One of the standout features is the compatibility with screen readers, making it accessible for visually impaired users. This inclusive design ensures that everyone can benefit from the valuable content available on the platform, regardless of their disability.

Moreover, the platform's efficiency is commendable. It allows users to swiftly accomplish their daily goals without any unnecessary hassle or complexity. The user-friendly layout and intuitive controls make it a pleasure to use, saving you precious time and effort.

Now, let's talk about writing this review. Despite the platform's ease of use, expressing my thoughts about it has unexpectedly proven to be the most complicated part. Not because of any shortcomings on the platform's side, but rather due to the sheer excellence and seamlessness it offers.

It has helped me through clinical depression and it has helped me with simply a bad day/week/month. TLDR: i’ve used a million habit forming apps, but this one is the best due to the creative storyline, engaging art and sounds, gentle consistent reminders, automatic daily goal suggestions and supporting SMALL STEPS!! It has lasting impacts I’ve remembered for years after and always return when I need a boost.

title: Second time using premium, first time purchasing lifetime
body: I enjoy this app, immensely. It helped me when I was at my lowest (depression/suicidal ideation/ eating disorder) and now it’s helping me at my highest. If it weren’t for this app, I wouldn’t have gotten out of the house to go in walks, found gratitude in even the smallest blessings, and kept what was important at the forefront of my mind when I was in my darkest chapter of life. I don’t believe this app single-handedly saved me from suicide but it definitely played a part in my healing journey. It made my unimaginably hard tasks at the time (such as drinking water or brushing my teeth) simple and made them felt like reachable, fun, meaningful goals. Now, I use this app to push myself closer to success rather than doing the bare minimum. It’s customizable and it can work for anyone at any point in life. Highly recommend the premium or lifetime version. I accidentally purchased the lifetime version but I’m not even mad about it because it has helped me so much and I am excited to have it forever.

title: Love the idea, bugs are annoying, billing is predatory
body:
Lots to love in this app. It’s thoughtfully created and beautifully executed. Meets a lot of my needs that I was previously tracking myself in other ways. The bugs are obstacles. Listening to the coaching sessions never works smoothly. It pauses and I have to restart many times ruining the flow of my concentration. It prompts me to start and restart challenges that I’ve already been doing. It asks me to fill in weekly reflections that I’ve already filled it. It has my correct name, yet in the profile display it changed an “a” to an “o” and there’s no way for me to change that.

Update: the billing issues, wow. The free trial went into a subscription although I thought I cancelled it. The subscription does not show up under my apple subscriptions, not even under “inactive,” so there’s no way to know you’re subscribed even if you regularly audit your subscriptions. Digging into my account in the app to try to cancel took a while. When I finally got to the button to try to cancel, it says you must cancel on the web, but does not include their website, and searching for a fabulous app website provided no results. I’ve had to go back and forth emailing and dispute the charge with my bank. So, all in all, a drop in mental health rather than an improvement. Like I originally said, I like the idea. The execution could be better. The billing is predatory.

I’ve been bounced around Fabulous support for weeks trying different things to fix it, have deleted and reinstalled the app a dozen times on my new device and nothing works. I have not heard ANYTHING from support in five days now. Again, I can’t even restart or access any content in the three journeys I already engaged with on my old device—I can click on them but they won’t load in the app and I can’t see any of their content. I’m so disappointed that I prepaid for Premium for a year as I have basically been completely unable to use Premium content for over two weeks now and the services don’t work as advertised. title: Not free - Bait and switch
body:
I wish Apple would somehow flag apps like this. There is a difference between apps that are free but then offer premium subscriptions or additional content for a price, and apps that are “free” but you get no content until you agree to a subscription. Just tell us this is a paid app in the App Store. This is so dishonest. It is designed to trick people into signing up for something without telling them the cost up front.  You get them to agree to paying a subscription in the fine print prior to telling them the cost.  The cost should always be front and center before agreeing to terms and conditions.  “Legal” but not transparent and clear up front. 

P.S. I did not agree to terms and conditions, but judging from a plethora of other reviews, it appears the company doesn’t always honor the “free” trial either. Apple should revoke editor’s choice designation based on that alone.

I was given access to a 14-day free trial, but was charged for a subscription after only 7 days. I’ve canceled my subscription and have requested a refund.

I can see how this would be great for some people. My ADHD is not helped by this app, however. It’s great for setting up habits, and allows you to customize. But my basic habits, such as drinking water upon waking, taking vitamins, etc are set. It also includes threads to chat with community members, which is one of my time-sucking poor habits that I have to avoid.

title: Too many glitches + nonexistent customer support
body:
I came upon this app when I was searching for a mood tracking app.

There is a lot that I like about it.  I like the extensive list of habits you can choose from and that it encourages you to go slowly. I like the short daily coaching sessions. 

I used this app for about a month and enjoyed it for the most part except I noticed that it would glitch frequently. I couldn’t go back retroactively and log habits that I had completed, which would affect my progress.

I finally got so frustrated I deleted the app. I then realized a week later that I might as well keep using it because I had paid for a year. I reinstalled the app and could not get back into my account. The app wanted me to provide my email address and password associated with the account, but I had never created a password originally. I attempted to reset the password several times and have yet to receive a link to do so. 

I have reached out to Fabulous support multiple times over the past couple of weeks to resolve this issue and have heard back from no one.

I am frustrated and disappointed, and will attempt to get a refund unless someone from the Fabulous team can help me get back into my account. Resolution should be simple, yet with the lack of response whether through automatically generated links or actual human presence, it appears impossible.

title: Looking forward to the future
body:
I’ve been looking for an app to help curb and establish habits and a more healthy life style and this one has been wonderful so far! I appreciate the 7-day trial, though I wish it could be longer, maybe 21 days since they say that it takes 21-days to form a habit, and especially given the fact that a guest pass is equivalent to 30 days. If you’re referring people, it feels like your being slightly cheated. That’s my only reason for giving a 4 not 5 star review. 

I thoroughly enjoy the small coaching snippets and the encouragement to trek slowly into your new “journey”. The illustrations are bright and colorful which I absolutely adore, especially the info graph-like pictures on the “Circles” posts, and the voice overs for the coaching are fantastic along with the choice of music to match the routines and animations. I also like the Circles feed and how you can make pledges to help keep yourself accountable.

Since I’ve been digging for a while, I do think that $40 is reasonable for a year’s worth of service, though I don’t necessarily think it will be worth it for the Shape app, but I haven’t explored that app as much as Fabulous.

Regardless, I am curious to move along the journey to see what unfolds with Fabulous.

title: Worth The Time AND Money
body:
I knew the journey would take time, which is why I decided to use it for a while before reviewing. I encourage others to do the same as well!

I have been using this app for about a year. Even though I still have trouble maintaining routines, I have been doing MUCH better with my productivity and mental health. This app helps you exercise patience in yourself. It doesn’t force you to do anything or make you feel bad if you fail to do something. It’ll encourage you to try again at YOUR pace.

If the money makes anyone skeptical, I personally believe that this app is SO much more than some easy cash grab. The resources on here are plentiful and clearly full of love from the artists, developers, and researchers involved. Even though I don’t use all of the features all the time, I believe that my money is well spent if they go toward these lovely people, who work hard to put beautiful messages into inspiring visuals. 

Another thing I enjoy are the “circles”. The fabulous community are FULL of different people who are going through different things. I definitely encourage interacting with this feature and reading about other’s journeys, because you will not only see the successes but also the failures. Everyone is non-judgemental and encourages eachother to keep trying.

title: This App proved me wrong
body:

As a full time student (online) I have very little structure which has me absolutely flailing and never getting anywhere. I’ve built 2 habits, I don’t even need the app to remind me, I wake up, drink water, listen to my morning coaching session, and start my day. I feel so much more confident that I can start to live the life I’ve wanted. I can only imagine where I’ll be in a year! 
If cost is a concern for you, it was for me too, but it’s only $40 a year, but if you break it down, that’s .11 cents a day. There is a higher cost if you choose to do the live coaching, as there should be, someday that will be part of my budget, but for now it’s a reward I’m working towards. 
I absolutely recommend this App if you struggle with making new habits and shout to Ky, thank you so much for the recommendation 🥰

If you are interested in having support around a specific goal or want to sharpen the life-skills/habits you have already developed - I suggest giving fabulous a try. If cost is an initial friction point for you...I suggest considering that the business model is, ostensibly, designed for sustainability and longevity.

title: Very Motivational
body:
I typically don’t write reviews, but I have been really appreciating this app, so I wanted to leave something here for people on the fence about trying it.

Fabulous is a really motivational and beautiful app. I have struggled with trying to make life changes to become a healthier human being, but this app seems to really be helping.

The goal of Fabulous is to help you understand that it’s the little things that will help you achieve big things. That the little environmental things you do to make it easy for you to do the actions you want to do are the things that really help you to be successful.

It does this through audio and visual motivational messages, giving you spaces to track your progress, congratulating you on each success - big or small. It is all visually beautiful and the messages are really crafted to feel like it is for you. I also like the little messages we can write to our future selves, reminding us, in a way, to be kind to them and love them.

I’ve only been using this for 5 days, but, all in all, I think it’s wonderful and I am planning to continue to stick with it. I’m already feeling more positive and optimistic about what I will achieve.

If you’re on the fence, just try it!

title: Disguised Diet App
body: I downloaded this because I have trouble focusing & getting important things done. When you open the app for the first time, there’s a little assessment to figure out what kind of coaching you need. If it’s physical health, sleep, productivity, etc etc. I said mine was productivity. My first daily goal was to drink water in the morning, okay easy enough. A simple task to start. Then they added on eating a healthy breakfast every day. Okay, I guess sometimes I skip breakfast so it’s nice to have a reminder. Then it’s telling me to go to the grocery store and buy fruits and oatmeal. Then to throw away any candy I have in my house. Then to work out every day. Like we’ve completely lost the plot, I’m not struggling with my weight or physical activity at all. And I’m not taking diet advice from anyone who’s not literally a licensed dietician who has consulted with me and learned about my specific personal needs. It’s a bummer because I was really hoping fabulous could help me.

title: Confusing, Very Poor UI
body: I’ve been trying to use this app for a few weeks now with the premium trial, and while I like some of the aspects of the challenges and coaching, the user experience is really lacking. I cannot figure out how to properly track what I am actually working on, whether it’s a “journey” or a “challenge” or just the daily tasks. The home page is way too busy. The “journeys” are not well explained which makes it hard to see the impact. Interactions also change dramatically based on what you are doing and I’ve marked off goals as completed without understanding what the goal has actually asked me to do. It’s to the point of the app being so difficult to navigate that I have accidentally deselected the “journey” I’d started on and I cannot for the life of me figure out how to get back to it, despite the app making it seem very easy to pick up on things where you left off. I may be missing something as I am not the most savvy with different UI’s, however I really feel if the point of your app is to help people creating lasting behavior change, it should be very streamlined and not just one more over-complicated “tool.” I’m not going to give up on it entirely yet, but I’ve definitely been more frustrated with this experience than I would have liked to be.

title: Plagiarized!
body: I have found myself downloading this app and wondering why I haven’t used it before several times… and then I remember the glaring issue that stares me in the face despite the fact that I want to love it - the artwork is plagiarized. For anyone who has played Monument Valley, it is extremely clear that this app was heavily “inspired” by that game’s unique and highly recognizable style. While I like the idea of a habit tracker designed with behavioral science, I do not support plagiarism and taking credit for a design you did not create. What’s more, there was an article written about this issue in 2019, and no clear action has been taken in four years. You would think that even if one’s initial intentions were pure, one would reconsider continuing to use a morally dubious design after learning of such an issue. Disappointed.

I realize due to my physical health, my mental health is beginning to go downhill, so I was looking for apps like any other person. title: Motivation or Long Scam?
body:
I have really mixed feelings about this app. The purpose is a good one. I definitely need something like this that would pull together all my efforts toward mental health (dealing with ptsd, chronic depression, anger issues, and some types of anxiety, oh, and some slight [?] substance abuse. oh, and suicidality. oh and...), integrate them, and guide me forward. But. I started the one week trial this morning using an Apple subscription I can cancel through Settings. Right away, it seemed very lock-step under the guise of slowly building the better me. I already drink water every morning, but I have to complete that task for three mornings before I can step up. Ugh.

Worse, a few screens in, I was asked to make suggestions with a survey that went on and on till I just closed the app. Then I got a "friendly" email suggesting that I should get Premium and enjoy all the great features when I haven't had a chance to look at the basic ones (because of that lock-step feature I mentioned). Right...I mean *right* after I got another email suggesting I should use a free month coupon, but I would have to supply a credit card number AND  use a different way of cancelling. Doing that, if I'm disappointed, and I'm now anticipating I will be, I will have to remember to cancel in both places. It's tough enough to remember and figure out one.

Maybe they're just super enthusiastic about helping me. Like, toxically enthusiastic. But not long after my bug trauma, I made a similarly enthusiastic "friend", who was affirming and helpful in small ways...until he offered to house/dog sit for a few days and proceeded to steal various high value things and some checks from way down in my spare checks box. So, their constant messages feel a lot like they're going to ask me to help them fly over from Nigeria so we can finally meet.

Oh, and in the time I've been writing this, they've hit me up twice more!

So...I'll drink my three glasses of water and see how I feel then. But I'm only going to have one subscription to cancel when I do.

title: Not So Fabulous
body: I regret everything about this app. I don’t like leaving negative reviews, but Fabulous is unfortunately the worst app subscription experience I’ve ever had. I liked it for the first week and hoped it would help improve my routine, so shame on me- I got a year long premium subscription. A month or two in, the daily notifications were more irritating than helpful and the voice overs for the lessons and meditations were so cringey or cheesy I couldn’t focus on the material. I cancelled auto renewal for the premium membership. Fast forward a year, and I was getting notifications that my premium account was about to expire. Great, it seems to be working. It now appears as expired in my Apple subscriptions. However, I added a new card to my Apple wallet a few days later and that card was charged for a premium subscription to Fabulous! They make you jump through too many hoops to issue a refund. I was redirected to so many different web pages, all of them dead ends. It ended with a long back and forth with the website chat bot, it saying that they’ll send me an email to continue the conversation, and surprise- days later and still no email. 🤦‍♀️ And that’s not even the half of it. I’m reeeeeally disappointed in how this app is managed. If it works for you, save your money and stick with the free version. It’ll spare you any stress better than a paid Fabulous exercise will.

title: Not Great for my ADHD/Executive Dysfunction
body:
I originally got this app based on a recommendation I saw online, and I sprung for the bundle with a personalized plan because I thought maybe I would get something really unique out of the experience I’d it was tailored to my interests.

The interface is extremely, paralyzingly busy and not intuitive at all, which made it stressful for me to interact with it. Oftentimes the letters and daily coaching were distracting and hard to navigate out of, and I never could figure out why I would want to “play” a morning habit versus just check off tasks.

Worst for me was that if I broke my streak for a day, the timer restarted. So I used the app for 3 weeks and barely got anything done because until you build a “successful habit” it just keeps you in place. I’m ashamed that I didn’t spend more time researching the app before I paid for the personalized plan because that’s wasted money, as the app offers me no real incentive to keep using it and the whole plan is basically useless to me if I can’t keep a streak going.

Other apps with minimalist interfaces, no consequences for streak-breaking, and gamification regardless of streaks have helped me way more.

title: Mostly Good
body:
Of all the habit tracking apps, so far, I like this one the most. The daily coaching is inspiring. It allows you to go at your own pace, and falling short of your goals doesn’t feel as discouraging as it used to. I also like that it addresses emotions and uses reasoning to help me overcome my apprehension and makes me aware that it’s not that I can’t do things, it’s just a challenge to get them done.

I only have two complaints:

One, it doesn’t allow you to account for onetime events, like becoming sick or going on vacation, where you can’t complete all of your activities. For example, after getting sick, it’s extra-hard to get back into a routine, and knowing I lost my streak makes it harder to establish one up again because any streak is just a “few days away from starting over.”

Two, it doesn’t give you “optional time period” habits. My goal may be to exercise three times a week to start up with, but my schedule may not afford the same time each week. I want to be able to set a goal with a week-to-week deadline, but not a set time. 

Other than that I love the app, and hope it keeps evolving!

title: Why I changed my 5 star review to 1 star
body: Fabulous sold me a lifetime membership and failed to deliver. Though Fabulous charged me more than $250, the app subscription is listed as inactive. When I contacted Fabulous support, they referred me to Apple. Apple said all it could do is issue a refund. In other words, Fabulous was not fabulous. It did not make good on its lifetime membership promise. It showed ZERO interest in getting to the bottom of the bug that led to the problem. I was willing to put up with its at times confusing UX and with being asked incessantly to share progress publicly — when I prefer to keep that private. It repeatedly requests that I refer others, which I did already. It shouldn’t attempt to force me to get accountability partners. Again, there isn’t a way to tell the app that is not applicable. The people in my life aren't equipped to do that. There should be a way to opt out of those annoyances. But treating a lifetime member poorly — failing to deliver on its promised life time membership — that’s just wrong. It is a betrayal of my trust.

title: Scam
body:
I really wanted to like this app but I’m scared that I just fell into some scam. Read the 1-star reviews and believe it. I read reviews AFTER I provided my credit card and got charged a dollar. Sure no big deal other than that they didn’t say anything about it (Red flag #1). 

Red flag #2: right after I provided my card, they proceed to sell me a premium prescription for “One time price of $49! Original price is $200. Save 75%!” 

 Red flag #3: I receive an email about a 30-day pass and asks for my credit card again. 

Red flag #4: no in-app subscription. Why? Obviously to make it harder for you to cancel. 

Red flag #5: not transparent about pricing. They hide it, make it hard for you to look for it in an obvious attempt for you to quit looking for it. 

They are VERY loud about getting your credit card, getting you to buy more things, and getting you to advertise to your friends for some discount. On. The. First. Day. Scam.

title: DO NOT SUBSCRIBE - CHARGED 14 TIMES FOR ANNUAL SUBSCRIPTION
body:
I subscribed to this app for 1 year and it was set to expire on January 21st (because I cancelled in advance). I received the email confirming it was expired. Fabulous charged me for a year on the 21st anyway. Then charged me for the annual membership two more times on January 27th. Today is February 15th and they have tried charging me 11 more times. My card issuer flagged it for fraud, but they keep having to close my account with every charge but can’t block the charges - may have to close the account completely.

I reached out to Fabulous support three times before I got a response saying that there’s nothing they can do and that my subscription will expire in 2024. I provided screenshots and have not received a response.

tldr; app made to better your well-being ends up destroying it. (Dramatic, I know. All payment issues aside, it’s not that great of an app anyway. Read a self-care book, spend time outside, lean into your supportive relationships, habit stack, build a gratitude practice - I believe in you)

title: Busy Design/Aggressive messaging
body:
I love the concept and I think they are definitely on the right track but it’s just not there yet. My hope is that data aggregation  on existing customers will help improve the experience. Where do customers drop-off? Why aren’t they subscribing? Are there to many push notifications causing customers to turn-off? 

For me the app is to busy and their messaging has to much content. I understand the need for a subscription model but wonder about the apps approach. I don’t like how the trial period is structured and feel a no card on file option would allow customers to see what they are missing, “to look around”

In the end experience simplification is desperately needed. The Home Screen cards appear busy and the amount of text content combined with colors is not easy to digest. The “afternoon” mustard yellow is definitely not a pleasing color, I would limit color pallet and reduce the amount of color fading on buttons etc… all together it just adds to the apps busy feel.

Final thoughts, the apps core concept is excellent but not in a state that makes me want to subscribe  at such a high price.

title: La mejor
body: Honestamente una de las mejores aplicaciones y en tu idioma. Sufro de trastorno de ansiedad, y depresión. Casado con 3 hermosas hijas, y una hermosa esposa, pero lamentablemente  deje de hacer todo lo que me gusta por la ansiedad. Deje que tomara control de mi. Fue el peor error, ahora recibo ayuda Psicológica, y Psiquiátrica por que estaba apunto del divorcio. A lo que voy cuando entro un día que estaba súper enojado, así es mi ansiedad me da mucho coraje. Estaba en Apple la App Store, buscaba algo que me ayudara a mi a salir de mi méseria. Tomar el control Otra  vez y hacer lo que me gusta. Encuentro esta App, le doy la oportunidad y mira lo que son las cosas, poco a poco estoy volviendo a la normalidad. Se los recomiendo y está en varios idiomas que es la mejor parte. Cuando miro que está a mi idioma el español dije carajo tengo que darle una oportunidad a esto. Mi psicóloga ya me había dicho, que buscara algo cómo está aplicación. Las primeras Semanas va hacer difícil, pero saben que es todo fuerza de voluntad. Ahora empiezo a leer poco a poco. Empieza de poco a poquito. No se te vaya ocurrir hacer todo en una semana que no podrás y tú ansiedad será peor. Yo empecé con la ayuda de fabulous primero dos cosas a la vez. Ya cuando mi mente fue aceptando esto ahora como sin nada me levanto y vuelvo poco a poco a la normalidad. Ahora dijo que soy como un bebé que apenas empieza a caminar. Señores/as, jóvenes. Si ustedes pasan por ansiedad, no dejen que la ansiedad los controle, mi ansiedad me controlo por mas de 20 años ya no hay vuelta atrás, ya el pasado está atrás. Pero ustedes si son jóvenes busquen ayuda profesional y dense una oportunidad con esta aplicación y verán el cambio. Tenemos en nuestra mano un teléfono inteligente donde podemos hacer un montón de cosas con el. Pero lamentablemente muchos no queremos buscar más, por el simple hecho de que queremos olvidarnos con las redes sociales y perder el tiempo ahí. Jóvenes tengo 38 años no estoy tan viejo pero ustedes saben 20 años a no salir casi por la ansiedad. No dejen que la ansiedad los controle. Nosotros somos más fuerte que la ansiedad. Gracias Fabulous

title: I’m not the priority - they are
body:
I honestly have tried to use this app, really gave it a shot several times after I paid $40 for a year subscription, revisiting it after I had to stop using it multiple times.  It has made me that frustrated to try and tackle goals and changing my daily habits into more productive ones.  

I will say that hearing or reading an uplifting antidote, one of the features of this app that I’ve not come across in others outside of meditation apps, felt like a more palpable pep talk than practicing daily affirmations or reading an online article - a positive for sure.  That they were geared to helping me and encouraging me is what enticed me to buy into this app after the too short one week trial period was up (this should have been the red flag for me).  

To say there’s a learning curve to understand their interface is an understatement but also - it does nothing to bolster why I got the app to begin with.  I get it.  When we put a product out there we want to be different.  We want to stand out.  But if navigating around an app is harder than getting out of the woods without a compass and map - there’s a problem.  

It was never obvious / clear cut where my routines (that I had created and put a lot of time and personal thought into) were located.  The fact that the interface doesn’t give me a tab dedicated to *my* agenda / goals / habits / routine in order to let me clearly see the routine and challenges I’ve taken on and land on them immediately every day was annoying at best.  Instead, I have to scroll past what you guys deem more important for me to see before I can get to my routine to start my day (coaching you want me to buy into, challenge recommendations - as though that’s going to help me in the current ones is to take on more, and some other app recommendation you want me to buy).  It makes no sense whatsoever and is 100% counter-productive.  If I buy a calendar app to keep track of the hectic days I have and loaded schedule and you insert right in the middle of my daily schedule your addenda of me using other parts of your app and trying to get me to buy into calendar coaching as well as some other app you’ve made - even *after* I paid $40 for a years’ subscription - who is wanting me to fail at this point instead of succeed??  

It’s been completely frustrating to say the very least and left me wishing I had spent my money on a notebook and pen and taken myself out to dinner.  As a single mom who has so many things to juggle and keep track of and things that constantly overwhelm me, I needed an app to encourage me and help me stay on track.  Instead, I paid $40 for an app to try and get me to buy more by cluttering the screen and keeping me from using the app for its intended purpose.  I don’t have $40 to spend or to waste, but I took a leap and on a whim I thought I’d ‘spoil’ myself and spend money on me - after all, it was supposed to help me so maybe I didn’t have to feel so guilty spending the money.  Disappointing that my success is not their priority.  That doesn’t sound fabulous, does it.
