title: Can’t Say God
body:
I appreciate all the great features this app has to offer. I also appreciate the fact that many of those features are offered in a free version for people who may not have it in their budget to splurge on the premium version. There are lots of choices for not only areas for life improvement, but also tools to help you improve. The common challenges you offer are great and so are the community groups. Sometimes it takes a village and it definitely shows that you have that figured out. Kudos to you for a well thought out app. I only currently use the free version so I cannot speak to the full features the app has to offer, but so far I am impressed. 

The only area that I recommend a change would be in your community groups. I definitely understand that there are trolls out there who like to cause issues and stir the pot anywhere they can. That being said, I tried to post this in one of the health and fitness groups:

Can’t wait to feel better this year with a new and improved healthy outlook on life. I know through prayer and God’s help I will be successful. The better I feel and the healthier I am, the more I can do for God’s Kingdoms. That in and of itself is enough. “ 

This was the pop up message I received in response:  “Oops! Your post contains words or phrases that we don’t allow. We strive to build safe, meaningful communities. Please modify your post if you’d like to share it.”

The only way I could share my post was to remove the word God. Many people rely heavily on God to get through their problems. I also realize that some don’t. However, if there is the ability to post in a community to help each other then we should be able to post what has helped us. I understand the need to filter out derogatory language and hate speech. A community group is no place for vulgarity. However, if God is a source of strength we should be able to share that. Maybe have an option to report a post if they get out of hand. I would consider an annual purchase because I truly do like the app, but not being able to share that I have God as a source of strength would keep me from purchasing. 

Again, I think the app is great, but eliminating the ability to say God keeps me from a purchase and a higher rating.

title: Annoying and Shaming
body:
I did ok at first with building a morning routine. Something I didn’t like was that I couldn’t avoid exercise as a routine option. I am not a morning workout person so I hated that the app wouldn’t let me edit my goal to do something else. I also knew I wouldn’t be able to achieve that on days I commute so it felt like a setup for failure. Maybe you can edit in the premium version but I didn’t want to buy it yet since I was new to it. 

Then I got sick and didn’t use the app for about two weeks and when I first opened the app it asked a number of questions of why I “fell off” my journey and all the reasons are about being overwhelmed or losing motivation which are valid but not applicable in my situation. Why is there no option for a life event or being physically sick or being on vacation? Or anything to cover out of ordinary things but nothing to do with mental health? and actually prioritizing rest when sick or on vacation are very good for mental health. I hated that it hinted that it was my lack of motivation or my attitude when that wasn’t the case. It seems to bully you when you miss a day with toxic positivity and I find that irritating and unrealistic.

title: Fabulous
body: I decided to name the review after the name of the app. After receiving life coach training some years back, I have struggled with the new skill set and how I could apply everything and start coaching almost immediately. I told myself I was ready, but had no real niche or clients. I still do not know if coaching will bear fruit, but this app has helped me see the fallacy in my approach. To truly effect change, but more importantly the path to a future is to take one small step. Based on whatever goal I choose to move toward, I must break that goal into bite size chunks. Repeat them, celebrate and before one knows it they will have come to see the change they want. Additional this app has coaching moment, which for are gentle reminders to slow down, breathe and catch hold of your emotions. It reminds me that we all have choices and that choice is ours and ours alone. The app’s reminder to be positive in your thinking and choices helps me frame my day, which has made the last three days very good days! This app is Fabulous!

title: Not sure what I’m paying for
body:
First, the screenshots you are seeing are not representative of the app’s interface or even art style. There are a couple of art styles used, but this doesn’t look anything like the actual app and I can guess why. You will too. 
Because the UX is a mess. I have no idea why I paid for this app, because I don’t see what I’m getting. Other than constant nagging to pay more for personal coaching. 
And then there are the bugs. I’m now half an hour off track on my morning because the very first thing I did broke the app and I had to record a video to file a bug. That’s not helpful. 
I have asked the developer a few times for help, but they seem unwilling to listen to feedback and instead keep adding bugs. Since I started using this app almost a year ago, I quit using it a few months ago because it was just awful. The challenges are nonsensical in many cases, it’s definitely not set up for home workers, and toss in bugs that make it impossible to do things, and the app could actually be harmful to your health. Another unregulated cash grab.

title: I really wanted to like this
body:
I really wanted to like this app. I truly did, and I really wanted to make it work.

The first habit it wanted me to establish was drinking water in the morning. Fine, whatever, not something I really needed help with but I did it. The second one was breakfast, and that's where I checked out. I've struggled for years with my weight, and last year I stumbled upon intermittent fasting. Eating one meal a day has helped me lose 60 lbs, and I'm still going. Now this app is forcing me to eat breakfast? And throw the only diet that's ever worked for me? And there's no way to skip this particular goal and move onto the next one? No thanks.

This app has a number of flaws that made it really not work for me. Beyond the lack of customizability, the cheesy self-help language made me check out. There's also a lot of potential for triggering issues for people (like my breakfast issue) that the app doesn't let you skip. I have firm routines set in my life, but I wanted something to add a few good habits of my choice. If you're somebody who's a hot mess, this might be the app for you. If you've already got your act more or less together, there's probably something out there with more customizability and less hand-holding that would probably suit your needs better.

I’m giving it 4 stars because I know they’re still working on the user interface. It can be a little confusing as to which lesson you’re on, what’s next, and what you should be doing today. This is a solid partner for change in your life if you give it a chance.

title: Amazing!!! but…
body:
I love fabulous, one of my favorite ways to complete my morning routine and get me into my habits.

I just don’t like the fact that after paying (and telling me that I have access to almost every thing) they eventually are trying to upsell me to premium on small things I was enjoying before hand. 
I was using the different noises for meditation and reading, but now you need premium?? 

If you’re gonna add a premium, only apply it to new subscribers because delivering something that you take away later is worth a refund. Also add different levels of payments, I was only offered to pay for regular membership in the beginning, and didn’t even know premium existed.
All these features I now cannot use and I have to pay extra for them.
App had anticipation effect. Gave me what I wanted and later showed me there’s more to it and now I’m upset because I thought these things should already come with a regular subscription.
Should use the surprise effect in your app, over deliver on what you said you were going to bring for these subscribers. And to have plenty more from which you offered initially. Increases dopamine substantially and you will have more people on your app.
 
Was good before. Is okay now

title: Only three days in so far but definitely worth it
body: I have a few mental issues that unfortunately often keep me from living the balanced life I want. And yes it has only been three days but for me it’s closer to being like a couple of weeks. Not only have I finally been able to slow down enough to start taking steps to improving my health with this app I’ve also seen that I’m not alone in the feeling. I enjoy the quotes and community portion along with the way the app breaks down what’s important in a gentle and informative way. Plus the soothing sounds, the beautiful colors and artwork, and also the almost game like features really appeal to my inner child making it feel less like work and more like a fun learning game that keeps me coming back and actually getting excited about caring for myself again. In fact just the satisfaction from the ding sound that plays when I drink water has actually increased my water intake from about 8oz daily to closer to a liter daily and I’ve been feeling way more energetic and patient even with it being such a short time. I don’t know why I procrastinated so long on just caring for my basic needs but if I knew it could be this easy and fun I’d have done it years ago. I’m not sure how this journey will continue or where it’ll take me but I’m honestly feeling pretty optimistic about it. If you are unsure about fabulous is right for you I suggest just downloading it and doing it for a day or two. If you don’t think it’s for you ok but if you do then you have a great new app for support in your daily life. You won’t truly know for sure though until you at least just try it out for yourself.

title: Fabulous to set routines
body:
This is app is great for making routines a part of your day. Example:  drinking water. I have been drinking a glass of water or a bottle of water every morning for years and years and years. I don’t even think about it I just do it. It’s a little annoying to have to go into the app and actually mark down that I did it. It’s the recordkeeping that’s difficult for me. Gratitude is a normal part of my day. I actually use the word “appreciation” because  really who are we being grateful to? The universe? I am appreciative for the sun coming up, from my heart continuing to beat. For the beautiful greenery that I look at every single day. But then there is the recordkeeping part of it again, an annoyance.

The concept is fabulous. Ha ha ha. I guess it might do me more good to work on things that are not a normal part of my day and a little bit harder.
I would recommend the app to anyone (my son!) who has routines that they need to set up to make their days and lives more productive and healthy.

title: Love this app! A couple suggestions….
body:
Let me start by saying I would rate this as 4.5 stars if I could. Consider trying the free trial if you’re even a tidbit interested in trying Fabulous.

This app is fantastic - it helps me stay on track and celebrate when I complete my goals. I have ADHD and struggle with forming habits and setting goals. This app provides exact journeys and layouts to help me improve upon that. At $40 a year, I find it to be an incredible investment in my personal development. I personally feel that the $250 lifetime fee is a bit steep, but I have no experience in the development of the app and I don’t know how much work goes into it, so that’s not a complaint, just my perspective. I choose to go the $40 a year route so that I make the effort to use it every day due to the cost.

As for suggestions, every time I get a new letter or a daily coaching, the app immediately reads it to me. I appreciate that it’s a male voice because I prefer that but I wish there were an option to opt out of that every day. I prefer to read these letters rather than have them read to me because I stop listening almost immediately (perks of inattentive ADHD.) That being said, I do love the colorful images and user interface - this keeps me interested and excited to log my habits and routines every day.

While the app isn’t difficult to navigate, I think a few minor improvements would allow me to understand where to find things much better. I don’t have an exact idea of how to do this, just that occasionally it seems to take longer than I would expect to find something I’m looking for.

title: I like the content - disappointed in implementation.
body:
So here’s the deal: I really liked what I was experiencing within the app during the trial period, but became extremely frustrated when trying to use it across multiple devices.

Let me start with, I understand that the vast majority of people use there phone as an extra extremity to their natural body and that is driving development of design to production decisions.  That being said, I am not one of those people. My phone is not my typical UI for anything outside of phone calls - messages- and lately voice command control of home kit devices.  The majority of time time is spent on my iPad or desktop . Which is where I prefer to be to do certain tasks, like journaling.

Yes, I understand that the Apple emulator exists and the app is available on these devices, but quite frankly - it’s not a great user experience and the emulators have there own set of problems. Also, it was not very intuitive or considered how to handle this multi device interaction during the trial introduction setup - so I spent more time on trying to make the habit building app work the way I work, rather than working with the content of the application in a meaningful way. Which directly conflicts with my intent of correcting my habit of fixing things that are not mine to fix utilizing a tool like this to keep me prioritized and on task. My phone is not my life, please don’t make me have to use it more than I need to.

Also, it would be wonderful if the journal function would be able to create entries in journals already implemented.

I like where this is going, good luck!

The developer will not help you if you made your purchase anywhere but their website & Apple (understandably) can’t help me get a refund on a subscription that’s not even listed as current on my account there. The only workaround I found was to submit a “white lie” by entering my request as if I had purchased it on their website & explaining their error with a screenshot showing that I didn’t have a current subscription. Supposedly, they will respond in 10 days, which is way beyond what I consider acceptable for this type of issue.

With such a complicated and busy design, it made it hard to motivate myself to use it daily, which completely contradicts the point of the app. 

I think my main issue with this app though was the recommended meditation and mental exercises. The app promotes small and steady growth at the beginning, which is what initially drew me to it. It promoted treating yourself and your impulses with kindness, something I really agree with since in order to form new habits, you need positive associations with them, therefore you shouldn't shame yourself throughout your healthy journey. 

However, one of the mental exercises promoted tells you to treat your impulses like a "spoiled" and "malicious child". It also gives an example of this "malicious" child telling you to take a break when you're tired from working out and having your "wise sage" tell you that you have endless willpower. This pretty much completely goes against the initial meaning and can be harmful to people trying to establish long term healthy habits, since using all of your willpower and shaming yourself for something as innocent as taking a break leads to complete burnout for most people.

title: Frustrating UI
body: This app is not for me, which is fine, but what prompts my rating is the poor and frustrating UI. Immediately upon opening the app you’re given the option to explore or go through a guided tour, but both experiences force you through the tour. The tour forces you to take on challenges even if you don’t want to (like drinking water immediately upon waking, which makes me sick) and doesn’t give users the chance to pick and choose what they want their own morning routine to be. Several times when I opened the app I was promoted to answer the same questions over and over again, like inputting my email address. Apps that force users through one homogenous experience while touting personalization are a huge red flag to me, and this one was made worse by not allowing users to tap out of the guided tour. Additionally, when trying to cancel my subscription, the web page that I have to do that through conveniently will not load. It sure feels like a scam.

title: Trial is great, but enjoyment drops off quickly
body:
I really enjoyed the app  when I first got it. It had a lot of interesting things going for it, such as a sort of story that seemed to progress with you as you were completing habits each day, and they had letters that came to you with the voice overs that read it aloud, and also was just very enjoyable. After the first week trial I received a one-month free trial, but I became completely disenchanted not long into the second week, and then was bored but put forth the effort to continue through 17.5 days in a row. Basically, after the free trial the gamified aspect feels like it disappears except for meeting tiny goals in the journey, but half the time I couldn’t find that page, and they were a bit frustratingly slow. There aren’t any more little intermission/progression story videos not long after too. It dropped in enjoyment before I even completed the first Journey 100% and was into a second one. The read-aloud options for letters stopped, and then the letters stopped as well. They do have a morning and evening coach audio every day, which was nice, but all the things that got me to use the app in the first place and kept it engaging were gone. I was getting all of my routines done and it was just so boring- and I was annoyed that I couldn’t add a small challenge to my routine without having to pause a journey. Especially after I was steadily getting all of my routines done, an extra little challenge would have kept me using the app to check it off.

The app layout is also a little clumsy and doesn’t always feel intuitive for like finding the journey goals and such. I would not give them money until more effort and updates make it worth subscribing for a whole year. The one-week trial feels like a trap to get people to pay for it and then just gets sloppy after that.

There’s loud obnoxious music that plays, so you have to keep your volume down if you don’t want to hear it. This is the dumbest app I’ve ever used. Don’t bother. *EDIT* Their response: “Hi there, sorry to learn about your experience. The first journey has foundational habits. This is because we want to make sure all of our Fabs are on the same page moving forward. So, even if you already drink water regularly, or eat breakfast each day, we recommend sticking with this first journey to cement these habits and learn more about how Fabulous works in the meantime.” All I heard was “we think our goals for you are good enough, and we want you to follow OUR journey at OUR pace, rather than create your own.” What a joke lol

title: Not ADHD friendly.
body:
To be fair I only tried it for a few days. It’s a beautiful app but I felt it offers way too many different things to click and I had to search for my established routine. It starts simple by suggesting water daily. I drink water. So I added more of my usual things to the morning routine. Breakfast, breakfast for my daughter and meds etc…anyway I would go to click things off and a screen would pop up, “would you like to read a letter from the CEO?” “Press here for”…..whatever. It’s got too much going on. 

Building a routine is hard enough I shouldn’t have to go through what felt like internet pop ups to check off my progress. The app uses “behavioral techniques” like holding a button on your phone for a certain period of time to “pledge” you will drink water. This was just the trial, the premium features appeared much more detailed. It seems it may replace other apps like meditation ones? I think it offers guided meditations. So if you’re looking for an all in one you may like it. 

If you have time to really learn the app you may really enjoy it. Like I said it is really beautifully made. The illustrations were really pretty. It was advertised to me as ADHD friendly and I personally think it’s got too much going on for that. Also your free trial isn’t really free. They ask you if you want to pay $1, $3, $5 or $16.78 and then point out the $16 one is what will pay for their employees that run the app. I felt like that was a bit much. I’m glad I was cheap and not guilted into the $16 😬 because I’m deleting it.

Edited to add that when I just tried to cancel you have to go to the website not through the app or your apple subscriptions so I did that, a few more hoops and then it offered me a cheaper price for the premium service. I declined but if you got to the end of this review then you deserve that tip.

title: Sounds Promising but Too Many Privacy Concerns
body: An app like this doesn’t need personally identifiable information … period. This app gives me two red flags right off the top. First they fail to disclose if your information is used for marketing purposes, e.g., you want to improve your fitness, will you get bombarded with pitches for gyms and personal trainers? Even diving into their legalese Privacy Policy, it’s not clear … but the fact they require you to use your real identity is a 99.9% guarantee they sell your data to marketers. That’s probably where the real money is made. They also fail to disclose their prices. I had to go look it up on a review site, so they completely lose their ethical credibility. Folks, if your product can’t stand on its own two feet, then go find another line of work. Scammy sales practices will send you right to the trash bin. I deleted the app. I wish the FTC or Apple would require full disclosure of prices even before you download the app. It’s a waste of time and a privacy threat.

title: Perfectly Progressive
body: To begin with just a bit bout myself, I am someone who’ll stick to something for a while then I break the habit and don’t do anything until it comes to mind, if at all. This app has been constantly on my phone and/or mind. It’s because even if you’re someone like me, or someone who’s better at building habits and sticking with them, you can benefit immensely from the lessons for skills and a healthier life in many different areas! I have always (re)started my journey with yoga, water every morning (now I’ll actively drink water throughout the day) and a healthy breakfast! But I can’t wait until I get to experience more of what this app has to offer, especially as someone who tends to keep bad habits easier than healthy ones! Beyond what the app provides directly, you can find a lot of support and positivity from the online communities in here! Making a positive change and sharing it with others can go a long way for encouraging and motivating you. It also really does help to see that you are not truly alone in your struggles, even if you choose to pursue it independently! Overall an amazing app that has helped me feel better physically and mentally countless times. Many thanks to those who’ve made this app✨

title: Don’t bother if you have ADHD or don’t have time/money to waste
body:
ADHD short advice: my guess is that once the bells and whistles lose their luster; this will just join the 50 other apps in the land of the forgotten toys in the back of your phone (but this one is a fat chunk of change). We lose thousands of dollars on things that we don’t use and I almost feel like this app preys upon people like us.

This app has a lot of really great ideas and the recorded peptalk‘s are beautifully done. The whole idea behind it is amazing and for the first few days I really thought they might be onto something. It’s now day six and I am just about ready to cancel so I don’t have to shell out $40.

The first thing I don’t like about this app is the fact that I only get a one week trial to figure out if this is helping me when it takes at least 21 days to create a new habit. Then it costs $40 per year. What is more insulting on top of that is the fact that I have five gift subscriptions I can give to other people that are for 30 days! How is it that I don’t even get that many days but I can give someone else that many days?

If you try to contact them you are put in the most frustrating chat bot situation. If you are already experiencing any kind of mental health issue don’t even bother because it will make matters worse. 

Today is the last day to cancel before I get charged and I am trying to work out an issue and the bot just gives me these pre-determined problems. There is no room for nuance or option to actually chat with anybody from customer service. When you finally get to the end and you haven’t gotten any help (only wasted time) the devil bot tells you to wait 72 hours for a response. HUH? how does that help me when my stingy trial is over today? 

I have ADHD, I’m self employed, and I am a caregiver for a family member, and I am already drowning in unread emails. My executive functioning is so stretched that I probably only manage to see about 20% of my emails. I don’t even think that an actual mental health person is behind any of this because they would know better.

If you go to the Facebook page there is no option to send a message or anything. They are just clamoring for more likes. 

One small example of something that doesn’t work for me is that I accidentally opened the mood checker page as I was bumping around trying to get back to my journal entry. It is the first thing in the morning. One of the three responses is that the day didn’t go well… How am I supposed to know if my day didn’t go well or not? Normally it would not be an issue, just back out of it; but there is no way to close that page and you have to completely close the app or select a mood. 

So I am trying to tell this evil bot about the issue and it demands that I take a screenshot but tells me I can close the chat and it will still be in the same spot. That would be great except for the fact that then I have to go back to the mood tracker, open it up, select a fake mood that I’m in so that I can get a screenshot of the mood tracker page. Mood is quickly descending into not so good but I still wasn’t ready to track that but had to anyway so that I didn’t have to close the app in order to get back to my Health chat. As far as I know there is no way to delete that mood. 

Bottom line is that this app is so complex that you need more than one week to decide if you want to shell out 40 bucks for it. Maybe that is not a lot but when you add it up on top of everything else that you have to subscribe to nowadays it starts to get a little ridiculous. It’s a bummer, I really think that once I figured out how to navigate this app it would have been very helpful for me but I just don’t see myself committing to that after only a seven day trial. If I had a 30 day trial I would probably have a much better opinion of this app. I guess I’ll never know!

title: This is a win
body:
Whoever made this app, I physically love you. It has everything that ticks my brain just right to be able to finish goals and set them easily enough so that I can check them off and while that may seem easy to some, I’ve always struggled with sticking to my word. This app helps do that in such an efficient way so that no matter what you’ll get it done. The little feed of good motivations always seems to brighten my day and I save almost all of them! It’s adorable yet put in a way that’ll help you build yourself into the best you. 

I think everyone needs this app. I can’t think of a reason not to get it, it’s simply the best routine/healthy habits app out there and I say that whole-heartedly. It doesn’t just let you set a goal then alert you at a time when that goal needs to be done. The first goal for me from the app was to drink water first thing every morning, and while it did have a reminder it didn’t go off or was loud, it was gentle AND the app reminded me the night before to put a water bottle beside my bed so that the goal could be easier to reach. Not to mention the small map of your person traveling through obstacles and mountains? Genius. It gives you every bit of motivation. It even gives you daily motivational speeches AND nightly speeches. This app is 100% my favorite. 

Sincerely, a happy customer.

title: App needs more flexibility and less “flash” to work for neurodivergent folks
body: I have a love/hate relationship with this app. The Journey’s appealed to me by “gamifying” habits so I would stick to them (like an RPG!) but because the progression through the journey’s themselves are inflexible, my 15-day “First Mountain” has taken almost half a year. I am stuck on the “better sleep” journey because the developers want me to exercise when I get up because neurotypical neuroscience says so. (I am a night workout person - I even made specific routines for working out.) I am being a completionist and don’t want to quit the journey just because the suggestions won’t work for me or my brain. ( I think starting with a morning routine is the wrong choice too.) The evening and morning routines in particular seem to have a lot of extra, nonessential tasks autofilled. Yes, meditation is nice, but I need help actually getting in bed before 11pm, not meditating once I get there. Making my own habits and routines seems to work well, but I have to create separate alarms on my phone to remind me to do them (The app notifications are worthless to me) It would be nice to have an app that actually triggered an ALARM - loud and annoying - so I would do the thing. Even the timers that are included are too quiet. I have NO IDEA when they are complete. Many of the habits are not habits - they are vague ideas of things to do. I would appreciate more specificity with the habits I am expected to implement. Finally, I don’t care for the “challenges” or “community.” To my mind they are distracting side-quests and wholesale distractions from building habits that put a LOT of clutter on the homepage of the app. The journey’s and the animations are all I need to get reenforced. A simple home screen that has JUST the habits and maybe a daily coaching option would be nice.  I think if I hadn’t forgotten to cancel my 7-day trial I would have moved on to another app. Overall this is a good start, but the app needs to be more customizable - including the journey’s themselves - to work for neurodivergent brains.

title: Good luck canceling your subscription.
body:
Tried it out from an ad on a YouTube channel I like. Looked cool. I didn’t like the habit suggestions and wasn’t able to set my own or adjust the frequency of tracking progress. For example, they gave me the goal of brushing my teeth three times a day. It showed up in my morning routine but when I checked that box, it said it was done for the day rather than giving me three boxes/buttons a day to check. 

After two weeks it wasn’t for me. I didn’t get any notification about the upcoming end of my trial period nor a confirmation that my account was charged. I was aggravated to see a charge a few weeks later, again with no notification or confirmation. I had gone into the Apple Apps app and checked my subscriptions; Fabulous was not listed, and I assumed everything was OK. When that second charge came through, I looked deeper to see how to cancel. Going into the fabulous (Ha!) app, I went into setting this and looked for premium subscription management. Once you click on that setting a pop-up explains that you have to login online to cancel your subscription. This is where it gets BAD! There is no link in that pop-up to take you to the website to cancel your account. Good like searching for it online. When I finally found the fabulous website, it wanted me to complete the journey start-up before I could find a link to a help desk or profile management. I ended up sending a very colorful email to the only addresses I had from fabulous. I will now wait 10 days to hear back from the service desk.

title: Hopeful, at long last
body:
I’m 58, and have not taken the time to care for myself, like, ever. And now I realize: it’s now or never. I live in my head, not my body, which, intellectually, I understand makes my risk of earlier death much greater, not to mention the effect on my quality of life. 

The breakup of my 26-yr marriage in 2019 and desperately trying to teach vocal music online (MS & HS kids) during the first year COVID broke me. So I guess it took reaching rock-bottom to make me take action 🙁. I retired early in June, sold my condo, and took off for Portugal. It is here that I stumbled across this app. 

Fabulous uses the metaphor of a hero’s journey to teach, suggest, remind, and encourage in the gentlest, sweetest way. As corny as the Disney-esque animations and rhyming, seem, I think it’s working! The only reason I decided to try it is that it is created by Duke and is based in science, but I’m seeing the advantage of presenting the information in this manner. I’m as shocked as anyone that it is helping me build healthy habits, which I’ve always been terribly undisciplined about. I’ve tried other health apps and have never stuck with them. It’s early days, but I’m seriously hopeful that this approach will ultimately help me take control of my destiny. I have nothing left to lose!

title: Great app tarnished by difficult cancelation process
body:

To clarify, canceling on App Store is easy; however, what they do when you cancel your first 7 day trial is they give you a link to a 30 day trial.  This is the part that makes you go through hoops to cancel - 1) the app tells you to go to the website to cancel, 2) once you get to website, there’s no way to sign into an account to manage your subscription even though their help center refers to a sign in link. In order to cancel, you then have to chat with customer support, and they provide you with a sign-in link.  All in all, this experience left a bad taste in my mouth which is a shame because I really like the app.

title: Changed my life! (Only one issue)
body:
This is probably the best app you could EVER HAVE on your phone. I left a rating a while back but it really deserves a full review. Im a 20 year old college female who suffers from severe mental health issues and addiction, and have for most of my life. I was so depressed that getting up to shower felt like an 8 hour shift, so most of the time i let basic self care take a backseat. During my trip to rock bottom i stumbled across Fabulous. Its exactly what i wanted that other programs didnt have, it keeps you on track and its ENJOYABLE. and i can say its great for people with ocd, adhd, or autism. Now, after only 3 months, i drink water, eat 3 meals, exercise daily, practice mindfulness, and take care of my hygiene better than ever before! Im even about to QUIT VAPING after 4 years, which is something i never thought was possible. I can actually relax at the end of the day because i know i have done everything i need to do, and Fabulous will remind you of that. My mental and physical health have improved so much in so little time, I will probably never stop using this app.

Unfortunately, the poor reviews here arent (completely) asinine. They do have severe billing issues that they have yet to fix. Please, be VERY CAREFUL if you decide to accept a free trial or purchase a subscription. I have fallen victim to the double charging, double subscriptions, etc. (pro tip, contact apple, not fabulous)

title: Tiny changes add up
body:

Fabulous is like that super loving, supportive friend who cheers on your successes and never judges you when you forget to exercise for 6 months. You see yourself through their gentle point of view and change gets easier. 

I have my son, my best friends, and half my family trying Fabulous. It’s so nice to feel better about myself and my place in this crazy beautiful world.

title: Deceptive Subscription Practices
body:
Shady company. Do NOT give them your credit card. Do a week long trial through Apple and immediately cancel so you won’t forget about it. The trial will stay in place and then you can make a decision. (I do this with all apps after forgetting to cancel a couple.)

They will send you an offer for a free 30 day trial as soon as you cancel. BUT you will have to give them your credit card. Don’t do it. Other reviewers have warned that they charge you immediately for a full year and then don’t refund if you use the process in their FAQs for cancellation. You never get your money back because customer service is pretty non-existent AND they will charge you again when the year is up with nothing you can do about it except dispute the charges with your credit card company.

There are plenty of great apps not using shady business practices. This isn’t one of them. Avoid!

title: Premium Subscription and Ease of Accessibility
body: I went to delete this app because every few days it sent a notification that I fell off the wagon and should drink water at 8am, which didn’t match my schedule so I could never swipe to address the notification. Then, I noticed this app automatically charged me $40 on auto renew for the premium subscription which I never used and was unaware or forgot I even had. I assume this was some auto-renew charge after a free trial. When I tried to sign into my account to see if I could cancel this charge all together, the app interpreted me as a new user— so, even if I had used premium features before, my progress was unsaved. For this reason, and also the verbiage of the “fell off the wagon” notifications, I feel like other apps—such as Finch, may be a more beneficial to your self-help regime. If I were able to easily utilize the rest of my premium subscription before my cancelled auto-renew date and see the benefits of this app or even cancel the charge since I never used this app, I may have given this app more consideration and more stars. I rate it 1 star for not being transparent about it’s subscription (imo), for not being easily accessible to retrieve any data/progress I may have had, and for the conflicting verbiage (imo).

title: Ads/suggestions even with premium.
body:
First, they were difficult to try and get a free trial, and then a hidden subscription charged my PayPal. Once brought up they refused to refund due to terms. Oh well. My fault for not noticing I had a random subscription in PayPal where I never have subscriptions. I even managed to cancel the one they placed in my Apple account so I thought I got it.

Second, horrible app. Idk how others are able to scroll past the multiple pages of distracting “ads” begging you to watch coaching videos, recommendations, daily picks, challenges, and recently added videos before you get to your routine. There’s also a section for Upcoming Routines that they’ve had to add near the top due to the length of their main page. You have to scroll all the way down to the bottom to get to your routines. This has made it so that even with the accidental yearly subscription I dread even opening this app. Other apps when you open you can glance and instantly see what is required of you. With this it is so cluttered it’s difficult to see where your routines are even at the end as there is another advertisement for a mood tracker and journal.

There is also no way to toggle these off. You can already search for these videos/additions if you wanted them, so I see no reason to force me to scroll past these to get to the main function of the app, especially since I have the paid version. Wouldn’t recommend. I would recommend the app Habitica, it at least allows you to instantly interact with your set tasks and habits so you can stay on track without getting bombarded like you are on Fabulous.

Do not download, and do not try to do a trial run. If you do check your phone for auto subscriptions.

title: Don’t bother
body:
I really, really, *REALLY* wanted to give this app a shot. So badly. I love the concept and design, but their customer service is garbage, and don’t expect a response from them if you have any issue whatsoever.

I tried signing up for the trial for premium, my payment never went through. Continued to get bombarded with emails telling me to do the trial—and I continued to attempt to sign up for it. Never went through, never got to try the premium. 

Contacted them for help repeatedly, didn’t get any response whatsoever. Fine, whatever, doesn’t matter. I can find other ways to develop habits. Stopped going on the app. 

I then get CHARGED for the annual premium, when I didn’t even get an opportunity to try the trial in the first place! To make matters worse, when I go to the app, I still don’t have access to premium on my account. I still get bombarded with those “sign up for premium” emails daily, by the way, even though they charged me for it already. 

To summarize:
1) Tried to sign up for the trial for premium. 
2) Didn’t work. 
3) Emailed for support repeatedly, no response. 
4) Got charged for the annual premium.

6) Emailed them for support, STILL NO RESPONSE.

title: Horrible App & Customer Service
body: I started a trial of this app because a YouTuber I like highly recommended it for getting organized. I was excited! I don’t want to be overwhelmed by an app that is supposed to help me with a daily routine. So after I subscribed, I immediately wanted to unsubscribe so i wasn’t charged $39.99 for a premium subscription. I searched the entire app, my settings within the app, my Apple Subscription settings, etc and could not find ANYWHERE where to cancel. When messaging for help within the app, you can only talk to a bot, not a person. The bot told me if I purchased the app in the Apple App Store I had to cancel my subscription through there too.  However, as I already said there was nowhere at all to do that on my account. I found out after being charged the $39.99 that I was trying to avoid, the payment was through PayPal instead of through the Apple App Store. I also tried for days to find a way to contact a person instead of a bot in hopes to cancel my subscription via email before being charged, but it was not clear on how to do so and had no way of contacting them at all on their app or their website. After I was charged via PayPal, the receipt had an email from the vendor attached to it so I tried to reach out to that email but was immediately sent an email that said the recipient did not exist. I tried to appeal the charge via PayPal but PayPal said they reached out to the App & I was denied lol. This app is just trying to get money out of you and the customer service is absolutely horrible. Don’t waste your money or time even trying it out!

title: Great for the ADHD brain
body:
I’ve struggled with ADHD since childhood. It began to gradually worsen as I grew into adulthood. The past three-ish years has seen a major uptick where I’ve had little time management and organizational skills.
This app has been one piece of guidance that has helped me setup routines and manage my time better. I fell off from using this app for several months and I regressed. Happily, I started using it again and in only a weeks time, it’s already helping me strengthened my cognitive abilities.

I cannot recommend this app enough! For people with ADHD, it’s extremely important that we learn routines so we don’t forget what the next step is. This app is extremely user friendly, it’s engaging without being overwhelming, it gives you suggestions for which habits you’d like to build, or get rid of, and it lets you customize habits that aren’t pre-selected. 
Drinking water first thing in the morning, by the way, makes a huge difference. It’s the first habit you’re encouraged to build.

title: A staple to life
body: I’ll be honest. I do not rate any apps. But this one deserves it. As a young aspiring entrepreneur who’s also a college student, I’ve always wanted to find a way to fix my morning routine and control my 11-12 hour work day. I’ve tried many methods— like Apple alarms, writing it down, and other applications— but none have resulted in true habits like this app has done. When I used to wake up at 5:30am for work, I would be drowsy and sit in my bed for an hour to go to work. No breakfast, no water, nothing. Just my phone. But now, I wake up pretty well rested, get up to do 10 minutes of yoga, drink a glass of water, make a nice breakfast, and somehow I still have time to go to work early or reward myself for my efforts. If you’re unsure about getting this app, do it. This app was made to perfection. My only issue is I wish it would tell the user to reward themselves after completing a routine. I’m a strong believer in fulfilling your dopamine levels after doing a difficult task. But honestly, that’s me cherry-picking. TL;DR. GET THE APP ALREADY.

I’ve really been enjoying it so far, as well as the daily listening and journaling that the app offers. I’ve been incorporating the habits without really trying because you are indeed starting small. But I can totally see how starting small and working up is not only the best way, it may be the only way for someone in my position. Tiny commitments you can actually keep and build on will become the things you don’t have to try so hard to do in time. This app is great, the membership is reasonable, and best of all, I can actually see its working for me. 10/10 I can’t say enough about how great this app is!

I just got an automated email back saying “oh it looks like you want to cancel, here’s the super convoluted journey you have to go on to figure out how to even begin cancellation.” Totally ignoring my issue of not having access to the content I paid for. Two ignored messages later and I’m trying to file a dispute through PayPal but that’s also a convoluted and fruitless process. So… BUYER BEWARE! They will take your money, keep charging you, not provide the service, and there’s nothing you can do about it 😤

title: If you have a short attention span, this is NOT for you.
body:
Used this app for a week, bought the full version. Wasn’t very wowed with what it had to offer.

Like I said people with short attention spans will struggle to use this, the app is filled and mostly comprised of watching cute little motivational clips they put together, with long-form text meant to keep you focused.

As ironic as that is I didn’t find it to be useful, and exited out of the short clips most of the time, which made me feel like I wasn’t using the all the way it was meant to be, so I fell off quite early.

I like the base of what Fabulous has to offer, easily being able to set goals and tap to complete them, but there is so much Fluff and the UI is not intuitive with all its menus it actually wastes a lot of my time when I go in and try to figure out how to use all of its features.

This app may work for a lot of people, but for me I found there was too much stuff I didn’t need like guided coaching stories about being in the moment.

title: Decent app with poor customer service support
body:
First, keep a close eye on the subscription bill. I believe I set up a monthly subscription but was charged for the year. 

Second, I had not logged in the app for quite some time and decided to log back in. The app automatically reset and walked me through the original set up questions. At the end of the set up I was prompted to do a seven day free trial and then $39.99 for the year. I checked my apple subscriptions and clearly see that my subscription is active until February 2023. I contacted support via email twice and never heard from them. 

Third, the app itself is okay. I personally find the navigation of it slightly confusing and not totally intuitive. Seems like there’s a lot to it which makes it difficult to navigate. Also, I think this can be a tool to help people who truly are ready to make changes. Key words- wanting to make changes. This isn’t a miracle and will not make you inspired to make changes unless you are ready. There are no short cuts in life for making changes - it is hard work. But this app can support that process and does use some good behavioral psychology to help.

title: BEWARE of aggressive billing!
body:
The app may be Fabulous, but its customer service is not: 

I signed up for a Premium trial, with Fabulous promising free access for 30 days while I tried out its services. 
It wasn’t a good fit for me, so I canceled my account, and Fabulous confirmed by email.
A week later, Fabulous billed my credit card €39,00.
Over the course of a week, I contacted Fabulous via their web site, email (twice) and Twitter DM. They did not reply to any of those messages.

So BEWARE — if you try the app, stick with the free version until you’re POSITIVE you want to purchase a subscription, because my experience suggests that  the “trial” is actually a commitment. As of this review I still haven’t heard from Fabulous, and have submitted a dispute against their charge with my credit card company.

title: Limited scope and not user friendly
body:
How many moods would you use to describe what’s happening in your day? Happy, sad, depressed, stressed, optimistic, etc… On Fabulous you only have the option of feeling good, okay or bad. That’s weird and limiting. Or, if you want to set reminders to do things, there’s no option for having different times on different days. I wake up at 6 on weekdays, but try to sleep a little longer on weekends. Can you adjust the alarms for this? Nope. 

Then there are the habits. They offer ones to choose from, but so many of them are just having the user advertise their app. I think it’s great to bring a friend in for accountability or to thank them, but it is just really yucky to have it be a big ad for Fabulous. 

I found it really difficult to maneuver the tasks in my day. And if a new habit wasn’t a great fit, I couldn’t figure out how to edit it. So then I had the app pestering me to do something I didn’t want to do. 

I would have liked it if they addressed these issues, but I’m deleting the app so it will stop bothering me.

title: Charged 12 times by faulty website
body:

Evidently I received that error 11 times before giving up on trying to pay with PayPal and entered my card details, because I later discovered 11 charges from PayPal. 

I have filled in the reimbursement request form several times and been (very condescendingly) told several times that I do not qualify for a refund because the form makes incorrect assumptions about my situation. I finally managed to convince it that I should be able to submit documentation for a (hopefully) human to review and I was told I might be waiting 10 days to receive a response. 

I also tried to find an email address so I could just email support directly but everything is a form to fill in that results in an unhelpful message or a chatbot or some other “clever” attempt to be helpful that missed the mark. 

If you enjoy shouting “Operator” into the branches of an endless phone tree and then being hung up on this is the app for you! At this point I’m so frustrated and appalled that I want all 12 charges refunded as I won’t be bothering with the trial at all.

title: Ambitious & Unique, But Falls Short
body:
Fabulous is a beautiful application and it’s clear there’s a lot of effort put into to. But the more I used it the more I realized it wasn’t for me, and that it’s got some UX issues to address.

- It repeats the same posts and quotes. I used the app for 2 months and not several instances of repeats.
- You cannot retroactively edit you mood tracker, and there’s no way to independently access it. I don’t want to record my mood first thing in the morning, and also, sometimes I forget to track on a specific day. But because there is no way access it, if it’s it not on my home screen then I miss out.
- They way routines and habits are edited is inefficient. 

Ultimately, the application lost its luster after about 6 weeks, and this is from someone who made positive habit changes in that time. But I don’t think it’s necessary to pay 40 dollars a year for an app that seemingly just repackages the same several points. I did not try any coaching or challenges, so I can’t speak on them.

TL;DR - this app is beautiful, but there’s probably more effective apps out there.

title: This amazing app needs disability accommodation
body:
I have used this app for over 2 years now, and I love it. However, I have very different energy levels during different times of the year. See, Ive had chronic migraines since I was 12 which come and go in waves. One week I’ll feel on top of the world, and then the next week I will fall asleep every night with blaring migraines. 

I loathe when I fail to meet my daily routine goals. I show up, try my best, and still lose my streaks. Fabulous tries to encourage me back on the wagon with your pep talks, but sometimes they make me break down. Sometimes I physically am unable to finish them. I could go through and manually remove habits from my routines every time I feel like crap, but then I have to remember which ones I had and put them all back. It’s clumsy. 

I wish Fabulous allowed for different routines based off different energy levels or abilities. Or perhaps the ability to prioritize core tasks (e.g. brushing teeth, drinking water) over others (journaling, making the bed). For example, close your morning ring with three basic tasks, and go above and beyond with the rest.

title: Used to be simple, now buggy and bloated
body:
I downloaded this app a few years ago at the recommendation of a friend. At the time it was a fairly simple researched-based app that helped you add short healthy habits to your morning routine and backed it up with research results. I liked it but stopped using the app as I fit those habits into my life myself, but every so often I will come back to it when I am failing at my habits and need a boost. I especially like to use it for the simple guided workouts, because although the instructions are not always the clearest, the routines are short and easy enough that I can convince myself to do them even when I’m in a rut.

However, currently the 7 minute workout (one of the research-based things Fabulous used to support) is totally broken. A month or so ago it was usable but had sporadic voice guidance as though multiple conflicting instructions were being overlaid, so only some of the exercises and rests had voice cues and there were random other cues sometimes. Now, the first exercise will not even start at all. This could be because of the latest iOS version altering video playback but I’m not sure.

Also, the current version of Fabulous just takes a lot of your time for unexplained reasons, and produces sounds you can’t turn off until you finish your morning routine. 
- I have to close the app for it not to interfere with my meditation app, even though I’m using it to do part of my fabulous morning routine and I turned the sound off on the meditation step—doesn’t matter still makes noise.
- it’s started doing this random storytelling thing after your morning routine without explaining why—maybe this is also scientifically backed but I don’t know what it’s talking about and I need to get on with my day. I gave it a chance for the first couple times, but the badly rhymed vague hero story felt like a waste of time so I skip it now. It’s annoying to have to skip another thing but not the end of the world—I just doubt the usefulness of that feature.
- when you skip a day and come back it invites you to a challenge (it did “one big thing” for me) which it totally fails to explain or track, and for some reason it did the same thing two days in a row even though I only missed my routine the first time. Again taking up more of my time without explaining why. What even is the “one big thing” challenge and what does it mean to do it? And why should I add yet another task when I’m failing at my existing routine? Maybe there’s a good reason but the app didn’t explain anything.

I miss when this app was a concise science-based habit helper that encouraged you, explained itself, and actually worked. Please fix the 7 min workout, let me turn off morning routine ambient sounds, and explain what the point of the other content is if it’s going to be played automatically, like the challenge and the story.

body:

My only complaint, and this is just because I know the app developers probably never thought of these bad habits, but I suffer from Trichotillomania. I pull my hair. When I found this app and it said it could help form better habits and break bad ones, I wanted to break my habit of hair pulling. Unfortunately there is no community in the app for this. There are for “no sugar”, “no alcohol”, and “no smoking”, which I understand are big ones, but adding small ones like Tric, or nail/cuticle biting, etc would be helpful to me as well as others. 

I’m a senior in college and about to graduate this December. My goal is to stop pulling from now and keep it up till graduation so that way I can wear my head down during my graduation ceremony. I have created my own habit to add to my daily list of “no hair pulling” but a community would be nice. Thanks for reading.

title: Activity slides not functioning
body:
I had really been enjoying this app, but recently I have not been able to use it to the fullest extent I had been.

I used to use the stretch and exercise activities built in, but for the last few weeks, the slides for each exercise end up skipping to the next slide after just a few seconds, so I have to pause each slide manually in order to hold the stretch for the length of time it says you are supposed to.

For example it will say “high lunge for 15 seconds” but it skips to the next stretch after 6 seconds, so you don’t get the full stretch if you just allow the slides to auto-play.

It is actually very frustrating because I used to love this app before that issue, now I just use it as an expensive checklist.

Hope this feature gets fixed soon!!

title: More Than I Expected
body: I was expecting to download the app, check it out then decide that I don’t like it and end up deleting it.  I love this app! I was not expecting the motivation and encouragement nor was I expecting it to be backed up with logic.  You start out with some pretty basic tasks that help you along your journey. These tasks are part of your goals. As you complete tasks you are supposed to celebrate along with the app.  I originally thought the tasks were too simple so I decided to add more and was immediately told by the app that adding too many tasks would make it harder to reach and achieve my goals.  The app explained that taking a goal and breaking it into small tasks is how to succeed.  The daily readings are short and packed with information. I love the journal feature as well because you are prompted each day with a question.  This app makes you think and teaches you how to be successful and to take care of yourself.  Slow and steady wins the race!

title: CALM THE FUZZ DOWN!!
body:
YOUR APP OVERWHELMS BY DEFAULT!
That's why I stop using it so much..
 
I have a year subscription. So can we act like the first two weeks isn't where we have to throw everything at the person?

"Start a new habit is hard." "Take it one step at a time." "Don't overwhelm yourself..." then don't bombard me with several different things every day within the first week. Drink water on the first day, I did that. The second day there were three things being offered (community, promises, accountability). On day five I stopped because not only was I not able to do the small tasks I wanted, but then the suggestions, the "check out the community "notifications, the widget chiming in with suggestions to add. 

Also can the meditations not be so repetitive.. or at least have a speed function? 

Take four..😤.. let's try it again..🚶🏽‍♂️

Since I was already doing most of the morning routine that they have, I would forget to tell the app I did it that day and then not realize till the next morning. Now I can’t update that I completed the task and I lose my streak but in reality I did everything only I didn’t mark it down that day so it doesn’t count anymore. 

Which makes me feel like why try if I can’t accurately track my progress.

Very discouraging when you’ve been making an effort all week to remember to keep up with it. 

But I guess maybe it’s the app’s way of keeping me accountable but it makes me more so want to delete it, than to try harder next time because I did it and can’t record it.

title: Way too busy time waster
body:
I’ve been using simple pen and paper for my daily goals and habit building for years now. I decided to try the free trial of this app. Totally regret forgetting to cancel before trial was up. 

 This thing is so incredibly busy that you wind up spending a bunch of time just navigating through all of the ridiculous pop-ups. “fun” graphics (am I 5?), attempts to sell coaching services, and just generally convoluted interface. I never would have continued my subscription if I remembered that I had signed up for the trial.

This is an app for people that want to talk about having a productivity app, not for people who actually want to be productive. That’s just how I feel about it. I don’t understand how any productive person could have the time to shift through all of these constant idiotic graphics on this thing. 

I leave very few negative reviews for anything. I just honestly despise this app that much. It’s like those fitness apps for people that never work out but like to talk about having fitness apps. Total waste of my money.If you are so addicted to entertainment that you can’t even check off your to-do list without fancy graphics and music, then you may want to attack that issue before attempting to do anything else.

title: Aggravating
body:
Remember being a kid, when adults would lecture you about breakfast being the most important meal of the day? Want an app that does that and strongly suggests you add their recommended goals after little videos about why? Want it to make that into a new agey experience with a story about how your journey begins with a single step? Fabulous may be for you, then!

Got depression or disabilities that make it tough to get out of bed in the morning, let alone exercise and have a normal breakfast? Well, then this app is like an aggravating person lecturing you on how these things will improve your life. You can put in custom goals if you’re okay with rejecting their ideas, but I’d rather build habits with an app that doesn’t tell me why it’d be great if I were capable of morning exercise and a normal breakfast.

I now use Finch, which has lists of suggestions but doesn’t really push any of them. It has a regular list and a list for tough days, which wasn’t an option on Fabulous. Plus, instead of a cheesy story about my journey, accomplishing my goals gives a little bird energy to go adventuring.

title: This isn’t for night shift workers
body: Overall I think this app is really interesting and interactive. I love the graphics, the colors, the calming music when you click on certain things, and I love how doing such a simple task like drinking water makes you feel like you’ve accomplished something. Having said that, I work 12 hr night shift, and I’ve tried to set” my morning” activities to start around 5pm when I’m getting up for work, and I’ve actually become more overwhelmed by how many tasks I’m NOT able to get done. On top of that, you have the constant reminders to do things and because my schedule is very different than than the average person, it kinda makes you feel like you’re still failing. Even if I don’t wake up and drink water to start. So going forward, I wish app developers would understand that a lot of people work night shifts, and design an app that can accommodate our hours. A lot of my friends are nurses on night shift so I know it’s not just me! I wanted this app to work for me, but because of my opposite schedule it did not. (If you wanted me to help design an app for night shift people, email me!) A lot of us get anxiety and overwhelmed very easily (especially after covid, we are burnt out!) That was my reason for getting this app!

title: Great, just one thing.
body:
I started this with a 7 day free trial. I would like to mention that it gives you the opportunity to allow friends and family to try it out for 30 days. It would have been beneficial if I could have done the same. And maybe instead give the friends and family a 7 day free trial instead. 

I’ve started and stopped the process of getting setup within the app, because it’s kind of difficult to navigate. I mean, it’s easy to get to where your going, but it lacks a clear sense of direction. So although I know where I’m at once I get there, I’d like to have either a quick reference map or something to explain in further detail. (Just how my brain operates) I almost deleted it for that reason. I clicked on the reviews and was thrilled to see how many people stated this app changed their lives. So I gave it another chance and set aside time to just click around and figure it out for myself. 

One other thing. I like not having the option to really be able to move forward into the content. It really keeps you on your toes! I will say I love the way the app is designed and created it has so far made me reflect on things in a way I previously wouldn’t have. 

I gave 4 starts for now, but I know this app is probably under lots of supervision/construction to make it the best experience for people. Hopefully the developers will see this review and consider some of the changes I mentioned. I’ll be back later for more feedback.

title: Success (Still No Dark Mode)
body:
Below is my original review. I've left it because I still dislike no dark mode; but mainly to show how far my opinion changed. 

I started using this app 1 month ago, on March 15th, and at that time I could barely get out of bed. Last year, in 3 months I went through 3 huge life changes: I was laid off, split with my wife, and my dad died. Together with therapy and meds, this app has helped me make a great Journey (SWIDT? dad joke inception–not like the Covenant's). As the app will teach you, small steps taken consistently can have a huge impact. 

Now I sleep at 9 pm and wake naturally between 5-6, plan my top 3 daily tasks and regularly complete the most important ones; meditate 10 min/day; walk 10K+ steps/day; go to social functions; put my priorities first instead of always sacrificing for others and being a yes man; and spend hours a day looking and applying to jobs. I even disassembled my 200 lb standing desk and moved my office between floors to avoid distractions! 

My mom loves this app because I went from FaceTiming once/month to daily during my lunch routine (I also never used to eat lunch and was losing too much weight). She (and everyone) also loves the British narrator's voice 🥵. 

My therapist said it was one of the fastest transformations she's ever seen. She had been coaching me on routines (broadly), but Fabulous is very focused and you don't move on until you master the current goal. Being able to use it daily is a huge part. That said, therapy helped me see my life and (re)-actions in a new light. If you have unprocessed trauma like I did, I wouldn't recommend this app by itself. 

My goal now is to get into Product Management (I'm a customer-facing Business Analyst who worked with PMs) and perhaps one day work at Fabulous. I've been telling all my friends about Fabulous when they ask me why I'm replying to texts at 6 am (I've always been a night owl). 

Also, work-around to no Night Mode: under Accessibility, you can set the side button to mode switch. There you can also find settings for zoom/dim (below default) and full-screen red filter. As one of the letters in the Sleep Journey says, dim red light in the evening is thought not to interfere with circadian rhythms. I also use a Philips Hue light at red/5% as I'm preparing for bed, and 1% as I settle in. Old 

Old Review: My eyes hurt looking at all the white at night. For the amount they want for this app (subscription fee), it's missing such a basic feature. Particularly when you want to do nighttime routines. I can't use this after sunset. For how much they're into behavioral health, they sure miss the boat on accessibility.

title: Quite useful structure and functionality
body: What I really like is you can add items to your routine in really flexible ways. You can add an item to morning afternoon or evening. You can be more specific and add it for a certain time. Or you can be even more specific and add it for a certain duration starting at a certain time. Other apps force you to add in every habit at an exact time, but that’s not realistic. Sometimes your morning routine starts a little earlier or a little later. With this app it simply prompts you to do the items in the order you’ve entered them however long it takes. You can just check one off after the other and if you have to pause in between one or one takes longer one day, you just do it and then check it off whenever you’re finished and go to the next one. It’s lower stress than feeling like you’re behind, or have to stick to very exact schedule. But you can also input I have to always be doing yoga at eight if you want to.. it’s your choice. I do find the requests to sign up for year long or lifetime memberships off putting and pushy. I also feel like the voices and some of the little inspiring animation things can be sappy and condescending. I like the British voices. But who doesn’t? That’s just the aesthetic stuff though. Personal preference. I think a lot of work and thought went into the development of this app.

title: I tried to like it
body:
I loved the idea of this app. I wanted to get into good habits and better myself. I’ve been making strides on my own, but wanted a little help to push myself more. 

I got this app months ago, and really tried to get into it, but there are a few problems with it. First, is the kinda tutorial they have. They’ll create goals for you, and try to encourage you to do them every day. There’s milestones set up, and it seems like you unlock features when you hit the milestones. I’m not really clear on that. And that’s the first problem. It really isn’t clear. I wanted an app to help encourage me to work on specific goals I had. This app starts off asking you to drink water in the morning. I didn’t find out until much later that I could just add my own goals. 

Another problem with the tutorial, is I’m not a morning person. At all. I would love to fix that, but all the tutorial goals are set to be complete before I normally wake up. A great starting goal for me, would have been to get to bed earlier. Once that habit is learned, then move on to the others. Again, it really doesn’t make it clear that you can customize early one. I thought I had to unlock that. 

Overall, the interface is pretty confusing. It’s made even worse by the constant asking you to invite friends. I get that accountability helps when building good habits. I also get that they make money when you get your friends to buy the app. With how often the app bugs you, it really just feels like an ad at that point. It’s an expensive app already, and then they throw in annoying ads. 

It sounds like it works for others. I may just be an outlier. I just really really don’t like this app.

Then I’ll fill out the requirement for the evaluation, please add the subscription back. It’s been over 3 days and no email back. This morning I get a $2 charge and my subscription is back, yet 5 days later and no coach plan, even though I was told 24-48 hours. I’m starting to think this app is a scam.

title: Not Helpful and Scammy
body:
I feel this app is beneficial for people who do not have an established routine. However, if you have a routine and you only needed an app to store it with a reminder, this app is not that. 

They build deterrents and blocks in their UI if you try to override whatever suggestion they give, even if you put in the questionnaire that you have a routine!

Obviously, I decided to cancel the subscription after 10 days since it wasn’t helpful.

Now it is April 1st, and I’m reviewing over my statements. 

I noticed that fabulous tried to charge me 3 times right after I cancelled my subscription. Fortunately, I use virtual cards, so I blocked any transactions over the promised trial subscription amount (which was $1 for the trial). 

If I hadn’t done that, this app would be  $149.97 dollars richer! There’s no invoice on their website to say why or what they were charging for. I would have never known if I didn’t look at my statements. 

Proceed with caution when using this app. You may get sneaky charges.

title: Roped-in and disappointed AGAIN.
body:
All these apps are the same: lame. 
I bought a premium subscription for this app based on the fun ads that look engaging and interesting and helpful in making changes but it's just another cluttered app that's trying to do waaaaaaay too much and crazy overwhelming. I don't have the time to become an expert on this one single app but it seems that's the only way to understand it or find anything. 
See all those cute pics up above of the daily routines that look so simple and useful....good luck finding them. I have no idea what I'm supposed to do with this app. It's constantly sending me notifications that do not inspire me to open the app or to engage at all. It's hard to use and understand, I can't find any of the features that persuaded me to subscribe in the first place (specifically the morning routine based on my personality type) I've looked EVERYWHERE and cannot find it. There's also so much going on in the app that it's just totally overwhelming. You cannot pick a direction and even if you did it would be a hoot trying to find your way back to it. Basically, I'm not saying this app shouldn't exist, I'm saying, don't market it in a deceptive way that gets people to buy it based on something you don't really offer. In a word: Simplify. There are millions of people out there who want so badly for something like this, and then you get the app and it's a cluster-f___ of this and that as if all I have to do all day is look at an app and master it. 
Again, simplify. Not a fan of this app, not going to use, want a refund.

I find it distracting and time-consuming and I am someone who needs focus and more time in my days. Very much wish I had remembered to cancel and that I still had that $40. The end.

UPDATE: got a super generic response from the developer, “we make it clear how to cancel..blah blah….trying to improve and your response helps…blah blah” but the link to “contact the developer” is broken, how shocking!!  Anyway, I clearly stated I forgot to cancel, which I own… but I also am gonna reiterate, I think this app is annoying and it didn’t work for me nor can I imagine it working for any of my clients…and if, like some of these other reviews state, I get charged again next year, I’m gonna be LIVID.

I have constantly been hating myself and at age 10 I went on a paleo diet until age 12 when I attempted to starve myself. Now at age 13 I have been exhausted all the time and this app has given me a way to fix my wreck of a life. It is giving me a safe space to work out and get fit and strong, I can meditate, it reminds me to eat and how it is okay to eat what I want, and this is the first thing I have used that really lets you harness self love. I’m still on my free trial days but I can already feel my life turning around and I am happy I can.

title: Fabulous helps establish routines for what’s important to you
body:
I’ve tried dozens of apps to try and re-establish fitness, eating & self-care routines I had when I worked in a typical office setting 10 years ago - Coach, My Fitness Pal, Noom, visible calendars, tracking sheets, etc. I’ve never succeeded, but after Week 2 with Fabulous, I believe I will. You can pick which health things you want to do - Exercise, Meditation, Sleep, Journaling, Gratitude, etc. & the app coaches you through incorporating the changes at a slow-enough pace to make sure you don’t overreach & then burn out. It gives reminders for the routines (Morning, Afternoon & Night) & provides positive feedback when you check something off the list. You can also add your own custom items to the routine - as an example, I added Flossing to Morning & Night. 

The one “con” is that the app is kind of overwhelming at first, & maybe a little tricky to navigate in some spots, but I actually found that engaged me more with it.

I’d rather not see any of it since it’s not relevant to me and I already paid for the service. 2. The communities aren’t actually built for discussions like a forum, they are a feed of posts from people you don’t know. title: Not helpful
body: I can’t help but echo the critiques others have made about navigating the app. The positive is that it feels layered and full, but when you first begin, it’s hard to tell what you’re supposed to do. The interface is certainly beautiful. It reminds me of Monument Valley. That doesn’t make up for the fact that in contrast, the method by which you’re supposed to improve has a MANDATORY starting place of “drink water.” For a person like me who drinks water all day, every day, spending the first three days of a 1 week trial proving to an app that I’m doing what I always do seems like a waste. When those three days are done, the app moves you to “eat breakfast.” Done. Again, not helpful for someone like me. I saw other goals/activities in different places, but when I tapped on them, the app didn’t open the goal and kept suggesting I don’t add them. After a seven day trial, this app is $39/yr. The price point is good, I think, for an app that works. I pay around the same price for both Balance and Sleep Cycle, but only because I think they’re both worth the expense.
