title: Mostly about the weekly check-in
body:
Hello everyone, thank you for taking the time to read this. I appreciate it :) 

So: in the weekly check-in that Fabulous has you to do every week, there were a couple things that bothered me:

1) with the question “do you remember being mindful this week?” There are the answers “yes, I have stopped to be mindful” and “no, I didn’t stop to be mindful when I could have.” This last answer option bothers me. It always makes me feel guilty for not practicing meditation or mindfulness even though I didn’t have time at all that week. So I couldn’t have been mindful because I literally had no time, but that answer makes me feel guilty and causes me anxiety. I would suggest putting a different answer, like “no, I didn’t practice mindfulness” or “no, I couldn’t practice mindfulness this week.” 

2) the “did I manage my bad habits?” There are two answers: “ My bad habits do not control me” and “ I feel that my bad habits still have control of me.” Personally, I have no habit worse than chewing my nails. This question bothers me because I don’t know which one to answer. Also, there is no question asking if I stuck to my habits this week, which I find puzzling since there is this question about bad habits. I think if there was a question that asked “have you completed your routines this week?” With answers “yes, I have completed many of my routines” (because some people might not be able to do every single one but do most or some) and “no, I did not complete many of my routines” (because there is the possibility that one could complete some of their routines but only a few). 

I appreciate you making it to the end of this!! Thanks so much for having the patience to finish. 

Overall, this is a really great app, but it’s hard for me personally to finish my morning routine daily. Most days I can’t exercise in the morning, so therefore I can’t hit the celebrate button which makes it look as if I only did half my routine, when I really did 2/3 (water, breakfast and missed exercise and celebrate, which is a smaller thing compared to the others). 

Thanks for reading this!! I love you and have a great day/night/afternoon/morning/evening/midday/midnight/whenever you’re reading this!

title: It grows on you.
body:
I forgot to cancel the free trial and at first I was kind of 😬 about it because I feel like I had unintentionally spent $40 for an app that reminds me to drink water…. then I realized a) it’s $40 for an entire year b) if you take the time in one day to set your habits and routines for every day in the next coming year then everything balances out. Now that my routines and reminders are set, I love it. I’m a single 29 year old who lives alone and has ADHD with Autism — It’s very important that I stay on a routine or my days can crumble. My old way was tolerable but it consisted of reminders and notes and alarms on my phone in different apps as well as calendars and random post it notes scattered throughout my life. After almost a month of fabulous I’m starting to feel like a lot of those things are becoming easier keep track of. On the surface it’s an app that reminds you to drink water and stretch but once you dig just a little, it’s a whole world of help.

My only complaint is that they should maybe consider ways of making the app easier for beginners, older people or people who are technologically challenged. I’m a millennial tech-nerd so it was fairly easy to maneuver but I recommended it to my mom, 58 years old  (who could also benefit) and she gave up after two days. She says that navigating it at her age was too frustrating. — Personally, I’m very pleased so far. (Almost one month in)

title: Beautiful, complicated and super useful
body:
When I first installed Fabulous, I loved the vibe but was overwhelmed by the interface.  Then I took some time, read the FAQs and dug in.  Once you figure it all out, this app can replace daily reminders, to do lists, exercise journals, and healthy living and diet groups and apps.  Personal wholeness and wellness, physical and mental well-being are all part of the process, and you can choose from so many guided journeys, plus add your own already healthy habits.  

I introduced it to my daughter, who is enjoying it, but I was hesitant to share it with my partner because it looked so "girly".  Well, duh, I figured out that the  background art of most functions is customizable.  It's all beautiful, and there are a whole range of styles and plain colors   available if you don't like what it is set at to start.  

The inspirational messages for morning and evening are well written, often right on target, and beautifully voice acted.  My day begins and ends with these uplifting and mellifluous voices.

The subscription is not cheap, so try a week or get a friend to give you a free month (you get 5 free month giveaway passes for friends when you start).  I'm very choosy with my app subscriptions and don't hesitate to ditch them when I'm not using them regularly, but this app is third on my home screen after my calendar and clock.  I'm staying with it.

title: The Fabulous app is perfect for people dealing with deep, traumatic grief.
body: As a widow, living on my own for the first time in my life, self-care is extremely important and not at all easy to do. This app provides the small steps necessary to take care of myself all day long. I have not added anything to my day except my morning disciplines. 2 weeks in, I still need the gentle reminder and grace for selecting to add more when I’m ready. I wake up every morning to the realization that my sweetheart is not with me and before I know it, it’s five o’clock in the evening and I haven’t eaten or drank anything. Then suddenly I’m hungry. Chips and popcorn have been my diet for a while now. I’m grateful for the guidance of this app! Thank you for understanding self-care is a discipline and a slow process. Thank you for teaching me to take small steps. The stories also gave me permission to take my time and to only add new disciplines when I feel ready. This is a great app for me! I’m so happy to have found you!

title: Login Issues
body:
I downloaded this app while on vacation in LA, and started using it and mostly liked it especially the Infograph’s and layout of the app for the most part. It was mostly user friendly but there were some aspects that could have been more user friendly and streamlined. When I went back home to a different time zone, the app did not appear to update with that new time zone since it still showed I was on day two of my progress but I was not actually on day 3. I deleted and downloaded it again, but it made me go through the entire set up page again. This is why the rating is so low! I couldn’t bypass this part and simply login again and when I went through and completed it, it overrode all of my progress and didn’t have any backup data saved (even though my phone had been previously connected to wifi for various days while using the app) I lost all my progress and don’t feel like starting over so I’m deleting it and moving on to something else. Hope they can get and issue like this figured out so people don’t have to be forced to go through a completely new set up each time they download the app again. 

Also save yourself time with going through that long survey for the live coaching, it’s not free and they wait to tell you until the very end. It’s $67. I wish they made that clear before having to go through that survey so if you didn’t want to pay for it you didn’t need to do the survey in the first place.

title: Is this some kind of joke? Or weird performance art?
body:
I signed up for a premium subscription. I did that even though I think I subscribed to this app several years ago and was unhappy with it, and particularly with the billing practices, which seem scammy at best and actually fraudulent at worst. I DON’T think that the app’s tendency to “lose” your monthly subscription status is a bug. I think it’s a feature— they really really want you to sign up for the annual. And I think that’s because the content really isn’t there to support the monthly subscription service profitably. Too many people are probably canceling after a month or two of low quality content. Anyway. The app is now telling me that I’m a basic member. Even though I have the email thanking me for subscribing in my inbox, right here in front of me. I follow the instructions they give you for this issue, which must be pretty common. It’s like the first thing in the FAQs. Doesn’t work. Delete and reinstall app. Nothing. Try accessing my account on the web, and clicking on “Account” on the page takes me to an FAQ about how to cancel my subscription. At this point I’m done. This app is supposed to help, and it’s just shooting my blood pressure through the roof. I sent a message to customer service— another ordeal of clicks and misdirections. This company really does not want to cancel subscriptions. But if that’s so, they’ve got some serious work to do on this app.

Update: It has been several days since I sent a message to “customer service” about canceling my account, since it was impossible to do via their web page. No response at all. Apple should delete this app from its service.

title: Helps achieve my goals!! I feel like a new person!
body:
I love the reminders it gives me. It helps me stay motivated throughout the day. If I forget to do certain tasks, it always helps remind me to check in. Plus, the sound it makes is so fun!

I haven’t been using it much lately, but that’s not due to any issues with the app. I honestly love this app when I use it.

The interactive goals/moments are quite fun and relaxing because I know each time I finish a goal for the day I’ll get a little story at the end!! Just getting that little push to do more every day really helps me in getting myself motivated. 

The Fabulous circles are, well, fabulous. Right in the name. These chats are very inclusive and I have found many people who share the same goals as I do!! 

Overall, it’s a very fun and inviting app and I give it 5/5 stars. 

I do not have the premium, but that’s a personal choice. I think the premium is rather affordable for me and I do not have any complaints about it. For someone who uses it more than I do, premium would be a great choice and worth your money.

But, I feel like you can still do a lot without premium, and I appreciate that aspect as well! Lots of self-care apps give you a taste of what the app is meant for and don’t really give you good features unless you buy something. This app does not do that!! 

Lastly, I’d just really like to say thank you to the people who made this app. It’s made me change for the better. Thank you!!

title: Can make you feel worse
body: This app is the most beautifully laid out habit tracking app out there. It has so many good features like journaling, adding new habits with baby steps, etc. It’s really geared towards self love as much as self improvement. That’s why I was so disappointed that some of the features act as psychological deterrents from trying again if you’re not perfect. In the app, you have a journey. Each day you complete your assigned routine, you go further on your journey and see yourself on a progress map. Every week takes you to a new “level.” But if you miss a SINGLE DAY (or even just forget to login to fabulous even if you did it), you start back at day 1. It makes it feel like any small mistake or misstep warrants a complete do over, and it creates the feeling of perpetual failure if you can’t make it past the first two or three weeks consecutively. This ends up acting as a psychological deterrent from using the app. My girlfriend and family expressed the same sentiment and we all stopped using it. I hope they see this and fix that. Because one bad day shouldn’t undo all of your progress, and this app about self love shouldn’t perpetuate the notion that it does.

title: Don’t waste your money, unless there’s been an update.
body:
This app seemed great at first, it appears to have good intentions and is aligned with what I wanted to improve in my life. That being said, it is nearly unusable. I have no idea how this app is organized, how to change notifications, or track my progress. Every time I open the app, there are different pop ups (sometimes with audio) notifying me of different features that are hard to find again. after a few weeks I just dismiss notifications and feel ashamed for ever paying for premium. 

The app has so much potential but at the moment it’s just overwhelming and annoying. 
If the experience is improved I might come back to it, but for now I’m just deleting it and cutting my losses. I can make improvements to my life without being frustrated with an annoying app.

Fabulous team: please rethink the UX. There’s too much information packed into a 3 tab layout and organization is a nightmare.  Progress is unclear. Routines are hard to understand or change & why are they at the bottom of a long scroll? Is coaching different than daily coaching? Are daily picks challenges different than other challenges? What is a journey? How do I change what notifications I get and when? 

You can do so much better!

title: “Inspired” by behavioural science
body: There is a lot of good potential that is definitely inspired by behavioral science (e.g., implementation intentions) but the app ends up just being a regular time-based reminder app, which are known to be insufficient to create real change. It also floods you with irrelevant notifications by default (e.g., vacuous inspirational quotes), which have been shown to hinder new habit formation. These can be controlled but I’m surprised that this was the default. Additionally, the focus on inspiration made the UI hard to navigate and just find, say, the plan I had built to follow. Again, some potential but I didn’t like the current layout and especially did not think it was worth anything near the $40/month premium subscription cost.

title: Struggling with this app
body:
First of all, there are a lot of benefits here. But. Even though I enjoy the app generally, I feel frustrated. I can’t seem to get to customer service. The link on the Apple Store app page is broken. There’s nothing within the app itself. I go to the website, and it wants to take me through this long “tell us about yourself” bit. I just want to email or chat with customer service. 
I’ll also say that I like the “Let go of what hurts you” habit. But it doesn’t say anything at all about the process of doing that. No one likes to hold onto pain. We do it because we don’t know how to heal from it and let it go. So, some guidance there would be good. 
Also, if you comment on someone else’s post and the end of your sentence is cut off, there’s no option to fix your comment. 
Overall, it’s a nice app with a ton of potential. But, there are some things missing. I might even not be able to find some things that are there for me. And I can’t find a way to communicate at all with the makers of the app to share feedback or get information. Posting this review is literally the only thing I can think of. I’m sorry I didn’t share much of what I like about the app. (I even have a subscription.) But first, I need some help.

title: Best app for developing TANGIBLE good habits…
body: Believe me I’ve tried almost every app in this category and “Fabulous” is so much more than just fabulous. For me, it is superior to the others because it starts with baby steps to ensure that you get a feeling of success and then builds upon those feelings to take you farther and, if you’re like me, beyond what you even thought possible. I also like the ancillary material /exercises that allow you to cement the foundation for or even extend your new habit. And these are practical, everyday habits that will greatly enhance your mind and body. For example, studies show that most Americans do not drink enough water on a daily basis and hydration is so important to our health. So Fabulous has on habit that is simply “drink water” and then you check it off once you complete it. They really help you keep your habits organized too with a morning, afrternoon and evening routine. I just finished successful treatment for colorectal cancer with the final treatment being an 18-hour operation and almost a month in the hospital.  The Fabulous app is really helping me make the transition back to a normal life and, at the same time, helping me to prevent a recurrence of the cancer. I give it five stars easily. It is what you make it, however, and you’ve got to keep up with it and maintain self-accountability by keeping an accurate record of your stats. Simply downloading an app, ANY APP, is not going to magically make you feel better about yourself or you situation.

title: Best investment I’ve ever made
body:
I downloaded this app after reading about it in a science journal. The appeal was managing my adhd and chronic fatigue symptoms, as well as taking a shot at healthy eating, which I’ve never been successful with. It did more for me than I anticipated. After nearly 9 months of use I have seen such a powerful transformation in my life, I can’t believe this all helped me get where I am. I love eating healthy now, I am concious of my body’s reactions to unhealthy choices. I notice when I am off my routine for a few days chronic fatigue and everything come back quickly. I enjoy the daily live challenges and most of all the readings that are part of the journey are so insightful and make me think harder. 
Although it’s been a long time, I still have a ways to go. I plan to keep pushing, becoming a better person, and more fabulous by the day. I hope this reviews helps, this app is great for everyone!

title: Very helpful
body: Great content and science-based way to help you look at the goals and habits you really want in your life and finally do something about them! There are many different paths you can take, from healthy morning routine to better sleep to more productivity at work. I am giving it 4 stars and not 5 because the app asks you to start with building a foundation for a few weeks and yet at the same time it keeps suggesting new challenges. But in order to say yes to those challenges, you have to pause your foundations challenge. It’s hard to know what the best path forward is even though some people might value the absolute freedom there is in this app. Freedom or clear instructions, that is the question!

It allows you to chat with others from all around the world and share your experiences and help each other. I think this feature is really great because you get to see others progress in their life and you also get to help them with it, and share your own progress. There are also journeys that you set up to help you with everyday problems. For example, social media detox, self-love, de-clutter, gratitude, being able to let go, journaling, etc. This app gives you a chance to reflect and change yourself for the better. It’s really inspiring all the positivity this app and the people using it radiates. Overall, this app is phenomenal and I would definitely recommend it if you struggle with different things in life.

title: There is something so special about Fabulous.
body: Being a person who had many changes to make, both personal and professionally I'm some what of an expert on the subject. I have purchased my fair share of self improvement apps. Hard bound planners, weekend seminars, books written by the best of the best in personal development. All that stuff is great and I believe in it. However; I still needed so much and adoption is the hardest part for me. Along comes Fabulous, under the radar, cute logo/ marketing presentation but nothing over powering. Not by any stretch. In a lot of aspects it’s underwhelming, and that’s why I took notice. I saw the download number and blinked twice and looked again. It’s the Millionaire Next Door of apps, or the Barry Sanders of apps. The creators must know they have something great. They don’t need to be the one in the marketing place talking about swinging a big D. Seems they don’t say much because they must have a big D.  This App works! It’s thoughtful yet challenging, compassionate yet motivating. If people  can keep their ego in check long enough, they will learn that is what keeps most of us from realizing our goals. The APP does a nice job of suggesting that we slow down and enjoy the process and not get ahead of our self. At some point I had to admit I wouldn’t have downloaded Fabulous if I was on a life skills win streak. Lol. I wasn’t but Fabulous is better job than any APP I’ve ever used in helping me realize real lasting change in my life. I still have  a along way to go but I sure am enjoying the journey thanks to fabulous.

title: Content is great but UX/Social needs work
body:
The methodology, most important part of the app, is great.  It is amazing that simply drinking a bottle of water in the morning can lead to forming so many more positive habits through out the day.  I downloaded the app wanting to put down a bunch of positive changes I wanted to make and the app prevented me from doing that so I was not to put too much on my plate at once.  Starting small and adding habits along the way has kept me on board when in the past I would have gave up after missing a day or two.  Still getting into the meditation part of it but that is personal preference.

It is easy to focus on the things that you don’t like so I’m going to do that.  As of right now, you can’t change your username that is used in the discussion (Circles) part of the app.  Some people may not care having their real name out there but some won’t feel comfortable sharing intimate details with their name attached to it.  The app development team said this is something they are working on though. 

I also recently noticed that there may be some inauthentic behavior/users on the social feed.  There are a lot of “Hi my name is X and I’m from Y and I want to make friends” type comments.  It would also be helpful to filter by language.

Some of the pages in the app are clunky and can be overwhelming.  There is a lot of content in this app when it comes to challenges, reading, meditation and tabs can look messy.  

Overall, I like the app a lot and a few small changes will make it much better.

It helps you to keep coming back each day for the rest of the story! It’s been a week and I myself waking up and automatically reaching for my water without a second thought. Looking forward to exploring the other features and slowly adding to my routine as the days continue. I’ll add that I have the free account and am very happy with what I can access! So many apps barely give the free users anything to access so this has been refreshing. Especially with how expensive the mental health apps can be.

title: This is an instrument, not a tool…

The first day of use I found myself wondering why it was asking me to drink water. I already drink water.

A week or so in as the layers get added and behaviors change, somehow a light goes on. This isn’t a self help app, a journal, a to do list, an alarm, a routine, a community… it’s all of those things if you want it, and none of those if you don’t.

Start small, try it.

title: Anxiety and depression
body: I don’t normally give reviews, but this app has made making good habits so easy. I have had extreme anxiety for a long time and have suffered from depression for 3-4 years now. I was self harming and suicidal. Now that I am on my journey to recovery I wanted to have a good routine that I would actually stick to doing. Sometimes I get impatient with myself and I want to start a whole bunch of good habits and get rid of all the bad ones overnight, it never works. This app makes me go on a journey. It makes me go slow, believe in myself, and not give up. I have only had it for 4 days and my energy is amazing, and my mood is like never before. I work in the healthcare field and I’ve been working 7 days a week with multiple 16hr shifts throughout the week. I was feeling drained and numb. The meditation and coaching sessions have made such a big difference. This app is a huge success in my book!

title: Pleasantly surprised!!!!
body:
I’m a week into this app, and it’s so far working for me great!
It starts off slow, but it reminds you slow is the best way to start and easiest to build up from. Im inpatient but I waited and stuck with it and now I’m already seeing improvement. 
It starts you off with a small goal to do every morning. One action, drink water. After some time and after you complete that first goal for a few days it adds another goal. Eat breakfast. Every time you add something to that morning goal your adding to a routine, and before you know it you have a routine! Im excited when I wake up to complete my goals and listen to the daily coaching. 
The circles page (a place where you can share wins, struggles, and ask for help from other users) is such an inspiring and safe place to look for help. I hate socializing especially to people I don’t know but everyone is so welcoming and nice and here for you. We are on each other’s sides and I can always count of having that support system. 

Im seriously happy with how things are going so far, I highly suggest this app to anyone whose struggling with getting up in the morning. Im working on self discipline and I can see a little seed of change has been planted.

title: Please change it back 🥺

There’s no way to customize or remove them, and I have to scroll down for pages to even get to my daily routine, which is (was?) the primary purpose of the app. Getting the sense that Fabulous is trying to pivot toward selling personal coaching packages rather than improving upon the original concept of gradual behavior change. title: Interactive and prompting!
body:
At first when I saw the interface of the app, I thought to myself that it was a bit much. 
However, once I started using the app I quite liked it. 
Using the concept of behavioral science is so important to help people set up systems for their habits in an achievable timeline. 
It also explains the use of certain timelines and warns against adding too much too quick. 
I use systems instead of goals because I feel like implementing systems gives us a better daily feel of achievement than an end goal. It focuses more on the progress and journey than the end, so it feels more wholesome than ticking off a goal. 
I also love placing large widgets on one of my home screen pages that I usually keep my phone on throughout the day to avoid the clutter of other apps that I only use when I need to.

title: Not What I Was Looking For
body:
I downloaded this app because I was advertised balance and have been searching for an app to track my goals on my phone instead of a journal. This app is not what I was searching for. 

The app is cute, but it forces you to complete all your goals every day of the week and at the same time each day. As a result, you can’t incorporate rest days from exercise or sleep in an extra hour on the weekends without failing to achieve your goals. What about vacation days where you don’t want to necessarily reach your goals but instead want to indulge in some much needed relaxation? 

I also feel too constricted with this app. It prefers for you to stick to their road map and recommends you don’t when you try to do otherwise, even though some of the goals are already second nature habits for many.

Overall, I think this app is good for those looking for a routine to be planned for them, but not for someone who already has a routine. 

In short, not a great routine tracker but could be a good option for someone who wants a healthier life style and has no clue how to start.

title: SCAM! they will charge you even if you cancel before the free trial ends!!
body:
I decided to download the app & try the 7 day free trial out. I was at a low point in my life & had no money so I even put a timer to cancel & delete the app before the 7 days so it doesn’t charge my card. Its kind of buggy & def needs upgrade but pretty ok for the most part. 

On day 3, I knew I wouldn’t be able to afford it so I decided to cancel the membership & delete but thought I’d most likely come back once I had the funds. 

 On day 7, my card got hit with a charge. It wasn’t even the monthly charge. It hit me with a full year charge of $39.99! That was all the money I had in my bank & It happened right before Christmas meaning I couldn’t call to dispute. 
I finally called today to dispute the charge & was given my money back. the experience alone put a bad taste in my mouth & I will not be returning back to it.

UPDATE: after reading more reviews, it really seems that this scammy company is 100% taking advantage & stealing from people who are at a low point & trying to better themselves. disgusting. 
They also DONT give refunds for accidental charges or for accidental renewal charges so you have to go through your bank. 

My husband and I are looking to make our own motivation app where there are no scams & fix all the buggy stuff this app has.

body:

I’ve downloaded apps for these purposes and they never particularly work. I saw an ad on social media and decided to give it a go and to be honest I was quite surprised by what I got myself into. 

Fabulous is such an engaging app, it reels you in with these calm and pleasant stories, it makes you want to come back and engage some more. I believe I’m on day 5 or 6 and I’ve opened the app 30 mins after I get up (I don’t like looking at my phone in the morning). It’s been enlightening and inspiring to have an app this dedicated to help you every step of the way. I’ve told some friends about it, even shared some things from the app. Sadly I am unemployed but the moment I do get employment again I’ll definitely purchase the yearly subscription because honestly it’s worth it and with everything you get $39.99 does not seem bad at all. 

I’m really glad I decided to experience this and I’ll be taking what I’ve learned so far and will continue incorporating it into my daily routine. I’d like to thank the team and the creative minds behind Fabulous. The app shows just how much time, energy, effort and thought went into creating it. So thumbs up and a chefs kiss and hats off hahaha.

title: So much noise
body: The app sends so many notifications unrelated to its purpose that I had to delete it after a few days. A constant stream of noise with motivational quotes, announcements about new coaching sessions, and unintelligible nonsense. My initial modest goal (set by the app) was to drink water three times in a week. It didn’t actually send me any reminders to drink water or prompt me to update my progress, things that might actually embed the new habit. But it did send me 5+ notifications throughout each day, constantly pulling my concentration away from other things. The designers have failed to understand that their app is not the center of the universe and that users who want to be more deliberate with their lives do not want to be interrupted five times per day with inane nonsense. Please refocus the app on its core purpose and reduce the intrusiveness, it has potential.

title: I really wanted to love this app

When I set up for the free trial, and started my journey, I was quickly reminded that I had installed this app in the past, and cancelled my membership because of the completely overwhelming interface. Honestly I had no idea where to go, what to do etc. there is just TOO much to navigate that it makes the experience very confusing and overwhelming. I am on a couple other “self help” apps that are very right to the point. And you understand your tasks in a very simple way. I feel like the concept of Fabulous is amazing but the developers could do a better job with simplifying it. If it was simplified- or if even the material they had was put into sub sections or something, it would be a much better experience. I am really baffled by all the positive reviews. I see such insane potential - and the art is awesome and beautiful- but the experience and interface really needs some help. It’s just too much all at once.

Ps- would totally be cool changing my review if things are cleaned up. But for now. 😵‍💫

The free option is pretty dumb, you can’t even use the calendar because there is a limit of 1 or 2 tasks you can add. I wouldn’t mind the full year option but it gives you 7 days to actually see if it would work out. Sure the first week might go great but what if I stopped using it after 2 weeks? Then I already commuted for a year! I was reading reviews and it seems like it used to be a month free trial and honestly that would be great for something that’s supposed to be game changing. If they ever change it to paying monthly (or having a month free trial) and not having to commit to a full year, I will for sure get the app. I hope the developers add this option because it doesn’t seem like a bad app, it’s just to difficult to commit to.

body:
I like fabulous, and I use it. For a way to keep track of and build routines/habits it’s wonderful. The amount of times it asks me to share it, or notifications for stuff I don’t want is insane. If you turn notifications off it will complain every time you open it. There’s also some premium features, like coaching, that I just don’t want. Despite having a toggle for them, I can’t disable it. So multiple unwanted notifications for that every day. They’re so focused on forcing you into this box of what they want you to do as a user that it can be very frustrating.

Let me disable stuff I don’t want and easy 5 star. Until then, I’ll keep an open mind to finding a replacement.

title: Best daily app I’ve come across yet
body:
Pros:

-genuine user interaction. I like that I can express my weakness and bad days freely. 

-creative storytelling. It’s nice to have something that’s meant to be personal but put into something that feels like a story. Makes your journey feel like a grand tale, and it’s very inspiring for me personally.

-beautiful art. Best design for daily habit app hands down. 

-allows for personal expression. Write letters to your future self, name your goals/checklists how you want them, etc. If you put some heart into this app, it really gives back what you put in.

Cons:

-kinda crazy and intimidating off the bat. There’s a lot going on and although it just means there’s plenty of resources in one app, it can be a little difficult to navigate some pages.

I double checked to make sure I did not have access to premium features. I tried to cancel again through the app and through Apple subscriptions, failed, sent in a help request and never got a response. I eventually had to go through my bank to stop payments. The app is still trying to charge me at least once per week even though it shows I’m on the free plan and it doesn’t show up at all in my Apple subscription list. We go round and round. The app has decent content, but it wasn’t for me. Don’t sign up unless you’re in it for life. It seems to me that there’s no way out.

title: Gotta pay to be healthy so if you’re suffering money issues -
body:
You’re better off finding your own way to get healthy and meditate in the woods or something. just remember anybody who requires money to help someone, especially mental help, is in some way involved with a scam. Anybody who truly wants to help wouldn’t need an incentive to do so. The incentive to them automatically would be to be of service to someone who needs help. 
And if money is needed to help with thing then it would be a non profit. Not requiring the people that need the help to pay. It’s cheap yes but pleasure recognize when you’re being targeted to be profited off of for getting help. They make it like sweet and nice and inviting and then hit you with the price at the end. It’s a marketing tactic.
Use this if you want but please recognize the signs of when your deeply important issues are being profited off of. Right now mental health apps and others are making good money off people going stir crazy because of COVID.

title: One of the best wellness apps out there!
body:
I originally followed this account on Instagram because they posted motivating content around creating routines and mental health awareness. I didn’t realize they were an app but once I did, I downloaded to try it out. 

I’ve been using it for a few weeks now and it’s been truly keeping me consistent with wanting to stay true to my practice and daily routine. You can add whatever tasks you’d like to accomplish for the day (take a walk, meditate, practice gratitude, exercise, take your vitamins) and the app will send you reminders to help accomplish those things, but in a way that’s motivating and gentle rather than “you forgot to do this!!” or “you haven’t done this yet!!” 

If you’re looking to add new things to your daily routine and stay consistent with them, I’d definitely recommend this app. It’s shown me that technology can be used in a way to positively impact your mental health, it’s just up to you how and when you want to use it.

title: Through thick and thin!
body:
Fabulous has kept me sane and hopeful in my darkest times and thriving in my greatest moments. I had it back in 2016 when it was only for Android and after making the request and joining the waitlist I was happy for their launch for iPhone. Paying for premium is an investment in my self-care and mental health. It pays off with all the features but especially the updates and improvements that show they read the feedback provided by users.

Edit: I lowered my rating from 5 to 2 stars. This app has grown so much that it’s quality has declined no matter how much they are using behavioral science. I stopped the premium membership about a year ago and this app has just become more and more cluttered. I keep using it because the journeys are helpful but the amount of inescapable prompts and pop ups is driving me mad. I click my routine items done and a pop up that I cannot close shows up asking me the same questions and prompting me to post my progress. This is frustrating, annoying and I doubt it helps with the behavior thing. I’m not a puppy I don’t need a reward every time I do my routines.

How can an app that tries to foster healthy habits have turned into a website full of pop ups and nagging notifications that I’m trying to stay away from? Can you at least give me the option to close or turn off the constant animated prompts? I get the positive feedback loop but this is ridiculous I can barely use the app without getting a bunch of pop ups!

title: Gorgeous UI, a huge pain to use
body:
I downloaded this app in hopes that it could help me establish some new routines. It's gorgeous, and probably offers a great option to people who know nothing about habit change or mindfulness. 

However, it doesn't allow you to create your own challenges/habit paths, opt out of things you already do regularly, or go back and mark things complete on days that have already passed. It also seems to really feel like users need some "soothing" new age music to accompany their tasks, which is both annoying and unpleasant. I don't need a soundtrack for brushing my teeth.

All in all, there's a lot of flash and probably a lot of good content here. But if you just want a simple app to help you track your habits, and maybe nudge you if you have let a routine go, then look elsewhere.

title: This app is so helpful but buggy
body:
UPDATE: I loved this app when I first discovered it. I was using it daily and feeling very good about it so I subscribed (yearly membership). New features were added, and for some reason I wasn’t able to use the new features. I reached out to their customer service three separate times. I never got a response. I don’t even use this app now because there were so many functionality issues and bugs. It used to be such a great app. I will not be renewing my membership as their customer service seems to not exist. 

———

As a TBI survivor, routine is the key to a better day. This app keeps me on track. It has a lot of what I’m looking for. Prompts for routines, challenges to work toward achieving more positive feelings. It’s helped with my anxiety. I have the free version and it’s pretty robust. Maybe I haven’t found some features yet or they are available on the premium version, but I wish it had journaling and mood-tracking in addition to all it does have. This would be my one go-to app—the app that had it all! But even without those things I do find this app to be useful, and it has helped me feel happier, less overwhelmed, proud of myself for completing challenges.

title: Best of the lot
body: I used to work for Wired so I know a thing or two about apps. I’ve testd out 15 or so health & wellness apps over the past 6 months and The Fabulous is the best one by far due to its design, UX, and customizability. A minor flaw is the scheduling function and I can’t seem to make the alarms work, but everything else is good—even th alerts which ar usually banal or annoying in these kind of apps. Lastly, it’s obvious a great deal of attention was paid to the voices used in spoken updates. There is just so much in this app and you can connect with a community if you want, groups are available, and posting and messaging within it. It’s more than just daily habits, it has audio pieces, quotes, stories, writing prompts, daily journaling but you don’t have to do stuff you don’t want. You can just skip but since you can customize when you start and make changes as you go you get things for YOU! Personalized for you. I am so grateful that the founder or founders came up with this and didn’t give up on this idea. It really does make a difference. It may not seem like much to drink water everyday first thing in the morning at first but when you actually do the prompts, listen to the clips, stories and interact with it you notice a difference outside the app in your life. I could write so much more about this app and it would all lead to my saying ITS WORTH IT ITS AMAZING GIVE IT A SHOT AND SEE FOR YOURSELF!! ☺️😁

author: kgffurgsrhv

title: Hopes dashed
body:
I tried this app a year or more ago, and gave in to the developers’ pressure, to pay for a year’s subscription after seven days. The experience slowly worsened, a flood of woo-woo nonsense compounded by unresponsive support.

After a few months of trying to succeed in spite of those barriers, I gave it up. I don’t need foofy imagery and pseudo-inspirational things the Buddha never actually said on top of the subtle MLM ploys—create a Facebook group! share this pseudo-inspirational message with your friends! tell people how great this app is!

Fast forward to two days ago, when a misleading advertisement—if you’re going to tout the benefits of chronotypes, then at least begin the user experience with that—made me wonder if the app had changed.

It had.

For the worse.

Not only were the woo-woo and subtle MLM elements intact—I’m sure they appeal to 25-year old PSL basic yoga folks—users are flooded with demands from the very beginning of the user experience. The app purports to get you to start slowly, but you are pushed to not only create a new habit but to join circles immediately.

And my old gripe remains true. The app promises a difference within fifteen days BUT your free trial expires at the seven-day mark. I can’t take it on faith that my new experience of a buggy interface—why was I shown three different woo-woo affirmations for completing one tasks?—will improve beyond the seven-day mark even though the developers tell me that miraculously things will change at the fifteen-day mark instead.

Ugh.

title: Love this app! & you will too
body: When I decided I wanted to change my life into the vision I had of myself in my head constantly, I kept putting it off because I didn’t understand where to begin. I wanted to change basically everything about how I led my life. But how do you just stop doing what you have been doing for so long? How do you get out of the perfectly confortable bubble you've built for yourself? I downloaded Fabulous. It was out of no where, wasn’t expecting much. I promised myself I’d give it a try, there was so many resources, categories to help with whatever I was struggling with & even a community of people sharing their stories. Unfortunately I wasn’t consistent for a while. It took me about 3 months on & off the app. What I liked about it is that it was always there, no judgement, I’d open it a couple times & some days I wouldn’t open it at all. That is the truth about change. I am now fully committed to bettering myself & wont stop until I feel like I’ve learned all of the information & techniques Fabulous has to offer. So if you’re reading this thinking this app is just like the rest, no my dear, this is the app for you. & you are the most important thing in your life, so go & get the resources you need to give yourself everything you want.

title: Can’t believe I skipped past this app this long!
body:
I’m a 27 year old female. I have ADHD which means habits are difficult, but once formed can treat a lot of my most frustrating symptoms. 

I love the idea of creating better daily no-brainer habits but was always concerned fabulous would take the “all or nothing” approach that relies mostly on the willpower.

The app meets users with compassion, encouragement, and understanding. It takes away the fear of failure and reminds you to just focus on the tiny task in front of you.

If you are worried about failure, willpower, or this app being another false silver bullet, my encouragement is to download and try the app for 7 days and see if you find it helpful. 

CONS
My only frustration is the complexity of the UI. It’s hard to find my goals and checkbox them sometimes. I also don’t love that I can see afternoon and night goals as an option when the app recommends that I only focus on what’s in front of me.

title: Great with one flaw
body:
I’m new to the app, being with it less than a week. It’s almost exactly the kind of thing I’ve been looking for. It lets you set up routines and helps you to structure your life. It gives advice and tries to help me maintain the right attitude. All of these things I struggle with, and it seems like this is a great resource for them. 

The app is missing the ability to set custom units or counters on habits, just times (and only on certain habits). While you can check off “drink water” and add it to any routine, you’d need a separate app or to use the notes to keep track of how much you've consumed, and there will be no reminders once you’ve checked it off the first time, unless you put it in another routine, as well. Small gripe, but many other habit tracker apps have this feature. They don’t do as much as this app, but they are also quite a bit cheaper,  if not free. 

Tl;dr: The ability to add a counter on habits (8 glasses of water/fewer than 3 cups of coffee/etc) would make this the complete package, but it’s still a good download.

I understand the purpose of the forums (they call them circles here) but I am not a fan of these. I find forums to be cacophony rather than supporting. It is not a price point for me, rather it is a decision as to whether or not I can truly gain focus and move toward my intended results while being confused through the process.

title: Wanted This App to be Great. It Missed the Mark
body:
I downloaded this app with great expectations based on other reviews and things like that. I canceled the free trial after the third day. Why? The app is very cluttered with too many screens and options to choose from. There doesn’t seem to be any clear-cut instructions on how to use the app or what all the many features are. Things pop up at random while using the app that lead you to other screens and features which aren’t explained at all. It was somewhat disorganized and very scattered. It’s a shame because the animations and music are top-notch. I think this app has great potential if it was made to be more streamlined and user-friendly. As of now, it’s just a melange of confusing features, instructions, notifications, and tasks. Very disappointed. The app is also geared towards females. None of the animations feature male figures. Seems strange that they would want to alienate 50% of their potential audience that way. 

NOT RECOMMENDED AT THIS TIME

title: Cool, but could improve.
body:
First and foremost, my eardrums were nearly blown out by the unadjustable notification sound. My phone volume was turned down to ~15% yet the notification sound came through so loud it made me jerk my headphones off and go “OUCH” so, that’s not ideal. 

Otherwise the only thing I’d change about the app is the inability to retroactively complete things from the prior day. 

I’m not addicted to my phone, and I try to put it away well before bedtime. However, my bedtime rituals/routines will only be allowed to get checked off on their specific day. If I refuse to use my phone in the two hours before bed, and I brush my teeth and read for 20 minutes right before bed, to check off my little tasks I either have to preemptively lie or induce more screen time as I’m falling asleep. Not cool.

Except for those two complaints, I love the ability to add notes to each task. The ability to tailor tasks for different days of the week. The notifications/sounds when I don’t have my headphones in are lovely. But seriously it’s either turn off notifications or risk damaging my eardrums because ya’ll can’t manage to connect to the main phone volume or give the user the option of an adjustable headphone volume option? Come on. I’m a musician and my hearing is important. Please, don’t make me turn off all Fabulous’ notifications and sounds, just to use my headphones for other purposes throughout my day. 

I’d like my money back, if that’s the case. The whole point is to have notifications that help me stay on track, not that damage my hearing permanently. 

If Fabulous fixes this I’ll update my review to 5*.

title: Always uplifting
body:
This app will allow you to understand the idea behind small steps make for a grand adventure. Motivations, challenges, journeys and support really cause you to look within to better understand your own individual methods for how you handle day-to-day tasks. Now whether those day to day tasks are positive or negative are another thing. Every positive move that we make get us further along on our betterment. Negative or regressive moves can be evaluated further and then turned around.
I’ve always found this app to take small tasks and equate them to bigger and better things. As someone who could easily become overwhelmed and then dog on myself for eventually falling wayside when it would come to completing a whole huge list of tasks. Fabulous allows me to begin to rethink how to manage everything. 
The app itself is gorgeous and well thought in the amount of motivation and inspiration you receive. Bear in mind that if you subscribe you will have access to an amazing amount of features. However, do not get ahead of yourself. Follow the course set for you and then slowly branch from there the better you are at understanding your goals. I only wish there was something like this years ago!

title: No Support…?
body:
I’ve been using this for about a month. Unfortunately, it locks up and insists I need to purchase access to the premium features - and I’ve already paid. I cannot find access to any support through the app, the App Store, or Fabulous’ website. I accidentally paid twice, too. I find the coaching moderately encouraging. I wish it allowed for more customization. Mostly I’m frustrated by the repeated messages that I need to pay … again. UPDATE: I found the answer to my question under the “Contact Us” section. It’s fixed, but I’m frustrated that finding support took so long. I’m not terribly enthusiastic about this app. I’ll keep using it for now, but it again told me I needed to upgrade to premium - after I fixed it. It feels sleazy, as if they’re hopeful I’ve forgotten I’ve already paid. 

UPDATE #2: I canceled. I’m happy for the folks this helped, but after a month the coaching felt trite. I already drink a lot of water and I walk my dog every morning, so ticking those as “goals” never felt like an achievement. (I would have skipped them but the app said I could only skip a limited number of goals.) After having to restore my premium subscription two days in a row I decided the annoyance wasn’t worth it.

body: Funny enough I found this app years ago before it got popular. I was a teenager and I used it for a long time before my phone broke on me. I loved it.  Back when it was still simple without such a cluttered interface and unnecessary animations. It kept me engaged while not wasting so much time. After every accomplishment I don’t need to read a lengthy letter or watch the mascot traveling through obstacles. The letters become less exciting and meaningless when you get them multiple times a day. I enjoyed them more when I got them once a day or after committing to my routine for a few days. And waking up to animations in the mornings can be jarring.  I hope y’all incorporate these things and notifications as options so some of us can opt out.

title: Fabulous
body:
This has been, so far, the most effective and life-altering app I have ever downloaded on my phone.
 It’s easy to use, has beautiful design, is clearly very mindfully constructed with solid behavioral research backing up its structure… it just seems to have everything that all the other apps that I have tried didn’t have. I enjoy using it and it helps me make change enjoyable and easy- and that’s the only thing that works! 

My only feedback for the designers/users would be 1. Slow down; even though the program cautions the user to not try and take on too many habits to quickly, by the end of the first month of using the programs/journey  as directed you can easily have a ton of “new habits” you have to keep up in order to meet your daily goals and it’s too much. 2. The support circles are kind of open message boards that any fabulous user can participate in and it’s too chaotic to feel inviting. There are other apps that I have used where people are put into small groups with moderators, and/or work with personal coaches. That I know that would make this app cost quite a lot more because it would have to be employ human beings to act as moderators or coaches, that to me would be the next level up.

title: Bad UX, Too much going on
body: This app seems to have a good idea, but bad execution. The app has ADHD. It jumps all over the place. I thought the beginning personality test would be more in depth but was thoroughly dissatisfied with a generalized set of questions and an impersonal experience. The routines and plans seem to be effective but everytime I’d open the app it would turn my sound on without my permission, open up some random section of the app and try to make me do things I didn’t want to. My fiancé in bed with me doesn’t want to hear noises from my phone at 7am, and neither do I. In the morning when I’d try to just quick mark that I did a routine, it would jump down some other challenge automatically. I don’t have time for that in the morning. It made it so I didn’t even want to open the app. For an app trying to help you be more mindful, procrastinate less,etc., it tried to engulf your entire morning. This feels like some “inspirational” product manager was given open range to make an app and absolutely flooded users with too many features. There seems to be no focus to the app. The vision is there but execution is terrible. I see the merit in all of it and agree with some of the tactics. But not for me.

title: Censorship
body: I was giving this app the benefit of the doubt because it was recommended by the editors here at Apple Apps. It looks pretty fancy, the graphics are pretty, though it’s a little bit clunky and hard to follow in the way that it’s structured. Some good ideas and suggestions. They have a section called circles for people to encourage each other in their journey to change. However, a large percentage of the messages are from young men and women battling depression and mental illness, and in some cases sharing suicidal thoughts. I wanted to post a comment to encourage one of them and happened to mention God. When I pressed the arrow to send the message, a pop up showed up saying: “Oops! Your comments contain words or phrases that we don’t allow. We strive to build safe, meaningful communities. Please modify your comment if you’d like to share it.” Interesting that it’s safe to post about how you want to end your life but sharing the hope I have in Christ is not safe… movin’ on.

body: I like the idea and am on board with the incremental habits training approach. The user onboarding was really rich, which is why I signed up for the trial. But after that, the UI got really confusing and cluttered. I get starting small, but drinking water and eating breakfast are things I already do, and it wasn't clear how those were connected to my overall goals. Worse, I didn't seem to get credit for drinking water for 2 of the first 4 days, so the quick wins phase just dragged on. There are too many panels and bottom sheets and it's never clear where I should engage next. The cartoon video poems are not my kind of thing.  I think this is an app full of good intentions and probably good for someone, but not me.

title: Great Idea, Bad Company
body:
This app has some great concepts and, when used daily, I think can really help someone learn habits and set goals.  
The issues come in when you have to interact outside of that basic function,  customer support, billing, backups, etc.  First,  for an iPhone11, this app crashes or freezes way to much.  Second, Backup your journey?  Forget it, I still can’t get that to work and even after over a month of emailing back and forth with customer support, their final answer is “we don’t know it’s probably you” (. Not many emails in 30 days , just lack of quick follow up on their part).   Next is Billing.  Be careful giving these guys your payment information.  Use apple or PayPal as a third party because they will not stop trying to bill you.  I’m still getting emails from PayPal that they are tying to bill me, even though all accounts are closed.  Trial before billing?  I got billed on day one, so be aware there as well.    In summary,  this app and the idea has a lot of potential but this execution is falling a bit flat.  I would be willing to pay twice the price if it came with a better app and better support.  Hopefully, someone notices this and builds a better alternative in the future.

title: Had promise but too complicated
body:
This tool is visually and audibly compelling and enjoyable.  I see where they are going in helping people achieve repeatable goals.  Unfortunately it is still too complex.  I signed up for the free trial even though I was willing to pay.  Unfortunately I have deleted the app and canceled my TWO subscriptions.  

The app was just too complicated.  Like *valley girl speak) how could I have signed up twice to the same subscription?  For surrrre.  

The graphs and supporting charts are helpful but not resizable.  I wear glasses, but needed a magnifying glass to see the text.  Also it was unclear if the app wanted me to do yoga, daily routines or just general daily tasks or everything.  All at the same time it wouldn’t allow me to start more repeatable alerts/habits.  However it recommended that I join several discussion groups.  I don’t like discussion groups as the value to me is usually limited. 

I have 30 years in IT and have done my fair share of support, development, and design on servers, web sites, kubernetes and everything in between.  I WILL be keeping an eye on this app. When they fix their complexity problems, this app is going to be awesome.  It’s early September 2021, I’ll probably come back in about 3 to 6 months and see what improvements the app has made.

title: I’m lovin’ it ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️
body: I’ve only been using The Fabulous app for a couple of days, but so far it has been absolutely wonderful. It has helped me stay positive. I love the way that it starts small and doesn’t even let you think about moving on to tackle more difficult challenges until you can prove that you will complete the small and simple habits that you commit to completing. I love the letters that teach you and inform you about why The Fabulous app is going about helping you create lasting habits in the way that it does. I love the alarms. I love the options available to me even though I choose not to pay for the Premium membership. It is nice to know that The Fabulous app developers still want to genuinely help people & provide the world with quality content even though we aren’t paying a fee. This causes me to feel like they are genuine & trustworthy, and because of that I’ll be more likely to upgrade to Premium in the future. I feel like they have struck a good balance between letting you know that the upgrade is available & beneficial to you without always being in your face about it. Which allows you to have a more positive experience using the version of the app that is free. I love that they cater to the different ways people learn. Some people learn by hearing things or watching a video or reading & The Fabulous app provide a variety of ways to learn so everyone can have an equal opportunity. I love the color schemes. I love the way the app is organized. I think it is simple & functional & pretty. I’m lovin’ it so far! I’m excited to continue to use The Fabulous app & I have a few friends that I will be recommending it to who would greatly benefit from using it as well. Definitely a five-star rating from me!!

I love the layout style, it’s very colorful and appealing. The app itself explains everything to you when you select different things so you’re never confused. It goes slowly which is great for true habit building. It offers what are basically specific podcasts based on what you’re interested in working on for yourself, and they’re random and interesting messages that get you thinking. I like the videos too that are like cartoons depicting your progress on your journey, they feel inspiring and like a kid’s story about yourself. I’m glad I found this app. ♥️

title: Testing it out
body: I’m not doing the 7-day free trial yet, because I wanted to see if I liked this or if I’d even use it. Today is Day 3 for me, and although I like the concepts and positivity of the app— it’s not quite user intuitive. I feel like I’m never quite sure that I’ve checked something off. In fact, I clicked on “Drank water” three times on my first day. Each time, saying that I drank water on Day 1… and I don’t really know the direction I’m supposed to go. They put so many bells and whistles on this app, I get overwhelmed. I only have 2 items in my morning routine & 3 items in my afternoon routine, so I’m not overwhelming myself— it’s definitely the app. Without the 7-day free trial, I can’t try out many of the features. I have to give them a promised-payment in order to really try this out. So, I’m just not so sure about this app. Great concept… but could definitely be more user intuitive. That’s not to say they don’t give you pop-up guides, but I feel like there could be better direction in the checking off of routine items (why am I clicking them over and over again to make sure it was counted?). I’ll give it a few more days.

title: didn’t get far—hated the “contract”
body:
I was hopeful as I started the app and selected my options. Then it gave me a “contract” I had to commit to with a finger press. It involved promising to “making the most of tomorrow”—but a big part of my mental health journey right now is learning that I don’t have to do “the most” all the time to be good enough. To always be aware that “I won’t live forever”—constant existential dread is NOT my idea of good mental health. Even the part that was semi-okay, about turning difficulties into fuel for success, was a little value-in-productivity oriented to me, and not something I resonated with. I didn't want to promise ANY of this stuff! It would all be bad for my mental health!
These things might be great for some people, but NOT for me. And there’s no way to change it, skip it, or even go back and choose different options in hopes of getting something different.
I *could* just do the finger press and not mean it… but if I’m going to start out this journey by lying, what’s even the point?
Very disappointed.

title: Good app except for the live challenges
body: This is a good app that I’ve used for a few years. The one thing that I don’t like are the weekly live challenges. The app uses cheesy and disingenuous code to make it seem that hundreds of users are joining these challenges, that there’s a capacity limit or these challenges and they will close when they reach capacity. In reality, these challenges are always open. I’ve never wanted to sign up for a challenge and seen it closed. Also the numbers of participants are fake and generated. (Similar to “X number of people also looking at this” when shopping online.) It’s disappointing that an app focused on honesty and personal growth would resort to such lazy and deceptive coding and product choices.

title: Decent idea awful execution
body:
User interface is unbelievably bad for something that is supposedly worth $40. 

- Useless little videos/readings pop up after you click on anything and are distracting (and invite you to spend more time on your phone??)

- You are heavily encouraged to share everything on social media which is extremely obnoxious to someone who doesn’t enjoy or care about social media and is making an effort to be on it less. A “don’t show me this again” option would be great for all of the “share your progress” screens. 

- Calendar and “map” of progress only show up after you complete a routine and there’s no way to revisit them. Not sure why neither of these are available for regular viewing.

- You have to unnecessarily pause your “Journey” to complete any “Challenge.” 

Bottom line, it’s slightly better than nothing and you might really like it if you’re unaccustomed to intelligently designed apps.

Every morning, afternoon, and evening, they have videos with either a story or an act you can do to help love yourself and feel okay with where you are in respects to where you want to be. There are also worldwide groups that you can join to make public promises to yourself (this might sound wired but publicly vouching to be kinder to yourself or promising to get something done does encourage you to do it). 
My only issue with it is that you have to pay (quite a large amount) if you want to get the full experience. I haven’t done this, so I can only add four reminders per morning, afternoon, and night. I also can’t unlock every video, infographic, or story, which can be very frustrating because it means that I don’t have as many resources available as I would like to. Overall though, very affective and fun for me!

title: LOVE the concept. But its very buggy 😵‍💫
body:
First of all let me say 5 stars for concept and the aspects of the app that work properly. However in my first 3 weeks of having this app I’ve experienced some pretty unfortunate bugs and UI issues. Not thrilled given I’ve upgraded to premium and am paying for this experience. I’m hoping one or the devs or PMs will see this as Support has been completely unresponsive. 

- signed up for Premium and the information would not back up. Each day I tried to backup my journey progress following the onscreen prompts. The loading screen spins continuously for as long as I’d let it (talking 10+ min on multiple occasions). It was as if the credentials were not recognized despite my being signed in already and actively using the app. I reached out to Support about this and did not hear back. 

- got a new iphone and since I was never able to back up my journey progress I had to start fresh and lose my first 15 days of progress. Super frustrating given I paid for the ability to restore progress on a new device. 

- now that I am using the new iPhone and restarted I do not seem to have access to all my premium features. On my profile it says I am premium but the app is constantly trying to upsell me into premium and I have lost premium features as well (daily coaching for example). I can not tell if the system is registering my premium subscription or not. It seems like it is in some places but not others. 

- journeys tab is totally blank. The developers are apparently aware of this but its been down for most of the time i’ve had the app so again not feeling like i’m getting what I paid a premium for. 

- as mentioned, daily coaching has not come back since I got my new phone last week. I know I had it by this point in my journey last time so idk why I am not getting the option this time. I contacted support about this also and have not heard back. The only hypothesis I have aside from this being yet another bug, is that this info might be on the Journeys tab which is blanked out. 

- going to double (triple?) down on support being incredibly unhelpful. I am a career SaaS tech support specialist and cannot stress enough how poor the support experience has been. I would be more understanding if this was a free app but since I’m paying for this service I would assume I could interact with Support in some capacity, especially regarding billing concerns and lack of access to entire modules of the software. Many other individuals in the Circles section of the app make posts about this as well so I know its not just me having unreasonable expectations. They force you to go thru a “knowledge tree” that feeds you answers but the logic is poor and I have yet to have been fed useful info. Then if you say the info is unhelpful enough times, it says they are sending info to support but its been well over a week with no reply so I don’t think that is happening. Either that or they are woefully understaffed. The only other option it gives is to submit a question- which seems promising- but then you go right back to the “knowledge tree” of canned responses. To date I have not been provided any kind of live chat, reply, or any support interaction at all. Seems my concerns have gone “to the void” which is why I’m turning to app reviews to raise my concerns and hopefully spur some UX improvements.

title: A great app, but has recently developed a glitch
body:

It’s a little pricey, but it’s worth it for me. The app allows you to hold yourself accountable and helps track your progress as time goes on. It helps set up customizable routines, provides daily coaching, and even has communities to join to chat with other users. They also offer different exercise and yoga routines, so you don’t have to go find it yourself (there’s so much more, but I’ll be rambling at that point).

However, recently, there’s been a glitch or an error that doesn’t allow one of the screens to load. It’s the Journey screen, which allows you to track progress on the specific track you’re on. A couple of other people have pointed this out. I’m not sure how long it’s been this way, and it’s only started recently, but it’s annoying because you can’t reach some of the activities on that page.

title: Beware if you suffer from anxiety/addiction
body:
Do you have anxiety or social media addiction? This app will make it worse…

They are quickly going downhill. I’ve had this app for several years and I’ve been watching it slowly self-destruct. It started with a very annoying feature posted at the top of the front page. You cannot opt out of it— it’s a constant-revolving set of questions made by other users on the app asking for advice on their personal issues. This is the first thing you see everyday. It’s very distracting and I’m sure it’s not doing people’s anxieties any favors. Not to mention the stream of notifications.

If you suffer from social media addiction:  
Fabulous is now a social media app with a section on the front page that takes you to several rooms with people posting what they please + pictures. It’s marketed as being a ‘supportive circle of people who can uplift each other’ or whatever, but this idea completely at odds with their ‘break your social media addiction’ challenge/journey. 

In order to break social media addiction, they tell you to delete apps that are especially addicting for you…all the while stamping their front page with TWO social media features. 
With ZERO option to opt of of them.

Also: the app crashes multiple times a day! 

Anyway I’m deleting Fabulous now, per their own recommendation 👍

title: Poor design, lacking starting features and options
body:
I went to cancel my trial subscription and it asked me why so I wrote this below. When I went to submit it I could not hit the submit button it didn’t work. Also it offered a cheaper subscription for six months which I accepted but it never changed the price or duration. Needs work! Cool idea though. 

1. I do not like the app design, it feels chaotic and not streamlined enough. There’s too many screens, too many buttons, too many options that essentially lead to the same thing. 

2. I have spent a week tapping buttons saying I eat breakfast and drink water- I already do these things. I have always ate a good breakfast and I drink water every hour because I have POTS. This start is too basic for me, I was expecting a challenge. Maybe give people an option of where to start. Maybe ask them if they are confident in their hydration/eating habits already. 

3. I do not like being told to workout in the morning, I have fibromyalgia and I move when I can. I used to do yoga in the morning but I found it always makes me more sore. I go for walks- when I can, and use a floor elliptical. I also have a two year old (Im a stay at home mom) and I am constantly moving all day long most days. I organize a lot, and pick stuff up constantly. Having a toddler is a workout in itself. Also, that video of the new mom going for the run appears to show her leaving her (what appears to be an older kid) home alone. A new mom wouldnt have time to go for a run unless there was someone there to watch her newborn. 

4. I would've stayed with this maybe to try it longer if the trial period was 30 days instead of a week. I am not intrigued by the thought of having an app reinforce habits I have already solidified, only to be charged $40 for a year after that less than exciting first week.

title: My honestly opinion!
body: I never write reviews on anything mostly because I believe it’s a waste of time! But I wanted to write a review on this app hoping people would read it and hopefully this helps. I’m a 22 year old female, I am ADHD, bipolar, over weight, have both depression and anxiety. I am also one who keeps everything bottled up to make sure everyone is happy. In honesty, this is my second day using the app and in my opinion it’s already starting to ease my mind and I feel relaxed for once. IConstantly think about death (not suicide but just the feeling after) or everything else around me. I never think about myself I honestly never journaled before and I’ve been to therapist but they never help. When I downloaded this app I honestly think it was just gonna be like every other app but I can honestly say it’s not this morning when I started logging my habits or habits I want to begin it says reminders for each thing and it will not let me add unless it warned me that too many habits to start with can make me overwhelmed and I never seen an app that had it to where I can see the support that the creators actually give until now.I never thought I can get my life in order but this app is helping me see that I can possibly do otherwise that if I feel like I have a problem with myself which I do feel that way just because of my mental disorders I can see that I can change my life around and hopefully not have to suffer from anxiety and depression the others will always be there but I’m hoping that I can change the small parts about myself that will eventually become bigger. And I honestly want to thank the creators for creating this app and I highly recommend!

title: Charged and then Info Deleted
body:
Do not download this app unless you’re committed to using it for a year. 

The first week of June I saw an ad for Fabulous on Instagram, went to their website and was interested in doing a free trial. Before the end of the 7 day free trial, my account was charged. I noticed that same day and immediately requested reimbursement because I did not enjoy the app and was planning on canceling the subscription before I was supposed to be charged for the full annual rate of $39.99. 

I never heard back but I kept the app to keep proof of the charge on my account. Now a week later, I tried to reach out to the contact team again and got an automated response and my information has been deleted from the app even though I have technically paid for an (unwanted) annual subscription. 

I have been getting notifications that I can’t turn off for some reason and daily emails offering me different deals on other/better “free” trials. 

I really wanted to love this app but the lack of customer service and messaging trying to “get me back” in marketing emails has completely turned me off.

body: I stumbled across this app and thought I’d give it a shot. One of the things I suffer from is lack of accountability, I’ll procrastinate and avoid things of I can, choosing to lay around and be lazy if no one is telling me otherwise. This app reminds me throughout the day to practice new healthy habits that I chose to create a happier and more active me! The support from the positive community here and the inspiring little messages that come with goal completion give you that extra push to continue on the path you set up. I’ve only been doing it for a week and albeit a slow start, I am beginning to really see some new habits form and I love it! Be the healthier, happier you that you know you can and want to be. It’s as simple as saying “I want to change” and you don’t have to do it alone. Having served 10 years in the military I recognize the importance of support in trying to develop yourself into your goals. Except instead of a DI yelling in your face to push through, you have a supportive community that provides the same support, but in a calm and motivating manner. Different tactics, similar results! So happy I found this app!

So they sent me a useless 30 day trial unless I want to create a second account and start over from day 1, again.

The ambience within the app—the soothing & uplifting colors & music, even the voice of the “coach” in the mini-coaching sessions (2-3 mins)—is especially appealing to me, as I am a very visual person/learner. There are a few other features within the app that I’ve not yet fully explored; but overall, this app has helped me more in one week than any other accountability & encouragement avenues I’ve tried so far.
