title: Surprisingly meaningful
body:
This app, while very unusual, has probably been the most meaningful one I’ve ever been downloaded/purchased, as it’s been a big source of foundational habits. 

I used to drink 5 Diet Cokes and a coffee a day. Now I mostly just drink ice water, and no caffeine. For the last few years, I’ve make a to do list most days in a notebook, and I prioritize it quickly and identify the three things I really want to get done. When I’m stressed, I now do some sort of meditation and I find I can focus better. 

All these are things I learned to do seriously in this app. Lately, for really the first time, I’ve started a regular exercise program. It really feels like it may be something I keep up with, unlike my many earlier attempts. 

There are plenty of goofy/questionable suggestions, some journeys (healthy eating?) that just don’t seem terribly effective, some other ones that just won’t end, and about a billion references to Teddy Roosevelt for some reason. But all in all, this is an amazing app I’d recommend to anybody.

title: Don't use!!!
body: HORRIBLE APP AND EVEN WORSE CUSTOMER SERVICE!!! I have never written a review but will today. I immediately contacted the company within hours of receiving the email and they would not back down. They don't care if you are unemployed and can't afford it. They don't care if you thought you unsubscribed. They don't care if you contacted the company within hours of receiving the email. They don't care if you didn't use the app or services. title: Be aware
body:
Be very aware of the limit of the free trial. Miss the deadline by even a minute and they will happily take your money and hang onto it. Of course they are within their rights, but many companies are willing to work with people in good faith if you address it quickly. Not so eh this company. They will send you perky emails telling you how to store your subscription while closing over your request for a refund. They don’t do refunds, of course. The process is the process, and they will make sure you know it. Again - they have the right to operate this way. 
Just be mindful this is who you are dealing with.

title: App quality has gone down
body:
I’ve been a member for over a year. Over the past 6 months the app has repeatedly frozen up, routines open without the habits loading with them, the habits being checked off on the watch but not reflecting in the mobile app, and the app completely crashing. I really like the content but the app is starting to heavily detract from the experience. At some point the pain of switching is less than the pain of staying. I’m a Dev so I get that this kind of app isn’t easy to build, but the foundations have to be solid.

You guys desperately need a feature freeze so the entire dev and design team can focus on fixing what is already there. Cleaning up the design, removing buttons that don’t need to be there, removing concepts that make no sense etc. (I have yet to understand the differences between sphere, premium, journeys and challenges). Simple things are painful, like how do I leave/end a challenge, how to I delete a routine? You mean we need to start another challenge just to end the current one? Why am I even given the option to join a challenge when the first journey isn’t done?

For all the talk about fabulous being like an instrument, and the need to learn new words to use it, fabulous is pretty bad at teaching those new concepts. Throwing up another letter isn’t a solution. UI elements need to be removed, concepts need to be simplified.

body: The app itself is great, the graphics, the ability to achieve your aspirations and track your progress is sound. I realized that no app can truly help you attain greatness, you must examine the situation yourself. Why? Because behind the app is a developer, and what does the developer need? Money, payment, dinero, dough, the big bucks. It seems ironic and comical that they are charging you an unreasonable price for something that should be available to every person on the face of this earth regardless of his/her paycheck; improving their lives and finding self induced-happiness. To keep it short I’m disappointed, but not surprised. I just ask that this app doesn’t FORCE the user to upgrade by taunting them with his/her future self. It’s low, and it defeats the whole purpose in believing that a person can truly improve.

title: A Fabulous, Happy Mistake
body:
I downloaded this app for the free trial, liked it and used it for a day or two. Then on the third day completely forgot about it. Well, as most of us do, I forgot to cancel my trial and ended up purchasing a year’s subscription. There’s a lot I want to improve in my life and it did seem to work for me... so I made the decision to just use it for a year. A couple of weeks after that, while trying to attempt exercising semi-regularly, I remembered this app. Then I said to myself, “I paid for it and I’m for damned sure gonna use it.” 

That’s how I started my new life. I set my goals in Fabulous for three times of my day. Then, even when I didn’t want to do any of the routines I had set for myself, I would use the app everyday anyway. By reminding myself that I paid for it and was going to get my money’s worth. 

Though honestly, Fabulous makes you want to login three times a day anyway. It can make different tasks so much more pleasant with the “Launch Fabulous Moment” feature that will time out for you when you’ve programmed it to, plays instrumental music, shows appealing images, shows how many days you’ve done this task, and has a pleasant sound that becomes rewarding when the timer let’s you know you’re done. Then it’s motivational challenges, motivational stories, and motivational “letters” are actually helpful, actually motivational, aren’t cheesy, and are relatable (and pretty). 

This is the Fabulous Happy Mistake I’ve fallen into, and I am beyond grateful for it. Best “mistake” ever. This is a system that works for me and makes me look forward to using it. Plus it also includes some directionals too. 

Download this app, seriously, if it worked for me of all people, it’ll work for you. Change your life and make a Fabulous, Happy Mistake too. You won’t regret it.

title: Disappointing
body:
This app has so much potential, but it’s just not in a great place yet. The language is inconsistent, the challenges and routines lack organization, and the educational piece frequently doesn’t download. For something that is supposed to improve efficiency, I spend more time trying to figure it out and subsequently becoming frustrated to reap any benefits. I did the free trial- and was confused but thought that by purchasing Premium it would get better. It got worse! I reached out because I wanted a refund (literally this app has caused more negativity than its worth) and was directed to a website with 12 options for requesting a refund. As it turns out, NONE OF THE 12 OPTIONS ALLOW FOR A REFUND. 

This app has potential but it’s just not there- and unfortunately for anyone who is looking for education, structure, and true improvement, this app is going to actually make things worse. 

I guess I am out $35.99 and have this ridiculous app for a year.

I am a young mother to two young boys, I work full time, and go to school full time. I have struggled for years now to learn how to take better care of myself due to my priorities are always making sure my children are taken care of while my health and wellness, both mentally and physically, took the back seat. For the first time in my life, I am actually creating healthy routines for myself. In the morning, I meditate, drink a glass of water, take my vitamins, and stretch. In the evenings I tidy up, read for 30 minutes and write down what went well today. And I’m still only using the free version! I think that is the best thing of all. Due to a strict budget, I cannot afford the premium version of Fabulous at the moment. However, I can still access a lot of the features that are essential to me bettering myself through this process. This also allows me to make sure that this app is everything I need it to be before I make the hefty $50 yearly subscription (I know $50 is not a lot by any means, I just can’t afford that right now🤷🏼‍♀️) and that’s okay! Because I can still thankfully do everything I need to do starting out. I sincerely appreciate the developers of this app, and I hope to stay with Fabulous for many years to come!☺️

The only bad thing I can say about the app is when you mark that you did an activity that you did not complete, the app won’t allow you to undo that you completed it, so for someone like me who is openly honest about what I do, it will get a little frustrating to know you didn’t complete that goal for that day but everything else on this app is great and to me life saving. title: Great app so far!!
body:
First off, to all the people complaining about the trials,

You don’t have to buy the subscription to use the app, there is an exit button at the top of the screen. Then after that the app explains that you need to start small. Then it has you drink water for three days. If you already do that just wait three days, but if your angry that it’s such a simple thing, read the app. You don’t need to rush into everything so fast! Taking it slow is nice sometimes.

Ok, now to the review! I downloaded this app about a half hour ago and love it! I like how it uses your name to make it seem more personalized. Apps that do that are really awesome because they grab your attention. I also like how easy it is to set up. I set it up in under a minute. I just had to answer a few questions and I was off! It gives you tips on how to achieve goals.

I also love how it takes it slow while still moving fast. Some apps have no introduction to self care at all and just tell you to set a goal. This app isn’t like that. It tells you a bit about the app and asks you a few questions, gives you a task and tells you why you should do it. It also doesn’t say, right you have the app now your on your own! It has a pre-made routine for you to follow! 

I’m going to use this app a lot, I’ll edit once I’ve seen how it is! ❤️ great app!!

title: Unexpectedly surprised
body: I’m really enjoying the app. Honestly I had very low expectations terms of its ability to improve my life and how I feel. And I definitely didn’t think it would actually impact my day to day habits. I’ve been suffering from extreme  burnout, and have tried a variety of approaches to mitigate the effect on my professional and personal life, including taking vacation without much change. Somehow since using this app, I’m now going on my third week, I have actually been feeling a little more positive, energized and motivated to work every day. This app has helped me design a routine and stick to it. Who knew that was possible. I magically seem to remember to do the habits because of their methodology. Furthermore the structure prioritizes my personal needs at the time of starting the program which was my own health and some other parts of life that are important to me but are often neglected and end up on the bottom of my to do list. It’s a bit surreal to think that since I began using this app, my work responsibilities and life balance has become more manageable and consistent but it absolutely has. It definitely didn’t happen over night and was impatient to see results immediately the first week, but after week two there has been considerable decrease in burnout symptoms and I look forward to completing the morning and afternoon routines so that I can mark them complete in the app. I was very skeptical and part of me would have thought the improvements were just placebo, but it’s really not. And at this point there haven’t been any other changes in my life much less anything that would create a positive sustainable difference in my day to day life other than the Fabulous app. Because the improvements began to occur when I began using the app and has continued to progress slowly (but with patience) since then. Thank you to the Fabulous team. I look forward to continuing the journey!

title: Love that it builds better habits one at a time

And boy am I glad I did and kept the app! I know the price can seem a bit steep at first (40$ per year or 250$ for a lifetime membership BUT when you break it down that comes out to about 3$ a month for their annual membership which isn’t all too bad), but if you take this app seriously and work hard at what it tells you to do, it actually helps at changing your daily habits and it makes it fun and exciting! There are letters you get when you start a new journey and coaching you get daily. I love the live challenges because you get to do it with the community and see people’s progress in the feed. If community challenges and a sense of accomplishment when checking of tasks helps you grow and change your habits then this app is for you, and it’s worth every penny!

Thank you, Fabulous app, for giving a new zeal for life, and the confidence to chase my dreams!

title: It’s really pushy
body:
This app would be absolutely amazing if it would give you the option to minimize distractions/suggestions after paying for it. 

I love that it gets me in the flow, but I’m pursuing minimalism in my digital life for some brain space and this app just WILL NOT HAVE IT. It won’t give you the option of turning off alarms for your routines (I dislike notifications on my phone for things I already remembered... you become numb to what all of them are telling you) without keeping a huge banner in your way asking you to set an alarm for your routine. It doesn’t allow you to turn off the feature where other users “ask you questions”... (why does another human care about my random, unscientific opinion on whether coffee is healthy?) and pass around infographics. The “coaching” feature pops up in your daily list whether you’d like it to or not. If you try to turn off notifications it will keep pushing you to turn them back on. Pushy.. that’s the word overall. I recognize that overall it’s to keep folks engaged with the app and it’s great that all that is an option... but it’s really too much to not have any control over it.

But please be warned, it doesn’t seem or look sketchy at all, until you actually read into it. I was charged $49.99 for a premium subscription I didn’t even ask for. And it was horrible trying get a hold of these people who didn’t even give me a refund.

The strange thing is, these guys not only don’t have a phone number or an email address, their own support page doesn’t work! If you have questions that aren’t answered by their very udimentary FAQ, they invite you to submit your question—-except the entire submit page is grayed out!

This app would get five stars for me if there was a way to contact actual human beings and get actual answers. Some of the stuff in the app is very tricky, not self evident and or clear and extremely frustrating . Guys you’d really benefit from putting a couple of scheckles into customer service.

If you’re fine getting absolutely no support, want the risk of being finned for a subscription, not being able to contact the people who run this app and to get answers to questions you most certainly will have—then by all means get it .  

I for one think we will never make a change in the way these companies do business if we don’t insist on customer service and refuse to give high marks and ratings to companies who clearly don’t think the customer matters.

And Fabulous— if you’re listening, which I doubt—that is EXACTLY the message you’re sending and we all get it loud and clear

It’s not an accident that you have no five star reviews. Try responding to customers and see what that does to your ratings —
I’m guessing you’ll be pleasantly surprised

The app is simple and has a lot of features you typically see as in app purchases elsewhere. You can choose whichever habits you’d like to start including in your morning/afternoon/evening rituals, there’s ambient music, timers for tasks or goals, and encouraging little snippets scattered throughout. 

It’s not cheesy either. A lot of this stuff is backed by research and the positive affirmations actually help habits stick. I’ve been using it for two weeks now. I haven’t been perfect at staying on top of my daily rituals and habits, but I’m becoming more mindful every single day and I can FEEL the improvement. I’m super impressed. Give it a try.

title: Honestly incredible
body:
I get lazy most times to do anything. It doesn’t matter if I’m hungry or I’m thirsty, the less work the better. Though after I stumbled upon Fabulous, I tried to motivate myself to be better (because life is a jerk). I thought from start that they would go on telling me to eat better and exercise, funny enough they didn’t. They started small and allowed me to climb on up to the top. First it was water, then breakfast (which I will say was hard to keep up with but I pushed myself), and after a long while then did they ask me to start exercising. 

It was weird in the sense that they started small. But I get it, they were trying to train my mind first before my actions, which is really helpful. So if you’re having trouble just go through this app’s instructions and u should be golden.

title: Just let the app guide you.
body: This app has brought me out of the COVID-19 quarantine feeling of helplessness and confusion. I am so happy that I did the trial and didn’t let my tendency to control things take over. My advice on how to do the trial: just let the app guide you. Content is slowly dripped to you. You don’t know what is next. Just accept that and trust your new coach, which is an app full of a ton of science-based content. The first thing you are told to do is start a morning routine of drinking a glass of water when you first wake up. If you already do this, then just check it off and be patient. If you must, start one of the challenges so you have something new to do, but try to start small. For the first few days of the trial I felt like the app was asking me to just totally trust it, even though it hadn’t given me a good enough reason. I also felt that 7 days was not long enough. But by day 5 I was feeling really good. I had set an alert on my phone to cancel if I didn’t want to start a paid subscription, but I decided that this is worth it. I am now on day 8 and really feeling good about my morning, afternoon, and evening routines! I love this app!

title: It’s deep cleansing; great illustration posters!
body:
This is not an app to simple check off your todo list. It’s a gateway to your true self. Besides daily habits you can choose from, it has behavioral science structure in place where it will encourage you, and set you up with mechanics to foster long term success. Bc most people do want to make positive changes but it is hard to be motivated all along.

I also like the poster after each action. It’s so simple, informative and great illustration in macaroon colors!

I especially like the ‘challenge project’ where you can choose your own focus, and join a community of people who shares their progress and struggles. I am doing 5-day decluttering challenge. First day is to ask yourself ’what ideas/thoughts are holding you back?’ 

That’s very cool, and helping me become more authentic to myself. That’s why we wanted change after all. 

Good job Fab team!

title: Lots of helpful hints and prompts
body:
Suggestion #1: fix the MANY typos! They’re everywhere. I’ve only been using the app a few days and I see some sort of typo each time I open it up. They look unprofessional.

Suggestion #2: put more detail into the yoga/stretching/workout activities. The voice sounds like a robot from a decade ago, the images I’m supposed to mimic don't match what the voice is describing, and the degree of instruction is practically nonexistent. I am a yoga teacher and if I didn’t already know how to have proper form in the suggested postures, I’d likely injure myself. Please teach your customers how to be safe with proper form, if you’re going to tell them to do an exercise.

**********
That aside, the free version is pretty handy! There are plenty of practical prompts to help build yourself a healthier routine and the design is pleasant to look at and navigate. I like how the challenges have little, attainable goals and give encouragement along the way. I also like that the process unfolds, starting off with one task and building on it consistently. Finally, it’s pretty cool how many options there are for customization of your routine and goals. Thank you for developing this app!

title: Love the app - dislike the subscription
body:
The app is really beautifully designed. I love the habit tracking features, how you can customize your morning, afternoon and evening routines to be whatever you want. And it’s effective: it’s more motivating to do the things you need to do when you get to check them off and see your progress each day. 

TL/DR: Be careful if you do the free trial, or skip it altogether if you can. 

The subscription was confusing. I tried to cancel it before I got charged, but there wasn’t an option in my settings. I even Googled how to cancel a subscription and tried following the instructions and there was never an option to cancel. I ended up getting charged $43 for an annual subscription, but I contacted Apple and disputed the charge and they issued a refund. Just be careful!

title: My family tried the stretching exercise together
body:
At first, I was disappointed with this app, as features like adding more than three habits to my morning/evening routines or trying about half of the “make me fabulous” activities requires me to buy premium.

However, I realized this app has so much more. The long journey is well paced, new infographics and editorials are available every day, and the app constantly sends positive notes. I also realized that once I made a habit out of my morning routine, I could change the three habits out for three new ones. The “make me fabulous” activities that are available without premium are stuff like the 25 min deep work session and the 10 min stretching exercise.

After my siblings and I played video games for maybe an hour or two, I started to get a headache. My brothers wanted to keep playing, but we agreed we should stop and I opened Fabulous. I started the stretching exercise. My brothers, who have never agreed to a fitness routine unless it was school mandatory or to get something in return, stretched for ten minutes with me and my sister.

Overall, a beautiful aesthetic, many sweet features, and gently motivating. I would recommend that you try it.

title: A fabulous app that can easily overwhelm you with too many options

I’ve been doing the one week trial and really like the idea of this app! The visuals and graphics are lovely, the background sounds and narrators’ voices are peaceful and relaxing, and the material are amazing and very powerful!

However, my problem as a user is that there are too many screens and clickable items for you that you can easily lost in the app. 

One of the most confusing parts for me is that I have no idea that what will happen next after clicking on something. Sometimes you could end up getting 2 or 3 more new action items within that! Im honestly scared to click on anything...

Instead of having so many options (too much of customization for what user want to achieve with this app) I’d rather selecting from a few options on “why I wanna use this app (my goal)” and then having a clear path that unlocks step by step and help me to focus on that goal.

I love using Fabulous in the future when it’s less confusing to use.

body: I’ve struggled with keeping habits consistent for most of my life. The hardest one—drinking enough water (okay really, drinking ANY water....what do you mean tea doesn’t count?!). title: The best habit tracker
body: I’ve never been so impressed with what an app could accomplish in my life. It’s too underrated and should get more love... this is the best thing that’s happened to me in quarantine! First of all, unlike other apps which only let you pick 3 or 5 habits, this lets you pick a total of 9, spread out into morning, afternoon, and evening routines. They limit you to three for each ritual at first to keep you motivated but later they’ll slowly add more for you as you continue on your journey. I even sent feedback only for a misunderstanding in the app, but the answer I received was thoroughly written. I could tell that they actually cared about my experience, so thanks for that! Fabulous is also (fabulous) at making my habits stick. When I used Productive, it gave me no motivators whatsoever so I was forced to push myself. But I’m lazy...so I couldn’t really do that, and I ended up just not completing any of my habits and discouraging myself. Fabulous has what they call a Fabulous Moment, where it pushes you to do everything at once. Having a timer for each habit is also very helpful. They even send you letters from your “future self” and so on to motivate you even further. The Coaching tab was so much more detailed than I thought it would be! And best of all, you don’t have to pay for any of the features I mentioned! They offer pretty nice stuff in Premium, however. One thing I would suggest is to make it an option to view the days of the week on the home screen so you can tap them and check off which ones you completed if you forgot to on that day. Productive had this option, but this is just a suggestion to make this app even more efficient! Thank you so much for helping me live a healthy and more productive life!

title: My quaranroutine is a work in progress

There are also SO many options for activities you can add to each of your three routines too, which is awesome. I feel like sometimes I don’t know what to do with my excessive free time, and this gives me so many different ideas. 

Only reason I’m giving four stars is because I’ve been having issues with the alarms not going off, but tonight I realized that it might have to do with my phone sometimes being on silent. I’m going to play around with that tomorrow and see if silent mode does in fact affect the alarm, and if so, then I’ll try to remember to come back and change my rating to five stars.

title: They make it impossible to cancel
body:
The app is not like the advertisement. I thought this would be something where I could manage my routines like in the work from home ad since I’m home all day from being out of work because of covid-19. All it is are reminders to do things that I already do AND YOU CANT CHOOSE THEM. You’re stuck with their “journey” for habits. I literally already drink water in the morning and make a breakfast. Absolutely worthless and not worth the $40 charge that they SNEAK in.

That being said, I accidentally signed up for the free trial and have been jumping through hoops to try and get it canceled before the $40 charge for the subscription. I haven’t been able to find a phone number and am stuck trying to email wherever I can. The first (and only) response I have received was a generic text expander that is sent to everybody that didn’t even answer my question (I don’t know how to ask it more specifically). I’m scared that my bank account will become overdrawn AND I’ll lose money that is supposed to go to food for my family, it’s tough times because of covid-19. If I don’t get a decent response soon I will have no choice but to cancel my card. I can’t believe how BAD their customer service is, much less the app. Jesus Christ.

title: You get what you put in
body:
This app is a great tool to help disorganized individuals get organized. Personally, I often find myself forgetting to do simple things because I am too caught up in thought. This app snaps me out of that so that I can remember other things I need to do. Furthermore, it has an incredible amount of great advice regarding a variety of subjects. This advice will make you both more efficient and effective in whatever you are setting out to accomplish. I greatly respect the way this app was designed.

Having said that, this app won’t cure you of laziness. You need to find a way to be intrinsically motivated to maintain habits. When you have cultivated that motivation, this app will serve as a way to hone that motivation. I don’t use it for work, as that is not something I need to be reminded of. However, I often forget to tidy up or make my bed. Even more, I forget to celebrate every little victory I have throughout the day, and to end the day with gratitude. These small tweaks in habit lead to enormous changes in wellbeing. 

For anyone who needs help (or even advice) with keeping their life organized, healthy, and productive, I highly recommend this app.

title: Wonderful but imperfect

I get really frustrated that the home screen is so busy, and that every time I check off a habit, I have to wait 30 seconds of cutesy music and slow -moving messages until I can get back to the home screen. I get they’re going for positive reinforcement, but it’s clunky. 

I’d like a more minimalistic interface, with all the other challenges/music/letters/social media in different screens.

Also, I don’t like that it keeps insisting I share things on my social media. I bought premium so that I wouldn’t get those kinds of marketing extras.

title: Life-changing app!
body: I downloaded this app not expecting too much from it. The name was cheesy and I figured that any help it could provide would be limited to premium paid users, like so many other health and wellness apps out there. I was so very wrong! Even as a free member, you have access to numerous guided meditations and exercises in a wide variety of styles, goal-based journeys which start simple and can be adapted to your individual needs, and so much more. I found this app to be so incredibly empowering. I felt heard about things that many doctors and professionals had left me feeling uninspired and alone about. I saw that my struggles were not unique to me but also finally gathered the strength to make positive changes in my life. I never use paid apps but hope to soon expand to a premium membership because I can’t imagine my life without this app and want to see how much more I can grow. If you’re in doubt about downloading, do it and see for yourself!

body: This app was not for me. It tells you to spend your time doing something without any reason other than “building a habit”. For example, my first habit was “drink water in the morning”. Why? The explanation given was to “start small”. My interpretation of that is it’s a pat on the back to make a user feel like they accomplished something. I have specific habits I’m interested in growing, and this app is just not customizable enough. I also found the look of the app distracting. I prefer a minimalist, clean look and practical functionality. I think this app is best for people who don’t know what they need to change and are looking for coaching vs self-directed goal achievement.

body: This app has helped me start to learn new habits time and again. I fall off constantly but I don’t feel shamed or down on myself when it happens. title: Life Saver
body: I’ve never been the type of person to steer towards the “self-help” or “self-improvement” section. In the last year, however, I began a journey of self discovery. It wasn’t on purpose. It just sort of happened. The more I learned, the more I wanted to learn. Some things need to change entirely. Some things I didn’t even realize that I was doing. This app is so well researched and written. The content is amazing. Especially for someone like me who is usually a total skeptic. I decided to give it a shot, and I am actually seeing results. I have always been a cynic, pessimist, and grew more and more neurotic as I got older. That pattern kept growing until I would have bouts of depression that I literally could not get out of. Spirals of self destruction, and I couldn’t stop the thoughts. Well, let me tell you - the thoughts will creep up. But I check myself. It’s starting to come more naturally now. My brain is like “hey, where do you think you’re going?”, and it stops all that negative stuff in it’s tracks. I’ve never been able to do that before. It’s absolutely stunning. I can’t thank the creators enough. I wholeheartedly believe that I’ve gotten a second chance at life. Not just existing anymore. And I finally believe that I deserve it.

title: The Good and the Bad
body:
I first installed this app because it was promoted by the App Store. I’m a skeptical person so I did not accept the trial. I used the app without it. After a while I accepted the trial and cancelled during the period. I had backed up my progress and did everything available to the subscribed user. I knew there was no way I’d pay $50 for a yearly app subscription - until I did. 

I’m someone who gives lots of support to others craves support in return. I rarely ever get it. As pathetic as it sounds, this is what this app does for me. It reminds me and encourages me. I realize that the processes used aren’t new and it’s things I’ve read in books, articles and such but that’s the whole point - getting tried and true methods at my fingertips. 

When I re-downloaded the app I really had to work to figure out how to restore my data. It’s not that it’s difficult, I just could not figure out where to look! Now that I’ve found it, it almost feels like a no brainer. Restoring my progress failed many times but I’m tenacious and kept at it. 

There have been many blank letters which I kept closing the app to try restoring, however that never worked. I ended up selecting that checkbox so I can move forward. 

Every bit of progress I make with this app makes me feel like I’m winning. I’m a perfectionist so it is rather difficult for me to feel this way.

Fabulous to me is that unwavering friend and personal assistant who is pushing me to be better. Of course I have many days that I ignore her, but she’s the reason I’ve started drinking water and working out three times a week.

title: Disappointed, easy fix
body:
This app seemed promising but turned out to be really unfortunate. I started with the 7 day free trial and after setting my intentions, I was given my first new habit. To drink water every morning. This is something I already do every day so I was eager to just move on to my next step. Unfortunately the app makes you complete the habit you’re on for 3 DAYS before giving you another. And you cannot preview what the next habit will be. So I stopped opening the app because it had nothing to tell me. I then realized that if the next habit was also something I already do, I would be forced out of the trial period and charged the yearly fee before I even got my third habit. I quickly cancelled the subscription.

This issue would be sooo easily fixed if when given a “habit” to begin you had the option to say “I already do this” so it could move on to something else. I searched everywhere in the app for an option to skip the task but if it exists I couldn’t find it. Developers, please add a skip option and this app would be so much more worthwhile. It’s almost like the app assumes you must not have any good habits when you begin. Either that or they are hoping customers will accidentally slip by that 7 day mark trying to make progress without realizing they’ve been charged $40.

title: Great App So Far!
body:
I’ve been using this app for almost 2 weeks now and I can honestly say it actually works! I’m sure part of it is because you already need to have a mindset that you want to add and/or change certain habits which makes it easier to stick with it, but this app really does help!

I’ve found that every day I make it a goal to try and complete all the habits and challenges I have on the app. The “Fabulous Moments”, “Motivators”, and little readings here and there make the app more interesting, interactive, and fun to use. There are days when I don’t feel like completing certain tasks and usually I just force myself to complete it and feel much better after. However, even on those days when I’m not able to complete everything, the app sort of teaches you that it’s okay if you can’t do everything that day so long as you tried your best is all that matters and that helps so much with your mental state because you become more motivated to complete all the tasks the next day.

This app (if used daily and as intended) can help you go from being a lazy person who feels as though they have unproductive days to a person that feels accomplished because they completed all their tasks that day. I really like this app and think I will definitely use it long term to complete my personal goals.

My only issue is that because I was one of the first to use it, I was gifted 50% off my 12-month subscription. However, when I go to purchase it, instead of $24.99 the price states it’s $49.99. If there was a way for the developers to fix that, then I would definitely go ahead and purchase the 12-month subscription!

title: Great design, needs some customization
body:
I’m currently using the free version but it’s quite limited. That’s fair and I appreciate all the work put into various parts of the app. The daily reminders, Journey Roadmaps and especially having guided meditation/exercise/yoga all rolled into the same app seems great.

My main issue is that there doesn’t seem to be a way to track things weekly or monthly. Daily routine is a good place to start, but this app clearly tries to take a holistic approach in changing your life. I think that naturally lends itself to building habits that may happen with a longer time frame.
Eg. Pay bills on time, go out with friends X times per month, go to the gym 3 times per week.

I would definitely pay for this app if it had that option. And it seems like a much easier thing to implement than some of the current features. 

(It would also be great if I could add some bullet points to habits like “Take my medicine”, I could list out what I need to take and check it off. Also, why can’t I do challenges and Journeys at the same time?)

title: Awesome App!!!!
body: I can’t say enough about this app.  I’ve been in therapy for years for some losses etc. I’ve currently been enrolled in a DBT course,8 weeks to get through 4modules.  You can’t reach knowledge or gain enough practice to be great at this in one course.  This app you have here is the perfect in between classes to work with as extra coping mechanisms..  it brings in soooo much helpful information for personal care and development.  It’s very easy to use.  For me, it is not overwhelming, you can do as much or as little as you want during the 3 parts of your days.  It has given me more practice in becoming one mindful where everybody should learn.  This mindfulness can be done in 5 minutes or less or longer.  It’s giving your mind a break.  Instead of racing around thoughts, you learn to focus and remain calm.  The meditations here are very easy to sit back and listen.  I’ve even been so relaxed I fell asleep which is very hard for me to do.  It has done wonders in just these few days to work with your app.  I love the challenges!  I also like the way you can choose what you want for your daily routine.  If what you offer isn’t enough you provide a way for us to add our own routines in, if it’s not working on the list.  Thank you so much for offering this FABULOUS app.

title: Baby Steps
body:
This app helps me be patient with myself when it comes to self improvement. At first, it was overwhelming with everything it has to offer, especially if you’re browsing the app. I let the app guide me after a while. You’ll likely do some self reflection and point out problem areas in your daily routines. I never had a set routine throughout the day, but Fabulous helped me build one. 

Fabulous offers an extensive list of healthy habits to pick and choose from. It’s best to stick to just 2-3 habits in your Routines in the beginning. Having too many was my first pitfall and I ended up not using the app for a looong time. Picked it up again to slowly get the ball rolling so that I can succeed.

title: Habit building made easy
body: I am finding this app really helpful. It is helping me to implement the ideas in Atomic Habits by James Clear. Tiny actions performed consistently lead to big changes. Not only is their app ridiculously expensive, they don’t offer refunds for accidental auto renewal, or if you did not like the app. EVERY other company I have ever had experience with will offer refunds if you are not happy with their service, if it did not meet your expectations, and especially if you were accidentally paying for an app for an entire year beyond when you ever even opened the app. It is clear to me that they cannot afford to be in this business if they are going to rob their customers of their money when they aren’t happy with the service. Again, I have experience with many many apps and services and everytime I have asked for a refund I get it, no. questions. asked.  The fact that this company has the audacity to tell me they are keeping my money when I don’t even have the app still downloaded on my phone is mind blowing to me. Get out of this business, you aren’t helping people, you are robbing me.  My auto renewal was on Dec 30th and I emailed them days later. they are keeping my money for the entire 2020 year. I could understand if they maybe kept one month but refunded me the rest but to keep this ENTIRE year of my money when I’ve been very clear with them I am not using this app is just ridiculous. Do not support this company, they clearly do not care about their customers whatsoever.

title: Fine app, way too much clutter.
body: My annual subscription for this app is about to expire and even though I kept up with it for the better part of the year, I’m not going to renew. This app utilizes some great techniques for motivation and accountability but it ultimately dogs itself down with too much content. It is constantly putting more and more information in your face about things to read and new challenges to accomplish and so on. It’s not abnormal to open the app in the morning to begin my morning routine and be confronted by two or three messages that I have to swipe away or close out of or decline just in order to use the app. Every time you finish a routine, which it encourages you to have three routines in a day (morning, afternoon, evening), it loads a motivational picture that you then must click out of to use the app again, and you have to wait a few seconds for it to even be close-able. I don’t need three motivational messages a day. So all in all, this app could benefit from simplifying its UI and content a bit. Being encouraged occasionally with small messages or goals or streaks along the way would be helpful, or at least the ability to customize or opt out of most of these features. Maybe I’ll check back in a few years.

title: Evidence-Based Behavioral Change
body:
I downloaded the Fabulous app not long after I finished reading Charles Duhigg’s “The Power of Habit: Why We Do What We Do in Life and Business.” Habit is the key to making lasting changes in behavior, and the Fabulous app is built on that simple fact. Step-by-step it introduces habits into every area of a daily routine, each one reinforcing the next, building success one habit at a time. 

The app’s genius is the series of “journeys” it leads you through tackling common problem areas like sleep habits, exercise habits, and food habits. Whole Day 1 was as simple as putting a glass of water next to my bed before sleep, just a few months later I was hopping on my exercise bike every morning! All along the way, the app was sequencing a set of “letters,” each containing information, encouragement, and insight into the science of behavioral change, timed to arrive right when I needed them.

If you’re already thinking about New Year’s resolutions, but worry that this year’s will just  be another false start, the Fabulous app is for you! #highlyrecommend

title: Very confusing app
body:
TLDR: NOPE.

- The app is really not intuitive, which is funny because behind all the motivational fluff it’s just a habit tracker and the biggest barrier to establishing good habits shouldn’t be the tool you’re trying to use.
- Premium doesn’t seem worth it. 
- Center the app around being able to create your own journey and offer pre-built journeys as another option for people who don’t know exactly what they want.

———

I like the idea of building morning rituals a lot and conceiving of building these habits as a “journey”. I also think the app *looks* simple to use.

It’s not though and aside from the concept I don’t care for much else. I gave the app a fair shot, spending 30 minutes trying to figure out what the tools are and trying to set up my journey. When I entered the app it was not clear that I could use the app without upgrading to premium. After that, there was absolutely no guidance on how to best use the app. The only intro given is more justification for why the app works.

The survey I took at the start to determine journey fit ended up not actually suiting my goals, and I struggled figure out how to edit the journey to include habits I actually wanted to build. I finally was able to add exercise to my list, but once I selected 7-minute workout as the type of exercise I wanted to engage in, I couldn’t figure out how to adjust it. To me building an exercise habit is an evolving process starting small and eventually building up to greater challenges. 

Premium doesn’t give you greater control, it just gives you access to preset journeys designed by someone who doesn’t know anything about me or my life. If you’re going to guide users through designed journeys that fit their goals, IMO it would be better to have them enter a workflow to select the behaviors they want to engage in, what their end goal looks like, and the make recommendations for how to set up the journey to get there incrementally. If I’m wrong about this, then that’s a problem with how you present your app and options.

Maybe recommend one goal to start with (I like drinking water as completely non-threatening goal to kick off the journey), and how to build from doing 10 sit-ups (for exercise) to working out for 30 minutes before work. Maybe the goal to start with is how to slowly adjust to waking up earlier so you actually have time to create the morning ritual that is the core of your premise. Michelle Obama might be used to waking up at 4:30AM, but I sure as hell am not.

If a dev happens to see this, a small part of why wellness apps like headspace are so widely popular is because they have a minimal, unique (but still fun!) look and feel that draws people in. Those visuals have a purpose too, they’re meant to calm the user and communicate a story. Purple haired girl does none of this. Weird letter reading VO does none of this. It’s distracting and strange.

The entire UX is a mess as well. There’s so many menus, choices, letters, buttons etc if this app is all about simplicity and not overwhelming the user with information to process. It’s unfortunately clear that whoever art directed this was non-existent or inexperienced. UX designers are not app developers. If you expect folks to pay $50 a year, these details really matter.

The app seems great other than that, but I just wish it had a simpler, more calming look and feel. (Because it’s meant to be a simple and calming app???) I couldn’t ever recommend it to anyone because it feels so cheap.

2. Screens hang up and I have to exit the app to reset.  I joined the recent no sugar challenge (great) but had to restart 4 times due to several of the mandatory accountability selections hung up and I had to exit the app.  The golden triangle shows a notification and so you select it and up pops a screen telling you to add an afternoon routine.  No thanks I think but there isn’t an option for no, so you have to hard kill the screen by exiting.  I have no other app issues with my iPhone and have the latest update of iOS and fabulous app. 

For the hefty price tag, the above issues are less tolerable than say a $10-20 investment — last greater flexibility for user selection would be great but very constraining set of choices.

title: Desperate to Change
body:

title: Must for anyone with Depression/Anxiety
body:
One of the things that stinks -literally- about mental illness is that sometimes I forget to shower, brush my teeth etc. Things that, as an adult, are disheartening and downright embarrassing to forget. I would try and try and dig myself further into a hole. Not with fabulous! This has literally changed my life. I now remember to do these things, and if I forget I know I did and check how I’m doing mentally (something I never did before).

 I get that a lot of people already drink water (the first challenge) but the point is to have something to check off and reward yourself for. If you have routines and things that you accomplish everyday, no matter how small, it is amazing how much it can increase your confidence. 

I have tried TONS of these types of apps, all felt overwhelming. And while some complain about the tricky navigation pages, they really help me as everything is minimal, warm, and calm in color. 

Now let’s talk about the deep work section y’all!!! It is amazing. I’m a student, and my greatest struggle is simply STARTING assignments. I get so anxious of failure that it can take me weeks to start something. I now have my own personal pep talk and guide to keep me on track.

Because of fabulous, my self care has improved, my school performance has improved, and my relationships have improved! I get the co$t is there but it is soooo worth it. Who would have thought an app could have so much impact. Please if you’re on the fence join! I’m in a better place because of it❤️

title: Not enough time to try
body:
I really regret spending money on this app. I can’t believe it’s $50 for the content. I took a leap of faith and gave them the benefit of the doubt because it’s a university or whatever. It’s so easy for the first week, then they pay gate you before you get to the actual meat of the app. I have been STUCK for MONTHS on the third week goals. Now it’s just a pest - nagging me every day for something I’m not committed to. I don’t feel like it’s working with me - it never offers to adjust the goals, or try something else since I’m clearly not keeping up with the very specific things it wants me to work on. I’m so mad I paid $50 for this. Also this app is just completely over designed. They try to get really fancy with the UI and gamification, but they are interrupting themselves to send you different messages. I’m never sure what’s the most important thing I’m supposed to be working on. 

My message to the developers is:
Extend the free trial period to 3 weeks
Cut down on the interface and the messages. Make it clear what to focus on. 
Keep up with your users. If they’re struggling, have the app sense that and try to work with them where they’re at.
Don’t pay gate it at $50 for a YEAR. Offer shorter subscription terms.

title: Do not try this app
body:
It’s not worth $60 and if you don’t cancel during the free trial they won’t give you your money back. They also don’t warn you that you’re going to be charged to give you a chance to cancel. They somehow have Apple manage the refund process and Apple deems the purchase not eligible for a refund. It’s a ripoff all around. Not a habit I intend to develop.

Fabulous has responded to this review. Basically, their position is that they make the terms of the free trial clear and that if you, the customer, fail to cancel the subscription 24 hours before the end of the 5 day trial, we’ll, you’ve just bought a 1 year subscription. Enjoy!

Of course they do all of that. But notice that you have to make a decision on your 5 day free trial in 4 days. Why not call it a 4 day trial? Because that would make it easier to remember to cancel it. 

This is the same approach that cable companies, phone companies, health insurers, and credit cards use to make the terms of their service complex enough that people fail to meet them and then in many cases can’t or won’t bother to escalate the issue to get the refund that they are entitled to if they don’t want the service.

That a company that’s supposed to be about helping it’s customers become more aware and develop better habits this is particularly egregious behavior.

These guys are fraudsters pure and simple.

title: It’s really Fabulous.
body:
Let me start by saying that I’ve been using the app for years, maybe from the very beginning of the app. I always change my habits and I always come back to this app. From Android to iOS.
I’m the kind of person that has potential but needs to be pushed to actually do something, I always hated that part of me, I can’t find time to actually do things like study, eat, read, and focus in my personal projects. 
I am a hardcore user of the app Any.do that helps me keep everything organized and to remind me of doing things, but they don’t tell me to do something to be healthier or to be more efficient. That’s where Fabulous comes to okay. It tells you to do simple things that will create habits, good habits, and it’s something you probably do by yourself but there are other tips and habits that you don’t do or do it in times where they’re not effective. Also the new live challenges they’re doing creating a community of people working together to reach a goal is something beautiful and I love it. 
I’ve beber bought premium mostly because in my current country I can’t spare money since our income is extremely low (Venezuela) but I’ve told a lot of people about the app and maybe they don’t buy premium either but it’s helping my coworkers and friends to live better and creating good habits. 
I thank the team behind Fabulous for not putting a High Paywall in the app so users like me can use the app. 
I really encourage people to get the premium, because the team deserves it. The letters they send are well crafted and on point. It’s not an app that tells you crap like you have to do this and that without proof or a base. I always search for things before actually do something and I love the tips Fabulous give.
Without a doubt Fabulous is a MUST in my phone.

title: It’s okay
body:
I like the concept and I’m sure it’s hard to organize an app like this but there’s a few kinks in it that makes it a little annoying.  After my trial, I thought I had unsubscribes but apparently not cuz it went thru anyway. I figured, what the hell I’ll give it a go since I have paid.  So either it isn’t user friendly or there is no end day with these challenges.  I thought I would be given progressive challenges but I still have ‘drink water’ on my list...yeah I’m over that.  Help me move on and incorporate healthy task to my day please lol
I have added some challenges to my list like the ‘one big one’...ok it helped me with being mindful of a big task to get done and completed it but then...yeah no progression and it just sits in my list.  
Added the financial task to my list.  I get...think about your debt.  Yeah I do every day, how about some advice or things to be mindful of?  If I could pay it off at once it wouldn’t be debt and it wouldn’t be in my task list.  
Don’t get me wrong, the app is cute and I do like the concept and I’m sure I am suppose to be doing the work.  It is my issues after all, but I wouldn’t have paid 50+ for a membership that is essentially just adding to my list of crap to do.  
I was hoping for something to give me pointers by giving progressive tips/task to accomplish a challenge in my life over a course of time. If that makes sense.  So a great starting point for someone to learn basic life skills.
Oooh what would be good it to have a spot for personalizing a task too.  So add to ‘lets exercise’ maybe the first one is to pick something to do for 5 min, then I could add sit ups.  Then progress from there.
author: Qwerty hiiiigh

title: One issue I see...
body: I started fabulous with an incredibly screwed up sleep schedule. And Fabulous seems to rely on me waking and going to sleep at the same time every day. Maybe have a pre-flight checklist that at least makes sure you’re sleeping normally if not helps you fix your sleep schedule. If I’ve been awake for 20 hours and I’m eating dinner at 10am when it’s reminding me about my morning routine... should I count that as my morning routine? That or even better—sync up with sleep tracking apps or track sleep within Fabulous using Apple Watch data and have the routines be dynamic based on that. Use that data to try to fix the sleep schedule and get the routines happening at the right time. I don’t really know what to enter when it asks me when I wake up and when I go to sleep. I wake up when I’m no longer tired and I go to sleep when I’m tired again.

The first “inspirational letter” told me I only needed to do one thing to be like.... and listed three white men who didn’t raise their kids. Yeah if you have a maid and a nanny this app will be relevant to you. If you already have fairly healthy habits like not going to bed at insane and irregular hours, never drinking water etc. it won’t. 

It’s obnoxious and pushy with purchases before you even see what’s in the app, and completely impractical to me as a mom.

title: Too corporate for genuine mindfulness
body:
The good: beautiful art design, clearly well founded in neuroscience. 
The bad: I would’ve loved to subscribe past the free trial period, but (paradoxically) the app has way too much sales promotion to ignore.  The “secret letters” one gets for achieving a goal are lovely encouragements, spoiled by the “special offer” of an annual subscription at the close of each letter. Likewise, the “info graphic”rewards are pretty pictures, which can’t be saved to one’d device but can be shared in a way that sends your friend to their site to buy the app. It just feels kinda manipulative and sleezy, but done so cleverly it should have an MBA watermark. 

If they’d offered a single month’s subscription option, I may have stayed with it to test this initial impression. But $60 for six months is too high a price to pay for a mindful app that seems to values corporate profit and performance enhancement over being here, now.

title: Great but glitchy
body:
TL;DR I like it, but many parts of the experience are irritating 

Pros: 
Helps establish new habits
Nice to be able to pause habit or complete at another time of the day and still get “credit” for doing it

Cons/Needs Fixed by Dev: 
Contact forms need to be replied to
Encouraging connection with others over the benefits of taking care of oneself 
Alarm/habit should be available users choosing (ie M-F only), and still recorded as “Golden triangle“

A friend recommended this app, and I signed up for the yearlong premium subscription to give it a whirl for even longer. 

During the first week I’ve reached out twice to ask what exactly I’m paying for. When I checked out the different purchase options through the App Store, there were something like eight different prices and titles. I wanted to know what was what. I’ve never heard back about what I am paying for, what the difference between the Fabulous Premium and Sphere are, etc. why do you give me a contact form if you won’t reply?

I’ve been using the app for almost the last month. I have found it really effective to help me develop certain habits. But just like other users have written, the alarms/habit settings are a little weird. Also it’s an all or nothing thing - you can have alarms/habits that go only on weekdays, but then you don’t get “credit” in the habit tracker for those if you don’t do them on weekends. That’s frustrating. Yes, I want to do “deep work“ every day of the week, but then I want the weekends off. 

Also, there is a major problem to me in the writings and encouragements. They are almost all written in a way that makes me feel like I should be doing more for other people. As a 40-year-old female empath, I do plenty for other people. Part of what I am personally working on is to take better care of myself. I literally just signed up for the meditation challenge, and was told that if I meditate regularly I’ll be able to care for other people EVEN MORE! I’ve been meditating on and off for years, have taken a long form face-to-face course in mindfulness based stress reduction, and would say having a mindfulness practice has changed my life for the better. What I would NOT say is that the main focus is to have more empathy, compassion and connection to others. It’s to have a mind that lets go.

Anyhow, my rant-y point is to say many of the challenges/journeys are really tilted towards connecting with others and doing more for others, and my guess is many users need to first help themselves. 

I also don’t like that occasionally I will find myself being forced to listen to something repeatedly, when all I want to do is accept the challenge. Additionally, there have been other times where I accidentally accepted something and didn’t get to read the blurb. I find it really bizarre that somethings are “letters“ and those are read out loud to me, while other times there are no letters included/the letter is only a written document. I’m sure there is some method to this madness, but I cannot figure it out. 

When being asked to choose three Super Powers to make my challenge succeed, I can never get the double alarm to work, not sure why it’s locked. Also those things feel so contrived and again, focused on others. I don’t like that once you choose a super power, you can’t unchoose it. I accidentally tapped one this morning, and I couldn’t get rid of it without canceling out of the entire challenge and starting over again. That felt quite frustrating. I wish the super powers changed between challenges too. 

I find the questions from other users to be bizarre, and the requirement that I use my full name and photograph to interact with the challenges to be frustrating. If I wanted social media, I would go to Facebook or Instagram and brag about my successes and document my challenges. Turns out you don’t have to include your full name or a photograph of your face, but, ugh!!

Sure, there are parts of this that would earn five stars to me. But there are parts that are so silly, I just can’t give it a five star rating. Maybe I’m not the “target market“ because I’m too old, and I grew up connecting with people face-to-face? I don’t really know. 

Anyhow, nice start The Fabulous, but consider making more of a focus on the actual science on the elements you’ve included.

title: Twitch streamer who NEEDED this
body:
Hey✌🏻 This app I needed. I’m a full time Twitch streamer and I needed this in my life. The first time I opened it up it started talking to me like it knew me, the struggles I was facing and what I needed. I shed a few tears honestly. I’ve recently lost sight of the purpose of a lot of things after going through a few rough times. Also full time streaming can cause you to loose track of a routine.
Losing the care to do certain things because the lack of purpose (from recent difficult personal things) I feel for it hasn’t been good for me. Not having the drive, but knowing something needs to change, I’m glad I found this app on Instagram. I love that I can set up routines and alarms for morning and evening. This is SO SO much better and WAY more interactive than alarm reminders because it’s AI talking to me, encouraging me, giving me gentle reminders to get up and do it. It’s almost psychological because I feel like it’s holding me accountable which I ultimately am holding myself accountable, if I’m making sense. 
Fascinating honestly. 
Its like the friend who’s there to give me encouragement but ultimately leaves it up to me. I also LOVE how it times you during the events during your routine & tells you good job after. Such a silly thing, but so helpful for me.👍🏼 
The different downloadable sessions of self care, exercise, imagination and breathing are FANTASTIC. It’s such a great distraction for me in the mornings because I struggle with negative thoughts when I wake up. I’m loving that it started me out small with just one thing (as to not get overwhelmed) as simple as drinking water in the morning then I was able to adjust and modify what I feel needs to change. 
I’m single and living with my own inner thoughts most of time so this has been a god sent for me to get back on a routine. Thank you Duke & Devs for thinking of people like me and others✌🏻 -DarkerOrc (Twitch)

title: Frustrating start to using the app
body:
I’ve bought the ticket and am taking the ride. The idea of a $50/year app makes me nervous, but the promise and reputation of the app has me taking the chance. 
I’ve only just started but I’m on rocky ground. Will upgrade my rating if things improve. 
First of all: no iPad version? For a paid app at this price, I can’t even use it on my iPad? OK...
After a fun and appealing onboarding process, you are left to your own devices with just one challenge to focus on your first three days of using the app: drinking water. Yup, no matter what goals you choose or how ready you are to start changing your habits, the app more or less forces you to begin your epic journey by drinking water for three days before the next challenge will unlock. If you navigate around to some less than obvious sections, you can “change your journey,” which luckily allows you to add another challenge to your routine (“write my daily to-do list,” thrilling). However, if you want to add another challenge to your routine to spice things up, you have to “change your journey” again, which just replaces the previous journey you were on. IE you can only be on one “Journey” at a time. Thank goodness it keeps the challenges, but now all the nifty audio guides and letters are pertinent only to the one journey you’re on. Look, maybe the extreme specificity is great for some people. But I’m young and willing to kickstart my “journey,” and Fabulous seems intent on slowing down that process as much as possible.

title: Useless for me
body:
During the few days I tried the app, I spent more time trying to figure out how to use it than actually developing good habits and routines. 

I can only imagine this being helpful if you have no self discipline and don't know that you're supposed to drink water. Maybe good for teenagers?

I couldn't even change the duration of a habit (I don't need a whole 25 minutes for a power nap lol) or customize an exercise (I already run several days a week, I would love to run faster/further but this only has exercise sessions to help you learn to start running). 

To get to the help section, you have to answer the same couple of "are you looking for help with XYZ specific problem" questions EVERY TIME, so if you're not looking for those few answers, you have to click thru several extra screens for no reason just to get to a FAQ section. 

The FAQ section has multiple instances of info in it that didn't even match the functions of the app (e.g. "click the plus sign on the right side" and there was no plus sign on that screen or "select XYZ option from the menu" and that option isn't in that menu). 

I'll stick with the "Productive" app. It's very intuitive, customizable, and has actually helped me do what I need to do without all this frustration.

title: Gas Lit To Good Behavior?
body:
I’ll start by saying that I’m still in the free trial stage of this app. I’ve used some of the  great features that they provide, and I’ve looked over the goals and journeys that they offer, and I’m really really impressed by this app. 

That being said, as others have pointed out, there is an odd, rather manipulative tone to the prompts in this app. Things like

“Good job! You’ve had water first thing in the morning for two days in a row, and you’re on you way to building great habits! Are you going to drink water tomorrow morning, and keep building your streak? 

- Yes! I’m Excited To Take Care Of My Body!
- No, I’m Not Going To Do That”

Sometimes it’s subtle, and sometimes it’s more overt, but there is a consistent feeling of reaffirming that the App knows best, and doing things differently is akin to throwing yourself away. 

Ultimately I canceled my subscription before they could charge me (I canceled through my iTunes account) because I need to feel like I can trust myself on this journey, which is not a feeling that this app inspires.

title: Wouldn’t Recommend
body:
This app has potentially to be something good. If it were a free app I would say it’s good for what it is. Like some others, I downloaded it to try it out and failed to cancel it before the subscription kicked in. Given that, I tried to make the best of it, since I’d already paid for it, and it was something I’d been interested in in the first place. However it is slowly proving more and more infuriating.

Issues:
1. It will constantly Flag you that something is wrong until you set up push notifications for it. I do not find push notifications helpful, as it becomes overwhelming quickly
2. Their prerecorded stretching/meditation sessions are jarring. With meditation, it will be silence, until a voice abruptly cuts in a startling fashion
3. It won’t let you uncheck tasks. It claims this is a feature “once you’ve committed to checking something off, that is a commitment you should keep.” Great, but I check it off accidentally and because I actually want to do the task, I’d actually like it to stay on my radar. What in the hell do they gain by stopping people from unchecking tasks?
4. There are these horrible screens that pop up when you’ve completed your task with a count and then a vapid quote. This is perfectly fine. My problem is that you cannot skip these. The quote will stay up until they decide to give you the x-out button. Be in the moment, fine, whatever, but often at the end of my tasks I’ve decided there’s another I want to add, and being forced to wait through 2 screens I can’t skip as a reward for doing well is irritating

I could overlook all of this if the app wasn’t designed to trick people into paying for it. I genuinely tried to make it work, but my breaking point was when they wouldn’t let me uncheck a task that I’d accidentally checked off while trying to start the timer. The entire app has a passive aggressive feel to its interaction with the user.

title: Noble cause. Terrible execution
body:

After 5 questions about what areas of your life you want to improve (yes/no), a screen comes up informing you of the $50 premium option. There’s no way I could find to continue in the app without agreeing to the premium subscription with 7 day trial. Once you agree, you’re taken into the main app dashboard where they have these things called journeys that you can supposedly customize. 

Only issue is that pretty much everything on the dashboard is locked until you complete the introductory journey, which takes a couple weeks. For the first 3 days all I can say is “yup, I drank water in the morning.” How am I to really assess the app when you provide (supposedly) a maimed version until after you take $50. I have no reason to believe it’s much better on the other side of my “secret letter” at the end of the introductory journey.

I really struggle to believe the behavioral psychology team at Duke has much input on this thing. It seems like it was put together by a money-grubbing undergraduate who did a summer research project in the lab.

title: Fabulous AND Sphere
body: I absolutely love this App and it’s programs.  They provide the motivation, scientific explanations, and reminders to focus and be successful in the goals I selected.  FABULOUS provides the base structures for learning how to change your habits or add new beneficial ones.  When you have learned and settled into your daily routines learned in Fabulous, you’ll know it’s time to take you to the next many levels by adding SPHERE programs.  They are the depth and breadth towards what you can accomplish and knowing who you are.  The most difficult thing is realizing these are not some simple scheduling or reminders applications - but behavior changing programs best accomplished one or two at a time.  They guide you through progress with a methodology that builds upon achievements towards your targeted objectives.  It will also recognize and help you through plateaus.  I have never used this word before in describing an App but THESE programs are truly existential.

body: This is a good idea, but the app isn't customizable for everyone. I find it very generalized and makes you rely too much on your phone to 'check off' your challenges. Even if you opt-in to a paid subscription, that doesn't unlock everything. I have to drink a glass of water every day for five days in order to unlock coaching? Cool, I do that already — all in all seems like a way to spend people's money and decide what's good for them.

title: Fabulous was good until I had to pay
Exceeds expectations
body:
I have to admit that my expectations for this program were very low. I get turned off by things that are touted as self help and are superficial and unrealistically optimistic. Life just isn’t great at every moment. I don’t improve everyday. I’m ok with that. But a lot of programs are not. This program strikes the right balance between recognition of struggle and the nobility of the effort needed to improve or more appropriately to become alive and awake. 

My one criticism is that it appears to let you add too many goals and journeys. Nothing turns a good program into just another monster like mission creep. So I have to police myself to not simply create and recreate the same self imploding list of perfection

title: Charged immediately! No refund!
body:

Here is the answer:
At the time of subscription, the date and amount of the charge(s) were stated. It was also stated that the subscription is automatically renewed until canceled, and includes that the subscription can be canceled at any time in the Google Play Store or App Store. For this reason, unfortunately, we are unable to offer a refund.
Basically, by downloading this app, you are throwing $50 to the street! This is ridiculous and non-sense. It is not about money anymore. This behavior is disgraceful and there should be a mechanism to protect consumers from companies like this one. I will keep looking for it.

title: Best Habit Forming App So Far
body:
So I’ve downloaded a few other habit-building/tracking apps in the past, since I’ve had trouble sticking to routines. None of them worked and I would forget about them after a few months.

So I was a little skeptical about Fabulous especially considering the price tag! I usually avoid subscription based apps like the plague but I figured “why not”. If I can drop $50+ on dinner with my girlfriend I can do $50 for an app that’ll help me build healthy habits.

I gotta say, so far I’m impressed. I completed the first journey, which helps you build a good morning routine. It starts very simple and small by getting you to drink water every day, and then eating a healthy breakfast, etc. Those habits are now ingrained in me and I do them without even thinking about it.

I’m now finishing up the exercise journey. I’ve lost 12 lbs so far, gained more muscle, and I’ve completely changed the way I look at exercising. I used to look at it as a chore, now I look at it as a privilege. 

Long story short....this app doesn’t just track habits and check them off like so many others. It gives you the reasoning and the WHY behind what you’re doing. Which keeps you engaged and motivated. Good stuff.

Lots of info abounds on how to pay them more money. 

 Also the first challenge is to drink water first thing in the morning but I’m already doing that. There was no obvious way for me to change it to something useful. Apparently this app thinks it already knows my life after the very shallow, short quiz they had me take in the beginning.

After reading some of the other reviews when people have complained about the value of the app versus the cost, the developer has responded that their app purchase was “optional.” Such an odd response. As far as I can see there is no way to try the app out without agreeing to pay $50 after a very short trial, which was difficult to figure out how to cancel. Are they saying, “We didn’t bend your arm to buy this app?” That’s their defense? So odd and not what I’d expect from a developer who claims to want to help people.

title: Best app on my phone
body:

Before Fabulous, I would wake up 10 minutes before I had to leave in the morning. I never ate breakfast, I didn’t make my bed or clean my room, I almost never had enough time to wash my face, and to be quite honest, I didn’t always remember brush my teeth. And it wasn’t just in the mornings that I struggled. During the day, I would hardly ever exercise outside of activities I needed to do, and overall I wasn’t making time for myself. 
Now, because of Fabulous, I have routines that I follow each morning, noon, and night that I customized to fit my interests and time schedule. I always remember to brush my teeth btw, along with many other things I used to struggle to do, and I’ve become more aware of my feelings, and my goals. I even feel that I have become more ambitious. I’m honestly super glad I got this app, and not only that, but I also highly recommend paying for the subscription. Through that, I got access to meditational practices, the ability to customize my routine, start new interests, and build many new habits besides the first sets. I just want to say, thank you so much for creating this app!

title: Disappointed, distracted app that still stresses running
body:
After I bought into the hype of this app several months ago, I found it virtually impossible to use as my job is demanding and I don’t have time to use the restroom over 8 or more hours.  I haven’t had a lunch break in three years and finally simply stopped trying to eat at all as I cannot find 10 minutes together where I can work and eat at the same time.  The app demands completion of tasks at exact times.  So, I’m out.  I could easily fulfill my habits if the app permitted me to enter them all at once at the end of the day, or at least as I got to them, earlier or later than scheduled.  But it’s not an option. 

I immediately complained about the stress on running as the ultimate habit.  I have severe early onset osteoarthritis in both knees. It’s genetic and even if I weren’t bone on bone in so much agony every moment that I cannot remember when I took Muay Thai during grad school getting my PhD and how awesome it felt.  How strong and muscular I was.  

The app also has a deluge of overly saturated colorful backgrounds that set my teeth on edge.  Each is a potential migraine.  But if you like running, a lot of jarring colors, and nothing in your life ever deviates from day to day to boring endless tedium, and you yourself have little creativity or drive to push yourself to expand your mind and abilities in ways that defy a regular schedule, then this is the app for you.  I have a few more months left on my subscription but have deleted it permanently.  I kept going back and nothing ever changed that would have made it slightly useful.
