title: App/concept is great but you've got 2b mentally prepared..there's no way to pause when life happens
body:
I was looking for something that would help me be reflective and deliberate in my habits/routine & life. This sounded great and it is..but I do feel I got baited as before I could evaluate whether it was an option for me & worth the $$, I was already being billed... AND the worst part is that there is absolutely no way to contact anyone to sort it out. 

I def felt like I got hustled but decided to tough it out since I guess the onus is on me to pay attention to the fine print. Wasn't the happiest but whatever, I decided to truly engage.

Then life got a bit hectic along w/ some unexpected events and I fell off my routine. I do plan on starting my journey again but I know that I have to mentally prepare myself (which is going to take a bit of time) for something like this to be effective. 

Changing behavior is ridiculously difficult & normally we are our own worst enemy.. I know I have to recenter myself before I re-embark on the journey to have even the slightest chance. Considering the cost & there doesn't seem to be a way to get your $$ back, I do feel like I should be able to use the app WHEN I'm prepared so that it'll be most effective for me. 

Right now, I have some work to do before I can open Fabulous & take it seriously. It will take me a few weeks at least. And so although I'm currently not using the app, its materials or any skills/knowledge from it, I've been paying $$ for a pretty icon for the past 2 months.

#tldr : I really really wish there was a way to pause my subscription (few weeks/months) until I know I am mentally prepared. Right now, I feel like I'm just throwing away $$$ on something I got pressured into.

title: Unsophisticated, useless, impossible to unsubscribe
body: The design of this app is lovely, and it claims to be based off of the research of a leading behavioral economics think tank but don’t let that fool you, the only thing sophisticated about this app is difficult it is to unsubscribe. Unable to find a prompt to do this in the profile or settings or in the app’s help section, I sent a message 4 days into my trial week period and received an automated « we’ll get back ». Yesterday I was charged for this useless app. If you’re like me, you eat well, sleep well, take vitamins, work out...this app will do nothing for you. It takes 3 days alone to « help » you build the habit of drinking water in the morning, which is no help at all of you already do it. The way I see it, perhaps six months in this app will be done « helping » me do the things I’ve already done for years and I can actually begin to fine tune my routine. If that weren’t bad enough, the app would not be complete with these pedantic « letters » it reads you advising you and congratulating you on all the things it helped you do. It takes so long to just confirm I drank water...did you? Did you really?...do you want to do it again?...how about breakfast? Do you like breakfast? Do you want to have it tomorrow? Do you like protein? Do you know what protein is? Let me list for you all the protein one could have for breakfast..(!!) I don’t know who this app is intended for, the person who needs positive reinforcement, from an app, to drink water and not eat a doughnut everyday for breakfast AND decided to get this app. If that’s not you, this app won’t work. Props to the design team! Love the icon! But that is quite literally all I liked about this app.

title: Agree with others: patronizing, limited, hard to cancel
body:
I agree with the many reviewers who rate the app poorly:

Patronizing: The pre-fab response button language is awful: “I want to exercise with my friend.” I have a solid, solo, headphones-in gym routine. Don’t talk down to users and don’t make me agree to a silly, set answer to use your app.  No one likes that kind of thing.

Limited and slow to start habits: this app  holds you back by not letting you select habits from the start. It forces a slow, small steps approach (Drink a glass of water, exercise for one minute) and won’t let you move forward faster. This is slow, frustrating, and gives user no agency.

Hard to cancel: the only way to cancel is to click the unsubscribe link in the email you receive confirming app.  There is no way to unsubscribe on the app itself.  Lots of reviewers are saying this and the company is not making cancellation more accessible.

This app basically made me realize I would appreciate a habits app, but one that allows me to structure the experience and doesn’t talk down to me.

title: How male-centered is this app?
body:
I just got this, really, I’ve only read the first letter. Right away though, the examples of successful people and their morning routines are all white males. It’s clear this app hopes to gain trust but building trust happens through relatable storytelling. From those examples it feels that this app is made for a male, with very goal oriented focus and no other pulls or concerns for others. How are Ernest Hemingway, Benjamin Franklin, or Steve Jobs (who clearly had no concern for those closest in his life) examples for others? Especially for a female, or anyone of color, or anyone of fluid gender, or any contemporary person? The main concern about what I’m trying out here with this app, is that without assurance of female examples, I’m not assured that the natural variations in the cycle of monthly living that females most strongly experience (though men experience this too in less overt ways) are not taken into account or were not part of the research. It feels as though this app is focused on male-centered performance. Many apps that I have tried tend to override, and not work in, the fact that one needs to listen to the needs of the moment while still maintaining self-care. That is a focus that is not only female, men need/want that too. ;)
Where are those good examples? What did Nanny of the Maroons do in the morning? Or what is Gloria Steinem‘s morning routine? Or Ru Paul? Or better yet, how about Tenzin Palmo? Or, even Oprah? Without better examples the inspiration falls flat and encourages apathy.

title: It’s a good start but has a long way to go. Do better.
body:
1) Why is it asking me to sign in when I look at my account (when I tap the person icon at top right of home screen)? I’ve already set up an account &, when I go to sign in, after I put my email in, the app tells me that I’m starting a new account. So, I stop signing in bc I don’t want to delete everything. Am I signed in or not?

2) There are habits that don’t always occur every day but are important to be mindful of. It’d be nice if we could set up habits that happen as frequently as we’d like (for example, once a week, I’ll create my own task to “go grocery shopping,” or twice a week, I’ll create my own task to, “water plants”). Stuff like that.

3) I read somewhere in your content overview map/letter no. 1 or something that this company, “has no ego.” Okay, everyone, even a monk, has an ego. That really gave me a laugh (& not in a good way). Maybe swap it out for, “we strive to contain our ego,” or, “we do our best to keep our egos in check.” 

4) Consider making your content mini-podcasts. You have a lot of content &, in this day & age, it’s *too much* stuff to consume. Keep the article format. Don’t get rid of that. But, go back & add in a way to hit play so we can listen to this on our daily drive to work or whatever. You’re already asking us to change our habits in the morning. Do you think we’ve got time to read your essay once we’re done? No. No one does.

5) I had a task appear for “exercise for 3 days,” this week w/ no warning & then disappear w/ no warning. You should announce new tasks/habits better after the completion of a new habit challenge. Where did my habit go? Will it come back? I’d like to do that habit w/o messing w/ your science of things. So, am I taking on too much if I do it anyway? These are all questions I have & don’t expect you to answer. But, I’m annoyed by this & hope you fix it/bring that habit back to me ASAP.

6) Your app layout is confusing, & I don’t understand all of the different areas you can go to nor why they are there. I suggest doing one of those “tap here to do this & this” walkthrough tutorials at the start of every new sign up. To fix the confusion now, next time you update, just do that for all users. Like, what am I supposed to do with the content that’s there right now or the challenges or journeys or whatever?? It’s frustrating & you guys talk yourselves up A LOT. Meet your own standards.

7) Stop trying to jock so hard on peer to peer marketing. It’s messed up. If you’re so good, you’ll succeed. Stop trying to force my friends to sign up for your app. If community is really so helpful to success, build a buddy system w/in the app. I’m serious, it’s a good idea. You’re welcome. (&, while we’re at it, don’t tell us to go visit your Instagram all the time). I want to feel like you guys care but, between your over-inflated egos & over-kill marketing, you really just make me feel like I’m a number & a dollar figure to you. Which, as a business, even if you say it’s not true, I know is. But, if you want to keep claiming you care, then act like it.

title: Money grab preying on people’s insecurities.....
body:
The app is pure at its core, based upon what its mission statement is.  However, the mechanics of the app and all of the subscription offers attached to each message you receive, say otherwise. 

I was really excited when I downloaded the app and setup my profile.  Once I was finished it took me through my 1st journey. Drinking water.  I get what the premise of this exercise was getting at and I played along.  Once complete, it took me to my first message.  Which explained that If i wanted the full benefits and access to premium journeys to sign up for $49.99 a year. Ok cool I can do that plus there is a 7 day trial.  

So I click out of the message to explore the app a bit before I make a decision.  I go into another message titled, “Your Personalized Journey.” I read a bit of it and scroll down a bit more and there’s another offer that says 2 week trial offer for some Sphere something or other.  So I’m like cool, i can try it out for 2 weeks instead of 7 days.  I click it because hey this just became a better deal I’ll try it out.  So I click the link to subscribe and what do I see but. Change in the price.  This pop up stated it would by a free trial for 2 weeks and then $12.99/Month for access to the Sphere whatchamacalit.  So I exit out and go to the first message again and then it clicked.  MONEY GRAB.

Issa MONEY GRAB.  I can accept one fee for everything your seeking to these people.  But you guys are not only asking for an annual fee to get this help you’re offering to be better and more functional humans.  But then you want people to also cough up more money every month.  ON TOP PF THE FACT THAT THOUGH THIS IS, “SUPPOSED,” scientific data, you’re a operated by students, professors and or faculty of a university.  Not that I’m questioning your credentials, but who is to say you aren’t some failed psychologist who is trying to milk people on their insecurities and their money. 

I just do not understand how you’re really helping people with what you’re doing.  Death to in app purchases.  Quality used to be built into what you were buying.  Not just a garnish that you have to pay $.99-$49.99 to experience.

title: Game changer for ADHD
body:
This app has two key positives that make all the difference in managing ADHD. 

1) Helps you build actions into rituals, in a simple way, long enough to become a habit, or more like one than I’ve ever had in my life previously. 

It might sound insane to say that I’ve never been able to drink water when I wake up, floss my teeth everyday, or know where my house key is. But if you have ADHD you probably understand, and thanks to using the tools in this app, I not only perform these reliably, but can get back on track if things start to go a bit haywire. 

2) Encourages positive self feedback. In addition to congratulating yourself for completion on a day to day basis, you might start to actually feel that you can rely on yourself. I did. I’ve generally felt like an out of control wreck my whole life, but strangely after a few weeks of drinking water and flossing my teeth I thought I could manage eating breakfast. These baby steps eventually included daily yoga and meditation, something I’ve wished for for two decades. 

I’m significantly less afraid to attempt change in my life, knowing I can get back to my routines and alter them if need be depending on changing circumstances. 

Fabulous isn’t a perfect app. It’s simple but the user interface isn’t always intuitive. Sphere costs money, and I think the true worth of the app is in Sphere. The golden triangle feature bugs me because it gives you a quote and a long loading period which you can’t turn off (and a choice to share to social media which I dislike). Although I understand the reasoning behind exercise being one of the first priorities, this did not personally work for me, and I chose to add exercise in during the mental toughness journey, having enough skills to actually fulfill my word. 

One size might mostly fit all, but despite it’s heavily designed nature, it’s up to you to use the app as a tool for yourself. Fabulous gives enough variety within it’s practice makes perfect scheme to make it a powerful ally.

title: LONG BUT IMPORTANT: Enjoy the free content as quickly as possible
body:
I think I know what people’s problems with this app is. I’ve had it on my phone for a month and fell off the wagon once the trial was up. I have a solution to people who want to enjoy this app’s free content. First, it requires you to sign up for a 7 day free trial, which will be renewed automatically if you don’t cancel before then. As soon as you sign up, go into wherever your purchases are stored on your phone, and cancel the subscription right away. You will still get the 7 day free trial.
It’s duplicitous to say it’s $4 per month for 12 months to pay but put in the fine print “One time purchase” meaning you’re actually paying 50 dollars once your trial is up, and it breaks down to $4 a month. ( I see they’ve since fixed this but when I was signing up, it was deceiving.)
The paid for content is too wordy and grasping for a deeper spiritual meaning. While that’s great, because I’m all about deeper reflection, it’s not what most people want based on these reviews. 

For the users: During your 7 day free trial, there’s an Plus symbol to add additional habits. I would add any and every daily task that you would possibly do. I added a few things and thought great! However, once the trial’s up, you can no longer utilize creating your own habits. Just the default ones and the ones you have previously made. So if you want to keep using the app because it’s helpful, write out all the habits to add before your trial ends. Since the developers read and respond to these reviews, if they advise anyone not to do this or discontinue that ability, then that should be a huge red flag for anyone reading this. 

One other thing, there’s an overwhelming and I do mean overwhelming amount of people complaining about being charged after 7 days, and of the cost. The terms of what is and is not available after 7 days is not clear. All it says is Sphere access. While I took some time to explore Sphere while I could, it was too much, Fabulous, the app itself with the day-to-day habits—is what is most enjoyable and useful. The reviews reflect that, yet the developers are still trying to make people pay over 50 dollars in one sitting. I pay less than that on a TRUE monthly basis, for 200GB or additional cloud storage for my iPhone. Wanted to add post review: it looks like now there is a monthly option of 14.99 or $50 a year. Still too much. You can enjoy Pandora Premium for less than that per month. 

Nothing should be completely free, but this app needs to adjust its price point. It just does.  Also, restricting the abilities of the Fabulous app once it’s past the 7 day trial is kinda sleazy.

The content of Fabulous should remain as it is, allowing people to use it. The paid for content should be absolutely stellar to demand the price its asking for.  More people will think about buying the paid content, if the developers were more clear about what is and isn’t being offered. In fact, a chart with a list of exact features is what most subscriptions do. This one is too confusing.

One last thing, and others have also commented on this. The developers reply to the reviews here. There’s a tone, while well-meaning, that just doesn’t rub me the right way. They comment to people like they just don’t understand the greatness of the app and to give them another try, instead of acknowledging they will work to make the terms of conditions and features more easily understood. 

Allow people to change their habits with the free content after the 7 day free trial. Make a list of features and the differences for both Fabulous and Sphere. Offer the app for less than 14.99 monthly or a one time payment of $50.

That said. I will happily change this review to 5 stars, if they change the Fabulous feature to allow people to adjust their personal habits after the 7 day free trial. This is a great app, but the mechanics of payment and the features offered need to be presented better.

title: Great Potential, Poor Execution and Shadiness
body:
To begin with I heard about this app from a friend who recommended it to me. Knew I would love a solid habit tracker and so decided to check it out. 

Now first thing I noticed was as soon as I downloaded and began, they had a mix of questions and quotes... like a lot of them. 

Afterwards they go straight to advertising claiming 7-day free trial then about $50 for a year or just by the monthly for about $5. Right away coming from a business standpoint, I saw this “shadiness” at the wording and that got me thinking about other hidden psychological tricks used. Well you darn bet I was going to investigate so I dropped the $5 for monthly.

Now it was not even 5 minutes into it that all things went downhill. Firstly, I knew a set of habits I was doing and wanted to add but there is no feature for adding your own habits. One must follow the habits they recommend one at a time (My first habit was drinking water every morning... for THREE days straight before another habit was added). Now I get the principals behind it that habits must be built upon step-by-step gradually but I believe the least the should allow is to add previous habits your currently building first then their recommended.

Now here is where alarm bells were ringing. After setting up my “Drinking Water Every Morning” habit, even before completing, they advertise about an upgrade from premium to some social circle for more content. Right way I was outraged and decided to check the difference between “regular premium” and “the upgrade”. Honestly the information was extremely vague.

Lastly, during this entire process, not once would they allow you to close the app. Now what I mean here is that there will always be some sort of pop up. From quotes and music, to videos, to notifying you on all features of the apps. I spent a solid half hour seeing when it would stop until my patience wore out and I forcefully exited the app. Now I can see the quotes being motivational but using them repetitively can have opposite effects.

Overall, good idea but poor execution. I’m just seeing this as an app with its first priority in creating cash flow followed by the actual habit tracker all covered by fanciful/motivational quotes and music.

UPDATE: Just went to cancel my subscription on IOS and I saw they had me down on the yearly service even though I payed for the monthly service. To top it off they had tens of options working it such as “Sphere Monthly”, “Sphere: Monthly (50% off)”, and yearly and what not. It seems like there is no clear definition on those services and now I’m sure this is a scam. Thank god I canceled prior to the 7 day free trial. Will also follow up why they took $4.75 from me and still had me on the free trial paying $50 in two days...

title: Life changing
body:
With a toddler, full-time job and 2 smaller side job/hobbies I never had time for with managing my household, I would say I was already very organized but Fabulous took me to the next level. Been using it a month and here’s what I like. Fabulous removes the mental load, that feeling that I’m busy focusing on the urgent thus always forgetting to do things that are theoretically important to me or my health. Having created Fabulous routines for Morning, Workday, Afternoon, and Evening, I accounted for every activity ideal to my day (even things like teethbrushing, eating more fruit, learning, plus goals that I would otherwise see no progress on). Scheduling even a meager amount of time for important activities daily gives me confidence it will add up over time and helps me get started, which is often the hardest part. (I’ve resisted packing my routine so full that I can’t continue on with something if I get engrossed). I also added some of the suggested minute tasks like deep breathing, a minute stretch, asking what is my purpose?, identify top 3 tasks, what inspires me, and more... these have turned out to be powerful refocusers that help me turn the corner to the next task instead of retreating to social media for a break (the black hole time sink lol). For days I continuously adjusted the order of my tasks, which routine they belonged on, duration, and how much structure was helpful vs. overwhelming, trying to feel out what puts me in a nice flow. I don’t have to do it in exact order, you get the idea. The important part is Fabulous shows you how long each routine takes overall (helpful for knowing if you overcommitted your time), so I had to admit to myself what I really had time for and settle for the realistic, knowing I would still be making progress. If something’s not working I keep making changes, which involves also changing my expectations (another powerful and unexpected side effect). Now I have confidence my routine is feasible and I even have time to sneak in social media/YouTube/text/calls without letting those overrun my day. When work gets crazy and I miss completing items on overwhelming days (or days I’m not on my A game), it doesn’t matter because Fabulous routines still make me more productive at work and life than I otherwise would be (and stay calmer and less overwhelmed), so it’s a win! Even after discouraging days I know my Fabulous routines are always ready to support my optimal day tomorrow, rather than having to waste time brainstorming it AGAIN and get motivated AGAIN to somehow keep it all in mind. Every day, I get to start over and probably do a little better, which is what I’m experiencing with Fabulous. Developing an optimal personalized routine is key!  But, Fabulous helps you build a routine slowly from the ground up and tells you the reasons behind each suggested item. The app also gives you guided meditation and  exercise sessions, motivational material and more. Really perfect for anyone wanting to see what they’re capable of if they let Fabulous assume the mental load for them. Worth every cent. 

I really haven’t found a downside, however, in reading the reviews I might be using it a little differently than others. I’d advise adding a few of your own daily tasks right away if you’re ready for that. The app has you start with drinking a glass of water when you wake up, and add other similar things slowly. As someone who was ready and needing to tackle my unique day, that would have been painfully slow for me. But it’s definitely an app that will not overwhelm you and is great for creating a foundation. 

I have 2 feature suggestions I would love to see: 1) A soft chime when a task countdown timer is over. Because for tasks like reading, meditation, deep focus and more, it’s not enjoyable when I have to keep watching the clock and can’t lose myself in those tasks. Kind of defeats the purpose. 2) As I check off tasks in my routine, I would LOVE to see the routine “duration” total decrease to represent how much time the remaining tasks will take. That would be empowering, and also extremely helpful. If for example I have 2 more hours to complete my morning routine before leaving for work, I’d like to be able to continuously see what my remaining total task duration is so I know if I’m over or under and know how to pace myself without having to add it up over and over. 

Lastly, the genuine passion of the developer for this subject is apparent (she writes letters to us). We’re in capable hands. Here’s to enjoying the journey. You got this!

title: Four stars. Developers: one small improvement for 5
body:
One of my favorite things about this app is how aggressively it makes you commit to yourself. Reiterated “Are you sure you will commit to this 100%?” Or “Do you promise you will do this, no matter what?”. Then it will typically ask you a second time. It makes me feel as though there is a party to whom I am accountable besides myself, which is the primary thing other apps haven’t provided me with. 

The interface is a little obtuse, but that’s supposed to be part of it. I’m retraining myself to build and maintain willpower and habits, and my takeaway is that I need to be teaching myself new visual and neural pathways. 

The app is unique in that I’m treated very individualistically. I’m addressed by my first name, next steps in the program are called “my sphere” and even though I know the app isn’t an immediate support network, I’m given the warm fuzzy that there’s someone supporting me. 

The app provides you with staggered “Spheres”, which are 22 day (the length of time it takes to build a habit) journeys down which you’ll focus on a suite of related daily habits and rituals of a particular theme. Beginning with “Building an exercise habit”, Fabulous leads you through a wide range of others like “Better sleep”, “Better eating”, “Focus and time management”, and “Mindfulness”. These are introduced in what seems like a predetermined order, and are meant to completely transform you into a “Fabulous” new you, hence the name. 

You are also given the option to build your own morning and evening routine from a variety of different prefabricated tasks. There is a reminder, and a graphic interface reinforcing how many days you’ve done said tasks in a row. You can add as many or as few as you like. 

Every few days, you’re given an “individualized” letter, briefly showcasing previews of the things you’ll be seeing in the proceeding “spheres”.

This is where my one piece of feedback for the developers lies, and how they can earn that fifth star. While this letters contain motivational quotes, stories about strong and successful people and their habits that are pertinent to this “sphere”, and personalized “attaboy, you can do this” messages, there is one problem. The end of these letters break the immersion with a very abrupt change in tone by turning all the message and warm fuzzies into a sales pitch for a “special deal” to save on a years subscription. 

“(Your name), we believe in you so much, we’d like to offer you an exclusive special deal, X% off a subscription”.

I acknowledge this platform is a business, and subscriptions are the backbone of what drives said business. That’s not the issue. The issue is that for every letter I receive, I’m motivated until I reach the end.

Understandably, these things drive this business, and at some point are necessary. However, having them staggered over the course of these personal letters (i.e. Every 4th or 5th letter) would do a lot to allow me to feel as though the letters are genuine, and not to interrupt my feeling of immersion. 

Four stars, five if that one issue is addressed.

title: Not Fully Convinced
body:
I just started Fabulous today. I was immediately drawn to the concept and presentation and was looking forward to getting into it. I’ve been coping with a chronic illness for going on 7 years now and I’m finally trying to get my spiraling mental well-being and physical state under control, so this seemed like a really good way to take steps towards that.

First off, the app is not free. It is $50 a year with a subscription. That’s not what I have a problem with, I’m just throwing it out there. My initial reaction to the price tag was that if this works for me, $50 is a small price and will put me in a committed mindset. The thing that rubbed me the wrong way, however, is that Fabulous gives you a 1 week free trial, but then asks you to try it for two weeks to see results. I don’t think trying something for two weeks is unreasonable at all, but if you’re going to ask me to pay for a year, why not give me a two week trial so that I can get a taste of the changes I could experience?

This was made worse by the fact that when I exited the app it forgot all of my information and actually asked me to subscribe again, so now I’m actually not sure what to do. That’s a pretty big error. 

I will still stick with it for a bit and see if it’s something I could benefit from, however, even just in the details of the apps presentation it started to bother me. 

On the apps first challenge for me it asked me to drink water when I first wake up. Ok, easy enough. But I notice a button that says “why am I being asked to do this?” I click it, not because I’m being pedantic but because I’m curious about the benefits of what they’re telling me to do. The answer? “I know, I know. It seems too simple. But just do it.” Hate. Why even let me ask why if this is the answer you’re going to give? The worst thing is in the letter they give you later there IS an answer. Your body wakes up dehydrated and needs to rehydrate, so by drinking first thing, you start of doing something positive instead of negative. 

Like I said, I’ll still give the app a chance, it just hasn’t made a very good first impression.

title: Ok if you like to be manipulated
body:
I'm all for a little extra motivation, and I've been flagging lately in some of my fitness habits, so I thought I'd give this a go. For starters, I found it frustrating that I couldn't begin where I wanted. I'm not great at drinking enough water, so ok, that's a good first goal, but the second and third were things I was already doing. I didn't need those reinforcements. I was glad I could at least add my own afternoon and evening goals. 

My real frustration, though, was with the "motivational" letters and suggestions within the app. The app is heavy on daily recommitment: when you mark a daily task as completed, a window pops up that insists you choose between, "I will do this again tomorrow," or "No, I do not want to succeed." Seriously with that wording? Back off. 🙄

There's also a daily or semi-daily prompt, similarly worded, that wants you to join a group, insisting that people really only succeed when they have to be accountable to other people. This is likely true for some personality types, but not all. If you prefer not to join a group, you have to click that you "Do not believe this" thing they're insisting is fact, like your some kind of flat-earther dolt. I ignored it a few times but finally I installed because I was so disgusted. 

Not sure how any of it is helpful, but as someone who's lost nearly 100 pounds under my own steam, I guess maybe I don't really need that much help with willpower so I'll survive.

I just got this app this morning so I’m basing my rating on user friendliness/ set up/ and its ability to hold my attention. The app kept me going, probably one of the easiest apps I’ve set up, definitely one of the fastest. Some apps can be work in just filling out the info but, this app was smooth & explained things clearly. I’m looking forward to seeing how this goes. I need something motivating in my life right now and I’m hoping this does the trick. I had always been a very disciplined, driven, fun, outspoken, and in great shape but, the last 18 mos~things have become very difficult for me. I had several big surgeries which left me in lots of pain but this pain is nothing compared to the pain in my heart... after loosing 3 loving people in our family. As my dad use to say... “Life happens kiddo”, but it seems I let it go on w/o me. I’m really hoping to find my fire again and hoping it’s as easy as finding this app~ something tells me... it’s not. All life’s greatest things~take work and I’m now desperate & willing~ just need reminders to keep going and I hope this app is a piece of the puzzle which makes the difficult times bearable. So, I plan on updating this review a few times, as I embark on my journey to become the once driven person I was~ 
so until then...

title: Feel like I’m being ‘nudged’ a little too much
body:
It’s clear that the authors of the app are using all the coercive approaches espoused by behavioral economists: from the pricing scheme ($15 a month vs $50 for the year is a classic trick that Dan Ariely writes about in the first chapter of his book) to being completely unable to find out how to cancel the subscription once you start the free service (I’ve emailed, messaged on social media, not in the iTunes subscription list that I have, no where to be found). All of this makes me feel like they’re ‘nudging’ me into buying their service more than I would like. Furthermore, their pricing scheme is very opaque. Why is a sphere membership separate from a regular membership? Please be transparent and honest in how the pricing works and what we get.

Let me be clear: the idea is great but the implementation is lacking. First, a minor annoyance, but even if you mute all the sounds within the app and have your phone on vibrate, the sounds will still play. This is ridiculously annoying in public spaces especially since sounds add nothing to the experience. 

You can’t load more than 1 journey at a time to see all your to-dos in a given day. I appreciate the idea behind this (don’t do too much at once) but I would like the option to do at least 2 unrelated journeys at the same time (energized and focus journeys, for example).

 I’m writing this because the opaque pay structure and they rope you into a subscription service that’s hard to figure out how to cancel. Please be transparent in your business practices.

title: Fabulous is a mediocre app cloaked in hype
body:
I’m still in my seven-day trial, so it’s possible I may change my opinion, but Fabulous seems more hyped than useful. What it has is a perfectly ordinary habit reminder function, some constructed plans for adding habits (“journeys”), and some videos for various things, like diet, exercise and meditation. Putting together a package like this is a good idea, but the core habit reminder function is weak. You have morning, afternoon and evening blocks, each intended to be a single time block with activities carried out always in the same order. The app times them for you. You have some flexibility, but not as much as with a typical habit tracker. I had trouble with the Watch app, and the different parts of the iPhone app are not all that well integrated.

The big problem for me is that the app is transparently bent on conditioning you to respond as it wants you to, asking for trust and agreement, offering praise and reward. The use of music and pictures makes it a little more sophisticated than a used car salesman or someone selling insurance door-to-door, but the principles are old as dirt. Now you might say it’s for a good cause, but the psychological aspects are too unsubtle and the app too inflexible for me.

title: Everything I Need
body:
This is such a great app for changing habits. I’ve tried building good habits and breaking bad ones before, but It’s never worked out. I always start strong as everyone does, waking up early, working out, meal prepping the whole week, drinking plenty of water, using all of my free time studying, but I always burned out within a week or so. I did this so often that my family knows me as the guy who doesn’t really follow through on anything but gets excited by everything. 

Fabulous is different though. It starts you off really slowly and adds habits to your routine when you’re ready to start making it long term. It was sort of difficult for me to start a program that goes so slow because I’m so excited to get started with all of the big life changing habits, but it’s been great. It’s helped me determine my difficulties with each little habit one at a time so that once I get to the daily routine that I’m working toward, I won’t have a hundred different little difficulties. 

The motivation from the app has also been pretty great. It gives you little articles on why the habits you’re building are great ones and even how to make it easier or just different ways to do them. 

And not that this is that important for the goals or anything, but the app is super well designed! I just really enjoy the look and feel of the whole thing.

Can’t wait to see where this app takes me 😊

title: how to cancel in free-trial period!
body:
to save everyone a little heartache, here is a step-by-step to cancel your subscription to Fabulous during your 7-day “free” trial period:

1. open Settings
2. tap iTunes & App Store
3. select your Apple ID
4. click View Apple ID
5. find Subscriptions
6. press the subscription you’d like to cancel

voila! happy canceling, y’all.

Developers, please tone down the motivational, rainbows and butterflies, speech; you sound like a mix between Joel Osteen and a greasy car salesman (if there’s a difference). Also, what’s with some of the sound effects? A woman (?) sighing when I touch the screen on my evening routine does not relieve stress, it weirds me out. 

I think the biggest improvement, however, would be to enable the user to vary their routines on different days. For instance, I may not have to rush through my tea and breakfast as fast on a Saturday as I do on a week day. Maybe that’s already possible to do in this app but I haven’t been able to figure it out.

title: Looking for a new planner...
body:
I love the idea. It’s motivational with telling you in the beginning about how famous people get their day started for success. The usability is difficult to navigate for those not willing to explore & just push buttons. You can’t uncheck things. 

I discovered that it does not ring or notify you when you set alarms when phone is locked or sleeping. It also does not indicate where to go to next after the first three days. 

It also asks you to make a commitment with them for a premium subscription for $50, in an odd way. You don’t know exactly what you are getting. There is mystery and secrets wrapped around this app. Your journey changes as you go, but you feel as if you are leaning on a total stranger. 

I canceled in 5 days without an issue-I simply went to my welcome email letter from apple that shows your subscribed trial purchase, and clicked “cancel subscription”. Not an issue if you do it before 7 days. 

I was sad to cancel it, but $50 is a bit much when other apps are free or about $4.99 permanently. This seems more like a program with the university-possibly even Illuminati elites-the whole triangle symbolism and very elitist feeling of Duke University is strange. 

You feel somewhat brought into a secret, yet kept outside of it. You don’t know at all where you are headed, except for promises of a better you-very mysterious. 

There is good mysterious and then there is just confusing mystery-this app is more confusing than helpful I find. 

If you like a more laid out “without mystery” normal planner & organizer, then this is not a good fit. This app will not tell you anything and if you push the wrong button it leaves you sitting wondering where you go next. 

I actually on the fourth day of having it, had to reset everything and start over with the water journey, due to missing the checkins and notifications that alert me for my day. 

In the end, it was too bizarre to pay $50 for. They invite you to meet the makers at Duke University. I just don’t feel this app was made for the normal masses-it is very elitist and just a bit “occultic” in its operation. I really don’t like the pyramid symbolism everywhere-the Book of the Dead was terrible for the masses-please stop with pyramids everywhere in this app and world. It’s not a sacred shape. I am happy Ancient Egypt is gone...those pharaohs were slave drivers. 

I may be back-if I can find motivation to pay $50, but first I am shopping the other apps available. Just being honest, because that is my personal journey to a fabulous me.

title: I love this app but had to give it two stars...
body:

So at this point, I just decided to stick with the premium membership. It was alright; the real meat of the app is the free content in my opinion but I can see what others would enjoy it.  I recently got a brand new phone and when I redownloaded the app, my premium membership has disappeared! So not only was I halfway duped into the expensive membership, I can’t even use it anymore and there seems to be no technical support or methods or recourse. I am very disappointed by this.

Let me be clear: this is a great app! I am just a little concerned about some business practices that at face value seem a little bit shady. If this was not an issue, I would give it 5 stars. If the developers read this review and are able to fix my issues, I would be more than happy to adjust my rating. Heck, it’s probably user error on my end! I just need a little assistance getting things fixed. 

I give it a firm but fair two stars.

title: Feeling Fabulous
body: What a wonderful app!! After meeting my first goal, I knew how easy motivation and self-improvement could be through this app. Soon, I started creating morning, afternoon and night routines. With alarms to help you stay on track, you complete everything you need to do in your amount of time. One thing I love is that it is all based around how you work. Plus, your daily goals aren’t a pain, difficult or time consuming so if you can’t complete them, you have no excuse as why. Not to mention, I have had this app for about 5 days, and I can see the difference in my lifestyle already. My first goal was to drink water as soon as I woke up every morning for three days straight and now I find myself constantly reaching for a bottle of water over a sugary lemonade or cherry coke. Honestly, it’s a reward when you get to check off your steps at the end of the day and say, “Yeah, I met my goal, and tomorrow I’m going to do the same.” Adding new goals within your schedule suddenly isn’t an anxiety attack but a fun challenge as “I wonder what I’m going to improve on today.” Plus, I’m in school so after doing a lot of things I don’t want to do, I would get caught in a bad mood. But after downloading the app and adding “I Feel Great Today” to my morning routine, I usually feel better and I’m calmer. Congratulations if you made it to the end of this paragraph. Anyways, I highly recommend the app and all it has to offer!! #notsponsered This will clean your life up, make you feel more motivated and have self-improvement!! Now I understand why the app was named “Fabulous” in the first place, but that’s because about after a week, that’s how you’ll be feeling! Fantastic, truly fabulous!!!

title: Research proven method works amazingly in improving my morning.
body:
I feel like the premise behind Fabulous has been done a million times. I think I see a new habit tracker show up my app feed every week. This happened to be the app of the day so I figured out I'd try it out. 

The first day of using it I thought it was a little childish; the colors and music were not like any other habit tracker I had used. There was lots of text and at the end of it the only habit I could track was drinking water in the morning. "That's dumb" I thought but gave it a try anyways. 

Over the next three days I added a few more habits. The tasks might not be something incredible but I've started to feel different. The app has a certain je ne sais quoi, and it's helped me feel more accomplished every day. The small "simple" tasks all sum up to a bigger change. My wife even commented that Im more awake and happy in the morning after checking off my morning routine. 

TL;DR
The app's scientific process of incremental small changes has helped me be happier and more productive in the morning.

title: Bad Role Models
body:
Yeah... I was with this app until I got my first letter saying “What do Winston Churchill, Ben Franklin, and Steve Jobs all have in common? Daily routines”

I’m sorry, you want me to model myself after Winston Churchill, an alcoholic egomaniac that almost destroyed the country with more needless wars, was obese, and was hated by everyone who had to deal with him. Or Ben Franklin, who was discovered to have the bodies of over a dozen young boys buried in his basement? Or how about Steve Jobs? A guy so full of himself and so abusive that he thought his own daughter was trying to get money out of him when all she wanted was a dad? Also, couldn’t find any amazing WOMEN to model after? That’s your target audience. I REFUSE ON PRINCIPLE to pay for an app that didn’t even do the slightest bit of research. I don’t trust this app. You shouldn’t either. And you most certainly shouldn’t take advice from it or give it your money. Try a dietician... available with most health insurance plans. Cheap yoga classes also exist. And the internet exists, as well. You should formulate your own diet and health plan and stick to it. Look at Google Scholar and read the latest research and find the best way for you to become healthy and keep doing it until you see results. You don’t need this app. No one does. And no one needs to be fed bad information. That’s the most dangerous health problem of all- misinformation.

Had to give this more than 4 stars to be posted. Also proof you can’t trust this company.

title: This is a life changer
body: As a sophomore in high school who is currently taking ap classes and college courses while still trying to be mentally and physically healthy, this is it. When I was a freshmen I LONGED for a way to engage myself in my studies and my mental/physical health. I had to find an equilibrium. I had no motivation or reason to try at anything. I was looking for help everywhere: talked to my parents, friends, counselors, and a crisis hotline. I couldn’t find a solution so I pushed myself to do a lot of good habits, but in the end, it only deprived me of my motivation and will. I was overwhelming myself as I wanted to find a solution to my ailment. An ailment that ruins many lives. Lives ruined by procrastination. Now as I was looking for help online, I came across fabulous. The app seemed to good to be true and I gave it a shot for my own well being. Needless to say, I am grateful for this. As of now I have completed the courses: “An Unexpected Journey” and “Staying on the Road.” I’m currently doing “A Fabulous Night.” I know it sounds cliche of me to say this but it has changed my life for the better. I now feel happier, motivated, focused, confident, and passionate about my studies and life. Whether you’re 16, a middle aged person, or in your late years of life, it truly never is too late to help yourself and nourish as an individual. 10/10

title: Love it
body:
I love this app sooo much. It’s really helped me develop strong habits— such that I basically know my daily routines by heart, and do them instinctively now! Even writing in my journal, something I always forgot/got too lazy to do. I immediately shelled out money for the paid subscription because I liked the features so much, and I’m glad I did. 

The app guides you gradually through different self-improvement processes (exercise, developing willpower and work ethic, eating healthy, going to bed on time) and goes very in-depth, sending letters and homework that is usually insightful. 

The paid version also comes with several fun meditations, work timers (which begin with solemn oaths to work hard and other fun warmups), interactive segments, and even practices to help you rekindle inspiration, get over your negative thoughts, and reassess your problem solving skills. Even though the work timer is glitchy, I absolutely adore this app and recommend it to everyone.

title: Very inspiring app
body:
I’ve struggled for the last year and a half to be alive. I’ve spent most of my time in bed with not much desire to do anything. Chronic pain has plagued me for about 18 years now and I’ve found myself at the point of total acceptance and really not even caring anymore. It’s taken my health, my career, my friends and my dignity and put then so far out of reach I’ve given up trying. I decided I needed to start living again and tried to find an app to help. Pathetic huh? My friends have become just acquaintances since I never go anywhere or do anything unless I HAVE to so I settled for an app, besides if it failed I wouldn’t have to tell anybody. The Fabulous app popped up pretty quick and looked like it could help coach me along. It seems I’ve gotten in right at the launch of the Sphere part. 
I did my one week trial and was thinking...a year membership? Seriously. The only thing I’ve been committed to faithfully is family, medicine and my bed. So I just did one month-because seriously, I know myself. I never follow thru. But here I am working on week 3 and I’m not in bed all day every day anymore!! Duke University understands the process of change and human habits and they have seriously hit a homerun with this. I feel like I am slowly rising like a Phoenix out of the ashes of my life. I am beginning to live again!! I take less medicine, eat healthier, drink a LOT more water than I ever did before and low and behold, I’m losing weight (and that wasn’t even a goal)!!
I highly recommend this to anyone looking to make changes in their life. Wether it’s getting off your bum, getting in touch with yourself, digging your way out of depression or just eating healthy. This is so worth every penny. YOU are worth every penny!! And the support is absolutely amazing. I am loving this journey and have no desire to stop it. Thank you Duke U!!

title: Dishonest marketing, so disappointed I may delete the app.
body: Earlier this evening I was just telling my boyfriend to download this app, after it got me back on my treadmill when I’ve been avoiding exercise for months. BUT, I’m not sure I want to continue using it myself! After checking off that I exercised, I received a letter congratulating me on using the app “so long” (I’ve had it for just a few weeks) and offering me “a gift” for a discount on a subscription to the fabulous sphere which is “being released the September 02”. Hold on... a quick Google search showed me the fabulous sphere has been available for quite some time. Why am I being lied to?! My guess is that science says people are more likely to pay money for something that seems new, so the app producers thought they could direct every user to think they were getting something new by literally lying to the user. Nice try, Fabulous. I have a Master’s degree in Clinical Psychology, you’re not fooling me. Now, I’m trying to decide whether or not to delete the app because of the despicable tactics. This is HUGELY disappointing because I really wanted to see how long-term use could help me craft better habits, and hoped to glean something to help my therapy clients as well.

body: This app is beautiful to look at and has nice soothing music. I have succeeded in establishing the three habits you start with. But I find the app hard to navigate. Every so often you get a “letter” which is nicely written and informative. But if you don’t have time to read it when it pops up, I can’t find a way to locate the letters and read them later. Same with recording your completion of habits—if you haven’t done the task when the app asks you about it, I can’t find a way to go back and fill in tasks I did but didn’t record. So my overall record looks a lot worse than it really is :-( I’m at the point now where I’m consolidating the first set of tasks. I’m supposed to let the app know when the habits are solid—but how? The app doesn’t tell me.—It’s both good and bad that there are a lot of places to go from a particular screen. But if you want to go back to the previous screen, I can’t figure out how. So: lots of potential, still has growing pains.

title: Unbelievably Helpful & Motivating!
body:
The best part of this app is that it’s basic features are free - I used this for a few weeks before doing the free week trial for the full thing. It’s pretty pricey, and normally I would have zero qualms about not paying, BUT this app is different than most. I could absolutely keep using the free version and use other apps/my own research to supplement the “gaps”. 

However, this app has really made it easy for me to change my habits and I’m making far more steady progress and am seeing a change in my overall behaviors because of it. I never get past the first week with habit trackers or similar. I’ve been using it for almost a month and I love it! I am absolutely going to spend the $50 for a year (costs about a cup of coffee a month, broken down, and I’m taking advantage of the 50% off because $100 is just excessive and wildly unaffordable for an app. $50 is really expensive regardless, but if it helps me as much as it has been this month, then I’ll call it an investment in my personal growth and gladly spend it). 

If you are looking for something to help you build routines in your life, help you celebrate even the littlest of accomplishments (awesome for those who struggle with mental health and esteem issues, and a good boost in general), as well as a beautifully functional app that encourages and supports you every step of the way - you NEED to download Fabulous and try it. 

I’m already seeing a huge difference in my energy levels, slightly lowered anxiety (routines and rituals add stability in my life), and just feel WAY MORE prepared to start my day since using Fabulous. I’ve been raving about it to my friends and family and will continue to do so. 

Developers: I love this app, please keep developing it! 

I’d love to see a feature where I can choose the colors of my icons, more icons and ritual pictures to choose from, and especially would love to edit the backgrounds and write reminders on the cards for my habits. For example, Drink Water habit has a little quote box that has encouraging messages every time I use it - I love these and would like to add my own for my custom habits. I would use it for encouragement as well as more detailed notes and reminders to myself. 

Thanks for such an awesome self-help app!!

title: Why a subscription?
body:
This app actually seems pretty cool. The presentation is very nice and the program seems like it would work. However, I have NO CLUE why it should be subscription based instead of just paying once to buy the app.

I understand the point of subscriptions. You pay monthly for something that has a constant cost. Electricity, food, printed magazines, water, etc. In those cases, the consumer uses a product and the company must create new product and therefore the consumer must pay again.

I don’t understand this new trend of paying for a subscription just to use software. Why would I continue to pay for this app over and over again? And once I stop paying, it’s not mine anymore. This makes no sense. Why would I “subscribe” to my computer, allowing Mac to own it, and the second I’m done, they come take it away? Why would I subscribe to use my sunglasses and then turn them in once I’m done paying a monthly fee for them? Why would I subscribe to a digital download of the avengers movie and keep paying monthly so that I can keep it? I wouldn’t. In all these cases I would pay once for the product then it is mine.

So why would I pay for this app once, then continue to give the developer money just to use it. I’m not wanting to RENT the app. I want to BUY IT!

Develop your app, sell the app, and fix bugs as you go for free because the buyer paid for a working app that should be free of bugs. Don’t fall victim to this practice. Don’t subscribe to this. Think of all the things in your life you wouldn’t have if you had to keep paying for them or you lose them.

title: Sphere book keeping
body:
This review is about the how Sphere/Fabulous deals with their accounting and money they charge and keep from a consumer.  The review of only one star is because:
When it was time to choose an offer after the initial trial period I received multiple personalized Fabulous/Sphere offers to continue.  The offers were for two different prices and each offer had a caveat that the offer was only for a limited time so hurry.  I elected to choose the least expensive yearlong offer price. I pressed the provided selection button.  FYI. All of the offers and renewal instructions were within my actual account on my phone with my name listed.  Nothing happened.  I pressed the selection button again and even tried rebooting my phone.  So I sent an email trying to explain the Applications site problem and to explain what I was trying to do and to try and lock in the price that I could afford.   After a day or so I tried again to purchase a yearlong choice and this time The sites’ business side was working-so I the followed the instructions.  The offer page I was working on had NO price; but, I didn’t think it was a problem since I had selected the ad for the least expensive offer right on my phone.  I paid and when the payment showed up on my bank statement, the price taken out was double the stated sale price!   I tried unsuccessfully to get my overpayment back.  Hence, the 1 star, which is really sad since the business end of Fabulous/Sphere should be as fabulous as I believe the concept and actual application is.  Fabulous is incongruent!

title: Best App for ADHD!
body:
This is the BEST app I have found for someone with ADHD.

 I have not managed to keep any type of routine (unless mindlessly jumping from one idea to the next counts as a routine). I’ve tried all sorts of ToDo list apps, calendars, schedules, setting a million alarms and reminders. I even paid for an app specifically designed for ADHD. 

Nothing worked. 😩

I’d look at ToDo lists and calendars, start on the first thing, then find myself distracted before I made it to the 2nd. Alarms, I’d just turn them off and forget about it (seriously I have an alarm that goes off everyday that says “get news paper” that I set over a year ago).

This app is amazing. I’m currently using the free version but I’m probably going to upgrade. The free version has plenty of features to get a routine started. They have lots of preprogrammed habits that are great to choose from. You can add your own as well and order them how you like. You can set a timer for each item.

 The best part is that when you press start on your routine it goes from one item to the next. So instead of looking at a list it will have a full screen timer. For example, you may have brush your teeth as your first thing. It will have a colourful screen that says “brush teeth” with a 3 minute timer. You can check it off before the timer or after the timer goes off. Then it moves to the next item on the list. This is probably the one reason it works so well for ADHD. Because I’d have to exit out of the routine to stop it, it keeps me from impulsively looking at other things on the app or wondering off into Facebook land. 

The timer on items also puts that little bit of pressure that us ADHD folks need in order to accomplish anything. It gives a sense of urgency. 

I’m so happy to have found something that actually works!

It seems to me as though the $49 allows you to subscribe to sphere - but how is sphere related to fabulous.  I get the sense that the group of developers just accepted every idea in the brainstorming session and dumped it all in the app without a road map.  It feels a little like Alice in Wonderland if it included random requests for additional cash she had to cough up to continue.
Also the water goal?  Okay I all ready do that but fine I kept with it .... breakfast ... really?  Again got that covered but okay - I began to wonder if I was starting in the wrong place so I sent an email and got back a “thanks for your input”.  Very “Alice in W”. So I wrote again and said I wanted to understand the interface and progression better.  Got a response in their jargon about sphere ... Like wonderland it seems exciting then you just get confused and want it to end.

title: Nice but lacking iOS Health app integration
body:
Update: according to their support, there are no plans to add Health app integration, which also means only they have the data.

The goal of replacing multiple apps will not work until the app includes the basic framework that the majority of other health apps use. Without HealthKit support, you must continue to rely on other apps if you want to keep your data. Considering the subscription price, this should be a 1.0 feature.

Timers do not work in the background or when the phone is locked. You have to keep the screen on to use timers.

If you accidentally mark a habit as done, there is no way to uncheck it.

Until then, it’s basically a nice to do list  with articles. Useful, but not what it could be.

title: Fabulous is .. well .. ok I won’t say it but it is!!
body: I have found myself off track & wandering through life after a few years of retirement and then a great deal of personal loss.  2018 resolutions were filled with hopes of finding something to restore some normalcy to my life; that reading a good book in front of the fire on a rainy day kind of normalcy.  I had already made the commitments to weight & fitness long before resolution season & they were going fairly well.  I just happened across the Fabulous app when I was in the App Store looking for a To Do list app.  It has truly been the answer to what I’ve been looking for, although I had no way of knowing for what I was searching.  Fabulous is taking me back to the basics, and teaching me how to instill habits again, something I had unknowingly given up.  Having this structure is giving me something to lean on as I begin to learn how to be myself again, after so much sadness and misery.  Thank you Fabulous developers for creating such an innovative program to help those of us that have derailed.  One thing, I did sign up for their upgraded program, Sphere, and it was just too much for me to take in.  Maybe later but for now I will let Fabulous take care of my needs!!  I am Fabulous after all!!

title: So far, finding Fabulous UN-fabulous.
body:
Not supported for use in more than once device AND does not save progress if has to be reloaded. 

I read about the app and got very excited. I am absolutely someone who struggles with change and who appreciates the idea of small steps with regular reminders. So, I signed up and paid $50 for a year. I was on my iPad when I did that. I decided to have it on my iPhone too, so I could have reminders on both the devices I use regularly. It didn’t work. I wrote to the fabulous folks, and they said that the app is only supported for use one ONE device. So then - since I use my phone most - I deleted it from my iPad and had to delete it from my phone, too, and start after. However, the app developers ALSO have not developed a way for people to keep our progress if we delete and reload the app. This is surprising given that the simplest games allow for use on multiple devices and remember my progress. 

I think the IDEA is fabulous, but the execution - so far - is a mess. I think hey rolled this out before they were ready and I am NOT happy to have spent $50. This has created anything BUT peace and equanimity for me.

body:

The sound doesn’t work anywhere in the app, yet it pauses my Spotify and podcast. Very annoying. The “sound doesn’t work? Enable notifications” tip isn’t helpful: notifications are fully enabled. Sound? Music? Alarms? I wouldn’t even know if this thing actually did have them.
The design is pretty, but it needs to be paired down quite a bit. Full screen pages for each step in a ritual is unnecessary, large 1/3 screen square icons in the stories advertising different rituals is unnecessary... everything is large and flashy.

I want to like the app in spite of its flaws but the cost just disgusts me. Don’t be greedy! I will be deleting this app for that reason.

title: Disappointed.
body: When I had an Android I loved this app so much. It was very helpful to me in reaching my goals, and had so many options that were convenient to me. Although they couldn’t reveal the release date, I was so excited to find that it would be available to ios in just a few weeks. When it was available I downloaded Fabulous, so excited to start with the app again on ios, but I was extremely disappointed to find that nearly all of the options that had been available for FREE before were now only available for purchase! All the options I had before were included in a membership, which is very pricy costing over $60 a year! Who’s going to pay that much money for a motivational app? People download this app in hopes that they can transform their lives efficiently and without cost. So upset that this app had to turn into an one that is no longer convenient and cheap for users, but is just asking for money. If these options were free again, this app would get a 5 star review for sure. But now, all this deserves is a 2 if not a 1 star review. Can’t believe this app had to turn into this.

body: My wife made me download this. I probably would not have given it much thought if I had not seen that this was coming from Duke and Dan Ariely’s insights. Ariely is the foremost behavioral economist in the world. (Sorry R Thaler). The team did a good job putting this together. I encourage you to download and pay for this app so they can continue putting theory into practice to help you realize your full potential. It’s not perfect right but it is only going to get better with your support and encouragement.

author: razzledazzlerex

title: So far I really like it
body: This app is very refreshing. Most other apps use language that makes you compete with yourself to be “healthier.” I usually lose motivation almost immediately. But not with this one. I feel like Fabulous is very intentional about creating new life changes by adjusting one habit at a time. It’s about holistic wellness and the easy/welcoming interface reflects that too. I don’t feel as overwhelmed with change and I appreciate the little tasks it gives me for a happier me. What’s nice is that you have the option to add your own tasks (e.g exercising, cooking, cleaning, meditating, disconnecting, calling parents, etc) to speed up the process if you’d like. It’s very go-at-your-own-pace kinda thing. I love it. Would definitely recommend anyone wanting to make small, but eventually big, changes in their life to try this out.

title: I have been waiting for this!
body: I used to have this app on my Android and I loved it. It’s really useful. No more setting various alarms and reminders. Doing it myself was a lot of effort, so I’m very grateful to have this again. The Rise & Shine tone is my favorite. It was the first thing I sought out after downloading. I’m still so impressed by the quality and lack of ads in the free version that this time I plan on purchasing the pro version. (A monthly payment option would be helpful tho; hint hint.) All in all, this app has helped me to be a better person. I can’t recommend it highly enough.
